statement: The Riemann hypothesis holds up to height $H=3\,000\,175\,332\,800$: the lowest $12\,363\,153\,437\,138$ non-trivial zeros $\rho$ have $\Re\rho=1/2$ (equivalently every non-trivial zero with $0<\gamma\le H$ lies on the critical line and, in the counted range, all expected zeros are accounted for).
hypotheses: correctness of Arb ball arithmetic and the producer code of Platt (2017)
rigorous truncation bounds of Platt 2017 (incl. bound for $|\Gamma((\sigma+it)/2)|e^{\pi t/4}$, A.2 of [21], slightly improved)

statement: With Schoenfeld's RH bound $|\psi(x)-x|\le\frac{\sqrt x}{8\pi}\log^2x$ valid for $x>59$ whenever RH holds up to $H\ge4.92\sqrt{x/\log x}$ (Buthe), one has unconditionally: $|\psi(x)-x|\le\frac{\sqrt x}{8\pi}\log^2x$ for $59<x\le2.169\cdot10^{25}$; $|\theta(x)-x|\le\frac{\sqrt x}{8\pi}\log^2x$ for $599<x\le2.169\cdot10^{25}$; $|\pi(x)-\operatorname{li}(x)|\le\frac{\sqrt x}{8\pi}\log^2x$ for $2657<x\le2.169\cdot10^{25}$.

The de Bruijn-Newman constant satisfies $\Lambda\le0.2$ (improving 0.22; Polymath15 Table 1 row 2 requires $H>2.51\cdot10^{12}$, with their X corresponding to 2H). Combined with Rodgers-Tao $\Lambda\ge0$ this gives $0\le\Lambda\le0.2$. RH is equivalent to $\Lambda\le0$.

Evaluate the completed zeta function (Hardy Z-type real-valued function) on the critical half-line on a lattice with sampling rate ~0.01 (about 25 samples per zero on average); each sign change certifies a zero on Re s=1/2; Turing's method (Trudgian's improvements I, II) shows the count of sign-change zeros equals N(H), hence no zeros off the line.
role: Core verification argument: rigorous counting + Turing completeness.

statement: Code rewritten from MPFI to Arb (midpoint-radius ball arithmetic, ~50% space saving); no attempt to isolate zeros beyond what is needed (the default sampling isolates 999 997.5 of every 10^6 zeros).
role: Performance; keeps rigor via ball arithmetic.

statement: About 7.5 million core-hours on 3.6GHz Xeons; ~110 000 units of height per GHz-hour (vs 80 000 000 for Gourdon's non-rigorous double-precision FFT and 3 800 for Wedeniwski).
role: Documents cost and comparison with unpublished/non-rigorous earlier verifications (Gourdon H=2.44e12, Wedeniwski ZetaGrid ~2.41e11 claim).

statement: Assume RH. For large real $t$, $|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|\ll\exp\Big(\frac{\log2}{2}\frac{\log t}{\log\log t}+O\Big(\frac{\log t\,\log\log\log t}{(\log\log t)^2}\Big)\Big)$. Equivalent: $\log|\zeta(\frac12+it)|\le(\frac{\log2}2+o(1))\frac{\log t}{\log\log t}$.

On RH with $\rho=\tfrac12+i\gamma$: $\log|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|=\log t+O(1)-\tfrac12\sum_\gamma f(t-\gamma)$, where $f(x)=\log\frac{4+x^2}{x^2}$ (from Hadamard factorization of $\xi$ at $s=\frac12+it$ and $-\frac32+it$ and Stirling).

For each $\Delta>0$ there is an entire $g_\Delta$ with (i) $-C/(1+x^2)\le g_\Delta(x)\le f(x)$ for real $x$ and $|g_\Delta(x+iy)|\ll\frac{\Delta^2}{1+\Delta|x+iy|}e^{2\pi\Delta|y|}$; (ii) $\hat g_\Delta$ real, supported in $|\xi|\le\Delta$, $|\hat g_\Delta|\ll1$; (iii) $\int_{-\infty}^\infty(f-g_\Delta)\,dx=\frac1\Delta\big(2\log2-2\log(1+e^{-4\pi\Delta})\big)$ [as printed; the exact normalization should be checked in the source].

For any $\Delta>0$ (RH): $\log|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|\le\frac{\log t}{2\pi\Delta}\log\frac{2}{1+e^{-4\pi\Delta}}+\frac12\mathrm{Re}\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\Lambda(n)}{n^{1/2+it}}\hat g_\Delta\big(\frac{\log n}{2\pi}\big)+O\Big(\frac{\Delta^2e^{\pi\Delta}}{1+\Delta t}+1\Big)$. With $\sum_n\Lambda(n)n^{-1/2}|\hat g_\Delta(\log n/2\pi)|\ll e^{\pi\Delta}$ and the choice $\pi\Delta=\log\log t-3\log\log\log t$ one gets Thm 1.1.

Explicit formula for $\sum_\rho h(\gamma)$ for $h$ analytic in $|\mathrm{Im}\,s|\le\frac12+\epsilon$, real on reals, $|h(s)|\ll(1+|s|)^{-(1+\delta)}$: $\sum h(\gamma)=h(\frac1{2i})+h(-\frac1{2i})-\frac1{2\pi}\hat h(0)\log\pi+\frac1{2\pi}\int h(u)\mathrm{Re}\frac{\Gamma'}\Gamma(\frac14+\frac{iu}2)du-\frac1{2\pi}\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\Lambda(n)}{\sqrt n}\big(\hat h(\frac{\log n}{2\pi})+\hat h(-\frac{\log n}{2\pi})\big)$.
role: Converts sum over zeros of g_Delta(t-gamma) into a short prime sum (imported, standard)

statement: For $f_\mu(x)=\int_0^\infty(e^{-\lambda|x|}-e^{-\lambda})d\mu(\lambda)$ with $0<\int\lambda/(\lambda^2+1)d\mu<\infty$, $G_\mu(z)=\lim_N(\cos\pi z/\pi)^2\sum_{n=-N}^{N+1}\big[\frac{f_\mu(n-1/2)}{(z-n+1/2)^2}+\frac{f_\mu'(n-1/2)}{z-n+1/2}\big]$ is entire of exponential type at most $2\pi$, $G_\mu\le f_\mu$ on R, and minimizes $L^1$ distance to $f_\mu$ among such minorants.
role: Source of the extremal minorant g_Delta

statement: $\int_0^\infty(e^{-\lambda|x|}-e^{-\lambda})\frac{2(1-\cos2\Delta\lambda)}{\lambda}d\lambda=\log\frac{4\Delta^2+x^2}{x^2}-\log(4\Delta^2+1)$, i.e. $f_\Delta(x)=f(x/\Delta)-f(1/\Delta)$ is of Carneiro-Vaaler type for $d\mu_\Delta=\frac{2(1-\cos2\Delta\lambda)}\lambda d\lambda$.
role: Shows log((4+x^2)/x^2) is covered by the Carneiro-Vaaler class

statement: $|G_\Delta(x+iy)+f(1/\Delta)|\ll\frac{\Delta^2}{1+|x+iy|}e^{2\pi|y|}$ via Poisson summation $\sum(\cos\pi z/\pi)^2(z-n+\frac12)^{-2}=1$ and $f(x)\le4/x^2$, $|f'(x)|\le8/(|x|(4+x^2))$.
role: Growth control needed to apply the explicit formula

statement: Assume RH. For t sufficiently large, $-\left(\frac{\pi}{24}+o(1)\right)\frac{\log t}{(\log\log t)^2}\le S_1(t)\le\left(\frac{\pi}{48}+o(1)\right)\frac{\log t}{(\log\log t)^2}$, with the $o(1)$ terms $O(\log\log\log t/\log\log t)$.
Assume RH. For t sufficiently large, $|S(t)|\le \frac14\frac{\log t}{\log\log t}+O\left(\frac{\log t\,\log\log\log t}{(\log\log t)^2}\right)$.
location: Sec 1 p.2; proved in Sec 4 (from Thm 1 via Lemma 7) and again in Sec 5 (directly, via extremal functions for an odd function)

statement: Assume RH, $f_1(x)=1-x\arctan(1/x)$. For $t\ge2$: $S_1(t)=\frac{1}{4\pi}\log t-\frac1\pi\sum_\gamma f_1(t-\gamma)+O(1)$, sum over ordinates of nontrivial zeros $\rho=1/2+i\gamma$.
role: Turns S_1 into a sum over zeros of a fixed test function, so extremal majorants/minorants can be applied. Proof uses S_1(t)=(1/pi) int_{1/2}^{3/2} log zeta(sigma+it) d sigma + O(1) (Titchmarsh Thm 9.9) and Hadamard factorization of xi.

statement: Assume RH, $F(x)=\arctan(1/x)-x/(1+x^2)$. Then $S(t)=\frac1\pi\sum_\gamma F(t-\gamma)+O(1)$ for t not an ordinate; F=-f_1'.
role: Same representation for S(t); used for the direct proof in Sec 5.

statement: Guinand-Weil explicit formula under RH for h analytic in $|\Im s|\le 1/2+\epsilon$ with $|h(s)|\ll(1+|s|)^{-(1+\delta)}$, h real on the real line: $\sum_\rho h(\gamma)=h(1/(2i))+h(-1/(2i))-\frac1{2\pi}\hat h(0)\log\pi+\frac1{2\pi}\int h(u)\Re\frac{\Gamma'}{\Gamma}(\frac14+\frac{iu}2)du-\frac1{2\pi}\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\Lambda(n)}{\sqrt n}(\hat h(\frac{\log n}{2\pi})+\hat h(-\frac{\log n}{2\pi}))$.
role: Imported tool (Iwaniec-Kowalski Thm 5.12); converts zero sums into prime sums and a gamma integral.

statement: For $f_1$ and $\Delta\ge1$ there are unique real entire $g^\pm_\Delta$ of exponential type $2\pi\Delta$ with $g^-_\Delta\le f_1\le g^+_\Delta$, $|g^\pm_\Delta(z)|\ll \Delta^2 e^{2\pi\Delta|y|}/(1+\Delta|z|)$, $\hat g^\pm_\Delta$ continuous, supported in $[-\Delta,\Delta]$, $\ll1$, and exact L^1 distances $\int(f_1-g^-_\Delta)=\int_{1/2}^{3/2}\frac1\Delta\{\log(1+e^{-2\pi\Delta(\sigma-1/2)})-\log(1+e^{-2\pi\Delta})\}d\sigma$, and similarly for g^+ with log(1-e^{...}).
role: Extremal majorant/minorant; supplies the sharp constant pi/48 and pi/24 (via integral of f_1 = pi/2 and the L^1 gap). Proved in Sec 6 by Gaussian subordination (Carneiro-Littmann-Vaaler).

statement: For $t\ge2$, $0<h\le\sqrt t$: $-\frac{h\log t}{4\pi}+\frac1h\int_{t-h}^{t}S(u)du+\vartheta^-_{h,t}\le S(t)\le\frac{h\log t}{4\pi}+\frac1h\int_t^{t+h}S(u)du+\vartheta^+_{h,t}$, with $\vartheta^\pm=O(h)+O(1/t)$.
role: Unconditional comparison between S(t) and averages of S, from monotonicity of N(t); with Theorem 1 and h ~ 1/loglog t gives Theorem 2.

statement: For $f(x)=\arctan(1/x)-x/(1+x^2)$ and $\Delta\ge1$ there are unique real entire extremal majorant and minorant $m^\pm_\Delta$ of exponential type $2\pi\Delta$ with Fourier transform supported in $[-\Delta,\Delta]$ and analogous size bounds.
role: Odd-function extremal problem solved via Carneiro-Littmann truncated Gaussian subordination; gives direct proof of Theorem 2.

statement: In H=L^2(0,\infty), with \rho(x)=x-[x], \rho_a(x)=\rho(1/(ax)), \chi=1_{(0,1]}, B^{nat}=\overline{\mathrm{span}}\{\rho_a: a\in\mathbb N\}: RH \iff \chi\in B^{nat}.
RH is equivalent to H-convergence of f_{\epsilon,n}=\sum_{a\le n}\mu(a)a^{-\epsilon}\rho_a as n\to\infty for all sufficiently small \epsilon>0.

Unconditionally, for the pointwise (a.e.) limit f_\epsilon(x)=\frac{1}{x\zeta(1+\epsilon)}-\sum_{a\le1/x}\mu(a)a^{-\epsilon}\{1/(ax)\}... one has f_\epsilon\to-\chi in H as \epsilon\downarrow0, via Mellin transform M(X_\epsilon f_{2\epsilon})(\tau)=-\frac{\zeta(1/2-\epsilon+i\tau)}{\zeta(1/2+\epsilon+i\tau)}\frac{1}{1/2-\epsilon+i\tau} and Lemma 2.2; under RH f_\epsilon\in B^{nat}.
hypotheses: convergence f_epsilon in B^nat needs RH; limit to -chi unconditional (as claimed)

statement: Let 1/2\le\alpha<1, \delta>0, \epsilon>0. If \zeta has no zeros in \Re s>\alpha, then for n\ge2 and \alpha+\delta\le\Re s\le1: \sum_{a\le n}\mu(a)a^{-s}=1/\zeta(s)+O_{\alpha,\delta,\epsilon}(n^{-\delta/3}(1+|\tau|)^{\epsilon}).
role: quantitative Littlewood: uniform-in-tau convergence of Mobius partial sums under RH (imported)

statement: For 0\le\epsilon\le\epsilon_0<1/4 there is C(\epsilon_0) with |\zeta(1/2-\epsilon+i\tau)/\zeta(1/2+\epsilon+i\tau)|\le C(1+|\tau|)^{\epsilon}, for all real \tau; unconditional, by functional equation and Gamma asymptotics.
role: gives K-domination of the Mellin transform uniformly in epsilon; makes epsilon->0 limit unconditional

statement: With Z(\sigma)=\sum_k x_k^{-\sigma}, x_k=\rho_k(1-\rho_k)=\tfrac14+\tau_k^2, \mathrm{Re}\,\sigma>1/2: \lambda_n=-n\sum_{j=1}^{n}(-1)^j\frac{1}{j}\binom{n+j-1}{2j-1}Z(j), where the sum is over the pairs of zeros \rho=\tfrac12\pm i\tau_k grouped as in Eq. (2).
hypotheses: Z(\sigma) is the secondary zeta function of the zeros
derived from the Hadamard product (3) and the generating function (7)

statement: \lambda_n=\frac{(-1)^n n i}{\pi}\oint_C I(\sigma)\,d\sigma with I(\sigma)=\frac{\Gamma(\sigma+n)\Gamma(\sigma-n)}{\Gamma(2\sigma+1)}Z(\sigma), and C a contour encircling only the poles \sigma=1,\dots,n.

The generating function f(z)=\sum\lambda_n z^{n-1} has simple poles of residue 1 at z_k=(\tau_k-i/2)/(\tau_k+i/2) and \bar z_k inside the unit disc. Hence \lambda_n\sim\sum_{|z_k|<1} z_k^{-n}+\mathrm{c.c.} \pmod{o(e^{\varepsilon n})\ \forall\varepsilon>0}, with multiplicities. This gives exponentially growing oscillations of both signs.
hypotheses: at least one zero off the critical line

statement: If all zeros are on the critical line and Z has a double pole at \sigma=1/2 with polar part R_{-2}\varepsilon^{-2}+R_{-1}\varepsilon^{-1}, then \lambda_n=2\pi n[2R_{-2}(\log n-1+\gamma)+R_{-1}]+o(n). Hypothesis (16): N(T)=2T[2R_{-2}(\log T-1)+R_{-1}]+\delta N(T), \delta N(T)=O(T^\alpha), \alpha<1.
hypotheses: meromorphic Z with the stated polar part

statement: RH holds iff \lambda_n\sim \tfrac12 n(\log n-1+\gamma-\log 2\pi) \pmod{o(n)} (tempered growth to +\infty). RH fails iff \lambda_n\sim\sum_{\arg\tau_k>0}\big(\tfrac{\tau_k+i/2}{\tau_k-i/2}\big)^n+\mathrm{c.c.} \pmod{o(e^{\varepsilon n})}. The values R_{-2}=(8\pi)^{-1}, R_{-1}=-(4\pi)^{-1}\log 2\pi are used for \zeta.
hypotheses: RH-true branch via saddle point or Oesterle real-analytic argument; RH-false branch via Darboux

statement: \lambda_n=S_n+\bar S_n with S_n=-\sum_{j=1}^n\binom nj\eta_{j-1} (from (s-1)\zeta(s)) and \bar S_n=1-\tfrac{\log 4\pi+\gamma}{2}n+\sum_{j=2}^n(-1)^j\binom nj(1-2^{-j})\zeta(j). Unconditionally, \bar S_n\sim\tfrac12 n(\log n-1+\gamma-\log 2\pi)+\tfrac34-\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{B_{2k}}{4k}n^{1-2k}. Then S_n=o(n) iff RH, while S_n\sim\sum z_k^{-n}+\mathrm{c.c.} if RH fails.

If all zeros lie on the critical line, \lambda_n=2\int_0^\infty[1-\cos n\theta(T)]\,dN(T) with \theta(T)=2\arctan(1/2T). After integration by parts and Riemann-Lebesgue (using (16)), \lambda_n=n\int_0^\infty\frac{\sin t}{t}[8R_{-2}(\log\frac nt-1)+4R_{-1}]\,dt+o(n).
role: A rigorous real-analytic proof of RH => (17), attributed to J. Oesterle (private communication, unpublished).

statement: Under s\mapsto z=s/(s-1) type change of variable ([2]), the zeros \rho map to z_\rho; RH is equivalent to all z_\rho lying on |z|=1, and zeros off the line give poles with |z_k|<1.
role: Input to the Darboux step for the RH-false branch.

statement: \delta\lambda_n=(-1)^n 2n\,\mathrm{Res}_{\sigma=0}I(\sigma)=2Z(0)=7/4, matching numerics at the sub-leading level.
role: Numerical consistency check of the saddle-point/residue picture.

statement: Let \sigma\ge0, X\ge2, P_X(s)=\exp\big(\sum_{n\le X^2}\frac{\Lambda_X(n)}{n^s\log n}\big) with \Lambda_X(n)=\Lambda(n) for n\le X, \Lambda(n)\big(2-\frac{\log n}{\log X}\big) for X<n\le X^2, 0 otherwise, and Z_X(s)=\exp\big(\sum_\rho[F_2((s-\rho)\log X)-F_2((s-1)\log X)]\big), F_2(z)=2E_2(2z)-E_2(z). Then \zeta(s)=P_X(s)Z_X(s)\big(1+O(X^{-\sigma-2}/(\tau^{-2}\log^2X))\big)-type uniform error as in (10), for \tau=|t|+2.

Assume RH. For \sigma\ge\tfrac12+\tfrac1{\log X}, |s-1|\ge\tfrac1{10}, any X\ge2: \zeta(s)=P_X(s)e^{R_X(s)} with R_X(s)\ll X^{1/2-\sigma}\big(\Phi(\tau)+\frac{\log\tau}{\log X}\big)+\frac{X}{\tau^2\log^2X}; moreover \arg\zeta(\sigma+it)=-\sum\frac{\Lambda_X(n)\sin(t\log n)}{n^\sigma\log n}+O(R_X(s)) for \sigma\ge1/2. Here \Phi is an admissible function (e.g. \Phi(t)=\tfrac12\log\tau/\log\log2\tau by Goldston-Gonek-type results).

Assume RH. For 2\le X\le t^2, |s-1|\ge1/10, \tfrac12+C\frac{\log\log2\tau}{\log X}\le\sigma\le1 with C>1: \zeta(s)=P_X(s)\big(1+O(\log^{(1-C)/2}t)\big). Conversely, if this holds for 2\le X\le t^2 in that region, then \zeta has at most finitely many zeros to the right of \sigma=\tfrac12+C\frac{\log\log 2\tau}{\log X}.

With \zeta_X(s)=P_X(s)+\chi(s)\overline{P_X}(1-s)-type reflection (in the text \zeta_X(s)=P_X(s)+\chi(s)\overline{P_X(s)}), \chi the functional equation factor: under RH, for 2\le X\le t^2, |s-1|\ge1/10 and \tfrac12+C\frac{\log\log 2\tau}{\log X}\le\sigma\le1, C>1, \zeta(s)=\zeta_X(s)(1+O(\log^{(1-C)/2}\tau)); conversely this implies finitely many zeros of zeta to the right of that curve.

(RH for \zeta_X) Any zero \rho_X=\beta_X+i\gamma_X of \zeta_X(s) with 0\le\beta_X\le1 and \gamma_X\ge C_0 satisfies \beta_X=\tfrac12. Proof: P_X never vanishes, so zeros need |\chi(s)|=1, which Lemma 6.1 localizes to the critical line.

N_X(t)\ge\frac t{2\pi}\log\frac t{2\pi}-\frac t{2\pi}-\frac1\pi\sum_{n\le X^2}\frac{\Lambda_X(n)\sin(t\log n)}{n^{1/2}\log n}+O_X(1) (unconditional, Thm 7.1). Under RH and 2\le X\le t^2 the sum f_X(t)\ll\Phi(t)+\log\tau/\log X (Thm 7.2). Under RH there is a constant C_3 with N_X(t) asymptotic to N(t) up to the same trigonometric sum for X<\exp(\cdot) and an unconditional count N\ll t\log t for X\le t^{C_4} (Thm 7.6).

Assume RH. There is C_3>0 such that if X<\exp(C_3\log t/\Phi(t)) then all zeros of \zeta_X(\tfrac12+it) with t\ge C_0 are simple and N_X^{(1)}(t)=N_X(t) is given by Thm 7.1. Unconditionally, for X\le\exp(o(\log^{1-\epsilon}t)), the number of simple zeros up to height t is (1+o(1))\frac t{2\pi}\log\frac t{2\pi}.

Assume RH. Let \gamma<\gamma' be consecutive zeta zero ordinates and I a closed subinterval of (\gamma,\gamma'). Then for all sufficiently large X, \zeta_X^*(\tfrac12+it) has no zeros in I and |\zeta_X^*(\tfrac12+it)|\to2|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)| as X\to\infty, uniformly in t in I. So zeros of zeta_X converge to the zeros of zeta.
Assume RH, \Phi admissible, \sigma>1/2 bounded. Then \sum_\gamma\frac{\sigma-1/2}{(\sigma-1/2)^2+(t-\gamma)^2}\ll\log\tau+\frac{\Phi(t)}{\sigma-1/2}.
role: Controls the sum over zeros defining Z_X(s) and R_X(s); converts RH into a bound in the right half of the strip.

statement: Let \sigma be bounded, \sigma\ge1/2, |s-1|>1/10, 1\le X\le t^2. The Lindelof Hypothesis holds iff \zeta(s)=\sum_{n\le X}n^{-s}+O(X^{1/2-\sigma}\tau^\epsilon).
role: Contrast: short Dirichlet sums approximate zeta on the right half-strip under Lindelof, while the unconditional argument in Sect. 2 shows short sums cannot work on \sigma\le1/2.
location: Sect. 2, Theorem 2.1 and the mean square argument (4)

statement: Assume RH, \sigma\ge1/2 bounded, |s-1|>1/10, 2\le X\le t^2. Then \zeta(s)=\sum_{n\le X}n^{-s}+O(X^{1/2-\sigma}e^{C_1\Phi(t)}).
role: Dirichlet-sum approximation under RH with an explicit error term, compared with the Euler product approximation.

statement: There is an absolute C_0>0 such that if |\chi(\sigma+it)|=1 with 0\le\sigma\le1 and t\ge C_0, then \sigma=1/2.
role: Gives RH for \zeta_X (Theorem 6.2).

statement: Let $s(x,y)$ be a symmetric bilinear form on a vector space E over Q or R, and $\xi_0,\xi_1\in E$ with (1) $s(\xi_j,\xi_j)=0$, $s(\xi_0,\xi_1)=1$; (2) for every x with $s(x,x)>0$, $s(x,\xi_0)\ne0$ or $s(x,\xi_1)\ne0$. Then $s(x,x)\le2s(x,\xi_0)s(x,\xi_1)$ for all x in E.

$\mathrm{RH}\iff s(f,f)\le0$ for all real compactly supported f on $\mathbb R_+^*$ with $\int f(u)d^*u=\int f(u)du=0$, where $s(f,g)=N(f\star\tilde g)$, $\tilde g(u)=u^{-1}g(u^{-1})$, $N(h)=\sum_{n\ge1}\Lambda(n)h(n)+\int_1^\infty\frac{u^2h(u)-h(1)}{u^2-1}d^*u+c\,h(1)$, $c=\tfrac12(\log\pi+\gamma)$.
hypotheses: imported: Weil positivity, reduced to a small class by [13,17] and Li's criterion

statement: In the nuclear-space setting, $\mathrm{Tr}_{distr}\int h(w)\vartheta^*(w)d^*w=\sum_v\int_{K_v^\times}\frac{h(w^{-1})}{|1-w|}d^*w$ with spectral side involving all nontrivial zeros; minus sign leads to 'absorption spectrum' interpretation.

The set of points of the arithmetic site $\mathcal A=(\widehat{\mathbb N^\times},\mathbb Z_{max})$ over $\mathbb R^{max}_+$ is canonically isomorphic to $X_{\mathbb Q}=\mathbb Q^\times\backslash\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q}/\hat{\mathbb Z}^\times$, with Frobenius automorphisms $Fr_\lambda$ corresponding to the idele class group action.

Frobenius correspondences $\Psi(\lambda)$ on the square of the arithmetic site satisfy $\Psi(\lambda)\circ\Psi(\lambda')=\Psi(\lambda\lambda')$ if $\lambda\lambda'\notin\mathbb Q$ or both rational; if $\lambda,\lambda'$ irrational with $\lambda\lambda'\in\mathbb Q$, then $\Psi(\lambda)\circ\Psi(\lambda')=\mathrm{Id}_\epsilon\circ\Psi(\lambda\lambda')$.

On the quasi-tropical curve $C_p=\mathbb R_+^*/p^{\mathbb Z}$: (i) for a divisor D with deg(D) >= 0, the limit $\mathrm{Dim}_{\mathbb R}(H^0(D))=\lim_n p^{-n}\dim_{top}(H^0(D)_p^n)$ exists and equals deg(D); (ii) $\mathrm{Dim}_{\mathbb R}(H^0(D))-\mathrm{Dim}_{\mathbb R}(H^0(-D))=\deg(D)$ for all D in Div(C_p). The Jacobian J(C_p) is cyclic of order p-1.
hypotheses: p prime, C_p periodic orbit of the scaling flow

statement: On the square of the arithmetic site one expects $\mathrm{Dim}_{\mathbb R}(H^0(D))+\mathrm{Dim}_{\mathbb R}(H^0(-D))\ge\tfrac12D\cdot D$ for divisors D(f)=\int\Psi(\lambda)f(\lambda)d^*\lambda, with $\tfrac12D(f)\cdot D(f)=s(f,f)$, which together with the strategy of Sec 2.3 would yield (17).
hypotheses: an intersection theory and Riemann-Roch on the square of A (not available)
conditional_on: a yet-to-be-developed intersection theory/Riemann-Roch inequality on the square of the arithmetic site

statement: Abstract Hodge-index type inequality s(x,x) <= 2 s(x,xi_0)s(x,xi_1) from isotropic pair xi_0, xi_1 with s(xi_0,xi_1)=1 and positivity-forces-nonorthogonality.
role: Abstract skeleton of Weil's positivity step transposed to explicit formulas

statement: Arithmetic site A = (N^ x, Z_max): the topos of N^x-sets with structure sheaf Z_max (tropical integers) with N^x acting by Frobenius k -> kn.
role: Geometric space of the Riemann-Roch strategy

statement: Points of A over R^max_+ equal X_Q = Q^x \ A_Q / Z^x with Fr_lambda <-> idele action.
role: Bridge between NCG and topos

statement: Riemann-Roch on C_p: Dim(H^0(D)) - Dim(H^0(-D)) = deg(D).
role: Test of the quasi-tropical structure on periodic orbits

statement: Assume RH. Then $\limsup_{n\to\infty} c(n)=e^{\gamma}(2+\beta)=3.6444150964\ldots$, where $c(n)=\big(\frac{n}{\varphi(n)}-e^\gamma\log\log n\big)\sqrt{\log n}$ and $\beta=\sum_\rho \frac1{\rho(1-\rho)}=2+\gamma-\log\pi-2\log2=0.0461914179\ldots$
Under RH, for all $n\ge N_{120569}=2\cdot3\cdots1591883$, $c(n)<e^\gamma(2+\beta)$.
conditional_on: Maple 30-digit computation of c(N_k) for k<=50847534 (pi(10^9))

statement: Under RH, for all $n\ge2$, $c(n)\le c(N_{66})=c(2\cdot3\cdots317)=4.0628356921\ldots$
Under RH, for all $k\ge1$, $c(N_k)\ge c(N_1)=c(2)=2.2085892614\ldots$

Each of the four assertions (1.4)-(1.7) is equivalent to RH. If RH fails, $\liminf c(n)=-\infty$ and $\limsup c(n)=+\infty$ (via $\log f(x)=\Omega_\pm(x^{-b})$, some $0<b<1/2$, imported from Nicolas 1983 Th.3(c)).

Under RH, for $x\ge x_0=10^9$, with $f(x)=e^\gamma\log\theta(x)\prod_{p\le x}(1-1/p)$ and $W(x)=\sum_\rho x^{i\Im\rho}/(\rho(1-\rho))$: $-\frac{2+W(x)}{\sqrt x\log x}+\frac{0.055}{\sqrt x\log^2x}\le\log f(x)\le-\frac{2+W(x)}{\sqrt x\log x}+\frac{2.062}{\sqrt x\log^2 x}$, and corresponding bounds (2.17) for $1/f(x)-1$.

Under RH, if $10^9\le p_k\le x<p_{k+1}$ then $e^\gamma(2+W(x))-\frac{3.7}{\log x}\le c(N_k)\le e^\gamma(2+W(x))-\frac{0.07}{\log x}$; in particular $c(N_k)\le e^\gamma(2+\beta)-0.07/\log x$ and $c(N_k)\ge e^\gamma(2-\beta)-3.7/\log x$.

It is not known whether $\liminf W(x)=-\beta$; via Landau one only gets $\liminf W\le -1/(\rho_1(1-\rho_1))=-0.00499\ldots$. Challenges posed: find largest M<N_{k_1+1} with $c(M)\ge e^\gamma(2+\beta)$ ($k_1=120568$), and all n<N_{k_1+1} with c(n)>e^\gamma(2+\beta); and, if RH fails, bound the first k>k_0 with c(N_k) outside the range.
For $x\ge121$: $K(x)-\frac{S^2(x)}{x^2\log x}\le\log f(x)\le K(x)+\frac1{2(x-1)}$.
role: Reduces log f to the integral K of theta-error

statement: For $\Re z<1$, $F_z(x)=\frac{x^{z-1}}{(1-z)\log x}+r_z(x)$; if $\Re z=1/2$, $|r_z(x)|\le\frac{1}{|1-z|\sqrt x\log^2x}(1+\frac4{\log x})$; explicit bounds (2.4) for z=1/2 and (2.5) for z=1/3.
role: Explicit evaluation of zero contributions in the explicit formula

statement: Explicit monotonicity of $H(x)=1+\sum_{k=4}^{\kappa}x^{1/k-1/3}$ for $x\ge2^j,j\ge9$ and $L(x)=\sum_{k=2}^\kappa T(x^{1/k})/x^{1/3}$ for $x\ge 2^j, j\ge35$.
role: Technical input for Lemma 2.4

statement: Under RH, $\psi(x)-\theta(x)\ge\sqrt x$ for $x\ge121$, and for $x\ge1$: $(\psi(x)-\theta(x)-\sqrt x)/x^{1/3}\le1.332768\ldots\le4/3$ (the latter unconditional in origin: Robin 1984 Lemma 3; here reproved).
role: Controls $J-K$, i.e. prime-power contribution

statement: Under RH for $x>1$: $J(x)=-\frac{W(x)}{\sqrt x\log x}-J_1(x)-J_2(x)$ with $0<J_1\le\frac{\log2\pi}{x\log x}$, $|J_2|\le\frac{\beta}{\sqrt x\log^2x}(1+4/\log x)$.
role: Explicit-formula expression of J in terms of the oscillating sum W

statement: If $n\ge2$ and either $\omega(n)=k$ or $N_k\le n<N_{k+1}$ then $c(n)\le c(N_k)$.
role: Reduces sup over n to primorials (monotone-in-n argument with Rosser-Schoenfeld (1.1))

statement: \zeta(1+it)\neq0 for every real t\neq0 (i.e. \zeta has no zeros on the line \Re s=1; at t=0 it has the simple pole).
hypotheses: \zeta(s)=\prod_p(1-p^{-s})^{-1}, \Re s>1, meromorphic continuation with a simple pole at s=1, entire otherwise

statement: Generalisation of nonvanishing: any function f(s) holomorphic except for a simple pole, uniform on the line \Re s=1, and with \log f(s)=\sum a_n n^{-s} with all a_n \ge 0 for \Re s>1 is non-zero on \Re s=1; likewise a product over an arbitrary split of the primes into two classes provided it is holomorphic on the line (the 'exception: possibly at s=1'). Example: Schlomilch's function \sum\frac{1}{(2n+1)^s}\ldots.
hypotheses: f holomorphic (aside from at most one simple pole) on \Re s=1

statement: Dirichlet series L_\chi(s) with periodic coefficients (combinations of the Hurwitz-Cahen functions) are entire of genus 1 with \sim R\log R zeros in |s|<R (apart from the pole); under the Lipschitz conditions (k\ge3, x odd, etc.) L_\chi(1-s) is related to \overline{L_\chi(s)} by an exponential-trigonometric factor, hence all complex zeros lie in the strip 0\le\Re s\le1 and are symmetric about \Re s=1/2; extended to all Dirichlet series L (n.9 remarks 1-3). Also L_\chi(1+it)\neq0 by the same positivity argument, using Dirichlet's fundamental equation n.10.

For a>1 let N_a(x) be the number of primes in (x, x^a)... As s\to1^+, \sum\log\frac1{p}\ldots gives: for any \epsilon>0, infinitely often N_x>(1-\epsilon)... and infinitely often N_x<(1+\epsilon)...; hence if \sum_{p\le x}\log p/x has a limit, it is 1. Hadamard remarks this is the same type as Poincare's inequalities (extension to complex primes) and Tchebycheff.

For \mu>1 (and \mu=2 as the key case), \sum_{p<x}(\log p)\log^{\mu-1}(x/p)=(1+o(1))\,x\cdot c_\mu (the normalisation by \Gamma(\mu) from the Riesz-type kernel \frac1{2\pi i}\int_{(a)}x^z z^{-\mu}dz=\log^{\mu-1}x/\Gamma(\mu) is dropped in the OCR, but the paper says 'asymptotic to x'); in particular, with \mu=2, \sum_{p<x}\log p\log(x/p)\sim x; and deducing, by differencing x and x(1+h) and dividing by \log(1+h): \theta(x)=\sum_{p<x}\log p\sim x (Halphen's theorem), equivalently the prime number theorem \pi(x)\sim x/\log x by Tchebycheff.
hypotheses: product formula of \xi with genus 1 in s (Hadamard 1893)

statement: For (k,m)=1, \sum_{q\le x,\ q\equiv m\,(k)}\log q\sim x/\varphi(k) (the primes in a given residue class mod k have logarithmic density 1/\varphi(k)); the analogous Cahen-type integral with L-series gives it. Authors remarks that the general equation 'for mu in the Riesz weighted form' cannot apparently be deduced from this endpoint case, and error terms are asked about.

The same method (non-vanishing on Re s=1 from the positive-coefficient log and the Weber/Meyer series) applies to quadratic-form L-series of Weber and Meyer; for negative determinant a formula of Weber already supplies the needed analytic continuation and genus.
conditional_on: uniformity of the Weber and Meyer series (not proved here)

statement: If \zeta(1+it_0)=0 then \sum_p p^{-s}\cos(t_0\log p)\to-\infty like \log(s-1) as s\to1^+. Split primes into those with t_0\log p within angle a of 2k\pi... (class 1) and the rest. The ratio \rho_n=S'_n/S_n of the partial sums must tend to 1 as s\to1; then replacing t by 2t_0 forces Q_n\ge\theta' S_n with \theta'=\rho\cos2a-(1-\rho)>0 for suitable a, so that \Re\log\zeta(s+2it_0)\to+\infty which would make 1+2it_0 a pole of \zeta, a contradiction.
role: Core of the nonvanishing proof; uses only positivity of coefficients of \log\zeta and the double-angle identity 1+\cos\theta... (equivalent to Mertens' 3-4-1 inequality in angle form)

statement: The Hurwitz-Cahen functions are entire (apart from s=1) of genus 1, with the number of zeros in |s|<R of order R\log R, by the contour representation (8) and Hadamard's genus theorems applied to the entire integral factor (coefficient comparison with \Gamma's integral).
role: Gives convergence of \sum 1/|\alpha|^{1+\epsilon} needed to separate finitely many zeros and bound the rest

statement: Choose horizontal lines at heights between consecutive zero ordinates with gap \ge cA(A-1)/ (K\lambda); on these \left|\frac{\zeta'(z)}{\zeta(z)}\right|\le K'\log z_0 (from the partial fraction expansion (20) over zeros \alpha and trivial poles \beta and the zero count \le K\lambda A^{3\lambda}); the integrals over those horizontal segments tend to 0.
role: Replaces von Mangoldt-type zero-counting/zero-free information by a self-contained estimate valid whenever the genus is known

statement: After shifting contours, the residue at z=1 is -x; the residues at zeros not among the first M have total modulus < \epsilon x (tail of the convergent series \sum 1/|\alpha|^{a}), and the remaining contour integral is o(x).
role: Yields \sum_{p<x}\log p\log^{\mu-1}(x/p)\sim x

statement: \zeta(\sigma+it)\neq 0 for all |t|\ge 3 and \sigma\ge 1-\dfrac{1}{55.241\,(\log|t|)^{2/3}(\log\log|t|)^{1/3}}.
For sufficiently large |t| (asymptotic, ineffective threshold), \zeta(\sigma+it)\ne0 for \sigma\ge 1-\dfrac{1}{48.1588(\log|t|)^{2/3}(\log\log|t|)^{1/3}}.
\zeta(\sigma+it)\neq0 for |t|\ge2 and \sigma\ge 1-\dfrac{1}{5.558691\,\log|t|}.
For |t|\ge e^{1000}, \zeta(\sigma+it)\ne 0 whenever \sigma>1-\dfrac{0.05035}{h(t)}+\dfrac{0.0349}{h(t)^2}, where h(t)=\tfrac{27}{164}\log|t|+7.096.

With Thm 1.1, a prime lies between n^3 and (n+1)^3 for all n\ge \exp(\exp(32.76)); with Thm 1.2 and Pintz, \pi(x)-\mathrm{li}(x)\ll x\exp\{-d(\log x)^{3/5}(\log\log x)^{-1/5}\}, d=(56/(2\cdot 3^4 c^3))^{1/5}\ge 0.2123 for c=48.1588.

Zero detector (Ford Lemma 2.2): for s=1+it, -\Re\zeta'/\zeta(s)=\frac1{4\eta}\int \frac{\log|\zeta(s-\eta+2\eta iu/\pi)|-\log|\zeta(s+\eta+2\eta iu/\pi)|}{\cosh^2u}du+\frac{\pi}{2\eta}\sum_{|\Re(s-\rho)|\le\eta}\Re\cot\frac{\pi(\rho-s)}{2\eta}.
role: Converts upper bounds on zeta on two vertical lines into a zero-detecting inequality.

statement: Mollified version (Ford 4.5+4.6) with smoothing f, Laplace transform F, |F_0(z)|\le D/|z|^2; bounds \Re\sum\Lambda(n)f(\log n)n^{-s}.
role: Mollification; choice f(u)=\lambda e^{\lambda u}w(\lambda u), w=g*g from Heath-Brown Lemma 7.5.

statement: For K>1, b_j coefficients of a non-negative trigonometric polynomial of degree K: \int\frac{\sum_{j=1}^K b_j\log|\zeta(1+\eta+ijt_1+iut_2)|}{\cosh^2u}du\ge -2b_0\log\zeta(1+\eta).
role: Generalises Ford Lemma 5.1 to degree K; the place where high-degree polynomials enter.

statement: For 0<\eta\le1/4, t\ge100: N(t,\eta)\le 1.3478\eta^{3/2}B\log t+0.479+\frac{\log A-\log\eta+\frac32\log\log t}{1.879}; and an explicit bound for \sum_{|1+it-\rho|\ge\eta}|1+it-\rho|^{-2} for t\ge10^4.
role: Local zero-count and tail-of-zeros control; uses Ramare e^{\gamma(\sigma-1)}/(\sigma-1) bound and HSW N(T). Corrects a restriction (eta<=0.019) in Ford's Lemma 4.2 (fn 1, p.9).

statement: If \beta+it is a zero, t\ge10^4, 1-\beta\le\eta/2, no zeros in 1-\lambda<\Re s\le1, t-1\le\Im s\le Kt+1, then an explicit inequality in \lambda,1-\beta,\eta,A,B,b_0,b_1,b,R is satisfied (see paper for full display).
role: Master inequality; contradiction with it gives the region once eta=E(L_2/(BL_1))^{2/3}.
Principal source of improvement over Ford (deg 4) and Nielsen (deg 5).

statement: For a suitable weight $g$, $\int_{-\infty}^\infty|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|^{2k}g(t)\,dt=\int P_k\bigl(\log\tfrac t{2\pi}\bigr)(1+O(t^{-1/2+\epsilon}))g(t)\,dt$, where $P_k$ is a polynomial of degree $k^2$ given by $P_k(x)=\frac{(-1)^k}{k!^2(2\pi i)^{2k}}\oint\cdots\oint G(z_1,\dots,z_{2k})\frac{\Delta^2(z_1,\dots,z_{2k})}{\prod_j z_j^{2k}}e^{\frac x2\sum_{j=1}^k(z_j-z_{k+j})}dz$, with $G=A_k(z)\prod_{i,j=1}^k\zeta(1+z_i-z_{k+j})$ and $A_k(z)=\prod_p\prod_{i,j}\bigl(1-p^{-1-z_i+z_{k+j}}\bigr)\int_0^1\prod_{j=1}^k(1-e(\theta)p^{-1/2-z_j})^{-1}(1-e(-\theta)p^{-1/2+z_{k+j}})^{-1}d\theta$ (the extract prints the signs of the shifts partly garbled). Shifted version (1.5.6)-(1.5.7) has $\prod_{j,i}(z_j-\alpha_i)$ in the denominator.
conditional_on: conjecture (proved only for k=1,2, with O(T^{1/2+eps}) error for k=2 only in smooth-weight form)
location: Section 1.5, p.13; general form Conjecture 2.5.2.4, p.30

kind: theorem (quoted from [CFKRS] random matrix paper, CAND-01369)
statement: $J_k(U(N),0)=\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\frac{j!}{(k+j)!}\prod_{i=1}^k(N+i+j)$, and for general shifts $J_k(U(N),\alpha)=\frac{(-1)^k}{k!^2(2\pi i)^{2k}}\oint\cdots\oint G(z)\frac{\Delta^2(z)}{\prod_{i,j}(z_j-\alpha_i)}e^{\frac N2\sum(z_j-z_{k+j})}dz$ with $G(z)=\prod_{i,j=1}^k(1-e^{-z_i+z_{k+j}})^{-1}$.

For fundamental discriminants $d$ and a weight $g$ supported in $(0,\infty)$ or $(-\infty,0)$: $\sum^*_dL(\tfrac12,\chi_d)^kg(|d|)=\sum^*_dQ_k(\log|d|)(1+O(|d|^{-1/2+\epsilon}))g(|d|)$, where $Q_k$ is a polynomial of degree $k(k+1)/2$ given by the $k$-fold residue (1.5.12) with $G=A_k\prod_{i\le j}\zeta(1+z_i+z_j)$ and $\Delta(z_1^2,\dots,z_k^2)^2$. Equating log-conductors gives $2N=\log(|d|/\pi)+\frac{\Gamma'}{\Gamma}(\tfrac14+a)$.

$J_k(USp(2N),0)=2^{k(k+1)/2}\prod_{j=1}^k\frac{j!}{(2j)!}\prod_{1\le i\le j\le k}\bigl(N+\tfrac{i+j}2\bigr)$, $J_k(SO(2N),0)=2^{k(k+1)/2}\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}\frac{j!}{(2j)!}\prod_{0\le i<j\le k-1}\bigl(N+\tfrac{i+j}2\bigr)$ (the printed factor in 1.5.26 uses the index range $0\le i<j\le k-1$ as extracted), with shifted contour-integral forms (1.5.18), (1.5.28)-(1.5.29).

For $q$ squarefree, $H_n(q)$ the newforms in $S_n(\Gamma_0(q))$, $\sum_{f\in H_n(q)}L_f(\tfrac12)^k\langle f,f\rangle^{-1}=\sum_f R_k(n,q)\langle f,f\rangle^{-1}(1+O((nq)^{-1/2+\epsilon}))$ as $nq\to\infty$, where $R_k$ is the $k$-fold residue (1.5.23) with $G=A_k\prod_{i<j}\zeta(1+z_i+z_j)$ and $A_k$ of (1.5.25) (integral over $\sin^2\theta$ for orthogonal symmetry); $2N=\log(q/4\pi^2)+\frac{\Gamma'}\Gamma(n/2)$.

(1) Start with the product of $2k$ shifted $L$-functions. (2) Replace each by the two terms of its approximate functional equation, giving $2^{2k}$ terms. (3) Keep the $\binom{2k}{k}$ terms for which the product of $\chi$-factors is not oscillating. (4) Keep only the diagonal of the Dirichlet-series sums. (5) Complete the sums to infinity; call the total $M(s,\alpha)$. (6) Conjecture that $L$ and $M$ have the same average, with error $O(t^{-1/2+\epsilon})$. The authors state that the recipe 'is not a heuristic', that steps can discard terms of main-term size, and that other steps add terms back, with the conjecture being that these cancel.
conditional_on: unproved cancellation of the discarded and added terms

statement: For $I(\alpha,\beta,\delta)=\int_0^\infty\zeta(\tfrac12+it+\alpha)\zeta(\tfrac12-it-\beta)e^{-\delta t}dt$, for every $\eta>0$, $|\alpha|,|\beta|\le\tfrac12-\eta$, $|\arg\delta|\le\tfrac\pi2-\eta$: $I=\int_0^\infty\bigl(\zeta(1+\alpha-\beta)+(\tfrac t{2\pi})^{\alpha-\beta}\zeta(1-\alpha+\beta)\bigr)e^{-\delta t}dt+C_\delta(\alpha,\beta)+O(\delta\log1/\delta)$ uniformly, with $C_\delta(\alpha,\beta)\ll\log1/\delta$ and $C_\delta(\alpha,-\alpha)=-2\pi\zeta(2\alpha)$. Consequently $\lim_{\delta\to0}\bigl(\int_0^\infty|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|^2e^{-\delta t}dt-\int_0^\infty(2\gamma+\log\tfrac t{2\pi})e^{-\delta t}dt\bigr)=\pi$.

For $k=1$, $P_1(x)=x+2\gamma$, matching Ingham's theorem $\int_0^T|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|^2dt=\int_0^T(\log\tfrac t{2\pi}+2\gamma)dt+O(T^{1/2+\epsilon})$. For $k=2$ the recipe agrees with Motohashi's main term $L_r$ and gives the Ingham/Heath-Brown polynomial, with leading coefficient $\frac1{2\pi^2}$ (so $P_2(x)=\frac{1}{2\pi^2}x^4+\cdots$ in (5.1.4); numerically $0.0507x^4+0.6989x^3+2.426x^2+3.228x+1.312$). A residue computation yields the restated 4th-moment form (1.7.13) with $\frac{\zeta(1+x)^4\zeta(1+y)^4}{\zeta(1+x-y)\zeta(1+y-x)\zeta(2+2x+2y)}$.

For $|\alpha_j|<\delta$, the Dirichlet series $R(s;\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_{2k})$ converges absolutely for $\sigma>\tfrac12+\delta$ and has meromorphic continuation to $\sigma>\tfrac14+\delta$, with $R=\prod_{i,j=1}^k\zeta(2s+\alpha_i-\alpha_{k+j})A_k(s;\alpha)$ where $A_k$ is an Euler product of local factors $B_p=\int_0^1\prod_jL_p(e(\theta)/p^{s+\alpha_j})L_p(e(-\theta)/p^{s-\alpha_{k+j}})d\theta$ times the correction $\prod(1-p^{-2s-\alpha_i+\alpha_{k+j}})$.
role: identifies the arithmetic factor $A_k$ and its analyticity region, which is needed for the residue evaluation

statement: Let $F(a;b)$ be symmetric in each group of $k$ variables, regular near $0$, $f$ with a simple pole of residue 1 at 0, and $K=F\prod_{i,j=1}^kf(a_i-b_j)$. Then $\sum_{\sigma\in\Xi}K(\alpha_{\sigma(1)},\dots;\alpha_{\sigma(k+1)},\dots)=\frac{(-1)^k}{k!^2(2\pi i)^{2k}}\oint\cdots\oint K(z)\frac{\Delta(z_1,\dots,z_{2k})^2}{\prod_{i,j=1}^{2k}(z_i-\alpha_j)}dz$ over small circles about the $\alpha_j$.
role: converts the sum over $\binom{2k}{k}$ shuffles in the recipe to the contour integral of Conjecture 1.5.1.1

statement: For symmetric regular $F$, simple-pole $f$ of residue 1, and $K=F\prod_{i\le j}f(a_i+a_j)$ or $F\prod_{i<j}f(a_i+a_j)$: $\sum_{\epsilon_j=\pm1}K(\epsilon\alpha)$ and the sign-weighted version equal the $k$-fold contour integrals (2.5.5)-(2.5.6) with kernel $\Delta(z^2)^2\prod z_j$ (resp. $\prod\alpha_j$) over $\prod(z_i-\alpha_j)(z_i+\alpha_j)$.
role: symplectic/orthogonal analogue of Lemma 2.5.2.1

statement: General statement for $F(a;b)$ with $m$ $a$-variables and $n$ $b$-variables, $G=F\prod f(a_i-b_j)$, $f=1/s+c+\cdots$: the sum over $\Xi_{m,n}$ equals $\frac{(-1)^{m+n}}{m!n!}$ times the sum of residues of $G\Delta^2/\prod(z_i-\alpha_j)$ at $z=\alpha_\sigma$ (printed form partially garbled in extract).
role: master lemma from which 2.5.2.1 and 2.5.2.2 follow

statement: For $L_p(x)=(1-\gamma_px)^{-1}$ with $|\gamma_p|=1$ an explicit evaluation (the extract cuts off the statement) shows the local factor of $A_k$ is a polynomial in $p^{-1}$ and $p^{-\alpha_i}$, as noted in comment 3 after Theorem 1.5.1.2.
role: explicit form of the arithmetic factor; shows $A_k$ is polynomial in $p^{\pm\alpha_i}$

statement: $P_k(x)$ has leading term $\frac{g_ka_k}{k^2!}x^{k^2}$ with $a_k=A_k(0,\dots,0)$ and $g_k=k^2!\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\frac{j!}{(k+j)!}$ (eq. 1.3.3). This recovers the Keating-Snaith leading-order conjecture, which is a special case of Conjecture 1.5.1.1 (derivation re-done in Section 2.7).
role: consistency with Conrey-Ghosh/Keating-Snaith

statement: $P_k$ is a polynomial of degree $k^2$: the poles from $\zeta(1+z_i-z_{k+j})$ cancel $k^2$ of the $2k(2k-1)$ degrees of $\Delta^2$, so the residue requires Taylor terms of $\exp(\tfrac x2\sum z_j-z_{k+j})$ only up to degree $k^2$.
role: degree count for $P_k$

statement: Assume RH. For every real $k>0$ and $\epsilon>0$: $T(\log T)^{k^2}\ll_kM_k(T)\ll_{k,\epsilon}T(\log T)^{k^2+\epsilon}$. (Lower bound is Ramachandra's, under RH, for all real k>0.)
Assume RH, $k\ge0$ fixed, $T$ large: $\mathrm{meas}\{t\in[0,T]:|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|\ge(\log T)^k\}=T(\log T)^{-k^2+o(1)}$.

Assume RH. Let $T$ be large, $V\ge3$, $S(T,V)=\{t\in[T,2T]:\log|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|\ge V\}$. If $10\sqrt{\log\log T}\le V\le\log\log T$: $\mathrm{meas}\,S(T,V)\ll T\frac{V}{\sqrt{\log\log T}}\exp\Big(-\frac{V^2}{\log\log T}\big(1-\frac4{\log_3T}\big)\Big)$; if $\log\log T<V\le\tfrac12(\log\log T)\log_3T$: $\ll T\frac V{\sqrt{\log\log T}}\exp\Big(-\frac{V^2}{\log\log T}\big(1-\frac{7V}{4(\log\log T)\log_3T}\big)^2\Big)$; if $V>\tfrac12(\log\log T)\log_3T$: $\ll T\exp(-\tfrac1{33}V\log V)$. ($\log_3=\log\log\log$.)

Assume RH. Let $t\in[T,2T]$, $2\le x\le T^2$, $\lambda_0=0.4912\ldots$ the positive root of $e^{-\lambda}=\lambda+\lambda^2/2$. For all $\lambda\ge\lambda_0$: $\log|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|\le\mathrm{Re}\sum_{n\le x}\frac{\Lambda(n)}{n^{\frac12+\frac\lambda{\log x}+it}\log n}\frac{\log(x/n)}{\log x}+\frac{(1+\lambda)}2\frac{\log T}{\log x}+O\big(\frac1{\log x}\big)$.

Assume RH. For all large $t$, $|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|\le\exp\Big(\big(\tfrac{1+\lambda_0}4+o(1)\big)\frac{\log t}{\log\log t}\Big)\le\exp\Big(\frac38\frac{\log t}{\log\log t}\Big)$. (Take $x=(\log T)^{2-\epsilon}$ in the Proposition and bound the sum trivially.)

Assuming GRH: for primitive $\chi\bmod q$ ($q$ prime), $\sum^*|L(\tfrac12,\chi)|^{2k}\ll_{k,\epsilon}q(\log q)^{k^2+\epsilon}$ for all real $k>0$; for fundamental discriminants, $\sum^\flat_{|d|\le X}L(\tfrac12,\chi_d)^k\ll_{k,\epsilon}X(\log X)^{k(k+1)/2+\epsilon}$; analogous bounds for quadratic twists of an elliptic curve with exponent $k(k-1)/2+\epsilon$ (sketched).

Unconditionally, for $s$ not equal to 1 or a zero and $x\ge2$: $-\frac{\zeta'}\zeta(s)=\sum_{n\le x}\frac{\Lambda(n)\log(x/n)}{n^s\log x}+\frac1{\log x}\big(\frac{\zeta'}\zeta\big)'(s)+\frac1{\log x}\sum_\rho\frac{x^{\rho-s}}{(\rho-s)^2}-\frac{x^{1-s}}{(1-s)^2\log x}+\frac1{\log x}\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{x^{-2k-s}}{(2k+s)^2}$.
role: Selberg-type smoothed explicit formula (Titchmarsh 14.20); integrated in sigma to get log|zeta(s_0)|.

statement: Assume RH, $T\le t\le2T$, $2\le x\le T^2$, $\sigma\ge\tfrac12$: $\sum_{n\le x,\,n\ne p}\frac{\Lambda(n)\log(x/n)}{n^{\sigma+it}\log n\log x}\ll\log\log\log T+O(1)$.
role: Removes prime-square and higher prime powers; uses RH-explicit-formula bound $\sum_{p\le z}(\log p)p^{-2it}\ll z/T+\sqrt z(\log zT)^2$.

statement: For $T$ large, $2\le x\le T$, $k\in\mathbb N$ with $x^k\le T/\log T$, and complex $a(p)$: $\int_T^{2T}\Big|\sum_{p\le x}\frac{a(p)}{p^{1/2+it}}\Big|^{2k}dt\ll Tk!\Big(\sum_{p\le x}\frac{|a(p)|^2}p\Big)^k$.
role: Mean value theorem for high moments of short Dirichlet polynomials over primes (Gaussian-like moment growth k!).

statement: For $t\in[T,2T]$: $-\mathrm{Re}\frac{\zeta'}\zeta(s)=\frac12\log T+O(1)-F(s)$ with $F(s)=\sum_\rho\frac{\sigma-1/2}{(\sigma-1/2)^2+(t-\gamma)^2}\ge0$ (RH); consequently $\log|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|-\log|\zeta(s_0)|\le(\sigma_0-\tfrac12)\frac{\log T}2+O(1)-\frac{F(s_0)}2$ (using $\log(1+x^2)\ge x^2/(1+x^2)$).
role: Key positivity: zeros near the point only help the upper bound for log|zeta| (the 'benign' effect), enabling a one-sided inequality.

kind: theorem (exact CUE identity; proof via Selberg integral)
statement: For \mathrm{Re}\,s>-1, \quad M_N(s)=\langle |Z(U,\theta)|^s\rangle_{U(N)}=\prod_{j=1}^N \frac{\Gamma(j)\Gamma(j+s)}{(\Gamma(j+s/2))^2}, independent of \theta; for integer k\ge0, M_N(2k) is a polynomial in N of degree k^2.

For s\in\mathbb C, \quad L_N(s)=\Big\langle \big(Z/Z^*\big)^{s/2}\Big\rangle_{U(N)}=\prod_{j=1}^N\frac{\Gamma(j)^2}{\Gamma(j+s/2)\Gamma(j-s/2)}, with the branch of arg Z fixed by continuous variation along \theta-i\epsilon, \epsilon\to\infty-type normalization (Im log Z has jump \pi at eigenphases); \theta not an eigenphase.

kind: theorem (CLT, new proof; Im part earlier due to Costin-Lebowitz)
statement: As N\to\infty, \mathrm{Re}\log Z/\sqrt{\tfrac12\log N} and \mathrm{Im}\log Z/\sqrt{\tfrac12\log N} converge in distribution, jointly and independently, to standard Gaussians. Under the identification N=\log(T/2\pi) (eq. (8)) this is the exact analogue of Selberg's theorem (eq. (3)) for \log\zeta(1/2+it)/\sqrt{\tfrac12\log\log T}.

Cumulants of Re log Z: Q_n(N)=\frac{2^{n-1}-1}{2^{n-1}}\sum_{j=1}^N\psi^{(n-1)}(j). Cumulants of Im log Z: R_n(N)=\frac{(-1)^{1+n/2}}{2^{n-1}}\sum_{j=1}^N\psi^{(n-1)}(j) for n even, 0 for n odd. In particular Q_1=R_1=0, Q_2(N)=R_2(N)=\tfrac12\log N+\tfrac12(\gamma+1)+\tfrac1{24N^2}+O(N^{-4}); Q_n(N)=(-1)^n\frac{2^{n-1}-1}{2^{n-1}}\zeta(n-1)\Gamma(n)+O(N^{2-n}) for n\ge3; R_{2k}(N)=\frac{(-1)^{k+1}}{2^{2k-1}}\zeta(2k-1)\Gamma(2k)+O(N^{2-2k}), k>1 (so higher even cumulants of Im log Z tend to constants, proving a Costin-Lebowitz conjecture).

f_{CUE}(\lambda):=\lim_{N\to\infty}N^{-\lambda^2}\langle|Z|^{2\lambda}\rangle=\frac{G^2(1+\lambda)}{G(1+2\lambda)} (Barnes G; for \mathrm{Re}\,\lambda>-1/2); for integer k\ge1, f_{CUE}(k)=\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\frac{j!}{(j+k)!}, giving 1, 1/12, 42/9!, 24024/16! for k=1..4. Also \lim N^{\lambda^2}L_N(2\lambda)=G(1-\lambda)G(1+\lambda).

Assuming the limit in (4) exists, f(\lambda):=\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{(\log T)^{\lambda^2}}\frac1T\int_0^T|\zeta(1/2+it)|^{2\lambda}dt\Big/a(\lambda) equals f_{CUE}(\lambda)=G^2(1+\lambda)/G(1+2\lambda), i.e. \frac1T\int_0^T|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|^{2\lambda}dt\sim a(\lambda)\frac{G^2(1+\lambda)}{G(1+2\lambda)}(\log T)^{\lambda^2}, with a(\lambda)=\prod_p(1-1/p)^{\lambda^2}\sum_{m\ge0}\big(\frac{\Gamma(\lambda+m)}{m!\Gamma(\lambda)}\big)^2p^{-m}. Equivalent to f(n)=\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}j!/(j+n)!.
hypotheses: RH is assumed for the value-distribution comparison; the moment conjecture is stated for 'all lambda where moments are defined'
conditional_on: heuristic factorization of moments into a CUE factor and a prime-product factor

statement: For \beta\in\{1,2,4\}, \langle|Z|^s\rangle_{\beta,N}=\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}\frac{\Gamma(1+j\beta/2)\Gamma(1+s+j\beta/2)}{\Gamma(1+s/2+j\beta/2)^2}; cumulants Q^\beta_n(N)=\frac{2^{n-1}-1}{2^{n-1}}\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\psi^{(n-1)}(1+j\beta/2); Q^\beta_2(N)=\frac1\beta\log N+O(1).
hypotheses: circular ensembles with Dyson index beta

statement: Selberg: for any rectangle E, T^{-1}\mathrm{meas}\{t\in[T,2T]:\log\zeta(1/2+it)/\sqrt{\tfrac12\log\log T}\in E\}\to\frac1{2\pi}\int_E e^{-(x^2+y^2)/2}dxdy. Goldston (under RH and Montgomery's pair-correlation conjecture): \frac1T\int_0^T(\mathrm{Im}\log\zeta)^2=\tfrac12\log\log\frac T{2\pi}+\tfrac12(\gamma+1)+\sum_p\sum_{m\ge2}\frac{(1-m)\cdot}{m^2p^m}\ldots+o(1) (exact prime sum as in eq. (18)).
hypotheses: Selberg unconditional; Goldston under RH+pair correlation

statement: J(a,b,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,N)=\int_{\mathbb R^N}\prod_{j<m}|x_j-x_m|^{2\gamma}\prod_j(a+ix_j)^{-\alpha}(b-ix_j)^{-\beta}dx_j=\frac{(2\pi)^N}{(a+b)^{(\alpha+\beta)N-\gamma N(N-1)-N}}\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}\frac{\Gamma(1+\gamma+j\gamma)\Gamma(\alpha+\beta-(N+j-1)\gamma-1)}{\Gamma(1+\gamma)\Gamma(\alpha-j\gamma)\Gamma(\beta-j\gamma)}, valid under Re a,b,\alpha,\beta>0, Re(\alpha+\beta)>1, -1/N<Re\gamma<\min(\mathrm{Re}\alpha/(N-1),\mathrm{Re}\beta/(N-1),\mathrm{Re}(\alpha+\beta-1)/(2(N-1))).
role: Imported (Mehta, Ch. 17). Evaluates the CUE average after the Cayley-type change x_n=\cot\theta_n, giving M_N(s)=2^{N+sN}(N!(2\pi)^N)^{-1}J(1,1,N+s/2,N+s/2,1,N).

statement: By Haar invariance the average is independent of \theta; set \theta=0, write |e^{i\theta_j}-e^{i\theta_m}|^2=4\sin^2((\theta_j-\theta_m)/2), use \sin(\theta_j-\theta_m)=\sin\theta_j\cos\theta_m-\cos\theta_j\sin\theta_m to reach \prod|\cot\theta_m-\cot\theta_j|^2\prod\sin^{2(N-1)}\ldots, then x_n=\cot\theta_n.
role: Reduction of the CUE moment to a Cauchy-type Selberg integral.

statement: Barnes G: G(1+z)=(2\pi)^{z/2}e^{-[(1+\gamma)z^2+z]/2}\prod_{n\ge1}(1+z/n)^ne^{-z+z^2/(2n)}, G(z+1)=\Gamma(z)G(z), \log G(1+z)=\frac z2(\log2\pi-1)-(1+\gamma)\frac{z^2}2+\sum_{n\ge3}(-1)^{n-1}\zeta(n-1)\frac{z^n}n for |z|<1.
role: Tool for passing from the Gamma-product (6) to the N\to\infty asymptotics (15) and (17); also for the cumulant expansions.

statement: Independence of Re log Z and Im log Z: the joint generating function \langle|Z|^{s}e^{it\,\mathrm{Im}\log Z}\rangle factorizes in the large-N limit (as products of Gamma functions), implying asymptotic independence of the two parts.
role: Gives joint Gaussian limit in (iii). Statement paraphrased from the section heading and introduction; proof body only skimmed.

statement: N=\log(T/2\pi) (matrix size matched to the mean zero density at height T).
role: Dictionary between CUE and zeta; used for Selberg comparison, Odlyzko data (N\approx 42 near the 10^{20}th zero) and the moment conjecture. Heuristic, not a theorem.

statement: Let $\pi$ be a cuspidal automorphic representation of $GL_m/\mathbb Q$ and assume $m\le3$ or Hypothesis (1.7) (equivalently H: $\sum_p |a_\pi(p^k)\log p|^2/p^k<\infty$ for each fixed $k\ge2$). Let $f$ satisfy TF1-3 (symmetric; $f(x+t\mathbf 1)=f(x)$; rapid decay on $\sum x_j=0$) and $\mathrm{supp}\,\hat f\subset\{\xi:\sum_j|\xi_j|<2/m\}$. Let $g\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$, $h(r)=\int g(u)e^{iru}du$. Then as $T\to\infty$, $R_n(T,f,h)\sim\frac{m}{2\pi}T\log T\int_{-\infty}^\infty h(r)^ndr\int_{\mathbb R^n}f(x)W_n(x)\delta\big(\tfrac{x_1+\dots+x_n}{n}\big)dx$, where $R_n(T,f,h)=\sum^{\ne}h(\gamma_{j_1}/T)\cdots h(\gamma_{j_n}/T)f(\tfrac L{2\pi}\gamma_{j_1},\dots)$, $L=m\log T$, $W_n=\det K(x_i-x_j)$, $K(x)=\sin\pi x/\pi x$. No RH needed.
hypotheses: cuspidal $\pi$ on $GL_m/\mathbb Q$, unitary central character

statement: With the assumptions of Theorem 1.1 and RH for $L(s,\pi)$: $R_n(B_N,f)\to\int_{\mathbb R^n}f(x)W_n(x)\delta(\tfrac{x_1+\dots+x_n}{n})dx$ as $N\to\infty$, where $B_N$ are the first $N$ normalized zeros $\tilde\gamma=\frac m{2\pi}\gamma\log|\gamma|$.
Hypothesis H holds for $1\le m\le3$ (proved using $|\alpha_\pi(j,p)|\le p^{1/2-1/(m^2+1)}$ from (2.3), $|\alpha_2|=1$, $|\alpha_3|=1/|\alpha_1|$ for $m=3$, and Rankin-Selberg).

Assuming H, $\sigma(x)\sim(\log x)^2/2$ and $\sum_{n\le x}|c_\pi(n)|^2/n=\tfrac12\log^2x+O(\log x)$ where $c_\pi(n)=\Lambda(n)a_\pi(n)$. This second-moment universality (independent of $\pi$) is the source of universality of GUE.

For $\Phi\in C^1(\mathbb R^n)$ supported in $\sum|\xi_j|<2/m$ and $f(x)=\int\Phi(\xi)\delta(\xi_1+\dots+\xi_n)e(-x\cdot\xi)d\xi$: $\sum_{\text{all indices}}h_1(\tfrac{\gamma_1}T)\cdots h_n(\tfrac{\gamma_n}T)f(\tfrac L{2\pi}\gamma_1,\dots)=\kappa(h)\frac{TL}{2\pi}\int\Phi(v)C_O(v)dv+O(T)$, with $\int\Phi C_O=\Phi(0)+\sum_{r=1}^{[n/2]}\sum_{\text{r disjoint pairs}}\int\cdots\int|v_1|\cdots|v_r|\Phi(v_1e_{i(1),j(1)}+\dots+v_re_{i(r),j(r)})dv$.
Assuming RH for $L(s,\pi)$ and $\Phi\in C^2$ supported in $\sum|\xi_j|<2/m$, the unrestricted-in-height sums satisfy $C_n(f,T)\sim N(T)\int\Phi(u)C_O(u)du+O(T)$.

For $\sum_j|u_j|<2$, the Fourier transform $\hat W_n(u)$ of the GUE determinant $W_n(x)=\det K(x_i-x_j)$ equals $R_O(u)$, the combinatorial sieved prime-pair expression (4.16). Proposition 4.3: for $S$ with $\sum_{l\in S}u_l=0$, $\sum|u_l|<2$, $X_S(u)=(-1)^{|S|-1}Y_S(u)$.

For $g\in C_c^\infty$, $h(r)=\int g(u)e^{iru}du$: $\sum h(\gamma_\pi)=\delta(\pi)\{h(-i/2)+h(i/2)\}+\frac1{2\pi}\int h(r)\big(\log Q_\pi+\sum_j\tfrac{\Gamma_R'}{\Gamma_R}(\tfrac12+\mu_\pi(j)+ir)+\tfrac{\Gamma_R'}{\Gamma_R}(\tfrac12+\mu_\pi(j)-ir)\big)dr-\sum_n\tfrac{c_\pi(n)}{\sqrt n}g(\log n)+\tfrac{c_{\tilde\pi}(n)}{\sqrt n}g(-\log n)$.
role: Converts zero sums to prime sums.

statement: Bound $|\alpha_\pi(j,p)|\le p^{1/2-1/(m^2+1)}$ at all finite p, obtained by a global argument via Rankin-Selberg $L(s,\pi\times\tilde\pi)$.
role: Controls prime-power terms and ramified places; proves H for m<=3.

statement: Estimates for sums over prime tuples $n_1\cdots n_r=n_{r+1}\cdots n_{r+s}$ ($C_{r,s}(T)$): only distinct primes matter (Lemma 3.8), and $C_{r,s}(T)=O(T)$ unless $r=s>0$ (Lemma 3.9/3.10). Statements skimmed, not read in detail.
role: Show off-diagonal contributions are lower order inside the support region.

statement: $C_{r,s}(T)=O(T)$ unless $r=s>0$; for $r=s$, $C_{r,r}(T)=\frac{TL}{2\pi}\kappa(h)\sum_{\sigma\in S_r}\int_0^{1/m}\!\!\cdots\!\int_0^{1/m}v_1\cdots v_r\,\Phi(-v_1,..,-v_r,v_{\sigma(1)},..,v_{\sigma(r)},0,..,0)dv+O(T)$.
role: Identifies the diagonal main terms (permutation pairings).

statement: For $u=(u_1,\dots,u_r)$ in generic position there is a unique cyclic rotation whose random walk lies below its chord.
role: Drives the identity of Prop 4.3 matching the pairing structure to cycle structure of the determinant.
Moebius inversion over the partition lattice to distinct indices.

statement: $\hat W_n(u)=\sum_F\delta_F(u)\prod_j(-1)^{|F_j|-1}Y_{F_j}(u)$ with $Y_S(u)=\sum_{\text{cyclic perms}}\int f_2(v)f_2(v+u_{i_1})\cdots f_2(v+u_{i_1}+..+u_{i_m})dv$, $f_2=\mathbf 1_{[-1/2,1/2]}$.
role: Expands the Fourier transform of the sine-kernel determinant by cycles.

statement: Let $0\le\beta<1$ and $0<c<\sqrt{1-\beta}$. For all sufficiently large $T$ there is $t\in[T^\beta,T]$ with $|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|\ge\exp\Big(c\sqrt{\tfrac{\log T\,\log\log\log T}{\log\log T}}\Big)$. In particular $\max_{1\le t\le T}|\zeta(1/2+it)|\ge\exp\big((1+o(1))\sqrt{\log T\log_3T/\log_2T}\big)$ (constant improved from $1/\sqrt2$ in Bondarenko-Seip [2] to $1$).
Assume RH, fix $0\le\beta<1$. There is $c>0$ with $\max_{T^\beta\le t\le T}|S(t)|\ge c\sqrt{\log T\,\log_3T/\log_2T}$ for all large $T$, where $S(t)=\frac1\pi\arg\zeta(1/2+it)$.
Assume RH, fix $0\le\beta<1$. There is $c_1>0$ with $\max_{T^\beta\le t\le T}S_1(t)\ge c_1\sqrt{\log T\,\log_3T/(\log_2T)^3}$, where $S_1(t)=\int_0^tS(\tau)d\tau$.
location: Thm 2 (p.3); proof Sec. 5 (via formula (10), even kernel)

statement: For $1/2\le\sigma<1$ and $K$ analytic in the strip $\sigma-2\le y\le0$ with $\max|K(x+iy)|=O(|x|^{-2})$: $\int_{\mathbb R}\zeta(\sigma+i(t+u))K(u)\,du=\sum_{n\ge1}\hat K(\log n)n^{-\sigma-it}+2\pi K(-t-i(1-\sigma))$.

For $1/2\le\sigma<1$, K analytic in strip with $V(x)=\max|K|=O(1/(|x|\log^2|x|))$, $t\ne0$: $\int\log\zeta(\sigma+i(t+u))K(u)du=\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\Lambda(n)}{\log n}\hat K(\log n)n^{-\sigma-it}+2\pi\sum_{\beta>\sigma}\int_0^{\beta-\sigma}K(\gamma-t-i\alpha)d\alpha+O(V(t))$; under RH the zero sum vanishes, giving (8),(9),(10) for S and S_1.
role: Imported convolution formula for log zeta; makes the RH-dependence of Theorem 2 explicit (only through absence of zeros right of sigma).

statement: The resonator support set $\mathcal M$ (squarefree numbers with few prime divisors in each prime block $P_k$) satisfies $|\mathcal M|\le N$ for N large.
role: Size control of resonator (imported from [2, Lemma 2]).

statement: $\frac1{\sum_i f(i)^2}\sum_{n\in\mathcal M}f(n)^2\sum_{p|n}\frac1{f(p)\sqrt p}\ge(\gamma+o(1))\sqrt{\log N\log_3N/\log_2N}$.
role: Key combinatorial estimate: concentration of the multiplicative weight f^2 on integers with many prime factors in every block; yields the sqrt factor and the improved constant.

statement: $\int|R(t)|^2\Phi(t/T)dt\ll T\sum_{n\in\mathcal M}f(n)^2$ with $R(t)=\sum_{m\in\mathcal M'}r(m)m^{-it}$, $\Phi(t)=e^{-t^2/2}$.
role: Upper bound for resonator mass (diagonal vs off-diagonal via discretisation at scale 1+1/T).

statement: If $F(t)=\sum a_nn^{-1/2-it}$ converges absolutely with $a_n\ge0$, then $\int F|R|^2\Phi(t/T)dt\ge T\min_{n\le T^\epsilon}a_n\exp\big((\gamma+o(1))\kappa\sqrt{\log T\log_3T/\log_2T}\big)\sum_{\mathcal M}f(n)^2$ (as printed; the sqrt scaling with kappa=log N/log T should apply to the kappa factor).
role: Resonance lower bound for nonnegative Dirichlet series (used with F built from the kernel transform).

statement: For $G(t)=\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\Lambda(n)a_n}{\log n}n^{-1/2-it}$, $a_n\ge0$: $\int G|R|^2\Phi(t/T)dt\ge cT\sqrt{\log T\log_3T/\log_2T}\min_{p\in P}a_p\sum_{\mathcal M}f(n)^2$.
role: Prime-supported version used for S(t), S_1(t); the sqrt gain comes from Lemma 4.

statement: Let k\ge4 be an integer and \sigma_k:=1-\frac{k}{2^k-2}. Then |\zeta(\sigma_k+it)|\le 1.546\,t^{1/(2^k-2)}\log t for all t\ge3. (E.g. |\zeta(5/7+it)|\le1.546t^{1/14}\log t.)

\zeta(\sigma+it)\ne0 for \sigma>1-\dfrac{\log\log|t|}{21.233\,\log|t|}, |t|\ge3. Widest known region for \exp(170.3)\le|t|\le\exp(532\,141) (paper's own range statement; abstract says exp(171) to exp(5.3e5)).

Let a,N integers, N>0, f with k\ge4 continuous derivatives, f^{(k)} monotonic and 0<\lambda_k\le|f^{(k)}|\le h\lambda_k on (a,a+N]; K=2^{k-1}. Then S_f(a,N)\le A_k h^{2/K}N\lambda_k^{1/(2K-2)}+B_kN^{1-2/K}\lambda_k^{-1/(2K-2)}, with A_k,B_k given by explicit recursion (2.44)-(2.46).
For k\ge10, integers a,N>0, f with f^{(k)} monotonic, \lambda_k\le|f^{(k)}|\le h\lambda_k with 1<h\le3: S_f(a,N)\le 2.762\,h^{2/K}N\lambda_k^{1/(2K-2)}+1.02\,N^{1-2/K}\lambda_k^{-1/(2K-2)}.

Master inequality for a zero \beta+it, t\ge3\cdot10^{12}, 1-\beta\le\eta_k/2, with zero-free rectangle 1-\lambda<\Re s\le1, t-1\le\Im s\le Dt+1: explicit inequality with constants 0.17996, 0.20523, 1.546 (from Thm 1.1), c(R) from (4.58) (see paper).

Explicit second-derivative test: if f'' monotonic with \lambda_2\le|f''|\le h\lambda_2 on [a,a+N], then S_f(a,N)\le \frac4{\sqrt\pi}Nh\lambda_2^{1/2}+... (printed: \tfrac{4}{\sqrt\pi}N\sqrt{h\lambda_2}+N... )
role: Base case; derived from explicit Kuzmin-Landau (2.2)-(2.3) with interval subdivision and trivial bound.

statement: For integers a,N and q>0: (S_f(a,N))^2\le (N-1+q)\big(\tfrac Nq+\tfrac2q\sum_{r=1}^{q-1}(1-\tfrac rq)S_{g_r}(a,N-r)\big), g_r(x)=f(x+r)-f(x).
role: Weyl-van der Corput differencing with sharpened prefactor N-1+q (vs N+1+q in Cochrane-Graham / N+q in Patel-Trudgian).

statement: Explicit third-derivative test S_f(a,N)\le A_3(\eta_3,h)h^{1/2}N\lambda_3^{1/6}+B_3(\eta_3)N^{1/2}\lambda_3^{-1/6} for \lambda_3\le|f'''|\le h\lambda_3, f''' monotonic.
role: Starting constants A_3,B_3 for the recursion.

statement: For 1/2\le\sigma\le1, t\ge t_0>0, h>1/(2\pi): |\zeta(s)-\sum_{n\le ht}n^{-s}|\le \frac{1}{(ht_0)^{\sigma}}\big(\tfrac h{...}\big)... (Euler-Maclaurin remainder).
role: Imported; reduces zeta to a partial sum over n<=ht.

statement: For s=\sigma_k+it, r\ge2, R=2^{r-1}, 0<a<b\le ha: |\sum_{a<n\le b}n^{-s}|\le C_r(\eta_3,h)a^{k/(2K-2)-r/(2R-2)}t^{1/(2R-2)} (shape).
role: Applies the r-th derivative test on dyadic-type pieces; X_1=h_0t^{\theta_k}, X_2=\lfloor h_0h_2t\rfloor, \theta_r=R/(rR-2R+2).

statement: For k\ge4, s=\sigma_k+it, t\ge t_0, h_0,\eta_3>0, h_2\in(0,e), h_3>1: |\sum_{X_1<n\le X_2}n^{-s}|\le\beta_k(t_0)t^{1/(2K-2)}\log t, \beta_k=\sum_{r=2}^{k-1}F_k(r,t).
role: Assembles the three-range split ((0,X0] trivial; (X0,X1],(X1,X2] via Lemma 2.6) into Thm 1.1.

statement: For 0<a\le1/2, t_0\ge100, t\ge3t_0, 1/2\le\sigma\le1-t^{-1}, and |\zeta(\sigma+iy)|\le Xt^Y\log t for t_0\le|y|\le t: \frac12\int\frac{\log|\zeta(\sigma+it+iau)|}{\cosh^2u}du\le\log X+Y\log t+\log\log t.
role: Replacement of Ford Lemma 3.4 with log-power Z=1 suited to Theorem 1.1.

statement: For $\phi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R)$ with $\operatorname{supp}\hat\phi\subset(-1,1)$: $\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\sum_{1\le j\ne k\le N}\phi(\widehat{\gamma}_j-\widehat{\gamma}_k)=\int\phi(x)\bigl(1-(\sin\pi x/\pi x)^2\bigr)dx$, where $\widehat\gamma_j$ are zero ordinates scaled by mean density (under RH). Conjectured for all supports.

For curves of genus $g$ over $\mathbb F_q$ with moduli $\mathcal M_g(\mathbb F_q)$ and $k\ge1$: $\lim_{g\to\infty}\lim_{q\to\infty}\frac1{\#\mathcal M_g(\mathbb F_q)}\sum_{C}D(\mu_k(C/\mathbb F_q),\mu_k(GUE))=0$; hence almost all curves obey the Montgomery-Odlyzko law as $q,g\to\infty$ (order of limits: $q$ first).

For hyperelliptic family $\Delta\in H_n(\mathbb F_q)$ (monic squarefree degree n, $g=g(n)$) and $f\in C_0(\mathbb R_{\ge0})$: $\lim_{n\to\infty}\lim_{q\to\infty}\frac1{\#H_n}\sum_\Delta f(\theta_j(\Delta)2g/2\pi)=\int f\,d\nu_j(Sp)$ (monodromy full $Sp(2g)$).

Conjecture: (41) holds without inner $q\to\infty$ limit. For twists $E\otimes\chi_\Delta$ of the Legendre curve (monodromy $O(N)$), sign +1 sub-family gives $SO(even)$ and sign -1 gives $SO(odd)$ distribution of $j$-th zero as $n\to\infty$, $q\to\infty$ first.

For a family $\mathcal F$ of L-functions ordered by conductor, $W(X,\mathcal F,\phi)=\frac1{\#\mathcal F_X}\sum_{c_f\le X}\sum_j\phi(\gamma_f^{(j)}\log c_f/2\pi)\to\int\phi\,w(G(\mathcal F))$ for all Schwartz $\phi$ (no support restriction), with $G(\mathcal F)$ the symmetry type.

Under RH for $L(s,\chi)$, quadratic primitive $\chi$ of conductor $\le X$: $W\to\int\phi\,w(Sp)$ for $\operatorname{supp}\hat\phi\subset(-2,2)$. Symmetry type Sp; Rubinstein: n-level densities for small support.
conditional_on: RH (GRH) for the L-functions in family

statement: II: $f\otimes\chi$ quadratic twists of GL2 form: $SO(even)/SO(odd)$ for $\operatorname{supp}\hat\phi\subset(-1,1)$ [K-S2]. III: weight-2 Hecke eigenforms for $\Gamma_0(N)$, N prime: $SO(even)/SO(odd)$ for $\operatorname{supp}\hat\phi\subset(-2,2)$ [Iwaniec-Luo-Sarnak]. IV: $L(s,\mathrm{sym}^2f)$ weight k: Sp for $\operatorname{supp}\hat\phi\subset(-4/3,4/3)$ [I-L-S]. All assume RH for family members.

Density Conjecture implies $\#\{f\in\mathcal F_X:\epsilon_f=1,L(1/2,f)\neq0\}/\#\{\epsilon_f=1\}\to1$ and the analogue for $L'(1/2,f)$ with $\epsilon_f=-1$; with Kolyvagin and BSD gives Goldfeld's conjecture on ranks of quadratic twists (rank 0 for 100% of $\epsilon=+1$, rank 1 for 100% $\epsilon=-1$). Approximation II(b) gives, assuming RH, rank$(E_D)=0$ for at least 25% of D with $\epsilon=1$ (Brumer-Heath-Brown).

Zeros of each $L(s,f)$ should be eigenvalues of operator $U(f)$ on a space $H$, equidistributed in a symmetry class as $f$ varies; since $\zeta$ lies in Family I (symplectic), the putative operator should preserve a symplectic form (footnote 4).
Deligne's equidistribution: for continuous class function f on $USp(2g)$, $\lim_{q\to\infty}\sum_C f(\theta(C/\mathbb F_q))/\#\mathrm{Aut}/\sum 1/\#\mathrm{Aut}=\int f\,dA$.
role: Second ingredient of (37); needs Zariski-dense monodromy = full Sp(2g) (via $M_{g,3K}$)

label_in_source: Law of large numbers (22) of Section 2
statement: Spacing measures of Haar-random elements of $G(N)$ concentrate as $N\to\infty$ (type II groups give GUE spacings).
role: Third ingredient of (37)

statement: Monodromy of hyperelliptic family is $Sp(2g)$; of the Legendre-curve quadratic-twist family is $O(N)$ ([K-S1],[KA2]); footnote 2 explains the Sp/O switch via cup-product duality.
role: Identifies symmetry type for each family

statement: Let $f:\mathbb N\to[-1,1]$ be multiplicative. There are absolute constants $C,C'>1$ (one may take $C'=20000$) such that for all $2\le h\le X$ and $\delta>0$: $\left|\frac1h\sum_{x\le n\le x+h}f(n)-\frac1X\sum_{X\le n\le 2X}f(n)\right|\le\delta+C'\frac{\log\log h}{\log h}$ for all but at most $CX\left(\frac{(\log h)^{1/3}}{\delta^2h^{\delta/25}}+\frac1{\delta^2(\log X)^{1/50}}\right)$ integers $x\in[X,2X]$.

Let $f:\mathbb N\to[-1,1]$ be multiplicative. For $10\le h\le x$, the bilinear average $\frac{1}{h\sqrt x\log 2}\sum_{x\le n_1n_2\le x+h,\ \sqrt x\le n_1\le2\sqrt x}f(n_1)f(n_2)$ equals $\frac1{\sqrt x}\big(\ldots\big)$ the product of long averages $\frac1{\sqrt x}\sum_{\sqrt x\le n\le2\sqrt x}f(n)$ squared, up to an error $O\big(\frac{\log\log h}{\log h}+\frac1{(\log x)^{1/100}}\big)$ (the precise normalization of the main term is as printed on p.2: the square of the mean of f over [sqrt x,2 sqrt x]). Uniform in h and f.
location: Section 1, p.2 (display garbled in extracted text; normalization of the main term should be checked against the PDF)

statement: For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $C(\varepsilon)>0$ such that $[X,X+C(\varepsilon)\sqrt X]$ contains at least $\sqrt X(\log X)^{-4}$ integers that are $X^{\varepsilon}$-smooth, for all large X. For small fixed eps one can take $C(\varepsilon)=\rho(1/\varepsilon)^{-13}$ (via Theorem 4); remark: $\rho^{-7}$ and exponent $\log 4$ with extra work.

For every integer $h\ge1$ there is $\delta(h)>0$ with $\left|\frac1X\sum_{n\le X}\lambda(n)\lambda(n+h)\right|\le1-\delta(h)$ for all large X; same for any completely multiplicative $f:\mathbb N\to[-1,1]$ with f(n)<0 for some n. For h=1 also valid for multiplicative f completely multiplicative at 2.
hypotheses: f completely multiplicative with a negative value

statement: A multiplicative $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R$ has a positive proportion of sign changes in $[1,x]$ iff $f(n)<0$ for some $n>0$ and $f(n)\ne0$ for a positive proportion of integers n.

If f real multiplicative, f(n)<0 for some n, and f(n)!=0 on a positive proportion of integers, then for any $\psi(x)\to\infty$ almost every interval $[x,x+\psi(x)]$ contains a sign change of f. Via Theorem 3, exceptional set in [X,2X] has measure $O_\varepsilon(Xh^{-1/6+\varepsilon}+(\log X)^{-1/50})$ for intervals of length h.
location: Section 1, p.4; refinement in Section 2, p.7

statement: If $f$ is completely multiplicative, f(n)<0 for some n, and f!=0 on a positive proportion of integers, there is C>0 with a sign change of f in $[x,x+C\sqrt x]$ for all large x. In particular every $[n,n+C\sqrt n]$ contains integers with even and with odd Omega.
For $\psi(x)\to\infty$ and fixed $u>0$, for almost all x the number of $x^{1/u}$-smooth integers in $[x,x+\psi(x)]$ is $\sim\rho(u)\psi(x)$.

Variants of Theorems 1 and 2 restricted to a dense set $S_X$ of integers with a prime factor in each of a chain of intervals $[P_j,Q_j]$, $j\le J$ (parameter $\eta\in(0,1/6)$, $[P_1,Q_1]\subset[1,h]$). Theorem 3: $\frac1X\int_X^{2X}\left|\frac1h\sum_{x\le n\le x+h,n\in S}f(n)-\frac1X\sum_{X\le n\le2X,n\in S}f(n)\right|^2dx\ll\frac{(\log h)^{1/3}}{P_1^{1/6-\eta}}+\frac1{(\log X)^{1/50}}$.

For f real multiplicative with |f|<=1 and S as in Section 2, $\int_{-T}^{T}|F(1+it)|^2dt\ll(T+1)\left(\frac{(\log Q_1)^{1/3}}{P_1^{1/6-\eta}}+\frac1{(\log X)^{1/50}}\right)$ in the form printed (check against PDF), where $F(s)=\sum_{X\le n\le2X,n\in S}f(n)n^{-s}$; this mean-square bound on $\int_{(\log X)^{1/15}}^{X/h}$ gives (5) and hence Theorems 3-4.
role: Core analytic input: mean square of the restricted Dirichlet polynomial on the line Re s=1

statement: Halász-type pointwise bound: for f real multiplicative, $|F(\sigma+it)|\ll x^{1-\sigma}\big(M e^{-M}+\frac1{T_0}+\frac{\log\log x}{\log x}\big)$ with $M=\min_{|t_0|\le T_0}D(f,p^{it+it_0};x)^2$.
role: Gives saving on Dirichlet polynomials for |t|>(log X)^{1/15}, because f real cannot pretend to be n^{it}

statement: For $|f|\le1$ real multiplicative, fixed A, $1\le|\alpha|\le x^A$: $D(f,p^{i\alpha};x)\ge(\frac1{2\sqrt3}-\varepsilon)\sqrt{\log\log x}+O(1)$.
role: Lower bound on pretentious distance (after Granville-Soundararajan)

statement: Halász inequality for integers: for well-spaced T, $\sum_{t\in T}|A(it)|^2\ll(N+|T|\sqrt T)\log2T\sum_{n\le N}|a_n|^2$.
role: Imported large-values estimate (Iwaniec-Kowalski Thm 9.6)

statement: Halász inequality for primes: for $P(s)=\sum_{P\le p\le2P}a_pp^{-s}$ and well-spaced $\mathcal T\subset[-T,T]$, $\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}|P(it)|^2\ll\big(P+|\mathcal T|P\exp(-\frac{\log P}{(\log T)^{2/3+\varepsilon}})\big)\sum_{P\le p\le2P}\frac{|a_p|^2}{\log P}$.
role: New: recovers the log factor lost by the generic large-sieve for prime-supported polynomials when |T| is tiny; this is what saves the final power of log in the exceptional set U

statement: Mean-value estimate for the Buchstab/Ramaré-type decomposition: for bounded sequences with $a_{mp}=b_mc_p$ whenever $p\nmid m$, the integral over T of $|Q_{v,H}R_{v,H}|^2$ is bounded in terms of sums over short ranges of p; correct form uses the indicator 1_{(p,m)=1} (footnote 1: published version had a gap here, repaired in v4).
role: Handles the iterative decomposition over the sets T_j; footnote credits Sedunova and Wang for finding the gap in the published version

statement: Buchstab/Ramaré-type identity for completely multiplicative f: $\sum_{n\in S}\frac{f(n)}{n^{1+it}}=\sum_{P_j\le p\le Q_j}\frac{f(p)}{p^{1+it}}\sum_{m\in S_j}\frac{f(m)}{m^{1+it}}\frac1{\#\{P_j\le q\le Q_j:q|m\}+1_{(p,m)=1}}$ (restricted to X/p<=m<=2X/p).
role: Extracts a short prime polynomial that is small when t is in T_j

statement: Assume GRH for all relevant L-functions. Let \phi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R) be even with \mathrm{supp}\,\hat\phi\subset(-2,2). Then \lim_{K\to\infty}\frac1{M^+(K)}\sum_{k\equiv0(4),k\le K}\sum_{f\in H_k^+(\Gamma)}D(f,\phi)=\int\phi\,W(SO(even)), \lim\frac1{M^-(K)}\sum_{k\equiv2(4),k\le K}\sum_{f\in H_k^-(\Gamma)}D(f,\phi)=\int\phi\,W(SO(odd)); and for N\to\infty (N prime, fixed weight k) \frac1{M_k^\pm(N)}\sum_{f\in H_k^\pm(\Gamma_0(N))}D(f,\phi)\to\int\phi\,W(SO(even/odd)). Moreover for \mathrm{supp}\,\hat\phi\subset(-4/3,4/3): \lim_{K\to\infty}\frac1{M(K)}\sum_{k\equiv0(2),k\le K}\sum_{f\in H_k(\Gamma)}D(\mathrm{sym}^2(f),\phi)=\int\phi\,W(Sp). Here D(F,\phi)=\sum_{\gamma_F}\phi(\gamma_F\log c_F/2\pi), c_f=k^2 (F_K), c_f=N (F_N), c_{sym^2 f}=k^2; W(SO(even))=1+\frac{\sin2\pi x}{2\pi x}, W(SO(odd))=\delta_0+1-\frac{\sin2\pi x}{2\pi x}, W(O)=\tfrac12\delta_0+\tfrac12 (stated as \tfrac12\delta_0+dx? see audit notes), W(Sp)=1-\frac{\sin2\pi x}{2\pi x}.
hypotheses: GRH for L(s,f) (and Dirichlet L-functions where used)
support of hat phi in (-2,2) (GL2) or (-4/3,4/3) (sym^2)

statement: Theorem 1 holds unconditionally for \mathrm{supp}\,\hat\phi\subset(-1,1) (only the diagonal term of Petersson's formula contributes). The extension to (-2,2) (resp. (-4/3,4/3)) is where Kloosterman-sum terms enter; \hat W(Sp),\hat W(SO(even)),\hat W(SO(odd)) are discontinuous at \xi=\pm1, so the beyond-diagonal range distinguishes the symmetry types.

kind: theorem (conditional on GRH for GL2 and Dirichlet L-functions)
statement:
\liminf_{K	o\infty}\#\{f\in H_k:k\le K,k\equiv0(4),L(1/2,f)
e0\}/\#\{\ldots\}>9/16; for k\equiv2(4): \liminf\#\{L'(1/2,f)
e0\}/\#>15/16; same bounds 9/16 and 15/16 for H_k^\pm(\Gamma_0(N)) as N	o\infty; \limsup_{N	o\infty}M_k^*(N)^{-1}\sum_{f\in H_k^*(N)}\mathrm{ord}(1/2,f)<1; for sym^2: \liminf\#\{L(1/2,\mathrm{sym}^2f)
e0\}/\#>55/64.
hypotheses: GRH for GL_2 and Dirichlet L-functions

statement: With the weighted average A_K[X_f]=\sum_{k\equiv0(2)}h(k/K)\sum_{f\in H_k(\Gamma)}L(1,\mathrm{sym}^2f)^{-1}X_f (h\in C_0^\infty(0,\infty), h\ge0), for \phi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R) even with \mathrm{supp}\,\hat\phi\subset(-2,2): \lim_{K\to\infty}A_K[D_k(f,\phi)]/A_K[1]=\int\phi(x)W(O)(x)dx. (Parity not broken; D_k approximation (20).)

Hypothesis 4: for every \epsilon>0, X\ge2, c\ge1, (a,c)=1, \sum_{p\le X,p\equiv a(c)}e(2\sqrt p/c)\ll_\epsilon X^{1/2+\epsilon}. Theorem 5: assuming Hypothesis 4, Theorem 3 holds for \mathrm{supp}\,\hat\phi\subset(-7/3,7/3) (Prop. 4 of Sect. 2). Only a bound of the form X^\delta c^A with \delta<3/4 is needed for the extension; \delta=7/8 is essentially Vinogradov, \delta=3/4 follows from the density hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions.

kind: conditional theorem (quasi-GRH for GL2 in weight aspect)
statement:
Assume Hypothesis 4 and that the zeros of L(s,f), f\in H_k^*(\Gamma), lie either on \mathrm{Re}\,s=1/2 or on the real axis. Then for k sufficiently large (effectively), every such f satisfies L( eta,f)
e0 for  eta>13/14. (Proof: test function \phi=(\sin(2\pi
u x)/(2\pi
u x))^2, 
u<7/6, positive on the line and real axis zeros give k^{4
u\mu_f}\ll k^{2+\epsilon}, hence \mu_f\le(2
u)^{-1}	o3/7.) The remark states the assumption on zero locations can be removed by a different method [ILS] to get a quasi-RH for large weight.
hypotheses: zeros on critical line or real axis

statement: In the nonsingular case \inf_{g\in L^2[-1,1]}R(g)=1/A with A=\langle1,f_0\rangle>0 where (I+K)f_0=1 (Fredholm equation of the second kind), the infimum being attained at f_0 (unique if \lambda_1>-1). Corollary 2 determines when \phi=(\sin 2\pi x/2\pi x)^2 is optimal for the non-vanishing proportion; yields the constants 9/16, 15/16, 55/64 up to explicit tiny improvements.

role: Imported explicit formula converting D(f,phi) into prime sums, so that averaging reduces to Hecke-eigenvalue sums over primes.

statement: Petersson trace formula for \sum_f \omega_f\lambda_f(m)\lambda_f(n) with diagonal \delta_{mn} and Kloosterman-Bessel off-diagonal terms (statement paraphrased; exact form in Sect. 2.1 not transcribed).
role: Source of both the diagonal term (support in (-1,1)) and the Kloosterman terms (beyond).

statement: For a fixed real h\in C_0^\infty(0,\infty), the sums over weight k of J_{k-1}-Bessel-function series with Kloosterman-type arguments admit asymptotics for a=\pm1, x,L>0 (exact formulas (A),(B) in text, not transcribed).
role: Allows summing over k to obtain smooth cutoff of the Kloosterman terms, so that the k-sum kills off-diagonal contributions for support in (-2,2).

statement: Assume Hypothesis 4. For \phi with \mathrm{supp}\,\hat\phi\subset(-7/3,7/3), the asymptotic (29) for A_K[D_K(f,\phi)] (i.e. Theorem 3 in the extended range) holds.
role: Core analytic input to Theorem 5 and Corollary 6; handles prime sums of Bessel-type analytic functions by Hypothesis 4.

statement: Treatment of the symmetric square family F_{sym^2} (support (-4/3,4/3)): the non-diagonal terms from Kloosterman sums contribute a new main term in the range beyond (-1,1) that combines to give the Sp density.
role: Proof of the sym^2 part of Theorem 1, described by the authors as 'quite subtle'.

statement: Proof of Theorem 1 for F_N (level aspect, N prime), using Petersson over Hk(Gamma_0(N)) with Kloosterman sums S(m,n;cN) and separating parity via the sign of the functional equation, using the Atkin-Lehner pseudo-eigenvalue / trace of W_N.
role: Gives SO(even) and SO(odd) separately in level aspect.

statement: For all |t|\ge3 and 1/2\le\sigma\le1: |\zeta(\sigma+it)|\le A|t|^{B(1-\sigma)^{3/2}}\log^{2/3}|t|, and also |\zeta(\sigma+it,u)-u^{-s}|\le A|t|^{B(1-\sigma)^{3/2}}\log^{2/3}|t| for the Hurwitz zeta, 0<u\le1, with A=70.6995, B=4.43795.
\zeta(\sigma+it)\ne0 for |t|\ge3 and \sigma\ge1-\dfrac1{54.004(\log|t|)^{2/3}(\log\log|t|)^{1/3}}.
For sufficiently large |t|, \zeta(\sigma+it)\ne0 for \sigma\ge1-\dfrac1{48.0718(\log|t|)^{2/3}(\log\log|t|)^{1/3}}.
conditional_on: MTY argument with P_46 and B=4.43795

statement: For integer N\ge2, N\le t, \lambda=\log t/\log N: S(N,t):=\max_{0<u\le1}\max_{N<R\le2N}\Big|\sum_{N\le n\le R}(n+u)^{-it}\Big|\le 8.7979\,N^{1-1/(132.94357\,\lambda^2)}.

Explicit Vinogradov mean value bound: for k\ge90000 and 0.138128k^2\le s\le k^2\big(0.6494+\tfrac12\log\tfrac{8k}{25D}-\tfrac{1-D/k}{2-D/k}\tfrac Dk+\tfrac{2.051}{k}\big), 1\le D\le0.4k: J_{s,k}(P)\le k^{2.055k^3-0.414k^2+3nk+1.06nk+2(n^2-n)k+0.099912k^2}P^{2s-k(k+1)/2+\Delta_s} (P\ge1) with \Delta_s as in (1.10) (precise exponent as printed in paper).
For \chi mod q, q\le N\le qt... (2\le N\le qt): \max_{N<R\le2N}\big|\sum_{N<n\le R}\chi(n)n^{-it}\big|\le 9.7979\,\tfrac{\varphi(q)}{q}Ne^{-\log^3(N/q)/(132.94357\log^2t)}.
With c=48.0718 in (1.4): \pi(x)-\mathrm{li}(x)\ll x\exp\{-d(\log x)^{3/5}(\log\log x)^{-1/5}\} with d=0.212579 (via Pintz/Ford).
Vinogradov mean value J_{s,k}(P)<<P^{2s-y(s)} for s<<k^2 with y the inverse of x(y)=-y+2k-(k+1)\log(1-2(y-k)/(k^2-k)); explicit Lambert-W expression y(x) in Sec. 3.
role: Imported; basis of Thm 1.4 (case 1 of Tyrina) for s<<k^2.

statement: For 1\le D\le0.4k, k\ge90000 and 0.138128k\le n\le k(0.6494+\tfrac12\log\tfrac{8k}{25D}-\tfrac{1-D/k}{2-D/k}\tfrac Dk+\tfrac{2.051}k)+1: J_{nk,k}(P)\le C_nP^{2nk-k(k+1)/2+\Delta_n}, with C_n explicit (starts from Delta_{n_0}<=0.4k^2, n_0=ceil(0.1247k)).
role: Recursion for Delta_n starting at n_0 instead of 1 (modification of Ford Lemma 3.6); yields Thm 1.4.

statement: For integers k,r,s>=2 and h,g with 1<=h<=g<=k, N>0 and M_1,M_2 in [1,N]: S(N,t)<=2M_1M_2+... (bound in terms of J-type mean values, Weyl-differencing), see Sec. 8 Lemma 8.2 for the m-version.
role: Basic estimate of exponential sum S(N,t) via Vinogradov integral.

statement: For 84\le\lambda\le220, N\ge e^{288\lambda}: S(N,t)\le8.7979N^{1-1/(132.94357\lambda^2)}.
role: Critical range lambda>=84 (Ford had critical lambda=87); proven by combining Lemma 2.9 with (4.2),(4.4),(4.6)-(4.8) and Theorem 2.8-type parameter choices.

statement: For \lambda\ge220, N\ge e^{288\lambda}: the same bound S(N,t)<=8.7979N^{1-1/(132.94357 lambda^2)} holds.
role: Large-lambda range using Thm 1.4 (k>=90000) input.

statement: |\zeta(\sigma+it)|\le21.3t^{4(1-\sigma)^{3/2}}\le70.6995t^{4.43795(1-\sigma)^{3/2}}\log^{2/3}t (5.1), using (1-\sigma)\le4(1-\sigma)^{3/2} for \sigma\le15/16 (as in Ford Lemma 7.1); remark that with 4.4 one gets sigma<=459/484 but A unaffected.
role: Conversion from S(N,t) bound to A,B constants.

statement: For 1.001\le m\le2, \lambda\ge84: \tilde S(N,t):=\max_u\max_{N<R\le mN}|\sum_{N\le n\le R}(n+u)^{-it}|\le(m-1)\,8.7979N^{1-1/(132.94357\lambda^2)}.
role: Suggested route to reduce A to about 49 if an analogous bound could be proved for lambda<=84.

statement: For $s=1/2+it$ and shifts obeying (2.11): $\int_0^T \frac{\zeta(s+\alpha)\zeta(1-s+\beta)}{\zeta(s+\gamma)\zeta(1-s+\delta)}dt=\int_0^T\Big[\frac{\zeta(1+\alpha+\beta)\zeta(1+\gamma+\delta)}{\zeta(1+\alpha+\delta)\zeta(1+\beta+\gamma)}A_\zeta(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta)+\Big(\frac{t}{2\pi}\Big)^{-\alpha-\beta}\frac{\zeta(1-\alpha-\beta)\zeta(1+\gamma+\delta)}{\zeta(1-\beta+\delta)\zeta(1-\alpha+\gamma)}A_\zeta(-\beta,-\alpha,\gamma,\delta)\Big]dt+O(T^{1/2+\epsilon})$, with $-1/4<\Re\alpha<1/4$, $1/\log T\ll\Re\delta<1/4$, $\Im\alpha,\Im\delta\ll_\epsilon T^{1-\epsilon}$ (same constraints on all numerator/denominator shifts), error believed uniform so that it may be differentiated in the parameters (Remark 2.4).
hypotheses: conjecture itself unproved; uniformity of error in shift range assumed

statement: Analogous ratios conjectures for the symplectic family of $L(s,\chi_d)$ (real quadratic characters), and orthogonal families (twists of the Ramanujan tau L-function; Conj. 2.8 and 2.11 are the second-moment-type versions with $\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\ll 1/\log X$), averaged over $d<X$, with error $O(X^{1/2+\epsilon})$ under the same shift constraints (2.11) with $C=X$.
conditional_on: CFZ ratios conjectures for symplectic and orthogonal families
location: Sec 2.2-2.3, p.7-13 (conjecture statements located at text lines ~421, 526, 707, 789)

statement: Assuming Conjecture 2.6 and $f$ even satisfying (3.1), the one-level density of zeros $\gamma_d$ of $L(1/2+s,\chi_d)$ over $d\le X$ is $\sum_{d\le X}\sum_{\gamma_d}f(\gamma_d)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}f(t)\sum_{d\le X}\Big(\log\frac d\pi+\frac12\frac{\Gamma'}{\Gamma}(\tfrac14+\tfrac{it}2)+\frac12\frac{\Gamma'}{\Gamma}(\tfrac14-\tfrac{it}2)+2\frac{\zeta'}{\zeta}(1+2it)+A_D'(it;it)-(\tfrac d\pi)^{-it}\frac{\Gamma(1/4-it/2)}{\Gamma(1/4+it/2)}\zeta(1-2it)A_D(-it;it)\Big)dt+O(X^{1/2+\epsilon})$ (as printed, up to extraction of constants). Theorem 3.2 is the orthogonal (tau-twist) analogue from Conj. 2.9.

Assuming Conjecture 2.1 and $f$ as in (3.1): $\sum_{\gamma,\gamma'\le T}f(\gamma-\gamma')=\frac1{(2\pi)^2}\int_0^T\int_{-T}^{T}\Big[2\pi f(0)\log\frac t{2\pi}+f(r)\Big(\log^2\frac t{2\pi}+2\big(\tfrac{\zeta'}\zeta\big)'(1+ir)+\big(\tfrac t{2\pi}\big)^{-ir}\zeta(1-ir)\zeta(1+ir)A(ir)-B(ir)\Big)\Big]dr\,dt+O(T^{1/2+\epsilon})$ (principal value near $r=0$), giving all lower-order arithmetic terms of pair correlation (recovering Bogomolny-Keating).

Theorem 5.1 (unitary): with $P_1(0)=P_2(0)=0$, mollifier $M(s,P)$ of length $T^\theta$, assuming Conj. 2.1, $\frac1T\int_0^T Q_1(\tfrac{-1}{\log T}\tfrac d{d\alpha})Q_2(\tfrac{-1}{\log T}\tfrac d{d\beta})\zeta(s+\alpha)\zeta(1-s+\beta)M(s,P_1)M(1-s,P_2)dt|_{\alpha=\beta=0}=P_1(1)P_2(1)Q_1(0)Q_2(0)+\frac1\theta\,[\ldots]\int_0^1\!\!\int_0^1 P_1(w+r)P_2(z+r)Q_1(w\theta+u)Q_2(z\theta+u)\,dr\,du\big|_{w=z=0}+O(1/\log T)$ (Levinson/Conrey-type mollified second moment for any $\theta>0$). Thms 5.2 and 5.3 give the symplectic ($L(s,\chi_d)$, from Conj. 2.8) and orthogonal analogues for even polynomials.

Theorem 6.1: assuming the 4th-moment ratios conjecture (6.8) and polynomials $P,Q$ vanishing to order 4 at 0, for any $\theta>0$: $\frac1T\int_0^T|\zeta(1/2+it)|^4M_2(1/2+it,Q)M_2(1/2-it,P)dt=P(1)Q(1)+\frac1\theta\int_0^1\frac{(1-\eta)^3}{6}\big[2(Q^{(4)}P'+Q'P^{(4)})+8(Q^{(3)}P''+Q''P^{(3)})+\tfrac2\theta(Q^{(4)}P''+Q''P^{(4)})+\tfrac4\theta Q^{(3)}P^{(3)}+\tfrac{2}{\theta^2}(Q^{(4)}P^{(3)}+Q^{(3)}P^{(4)})+\tfrac1{\theta^3}Q^{(4)}P^{(4)}\big]d\eta+O(1/\log T)$ (coefficients as printed; extraction ambiguous). Theorem 6.4 treats the third-power mollification $I_3$ with two mollifier lengths $\theta_1,\theta_2$.
conditional_on: ratios conjecture (6.8) for 2 zetas over 2 zetas... generalized 4-over-4 setting

statement: Assuming the ratios conjecture (7.11): $\sum_{\gamma<T}|\zeta'(\rho)|^2=\int_0^T\frac1{24\pi}\log^4\frac t{2\pi}+\frac\gamma{3\pi}\log^3\frac t{2\pi}+\dots(1+O(t^{-1/2+\epsilon}))dt=\frac T{24\pi}\log^4T+O(T\log^3T)$, with full lower-order polynomial in $\log(t/2\pi)$ with coefficients in Euler's $\gamma$ and Stieltjes constants $\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\gamma_3$; leading term agrees with Gonek's theorem (7.1) (RH-conditional).

Assuming ratios conjecture (7.28): there are constants $C_0,\dots,C_6$ such that $\sum_{\gamma<T}|\zeta'(\rho)|^4=\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^T\Big[\frac{\log^9\frac t{2\pi}}{8640\zeta(2)}-\frac{(-2\gamma\zeta(2)+\zeta'(2))\log^8\frac t{2\pi}}{480\zeta^2(2)}+\dots+C_6\log^6\frac t{2\pi}\ldots\Big]dt$ (full lower-order structure given; the paper gives explicit $\log^9,\log^8,\log^7$ coefficients). Theorem 7.7 (Fujii) is an imported RH-conditional lower-order result for comparison.

Differentiation in the shifts of Conj. 2.1 (resp. 2.6, 2.9) yields formulas for $\int \frac{\zeta'}{\zeta}(s+\alpha)\frac{\zeta'}{\zeta}(1-s+\beta)dt$ and one-level auxiliary sums; (2.12) equals $\int_0^T(\zeta'/\zeta)'(1+\alpha+\beta)+(t/2\pi)^{-\alpha-\beta}\zeta(1+\alpha+\beta)\zeta(1-\alpha-\beta)A(\alpha,\beta)-B(\alpha,\beta)\,dt+O(T^{1/2+\epsilon})$.
role: Bridge from the conjecture to pair correlation and one-level density; relies on Remark 2.4 (differentiability of the conjectured error).
