statement: The condition $\Re\delta\gg 1/\log C$ can be relaxed if each denominator shift tending to 0 is matched by a numerator shift tending to 0 at same rate; bound $1/4$ on real parts prevents divergence of Euler products; uniformity allows differentiation.
role: Domain/validity hypotheses of the conjecture used in every application.

statement: Approximate functional equation $\zeta(s)=\sum_{n\le X}n^{-s}+\chi(s)\sum_{n\le Y}n^{s-1}$, $XY=t/2\pi$; use Dirichlet series for numerators, Moebius series for denominators, keep only terms with equal numbers of $\chi(s)$ and $\chi(1-s)$ factors, retain diagonal terms, extend sums, factor out zeta's as arithmetic factor $A_\zeta$.
role: Heuristic derivation of the ratios conjecture.

statement: If $N\ge\max\{Q-K,R-L\}$ and $\Re\gamma_q,\Re\delta_r>0$: $\int_{U(N)}\frac{\prod_{k=1}^K\Lambda_A(e^{-\alpha_k})\prod_{\ell=K+1}^{K+L}\Lambda_{A^*}(e^{\alpha_\ell})}{\prod_{q=1}^Q\Lambda_A(e^{-\gamma_q})\prod_{r=1}^R\Lambda_{A^*}(e^{-\delta_r})}dA=\sum_{\sigma\in\Xi_{K,L}}e^{N\sum_{k=1}^K(\alpha_{\sigma(k)}-\alpha_k)}y_U(\alpha_{\sigma(1)},\dots,\alpha_{\sigma(K)};-\alpha_{\sigma(K+1)},\dots,-\alpha_{\sigma(K+L)};\gamma;\delta)$, with $y_U(\alpha;\beta;\gamma;\delta)=\frac{\prod_{k,\ell}z(\alpha_k+\beta_\ell)\prod_{q,r}z(\gamma_q+\delta_r)}{\prod_{k,r}z(\alpha_k+\delta_r)\prod_{\ell,q}z(\beta_\ell+\gamma_q)}$, $z(x)=1/(1-e^{-x})$, $\Xi_{K,L}$ the set of $\binom{K+L}K$ permutations preserving the order within the first K and the last L.

Symplectic $USp(2N)$ (needs $2N\ge Q-K-1$), odd orthogonal $SO(2N+1)$ ($2N\ge Q-K+1$) and even orthogonal $SO(2N)$ ($2N\ge Q-K$) analogues of Theorem 4.1, each a sum over $\epsilon\in\{\pm1\}^K$ with sign factors $\mathrm{sgn}(\epsilon)$ and reflected shifts $\epsilon_k\alpha_k$ (with $\Re\gamma_q>0$).

If $\Re\gamma_q,\Re\delta_r>0$ and $\Re\alpha_j>-\frac1{2(K+L)}$: $\int_0^T\frac{\prod_{k=1}^K\zeta(s+\alpha_k)\prod_{\ell=K+1}^{K+L}\zeta(1-s-\alpha_\ell)}{\prod_q\zeta(s+\gamma_q)\prod_r\zeta(1-s+\delta_r)}dt=\int_0^T\sum_{\sigma\in\Xi_{K,L}}\prod_{k=1}^K\frac{\chi(s+\alpha_k)}{\chi(s-\alpha_{\sigma(k)})}Y_UA_\zeta(\alpha_{\sigma(1)},\dots;-\alpha_{\sigma(K+1)},\dots;\gamma;\delta)\,dt+O(T^{1/2+\epsilon})$, with $Y_U=\frac{\prod\zeta(1+\alpha_k+\beta_\ell)\prod\zeta(1+\gamma_q+\delta_r)}{\prod\zeta(1+\alpha_k+\delta_r)\prod\zeta(1+\beta_\ell+\gamma_q)}$ and $A_\zeta$ the Euler product (5.14) absolutely convergent near 0 (with Corollary 6.2: closed form of $A_\zeta$ as $\prod_p\int_0^1\ldots d\theta$ via Lemma 6.1).

Ratios conjectures for the symplectic family $L(1/2+\alpha,\chi_d)$, and the orthogonal families (even/odd, e.g. twists by weight-k Hecke forms), with sums over $\epsilon\in\{\pm1\}^K$ of $\prod_k (\text{conductor ratio})^{-\ldots}$, $Y$-factor and arithmetic factor $A$, error $O(X^{1/2+\epsilon})$, for $\Re\alpha_k,\Re\gamma_q>0$.

For $e(\theta)=e^{2\pi i\theta}$: $\sum_{\sum a_k+\sum c_q=\sum b_\ell+\sum d_r}\prod\ldots p^{-\ldots}\mu(p^{c_q})\mu(p^{d_r})=\int_0^1\frac{\prod_q(1-e(\theta)p^{-1/2-\gamma_q})\prod_r(1-e(-\theta)p^{-1/2-\delta_r})}{\prod_k(1-e(\theta)p^{-1/2-\alpha_k})^{-1}\ldots}d\theta$ (as printed, schematic), yielding the local factor of $A_\zeta$ as an integral over the circle.

Lemma 6.7: if $F(z;w)$ is regular near $0$, symmetric in the first $K$ and in the last $L$ variables, $f$ has a simple pole of residue 1 at 0 and is otherwise analytic in $|s|\le1$, and $H=F\prod_{k,\ell}f(z_k-w_\ell)$, then the permutation sum $\sum_{\sigma\in\Xi_{K,L}}H(\alpha_{\sigma(1)},\dots)$ equals a multiple contour integral (rewriting the combinatorial sum as a K+L fold contour integral, Section 6.4). Lemma 6.8 is the all-$K$ symmetric version.

Assuming the ratios conjecture: $\frac1T\int_0^T\Big(\frac{\zeta'}{\zeta}(1/2+r+it)\Big)^2dt=\Big(\frac{\zeta'}{\zeta}\Big)'(1+2r)+\Big(\frac T{2\pi}\Big)^{-2r}A_\zeta(-r,-r,r,r)\frac{\zeta(1-2r)\zeta(1+2r)}{1-2r}+c(r)+O(T^{-1/2+\epsilon})$ (scaled form as printed with $\frac Tte$ factor), $c(r)$ uniformly bounded for $|r|<1/4-\epsilon$ and given by an explicit prime sum (7.13).

For $a,c$ with nonnegative real part and $|a|,|c|\gg(\log T)^{-1}$: $\frac1T\sum_{\gamma<T}\frac{\zeta(\rho+a)}{\zeta(\rho+c)}=\frac1T\int_0^T\Big[\frac1{2\pi}\log\frac t{2\pi}+\frac{\zeta'}\zeta(1+a)-\frac{\zeta'}\zeta(1+c)-\sum_p\frac{\log p}{p^{2+a+c}}\ldots-\Big(\frac t{2\pi}\Big)^{-a}\frac{\zeta(1-a)\zeta(1+c)}{\zeta(1+c-a)}\prod_p\ldots\Big]dt$ (printed with an explicit Euler product; extraction partial).

Approximate functional equation for each numerator zeta; multiply out the $2^{K+L}$ terms; retain terms with equal numbers of $\chi(s)$ and $\chi(1-s)$; Mobius expansion for denominators ($\Re$ shifts positive); keep diagonal; express resulting arithmetic sum as Euler product $G_\zeta=Y_UA_\zeta$.
role: Derivation of Conjecture 5.1.

statement: $\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac1T\int_0^T(m/n)^{it}dt=1$ if $m=n$, $0$ otherwise (analogues for $\chi_d$ and Hecke twists in Sec 3).
role: Selecting diagonal terms in the recipe.

statement: Exact finite-$N$ ratios theorems for $U(N)$, $USp(2N)$, $SO(2N)$, $SO(2N+1)$ (proved in companion papers CFZ [7] via supersymmetry and Conrey-Forrester-Snaith/ Bump-Gamburd [20]).
role: Template and consistency check for the L-function conjectures with $N\leftrightarrow \log(T/2\pi)$ or $\log(|d|/\pi)$ conductor substitution.

statement: With normalized spacings $\delta_n=(\gamma_{n+1}-\gamma_n)\frac{\log(\gamma_n/2\pi)}{2\pi}$, the empirical pair correlation, density of $\delta_n$ and of $\delta_n+\delta_{n+1}$ for $N=0$ and $N=10^{12}$ (blocks $N<n\le N+10^5$) agree well with GUE predictions $1-(\sin\pi x/\pi x)^2$, $p(0,u)$, $p(1,u)$, and the agreement is markedly better at $N=10^{12}$ than at $N=0$. E.g. second moment of $\delta_n-1$: 0.161 (N=0), 0.176 (N=10^12), GUE 0.180.
hypotheses: zeros computed lie on the critical line (verified for the 10^12 block); accuracy $\pm 10^{-8}$ under stated floating-point model assumptions

statement: Kolmogorov distances $D$ of $\delta_n$ from GUE for blocks of $10^5$ zeros: $D=0.0207$ (N=0, prob ~$10^{-37}$), 0.0081 (N=10^8), 0.0052 (10^11), 0.0058 (2e11), 0.0045 (10^12, prob 3.5e-2); for $\delta_n+\delta_{n+1}$ at $N=10^{12}$: $D=0.0091$, prob $1.3\cdot10^{-6}$. Convergence to GUE is slow, consistent with $S(t)$ being tiny (typical size $\sqrt{\log\log T}$).

For the high blocks (N=10^11, 2e11, 10^12) the counts of $\delta_n<0.05$ (16, 20, 18) and $\delta_n<0.1$ (107,123,124) exceed GUE expectations (13.68, 108.80) whereas low blocks show deficiency; minimal spacings found by Brent ($\delta=0.001235$ at n=41,820,581) and van de Lune et al. ($0.000310$ at n=1,048,449,114) have low GUE probability (Table 5, e.g. 0.048). Author flags that persistence at greater height would question GUE and even pair correlation. (Later work, not in this paper, attributes this to slow convergence with $1/\log^2$ corrections.)

Autocovariances $c_k=M^{-1}\sum(\delta_n-1)(\delta_{n+k}-1)$ match Dyson's conjectured GUE value $c_k\approx -1/(2\pi^2k^2)$ for small fixed $k$, but for large $k$ (e.g. $k\approx 950$-$1000$) show statistically significant structured sign patterns, far above the independent-noise level $\approx 5\cdot10^{-4}$.

Spectrum $f(x)=c|\sum_n(\delta_n-1)e^{2\pi i nx}|^2$ has sharp peaks near $x=2(\log N)/\log q$... for prime powers $q=p^m$; explained via Landau's formula (under RH, as $N\to\infty$) $\sum_{0<\gamma\le T}e^{i\gamma y}$ is large exactly for $y=\log p^m$ (value about $-\frac{T}{2\pi}\Lambda(p^m)p^{-m/2}$-type), and the zero-spacing perturbation expansion (2.30). This shows the long-range correlations are an arithmetic (prime) effect not captured by GUE.
hypotheses: RH assumed for convenience (Landau proved an unconditional version)

kind: rigorous error analysis (computer-assisted, under machine-model assumptions)
statement: Zeros $\gamma_n$, $10^{12}<n\le10^{12}+101000$ were computed to within $\pm 10^{-8}$ via Riemann-Siegel with $m=206393$ terms, using Brown's floating-point model (b=2,t=47 sp, t=94 dp on Cray), with termwise error bound (3.9) $\le 2.14\cdot10^{-12}n^{-1/2}$ and total cosine-sum error bound (about $1.95\cdot10^{-9}$) plus RS remainder control; all those zeros verified to satisfy RH.
hypotheses: Cray sp/dp arithmetic obeys Brown model; sp cosine accuracy $5\cdot10^{-14}$ is assumed from sampling, not proved

statement: GUE predicts $\max_{\gamma_n\le T}(\gamma_{n+1}-\gamma_n)\sim 8^{-1/2}\pi\cdot$ (via $\log p(0,t)\sim -\pi^2t^2/8$) of order $(\log T)^{-1}\cdot(\log T)^{1/2}$-scale i.e. $\gg (\log T)^{-1/2}(\log\log T)^{-1/2}$ in normalized units, contradicting Montgomery's S(t)-based conjecture (2.27); data cannot decide.
hypotheses: GUE hypothesis versus Montgomery's conjecture on S(t)

statement: Under RH, $F(\alpha,T)=(1+o(1))T^{-2\alpha}\log T+\alpha+o(1)$ uniformly for $0\le\alpha\le1$ where $F(\alpha,T)=2\pi(T\log T)^{-1}\sum_{0<\gamma,\gamma'\le T}T^{i\alpha(\gamma-\gamma')}/(1+(\gamma-\gamma')^2)$.
role: Imported theorem motivating pair-correlation conjecture (1.3)-(1.4)

statement: $\int_0^T S(t)^{2k}dt\sim\frac{(2k)!}{k!(2\pi)^{2k}}T(\log\log T)^k$.
role: Imported; explains why spacing statistics converge slowly (S(t) tiny).

statement: GUE k-th neighbor spacing density $p(k,t)$ is given by a determinant/prolate-eigenvalue expansion over eigenvalues $\lambda_j$ of the finite Fourier operator (6.2).
role: Imported formulas used to compute GUE predictions (more accurate than the derivative formula (6.6)).

statement: $p(0,t)=\frac{\pi^2}{3}t^2-\frac{2\pi^4}{45}t^4+\dots$ near $0$ (normalized), and $\log p(0,t)\sim-\pi^2t^2/8$ as $t\to\infty$.
role: Imported; yields GUE probability for minimal spacing among M zeros (2.24) used in Table 5.

statement: Under RH, for fixed $y>0$, $\sum_{0<\gamma\le T}e^{i\gamma y}$ is $-\frac{T}{2\pi}e^{-y/2}\Lambda$-weighted at $y=\log p^m$ (i.e. $\approx -\frac{T}{2\pi}e^{-y/2}\log p$) and $O(e^{-y/2}\log T)$ otherwise.
role: Imported; basis for prime explanation of spectral peaks.

statement: For every $d\ge1$, the Jensen polynomial $J_\gamma^{d,n}(X)=\sum_{j=0}^d\binom dj\gamma(n+j)X^j$ is hyperbolic for all sufficiently large $n$ (n >= n_0(d)), where $-1+4z^2\Lambda(\tfrac12+z)=\sum_{n\ge0}\frac{\gamma(n)}{n!}z^{2n}$ and $\Lambda(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$.
If $1\le d\le8$ then $J_\gamma^{d,n}(X)$ is hyperbolic for every $n\ge0$ (effective proof of Theorem 1 for small d).
conditional_on: computations for small n (Section 5.2, not inspected)

statement: Let $\alpha(n),A(n),\delta(n)>0$ with $\delta(n)\to0$ and, for some integer $d\ge1$ and all $0\le j\le d$, $\log\frac{\alpha(n+j)}{\alpha(n)}=A(n)j-\delta(n)^2j^2+o(\delta(n)^d)$ as $n\to\infty$. Then $\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\delta(n)^{-d}}{\alpha(n)}J_\alpha^{d,n}\Big(\frac{\delta(n)X-1}{\exp(A(n))}\Big)=H_d(X)$ uniformly on compact subsets of $\mathbb R$, where $H_d$ are Hermite polynomials with $\sum H_d(X)t^d/d!=e^{-t^2+Xt}$ (orthogonal for $e^{-X^2/4}$). Corollary: $J_\alpha^{d,n}$ is hyperbolic for all but finitely many $n$ (Hermite roots are simple, real-rootedness is stable).

General form: if $\frac{\alpha(n+j)}{\alpha(n)}E(n)^{-j}=\sum_{i=0}^dC_i(n)\delta(n)^ij^i+o(\delta(n)^d)$ with $C_i(n)\to c_i$, then the same limit holds with $\exp(A(n))\to E(n)$ and $H_d\to H_{F,d}$, where $F(t)=\sum c_it^i$, $\sum H_{F,m}(X)t^m/m!=F(-t)e^{Xt}$, i.e. $H_{F,m}(X)=m!\sum_{k=0}^m(-1)^{m-k}c_{m-k}X^k/k!$.
hypotheses: expansion in powers of delta j

statement: For every $d\ge1$ there is $N(d)$ with $J_p^{d,n}(X)$ hyperbolic for all $n\ge N(d)$, $p(n)$ the partition function. (Conjectured minimal N(d) tabulated d<=32: 1,25,94,206,381,610,908,1269,...,35627; Larson-Wagner effective bound $N(d)\le(3d)^{24d}(50d)^{3d^2}$.)

For any weakly holomorphic modular form f on SL_2(Z) (possibly fractional weight/multiplier, real Fourier coefficients, pole of positive order m at infinity), for fixed $d\ge1$ the Jensen polynomials $J_{a_f}^{d,n}(X)$ are hyperbolic for all sufficiently large n.
hypotheses: weakly holomorphic, real coefficients, full modular group

statement: With $F(n)=\int_1^\infty(\log t)^nt^{-3/4}\theta_0(t)dt$, $\theta_0(t)=\sum_{k\ge1}e^{-\pi k^2t}$, one has $\Lambda^{(n)}(\tfrac12)=-\frac{F(n)}{2^{n+2}}\,n!\,/\ldots$ as in (11) (zero for odd n), $\gamma(n)=\frac{n!}{(2n)!}\big(8^n\cdot 2^{?}\ldots\big)=\frac{n!}{(2n)!}\cdot\frac{32\,2^{2n}F(2n-2)-F(2n)}{2^{2n-1}}$-type identity (13), and $F(n)\sim\sqrt{2\pi}\,\frac{L^{n+1}}{\sqrt{(1+L)n-\tfrac34L^2}}\,e^{L/4-n/L+3/4}\big(1+\frac{b_1}{n}+\frac{b_2}{n^2}+\cdots\big)$ as $n\to\infty$, where $L=L(n)\approx\log\frac n{\log n}$ is the unique positive root of $n=L(\pi e^L+\tfrac34)$ and $b_k\in\mathbb Q(L)$ ($b_1=\frac{2L^4+9L^3+...}{...}$ as printed). Consequently $\hat\gamma(n)=\frac{n!}{(2n)!}6^{-2n}2^{2n}\hat F(2n-2)=\gamma(n)(1+O(n^{-2+\varepsilon}))$.
location: Section 4, Theorem 7, eq. (11)-(14) (formulas as extracted; exact displayed constants should be checked against the PDF)

statement: The bracket $\sum_{i}C_i(n)\delta^{k-d+i}\sum_{j=k}^d(-1)^{j-k}\binom{d-k}{j-k}j^i\to(-1)^{d-k}(d-k)!c_{d-k}$ because the inner sum is the $(d-k)$-th finite difference of $j^i$ (zero for $i<d-k$, equal to $(d-k)!$ for $i=d-k$).
role: Core of the Hermite limit theorem

statement: For weakly holomorphic f, $a_f(n)=A_fn^{(k-1)/2}I_{k-1}(4\pi\sqrt{mn})+O(n^Ce^{2\pi\sqrt{mn}})$ (Rademacher/Poincare series); log of ratio $a_f(n+j)/a_f(n)$ has asymptotic expansion with $A(n)=2\pi\sqrt{m/n}+O(1/n)$, $\delta(n)=(\pi/2)^{1/2}m^{1/4}n^{-3/4}+O(n^{-5/4})$.
role: Verifies hypotheses of Theorem 3 for modular coefficients

statement: Saddle point at $t=a=e^L$ solving $n=\pi a+\tfrac34\log a$ for $f(t)=(\log t)^nt^{-3/4}e^{-\pi t}$; expansion $f((1+\lambda)a)/f(a)=e^{-C\lambda^2/2}(1+A_3\lambda^3+A_4\lambda^4+\cdots)$, $C=(\varepsilon+\varepsilon^2)n-\tfrac34$, $\varepsilon=1/\log a$; ratio $f/\theta_0=1+O(n^{-K})$ near a.
role: Gives all-orders asymptotics for the central derivatives of Lambda

statement: With $\hat n=2n-2$, $L=L(\hat n)$, $K=(L^{-1}+L^{-2})\hat n-3/4$, Stirling plus Thm 7 yields (16); expanding $\log R(j;n)=\sum g_m(n)j^m$ one gets $g_m(n)=O((n-1)^{1-m})$ and the choices $\delta(n)=\sqrt{1/\hat n-2/(L^2K)}$-type and $A(n)=\log\frac{nL^2}{4\hat n^2}+\ldots$ (18) satisfy (15) with $g_i(n)=o(\delta^i)$ for $i\ge3$.
role: Verification of the hypothesis of Theorem 3 for gamma(n), every d

statement: Assume RH. For all $x\ge 11$: $|\psi(x)-x|\le \sqrt{x}\,\log x\left(\frac{\log x}{8\pi}-\left(\frac1{2\pi}+\frac{1.465}{\log x}\right)\log\log x+1.2325\right)$.
Assume RH. For all $x\ge 101$: $|\psi(x)-x|\le \frac{\sqrt{x}\,\log x\,(\log x-\log\log x)}{8\pi}$.
Assume RH. For all $x\ge 2657$: $|\vartheta(x)-x|\le \frac{\sqrt{x}\,\log x\,(\log x-\log\log x)}{8\pi}$.

Assume RH. With B, C, E the Mertens constants: $\left|\sum_{p\le x}\frac{\log p}{p}-\log x-E\right|\le \frac{3(\log x)^2}{8\pi\sqrt x}$ for $x\ge 43.1$; $\left|\sum_{p\le x}\frac1p-\log\log x-B\right|\le\frac{3\log x}{8\pi\sqrt x}$ for $x\ge 24.4$; $\left|e^{C}\log x\prod_{p\le x}(1-1/p)-1\right|\le\frac{3\log x}{8\pi\sqrt x}$ for $x\ge 23.8$; $\left|\frac{e^{-C}}{\log x}\prod_{p\le x}(1-1/p)^{-1}-1\right|\le\frac{3\log x}{8\pi\sqrt x}$ for $x\ge 24.2$.

If $\phi$ is continuous, positive, non-decreasing on $[2\pi e,\infty)$ with suitable decay, then $\sum_{\gamma>T}\phi(\gamma)/\gamma^{?}$ is bounded by an integral against $N(t)\le\frac{t}{2\pi}\log\frac t{2\pi}$ (exact form: partial summation using the Backlund-type bound (8)-(9)); used to bound tails of sums over zeros.
role: Converts the explicit N(T) bound into bounds for 1/|gamma| tail sums.
location: Sec. 2, p. 4 (statement partly garbled in text extraction)

statement: Assume RH, $h=x/y$, $y\ge H_1:=10^7$. Then the sum over zeros in the smoothed explicit formula for $\psi_1(x\pm h)-\psi_1(x)$ is bounded by $\frac12\left(1+\frac2y\right)^{3/2}\frac{\sqrt x\log y}{\pi}+\frac{2.6\sqrt x}{\pi y}\ldots+\sqrt x\cdot O(\ldots)\log^2(y/2\pi)$ (with explicit constants, ending in 2.84); statement partially garbled in extraction.
role: Main analytic input for Theorem 1.1 at x >= 10^19 (explicit Goldston method).

statement: Assume RH, $y=\sqrt{x}/\log x$, $x\ge 10^{19}$. Then the Lemma 3.1 bound is at most $\frac{\sqrt x\log x}{2\pi}\left(\frac{\log x}{4}-\log\log x\right)$-type expression (exact constants garbled).
role: Optimised choice of y; ties to the 8 pi constant.

statement: Assume RH, $H_1=10^7$. A Rosser-Schoenfeld smoothed explicit formula bound (m, delta parameters, delta=log x/(m pi sqrt x)) gives $|\psi(x)-x|/\sqrt x$ at most an expression in T_0(x), omega_1, H_1 (log(T_0/2pi)/(2pi) type terms).
role: Gives (2),(3) in the range e^{30369.582} > x > 10^19 when combined with a case table of coefficients 0.99865 log x ... 0.87158 log x.

statement: Let $\chi\in\hat{C_{k,1}}$ (character of the norm-one idele classes), $\delta>1$, $H_\chi$ the Sobolev-type Hilbert space $L^2_{\delta,\chi}(X)_0$ and $D_\chi$ the generator of the action $W_\chi$ of $N\simeq \mathbb R_+^*$ (or $q^{\mathbb Z}$). Then $D_\chi$ has discrete spectrum, $\mathrm{Sp}\,D_\chi\subset i\mathbb R$ is exactly the set of $\rho\in i\mathbb R$ with $L(\tilde\chi,\tfrac12+\rho)=0$, where $\tilde\chi$ is the unique extension of $\chi$ to $C_k$ trivial on $N$; multiplicity of $\rho$ is the largest integer $n<\frac{1+\delta}{2}$ with $n\le$ multiplicity of $\tfrac12+\rho$ as a zero of $L$.

For Schwartz $h\in S(C_k)$ the operator $W(h)=\int W(g)h(g)d^*g$ on $H$ is trace class and $\mathrm{Trace}\,W(h)=\sum_{L(\tilde\chi,\frac12+\rho)=0,\ \rho\in i\mathbb R/N^\perp}\hat h(\tilde\chi,\rho)$ with $\hat h(\tilde\chi,\rho)=\int_{C_k}h(u)\tilde\chi(u)|u|^\rho d^*u$, multiplicity as in Thm 1.

Let $K$ be a local field with basic character $\alpha$, $h\in S(K^*)$ compactly supported, $R_\Lambda=\hat P_\Lambda P_\Lambda$ (infrared cutoff $P_\Lambda$ = indicator of $|x|\le\Lambda$, ultraviolet cutoff $\hat P_\Lambda=FP_\Lambda F^{-1}$). Then $R_\Lambda U(h)$ is trace class and as $\Lambda\to\infty$: $\mathrm{Trace}(R_\Lambda U(h))=2h(1)\log'\Lambda+\int'\frac{h(u^{-1})}{|1-u|}d^*u+o(1)$, where $\int'$ is the principal value determined by the unique distribution on $K$ agreeing with $du/|1-u|$ off $u=1$ whose Fourier transform vanishes at 1.

S-local trace formula: for finite set $S$ of places, $X_S=\prod_{v\in S}k_v/O_S^*$, $h\in S(C_S)$ compactly supported, $\mathrm{Trace}(R_\Lambda U(h))=2h(1)\log'\Lambda+\sum_{v\in S}\int'_{k_v^*}\frac{h(u^{-1})}{|1-u|}d^*u+o(1)$ as $\Lambda\to\infty$.

label_in_source: Equation (16) / Corollary 2 of Sect. VIII (global trace formula, conjectural)
statement: With $Q_\Lambda$ the orthogonal projection of $L^2(X)$ onto span of $f\in S(A)$ with $f,\hat f$ vanishing for $|x|>\Lambda$ (trivial $\delta=0$): $\mathrm{Trace}(Q_\Lambda U(h))=2h(1)\log'\Lambda+\sum_v\int'_{k_v^*}\frac{h(u^{-1})}{|1-u|}d^*u+o(1)$ for all compactly supported $h\in S(C_k)$. Proved only for $h$ supported in $C_{k,1}$; open in general.

Let $k$ be a global field of POSITIVE characteristic and $Q_\Lambda$ as above. For compactly supported $h\in S(C_k)$ the following are equivalent: (a) the trace formula (16) holds as $\Lambda\to\infty$; (b) all L-functions with Grossencharakter on $k$ satisfy RH.

Weil explicit formula rewritten: for $h\in S(C_k)$ compactly supported, $\hat h(0)+\hat h(1)-\sum_{L(\mathcal X,\rho)=0,\,0<\mathrm{Re}\rho<1}\hat h(\mathcal X,\rho)=\sum_v\int'_{k_v^*}\frac{h(u^{-1})}{|1-u|}d^*u$ with principal value normalized by $\alpha_v$ as in Thm V.3.

$\lim_{\Lambda\to\infty}\Delta_\Lambda=\Delta_\infty$, $\Delta_\infty(f)=\sum_{L(\tilde\chi,\frac12+\rho)=0,\rho\in B/N^\perp}N(\tilde\chi,\tfrac12+\rho)\int_{z\in i\mathbb R}\hat f(\tilde\chi,z)d\mu_\rho(z)$ with $B=\{|\mathrm{Re}\rho|<1/2\}$ and $\mu_\rho$ the harmonic measure of $\rho$ w.r.t. $i\mathbb R$ (Dirac mass if $\rho\in i\mathbb R$).
role: Computes the limiting Weil distribution from zeros without hypothesis; key to b)=>a) (positive char.): off-line zeros enter via harmonic measure, so $\Delta_\infty$ is positive iff RH.

statement: $E(f)(g)=|g|^{1/2}\sum_{q\in k^*}f(qg)$ is a surjective isometry $L^2(X)_0\to L^2(C_k)$ intertwining $U(a)$ with $|a|^{1/2}V(a)$; $E(B_{\Lambda,0})\subset S_\Lambda$ so $Q'_{\Lambda,0}\le S_\Lambda$ and $\Delta_\Lambda(f)=\mathrm{Trace}((S_\Lambda-Q'_{\Lambda,0})V(f))$ is of positive type.
role: Source of positivity: difference of two projections with one dominating the other gives a positive-type distribution; limit is Weil distribution, hence a)=>b) via Weil's positivity criterion.

statement: B_Lambda subspaces stabilize quickly in S; natural map L^2(X_S)->L^2(X_{S'}) maps B_Lambda^S onto B_Lambda^{S'} (statement as paraphrased in Sect. VIII), giving S-independent global cutoff.
role: Allows S-independent global formulation of cutoff and of trace formula.

statement: Let $s=\sigma+it$, $\sigma\ge0$, $|t|\ge2$, $X\ge2$, $K\in\mathbb N$ fixed. Let $u\ge0$ be $C^\infty$ of mass 1 supported on $[e^{1-1/X},e]$, $U(z)=\int_0^\infty u(x)E_1(z\log x)dx$ with $E_1(z)=\int_z^\infty e^{-w}/w\,dw$. Then $\zeta(s)=P_X(s)Z_X(s)\big(1+O\big(\frac{X^{K+2}}{(|s|\log X)^K}\big)+O(X\log^{X}\cdot X^{-\sigma})\big)$ (printed as $O(X\log X)^{-\sigma}$ in the extracted text), where $P_X(s)=\exp\big(\sum_{n\le X}\Lambda(n)/(n^s\log n)\big)$ and $Z_X(s)=\exp\big(-\sum_{\rho_n}U((s-\rho_n)\log X)\big)$; implied constants depend on $u,K$ only. The second error can be removed by using $\tilde P_X$ with $v(e^{\log n/\log X})$, $v(t)=\int_t^\infty u$.

For fixed $\Re k>-1/2$: $\frac1T\int_T^{2T}|\zeta(1/2+it)|^{2k}dt\sim a(k)\frac{G^2(k+1)}{G(2k+1)}(\log T)^{k^2}$, $a(k)=\prod_p(1-1/p)^{k^2}\sum_{m\ge0}\big(\frac{\Gamma(m+k)}{m!\Gamma(k)}\big)^2p^{-m}$.

For $X,T\to\infty$ with $X=O((\log T)^{2-\epsilon})$ and $k>-1/2$: $\frac1T\int_T^{2T}|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|^{2k}dt\sim\frac1T\int_T^{2T}|P_X(\tfrac12+it)|^{2k}dt\times\frac1T\int_T^{2T}|Z_X(\tfrac12+it)|^{2k}dt$.
conditional_on: unproved; true for k=1,2 by Corollary

statement: Let $1/2\le c<1$, $\epsilon>0$, $k\in\mathbb R$, $X,T\to\infty$ with $X=O((\log T)^{1/(1-c+\epsilon)})$. Then uniformly for $c\le\sigma\le1$: $\frac1T\int_T^{2T}|P_X(\sigma+it)|^{2k}dt=a(k,\sigma)F_X(k,\sigma)(1+O_k(1/\log X))$, where $a(k,\sigma)=\prod_p(1-p^{-2\sigma})^{k^2}\sum_{m\ge0}d_k(p^m)^2p^{-2m\sigma}$ and $F_X=\zeta(2\sigma)^{k^2}e^{-k^2E_1((2\sigma-1)\log X)}$ for $\sigma>1/2$, $F_X=(e^\gamma\log X)^{k^2}$ for $\sigma=1/2$ (as printed; $c=1/2$ allowed).
hypotheses: range of X restricted as stated

statement: For $X,T\to\infty$, $X=O((\log T)^{2-\epsilon})$, $k>-1/2$: $\frac1T\int_T^{2T}|Z_X(\tfrac12+it)|^{2k}dt\sim\frac{G^2(k+1)}{G(2k+1)}\Big(\frac{\log T}{e^\gamma\log X}\Big)^{k^2}$. Derived by replacing zeros with eigenangles of Haar $U(N)$, $N=\lfloor\log T\rfloor$.

kind: theorem (conditional on nothing stated; uses Hughes/Ingham-type mean values)
statement: For $\epsilon>0$, $X,T\to\infty$, $X=O((\log T)^{2-\epsilon})$, and $k=1,2$: $\frac1T\int_T^{2T}|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)P_X(\tfrac12+it)^{-1}|^{2k}dt\sim\frac{G^2(k+1)}{G(2k+1)}\big(\frac{\log T}{e^\gamma\log X}\big)^{k^2}$. Corollary: Conjectures 2 and 3 hold for $k=1,2$.
hypotheses: uses mean-value theorems for zeta times Dirichlet polynomials (Hardy-Littlewood, Ingham, Conrey mollifier-type for k=2)

statement: For $\phi(\theta)$ as in (20) (the RMT analogue of $\exp(-\sum_n U(\cdot))$) and fixed $k>-1/2$, $X\ge2$: $\mathbb E_N\Big[\prod_{n=1}^N\phi(\theta_n)\Big]\sim\frac{G(k+1)^2}{G(2k+1)}\Big(\frac N{e^\gamma\log X}\Big)^{k^2}\big(1+O_k(1/\log X)\big)$ as $N\to\infty$.
With $P_X^*(s)=\prod_{p\le X}(1-p^{-s})^{-1}\prod_{\sqrt X<p\le X}(1+\tfrac1{2p^{s}})^{-1}$... smoothed explicit formula yielding $P_X$-type approximations (printed as $P^*_X$).
role: Imported smoothed explicit formula used to pass from zeros to primes.

statement: For real $k$, $1/2\le c<1$, $2\le X\ll(\log T)^{1/(1-c+\epsilon)}$: $\frac1T\int_T^{2T}|P_X^*(\sigma+it)|^{2k}dt=a(k,\sigma)\prod_{p\le X}(1-p^{-2\sigma})^{k^2}\ldots(1+O_k(X^{1/2-2\sigma}/\log X))$ uniformly in $c\le\sigma\le1$.
role: Mean-value of Euler-product part; feeds Theorem 2.

statement: Properties of $u$ and $U(z)=\int u(x)E_1(z\log x)dx$ (e.g., $U(z)\approx-\gamma-\log z+O(|z|)$ for small $z$ and decay for large $z$).
role: Controls how many zeros effectively contribute: $\exp(-U(i(t-\gamma_n)\log X))\approx i(t-\gamma_n)e^\gamma\log X$.

statement: Arithmetic lemmas on sums over coprime $a,b$ and $\kappa(n)=\prod_{p|n}(1+1/p)$ used in the proof of Theorem 3 for k=1,2.
role: Evaluation of mean values of $|\zeta P_X^{-1}|^{2k}$.

statement: $\max_{t\in[0,T]}|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|=\exp\Big((1+o(1))\sqrt{\tfrac12\log T\,\log\log T}\Big)$ as $T\to\infty$.
conditional_on: heuristic models: Haar characteristic polynomial model for Z_X, random-prime model for P_X, independence of P_X and Z_X

statement: $\limsup_{t\to\infty}\dfrac{S(t)}{\sqrt{\log t\,\log\log t}}=\dfrac{1}{\pi\sqrt2}$.
conditional_on: Keating-Snaith RMT model for Im log zeta, independence heuristics

statement: For a family $\mathcal F$ of L-functions with $\#\{F: c(F)<D\}\approx D$ and symmetry type unitary/symplectic/orthogonal, $\max_{F\in\mathcal F,\,c(F)\le D}|F(\tfrac12)|=\exp\big((1+o(1))\sqrt{B\log D\log\log D}\big)$, with $B=1/2$ (unitary), $B=1$ (symplectic, orthogonal); implied constant depends only on $\mathcal F$. Contains Conjecture A via the shift family $F_y(s)=L(s+iy)$. Examples (1.6), (1.7): real Dirichlet L(1/2,chi_d) and weight-k level-N cusp forms with kN<=D, both B=1.

Fix $\delta>0$, $M=\exp(N^\beta)$ with $\delta<\beta<2-\delta$, $K_\varepsilon(N)=\exp\big(\sqrt{(1-\beta/2+\varepsilon)\sqrt{\log M\log N}}\big)$ [as printed: $\exp\big(\sqrt{1-\tfrac12\beta+\varepsilon}\,\sqrt{\log M\log N}\big)$ per (2.8)]. For independent Haar $U_1..U_M\in U(N)$, $P(\max_j\max_\theta|\Lambda_{U_j}(\theta)|\le K_\varepsilon(N))\to1$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ and for no $\varepsilon<0$.

Let $M=N^c e^{N\log X}$, $2<X<N$, $c>0$, $K_\varepsilon(N)=\exp\big((\tfrac1{\sqrt2}+\varepsilon)\sqrt{N\log N\log X}\big)$. For independent Haar $U_j\in U(N)$, $P(\max_{j\le M}|\Lambda_{U_j}(0)|\le K_\varepsilon)\to1$ for all $\varepsilon>0$ and for no $\varepsilon<0$ (sampled-points version of Thm 2.1).
hypotheses: Theorem 3.5 of Hughes-Keating-O'Connell [12] tail for log|Lambda_U(0)|

statement: The conjectured 2k-th moment asymptotic (3.3) [Keating-Snaith leading term times arithmetic factor, uniform in k] cannot hold for $k\ge(2\sqrt2+\varepsilon)\sqrt{\log T/\log\log T}$, any fixed $\varepsilon>0$.
hypotheses: formula (3.3) as the hypothesis being refuted in that range

kind: theorem (conditional on moment formula (3.3) in a range of k)
statement: Let $m_T=\max_{[0,T]}|\zeta(1/2+it)|$. If (3.3) holds for $k=\log^\delta T$ with $\delta<1/2$ then $m_T\ll\exp(\log^{1-\delta}T)$. If (3.3) holds for $k=\sqrt{2\log T/\log\log T}$ then $m_T\ll\exp\big(\sqrt{\tfrac12\log T\log\log T}+O(\sqrt{\log T}\,\log\log\log T/\sqrt{\log\log T})\big)$; if it holds for $k=\sqrt{8\log T/\log\log T}$ then the matching lower bound $m_T\gg\exp(\cdots)$ holds.
conditional_on: moment conjecture (3.3) (full CFKRS/Keating-Snaith) with k growing

statement: With $K_\varepsilon(N)=(\tfrac1{\sqrt2}+\varepsilon)\sqrt{N\log N}$, $M=N^ce^N$, independent Haar $U_j\in U(N)$: $P(\max_{j\le M}\mathrm{Im}\log\Lambda_{U_j}(0)\le K_\varepsilon(N))\to1$ for all $\varepsilon>0$, no $\varepsilon<0$.
For fixed $d>0$, $\frac1T\mathrm{meas}\{0<t<T:|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|>\exp(d\sqrt{\log T\log\log T})\}=\exp(-2d^2\log T(1+o(1)))$.
For fixed $\delta>0$ and $\delta\le\lambda\le1-\delta$: $P(\max_\theta|\Lambda_U(\theta)|\ge\exp(N^\lambda))=\exp\Big(-\dfrac{N^{2\lambda}}{(1-\lambda)\log N}(1+o(1))\Big)$, $U$ Haar in $U(N)$.
role: Tail of the sup of the characteristic polynomial; engine for Thms 2.1, 2.3 and Conj. D. Proof uses Bernstein's inequality $\max|\Lambda_U'|\le N\max|\Lambda_U|$ to pass from sup to discrete sampling.

statement: If $|\zeta(\tfrac12+it_0)|=m_T=\max_{[0,T]}|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|$ then there is an absolute $A>0$ with $|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|>\tfrac12m_T$ for $|t-t_0|<A/\log T$.
role: Local regularity near the max (Cauchy estimate on a circle of radius c/log T plus functional equation); justifies discrete sampling and Lemma 3.3.

statement: For all $k>0$: $m_T^{2k}\ll 2^{2k}\log T\int_0^T|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|^{2k}dt$, absolute implied constant.
role: Converts moment asymptotics at large k into an upper bound for the maximum.

statement: For $s=\sigma+it$, $0\le\sigma\le1$, $|t|\ge2$, $X>2$, $K\in\mathbb N$: $\zeta(s)=P_X(s)Z_X(s)\big(1+O(X^{2-\sigma+K}/(|t|\log X)^K)+O(X^{-\sigma}\log X)\big)$ with $P_X=\exp(\sum_{n\le X}\Lambda(n)/(n^s\log n))$, $Z_X=\exp(-\sum_\rho U((s-\rho)\log X))$.
role: Rigorous hybrid Euler product/Hadamard product used to split prime and zero contributions; unconditional.

statement: Independent real mean-0 variance-1 $x_j$, bounded $a_j$ with $V_J^{-2}\sum_{j\le J}|a_j|^n\to0$ for all $n\ge3$, $V_J=\sum a_j^2$; then $\sum a_jx_j$ tends to Gaussian of variance $V_J$.
role: Gaussian limit for the symplectic/orthogonal prime model, giving B=1 rather than 1/2.

statement: For $2<X<\log^AT$: $\max_{t\in[0,T]}|Z_X(\tfrac12+it)|=\exp((1+o(1))\sqrt{\tfrac12\log T\log\log T})$.
role: Zero-product half of the model; combined with $P_X=O(\exp(C\sqrt{\log t/\log\log t}))$ for X=O(log T) gives Conj. A; X large (random-prime model) and intermediate X give consistency.

label_in_source: Theorem 4 (Lagarias-Odlyzko, with Serre's removal of log d term)
statement: There is an absolute constant $c_0>0$ such that, under GRH for $\zeta_L$, for $L/K$ finite Galois with group $G$, $C\subset G$ stable under conjugation, all $x\ge 2$: $\left|\pi_C(x)-\frac{|C|}{|G|}\mathrm{Li}(x)\right|\le c_0\frac{|C|}{|G|}\,x^{1/2}\,(\log d_L+n_L\log x)$, where $n_L=[L:\mathbb Q]$, $d_L$ the absolute discriminant. (Oesterle: $c_0=2$.)
hypotheses: L/K finite Galois of number fields
conditional_on: GRH for the Dedekind zeta function of L (only no zeros with Re s>1/2 is needed)

statement: There is an absolute constant $c_5>0$ such that under GRH, if $C\neq\emptyset$, then $\pi_C(x)\ge 1$ for all $x\ge c_5(\log d_L)^2$ (Oesterle: $c_5=70$).

Let $L/\mathbb Q$ be Galois of degree $n$, unramified outside a finite set $S$ of primes, $G=\mathrm{Gal}(L/\mathbb Q)$. Under GRH, for every conjugacy class $C$ of $G$ there is a prime $p\notin S$ with $\sigma_p\in C$ and $p\le c_6 n^2(\log n+\sum_{q\in S}\log q)^2$ (proof gives $c_6=4c_5^{}$-type bound; $c_6=280$ using Oesterle).
hypotheses: L/Q finite Galois unramified outside S

statement: Let $G$ be a compact $\ell$-adic Lie group of dimension $N\ge1$, $E/K$ an infinite Galois extension with group $G$ unramified outside finite $S$, $C\subset G$ closed, conjugation-stable with $\dim_{\ell} C\le d<N$; $a=(N-d)/N$. Then (i) $\pi_C(x)=O(x/\log x\cdot \varepsilon(x)^{-a})$ unconditionally, with $\varepsilon(x)=(\log x)(\log\log x)^{-1}(\log\log\log x)^{-1}$; (ii) under GRH $\pi_C(x)=O(\mathrm{Li}(x)/x^{a/2}\cdot\ldots)$, precisely $\pi_C(x)=O(\mathrm{Li}(x)/\varepsilon_R(x)^{a})$ with $\varepsilon_R(x)=x^{1/2}/(\log x)^2$. Corollary 1: $\pi_C(x)=O(x/(\log x)^{1+a-\delta})$ for all $\delta>0$, and $O(x^{1-a/2+\delta})$ under GRH. Implied constants depend on $K,S,G,C,d$.
hypotheses: C closed, conjugation-stable, l-adic dimension <= d < N

statement: Same setting; let $r=\inf_{s\in C} r(s)$ (r(s)=dim of centralizer-type invariant, dimension of the conjugacy class complement) and $\beta=(N-d)/(N-r/2)$ . Then (i) $\pi_C(x)=O(\mathrm{Li}(x)/\varepsilon(x)^{\beta})$; (ii) under GRH $\pi_C(x)=O(\mathrm{Li}(x)/\varepsilon_R(x)^{\beta})$. Since $\beta\ge a$, with strict improvement iff $r\ge1$ (no finite conjugacy classes in C). [Exact definition of r and the displayed formula for beta should be re-checked against the scan: text reads $\beta=(N-d)/(N-r/2)$.]
hypotheses: C contains no finite conjugacy class, to gain over Th. 10

statement: For a non-CM weight-2 newform (example $f=q\prod(1-q^n)^2(1-q^{11n})^2$, elliptic curve $y^2-y=x^3-x^2$) and $P(x)=\#\{p\le x: a_p=0\}$: $P(x)=O(x/(\log x)^{3/2-\varepsilon})$ for all $\varepsilon>0$, and under GRH $P(x)=O(x^{4/5})$. For general weight and h=... ($h\neq0$ branch) exponent 1/4 in (177),(178_R) replaced by 1/2 when h=0. For elliptic curves (Th. 20): $P_E^{a}(x)=O(\mathrm{Li}(x)/\varepsilon(x)^{1/4})$, and under GRH $O(\mathrm{Li}(x)/\varepsilon_R(x)^{1/4})$; exponent 1/3 if $A\ne\pm2$, 1/2 if $A=0$. Intro (e): $M_f(x)\ge\alpha x$-type non-lacunarity with explicit constant for the level-11 form.

If $P(x)$ (Frobenius-type count) satisfies $\pi(x)\ll x/(\log x)^{1+\lambda... }$ i.e. $\sum$-bound with $0\le\lambda<1$, then the number $M(x)$ of $n\le x$ with $a(n)\neq0$ (multiplicative $a$) satisfies $M(x)\gg x/(\log x)^{\lambda}$ (with constant $\gamma_a>0$). Consequence: L-functions of l-adic representations with connected Zariski closure are not lacunary ($\lambda=0$).
hypotheses: multiplicative function with vanishing set controlled as in (127')

statement:
Let $E/\mathbb Q$ be an elliptic curve without complex multiplication with conductor-type product $N_E$ of bad primes. Under GRH there is an absolute $c$ such that $\mathrm{Im}(ho_\ell)=\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb Z_\ell)$ for every prime $\ell\ge c(\log N_E)(\log\log 2N_E)^3$. Th. 21: under GRH, if $a_p
e a'_p$ for infinitely many p (two curves, case (b)), there is $p
otin S$ with $a_p
eq a'_p$ and $p\le c_{34}(\log N_S)... (\log\log 2N_S)^{12}$-type bound (formula (251_R) reads roughly $p<c(\log N)(\log\log 2N)^{12}$; exact form not verified).
Discriminant ramification bound used to replace $\sum_{v\in V(E/K)}\log Nv\le\log d_L$ by $\le \frac{1}{|I|}$-type improvement (18).
role: Removes the parasitic $\log d_L$ term in Lagarias-Odlyzko's GRH error, giving Th. 4.

statement: Closed analytic subspace of an l-adic analytic variety X of dimension <= d has l-dimension <= d; the number of points of Y mod l^n is O(l^{nd}) and equals vol(Y) l^{nd} for n large.
role: Converts dimension of the exceptional Frobenius locus into a counting bound on a finite quotient G/G(n), feeding Chebotarev.

statement: Compactness estimate for sets of endomorphisms of a free Z_l-module underlying improved exponent beta.
role: Improves Th. 10 to Th. 12 when C avoids finite conjugacy classes.

statement: Estimates for counts of integers with prime factorization supported on a set of primes with density-zero control; Dedekind-type counts.
role: Prove Th. 13/14 (non-lacunarity of Euler products).

statement: Group-theoretic exclusion of maximal subgroup types (Borel, normalizer of Cartan, exceptional) for mod-l images, using inertia of order (l-1)/4 and GRH Chebotarev to locate Frobenius with trace/determinant conditions.
role: Gives Th. 22: GL_2(F_l) surjectivity for all l above log N_E bound under GRH.

statement: Assume \mathrm{Re}\,\rho=1/2 for every non-trivial zero \rho of \zeta. Then \psi(x)-x\to \ldots, more precisely \psi(x)-x+\log 2\pi-\ldots is O(x^{1/2+\varepsilon}) for every \varepsilon>0: the difference tends to zero after dividing by x and is of order at most that of x^{1/2+\varepsilon}. (Printed statement: 'la difference psi(x)-x (+ log 2 pi ...) tend vers zero pour x=oo et cette difference est un infiniment petit d'un ordre de petitesse au moins egal a celui de x^{a}... a>1/2'.)
hypotheses: Riemann Hypothesis: Re rho = 1/2 for all non-trivial zeros

statement: Under RH, \theta(x)-x = O(x^{1/2+\varepsilon}) for every \varepsilon>0 (since \psi(x)-\theta(x)=O(\sqrt x)); the difference \theta(x)/x\to 1 at a rate at least that of x^{-1/2+\varepsilon}.

If every non-trivial zero has real part 1/2, then F(x)=\pi(x)=\mathrm{Li}(x)+\eta(x), where |\eta(x)|\le K_\varepsilon\,x^{1/2+\varepsilon} for every \varepsilon>0 (K_\varepsilon depends only on \varepsilon). Proof: combine the estimate for \psi (via the Mangoldt-de la Vallee-Poussin formula (57) for f(x)) with f(x)-F(x)=O(\sqrt x).

Under RH: |\psi(x)-x|<B\,e^{2\sqrt{\ldots}}\ldots precisely |\psi(x)-x|<B\sqrt x(\log x)^2 for all x (OCR: 'B e^{2}(log x)^2 sqrt x'), and |f(x)-\mathrm{Li}(x)|<K\log x\,\sqrt x. Hence \pi(x)=\mathrm{Li}(x)+O(\sqrt x\,\log x) with an effectively computable constant. Proof uses von Mangoldt's estimate \sum_{\rho}|{\rho}|^{-1-a}-type bound (via de la Vallee-Poussin, loc. cit. p. 42) with optimal parameter a=2/\log x.
For x>0: \lim_{s\to\infty}(1-e^{-x s}\ldots)^{\ldots}=0 or 1 according as x<1 or x>1 (smooth step as discontinuity factor); this replaces Riemann's use of the Perron-type integral (B).
role: Elementary device replacing contour integration; the whole paper rests on it to convert Euler's product identity into formulas for f(x), psi(x).

statement: Hadamard's product: with H(s)=\xi-type entire function of order 1, \prod_{\mathrm{Im}\rho>0}(1-s/\rho)(1-s/\bar\rho) converges absolutely and represents H up to a constant; consequently \zeta'/\zeta(s) has the partial fraction expansion (20) over \rho and the trivial zeros -2n.
role: Imported (Riemann, Hadamard 1893): needed to evaluate the series of section 4.
Allows interchange of sums and yields absolutely convergent double series, giving the expansion (25) of \Psi(x,s) as main term plus sums over trivial and non-trivial zeros.

statement: As s\to\infty, \sum_n s/(2n(s+2n))=O(\log s) and, if \mathrm{Re}\rho=1/2, \sum_\rho s/(\rho(s-\rho))=O(s^{\alpha}) for every \alpha>0 (in fact O(s^{1/2+\varepsilon})-type bound after using \sum|\rho|^{-1-\varepsilon}<\infty).
role: Growth of the zero sums in the explicit formula with parameter s.

statement: For x=n+1/2 and s>2x\log x (so s large), the difference between \Psi(x,s) and \psi(x) stays bounded and, for s=x^{2}, tends rapidly to 0: \Psi(x,s)=\psi(x)+\Delta with |\Delta|<\ldots (via Mertens's remark and S_2<x^s\sum\ldots).
role: Passage from the s-regularised function \Psi(x,s) to the true Chebyshev function; this is where truncation s=x^{a}(x^{2}) enters.

label_in_source: Theorem 1 (analytic version of general shifted divisor sum, from CK3)
statement: $\operatorname*{Res}_{w=1-\alpha,\,z=1-\beta}\sum_{q\ge1}\mu(q)\sum_{d\ge1}d^{z+w-1}\zeta(w+z-1)D_A\!\left(w,e(-\tfrac1{qd})\right)D_B\!\left(z,e(-\tfrac1{qd})\right)=\mathcal B(A'\cup\{-\beta\},B'\cup\{-\alpha\})$, with $A'=A\setminus\{\alpha\}$, $B'=B\setminus\{\beta\}$. (Restated from CK3; follows from an identity in Sec. 3 of CK3 and the singular-part result of Conrey-Gonek [CG].)
hypotheses: A, B finite sets of small complex shifts, |alpha|,|beta|<eps
Conjecture 1 on the pole structure of S_{A,B}(s,h) not needed for the identity itself

statement: $\operatorname*{Res}_{\substack{w_1=1-\alpha_1,z_1=1-\beta_1\\w_2=1-\alpha_2,z_2=1-\beta_2}}\ \zeta(w_1+z_1-1)\zeta(w_2+z_2-1)\sum_{(M,N)=1}\sum_{q_1,q_2,d_1,d_2}\frac{\mu(q_1)\mu(q_2)d_1^{z_1+w_1-1}d_2^{z_2+w_2-1}}{M^{z_1+w_2-1}N^{w_1+z_2-1}}\,D_{A_1}\!\big(w_1,e(-\tfrac N{q_1d_1})\big)D_{A_2}\!\big(w_2,e(-\tfrac M{q_2d_2})\big)D_{B_1}\!\big(z_1,e(-\tfrac M{q_1d_1})\big)D_{B_2}\!\big(z_2,e(-\tfrac N{q_2d_2})\big)=\mathcal B(A''\cup\{-\beta_1,-\beta_2\},B''\cup\{-\alpha_1,-\alpha_2\})$ (display partially garbled in extracted text; the exponents of M, N and the exact placement of d_i,q_i must be read from the PDF), with $A''=A\setminus\{\alpha_1,\alpha_2\}$ (A=A_1 u A_2 split), B'' analogous.
hypotheses: residues taken at the displayed poles near 1
identity of meromorphic/residue expressions, not an asymptotic with error term

statement: Both the Perron/recipe computation and the convolution of shifted divisor correlations give the same asymptotic formula (with power savings, modulo the correlation conjecture used) for the mean square of a Dirichlet polynomial of length X, T^2<<X<<T^3, with coefficients a general divisor function tau_A, tau_B; all main terms agree with the CFKRS recipe including the leading term of Keating-Snaith.
hypotheses: Uses the conjectural/heuristic delta-method pole structure for shifted divisor sums of CK3 (Conjecture 1) in Sections 3-9
conditional_on: Conjecture 1 (meromorphic continuation and residue formula for shifted divisor correlations S_{A,B}(s,h), from CK3)

statement: For four functions a,A,b,B: $F(a,A;b,B)+F(A,a;B,b)=C(A\star b,a\star B)+C(a,A)C(b,B)$, where $F(a,A;b,B)=\sum_{K,L,M}a(K)A(K+M)b(L)B(L+M)X^{K+L+M}$ and $C(a,b)=\sum_{r\ge0}a(r)b(r)X^r$.
$F(a,A;b,B)+F(A,a;B,b)=C(A\star b,a\star B)+C(a,A)C(b,B)$ (formal identity of power series).
role: Converts the p-adic local factor of the circle-method sum into the C-function of the recipe; proved by integrating over theta with Y=X e(theta) and an inclusion-exclusion on r>R, s>S

statement: Need to show $\sum_{\min(M,N)=0}X^{-M(\gamma+\beta)-N(\alpha+\delta)}\Sigma_1(M,N)\Sigma_2(M,N)X^{M+N}=(1-X^{1-\alpha-\beta})(1-X^{1-\gamma-\delta})\,C(A\cup C\cup\{-\beta,-\delta\},B\cup D\cup\{-\alpha,-\gamma\})$ with explicit sums Sigma_1, Sigma_2.
role: The local (prime-power) identity whose verification proves Theorem 2

statement: Splitting A=A_1 u A_2, B=B_1 u B_2 so tau_A=tau_{A_1}*tau_{A_2}, tau_B=tau_{B_1}*tau_{B_2}; Farey dissection of [0,1] with fractions M/N, 1<=M<=N<=Q, and h_1=m_1N-n_1M, h_2=m_2M-n_2N giving m_1m_2-n_1n_2 = h_1m_2M+h_2m_1N-h_1h_2 over MN, so the off-diagonal sum becomes a double sum over shifted divisor sums.
role: Discrete circle method: decomposes the 4-variable off-diagonal sum O_II into products of two shifted correlations (*_1): m_1N-n_1M=h_1 and (*_2): m_2M-n_2N=h_2

statement: If h_2=0 then m_2=N l, n_2=M l with l integer; the h_1 sum reduces to a single shifted divisor correlation <tau_A(m)tau_B(n)>_{(*)} given by the delta-method formula (4), with explicit arithmetic factors G_A, G_B and Z(A)=prod zeta(1+a).
role: Semi-diagonal terms feed the main-term count and match recipe terms with one swap per side

statement: Each term arising from the recipe is produced 2^{k+l} times by the circle-method decomposition where |A|=k, |B|=l, one for each decomposition of m=m_1m_2, n=n_1n_2 into divisors; this equals the number of ways the recipe term arises from decompositions of A and B, so overcounting cancels and each recipe term appears once.
role: Explains multiplicity bookkeeping: correct normalization of the Type II convolution

statement: Assume RH and $J_{-1}(T)=\sum_{0<\gamma\le T}|\zeta'(\rho)|^{-2}\ll T$. Then (i) $M(x)\ll x^{1/2}(\log x)^{3/2}$; (ii) $M(x)\ll x^{1/2}(\log\log x)^{3/2}$ outside a set of finite logarithmic measure; (iii) $\int_2^X M(x)^2x^{-1}\,dx\ll X$; (iv) the weak Mertens conjecture $\int_2^X (M(x)/x)^2dx\ll\log X$.

Assume RH and $J_{-1}(T)\ll T$. Then $e^{-y/2}M(e^y)$ has a limiting distribution $\nu$ on $\mathbb R$: $\lim_{Y\to\infty}\frac1Y\int_0^Y f(e^{-y/2}M(e^y))dy=\int f\,d\nu$ for all bounded Lipschitz $f$.
location: Introduction p.7; proof Sec. 3 using Lemmas 6-10

statement: Assume RH, $J_{-1}(T)\ll T$ and LI (positive ordinates of zeros linearly independent over $\mathbb Q$). Then $\hat\nu(\xi)=\prod_{\gamma>0}\tilde J_0\!\left(\frac{2\xi}{|(\tfrac12+i\gamma)\zeta'(\tfrac12+i\gamma)|}\right)$ with $\tilde J_0(z)=\sum_m(-1)^m(z/2)^{2m}/(m!)^2$. Consequently $\{x:|M(x)|\le\sqrt x\}$ has logarithmic density in (0,1).

Assume RH and $J_{-1}(T)\ll T$. Then $\int_0^Y (M(e^y)e^{-y/2})^2dy\sim\beta Y$ with $\beta=\sum_{\gamma>0}|\rho\zeta'(\rho)|^{-2}<\infty$; equivalently $\int_1^X (M(x)/x)^2dx\sim\beta\log X$. The variance of $\nu$ is $\beta$ (via (19), mean of $e^{-y/2}M(e^y)$ is $o(1)$).

Assume RH, LI, $\sum_{0<\gamma<T}|\rho\zeta'(\rho)|^{-1}\asymp(\log T)^{5/4}$ and $\sum_{\gamma>T}|\rho\zeta'(\rho)|^{-2}\asymp T^{-1}$. Then $\exp(-\exp(\tilde c_1V^{4/5}))\ll\nu([V,\infty))\ll\exp(-\exp(\tilde c_2V^{4/5}))$ for effective $\tilde c_i>0$.
There is $B>0$ with $\limsup_{x\to\infty}M(x)/(\sqrt x(\log\log\log x)^{5/4})=B$ and $\liminf=-B$. Sec 4.3 gives a heuristic (not a proof) from Cor 12 assuming uniform convergence in (69).

(i) $J_{-1/2}(T)\ll T(\log T)^v\Rightarrow\sum_{0<\gamma<T}|\rho\zeta'(\rho)|^{-1}\ll(\log T)^{v+1}$; (ii) $J_{-1}(T)\ll T\Rightarrow\sum_{T<\gamma<2T}|\rho\zeta'(\rho)|^{-2}\ll 1/T$; (iii) tail sums via partial summation for $b>u\ge1$.
role: Converts Gonek-Hejhal moment bounds into the discrete sums used in all later estimates (partial summation).

statement: Assume RH and simple zeros. For $x\ge2$ and $T$ in a sequence $T_n\in[n,n+1]$ with $1/\zeta(\sigma+iT_n)\ll T^\epsilon$ (Lemma 3): $M(x)=\sum_{|\gamma|<T}x^\rho/(\rho\zeta'(\rho))+\tilde E(x,T)$, $\tilde E\ll x\log x/T+x/(T^{1-\epsilon}\log x)+1$.
role: Explicit formula for M(x), following Titchmarsh Thm 14.27.

statement: Assume RH and $J_{-1}(T)\ll T$. The explicit formula of Lemma 4 holds for all $T\ge2$ with an extra error term of size $\ll x(\log T)^{1/2}/T$ type, obtained by Cauchy-Schwarz and Lemma 1(ii).
role: Removes the restriction T in {T_n} using the k=-1 Gonek-Hejhal bound.
location: Sec. 2 (error term as printed in extracted text is garbled; exact form not verified)

statement: Assume RH and $J_{-1}(T)\ll T$. Then $\int_Z^{e^Z\cdot}\left|\sum_{T\le|\gamma|\le X}x^{i\gamma}/(\rho\zeta'(\rho))\right|^2dx/x\ll(\log T)/T^{?}$ (printed as $(\log T)/T^{1/4}$-type bound in extraction; exact exponent not verified).
role: Key mean-square bound on zero-sum tails; drives Thm 1(ii)-(iv) and weak convergence in Thm 2.

statement: Kronecker-Weyl variant: for reals $t_1..t_N$ and continuous 1-periodic f, the average of $f(y t_1,...,y t_N)$ over $[0,Y]$ converges to the Haar integral over the closure of the orbit, a J-dimensional sub-torus.
role: Builds limiting measures $\nu_T$ for truncated sums without LI (Rubinstein-Sarnak approach).

statement: Lemma 8: under RH there is a probability measure $\nu_T$ with $\nu_T(f)=\lim\frac1Y\int_0^Yf(\phi^{(T)}(y))dy$ for bounded continuous f. Lemma 9: Helly selection, weak convergence characterization, and Levy continuity theorem.
role: Standard probabilistic machinery for passing $T\to\infty$.

statement: Assume RH and $J_{-1}(T)\ll T$. For $T\ge2$, $Y\ge\log2$: $\int_{\log2}^Y|\epsilon^{(T)}(y)|^2dy\ll Y(\log T)T^{-1/4}+1$ (exponent as read from extracted text).
role: Shows the truncation error has small mean square, so $\nu_T\to\nu$ and the limit distribution exists.

statement: If $\Phi^{(1)}$ and $\Phi^{(2)}$ are both admissible gamma-factor products for $F\in S$ then $\Phi^{(1)}(s)=C\Phi^{(2)}(s)$ for a real constant C; hence the degree $d_F=2\sum w_i$ is well defined.
If $F\in S$ then $F\equiv1$ or $d_F\ge1$. (No degrees in $(0,1)$; $d_F=0$ forces $F=1$.)
hypotheses: F in S per axioms (1)-(4) incl. theta<1/2

statement: Every F in S factors into primitives (additivity $d_{FG}=d_F+d_G$ and Theorem 3.1); if $d_F<2$ then F is primitive.

Assuming Selberg's conjectures (regularity and orthonormality): $n_F=\sum e_i^2$ for $F=\prod F_i^{e_i}$; $n_F=1\Rightarrow F$ primitive; a pole of order m at 1 implies $\zeta^m\mid F$ in S; S has unique factorization; Dedekind's conjecture ($\zeta_K/\zeta$ entire) holds; no F in S vanishes on $\Re s=1$.

If $F\in S^*(1)$ (normalized functional equation with all $w_i=1/2$, degree 1) then q is a positive integer and there is a primitive Dirichlet character $\chi \bmod q$ and real $\tau$ with $F(s)=L(s+i\tau,\chi)$.

For $F=\sum a_nn^{-s}$ absolutely convergent for $\sigma>1$ and the GL(2)-type completed function $\Phi$ with parameter $\mu$ real, $\Phi$ is entire and satisfies $\Phi(s)=\Phi(1-s)$ iff $f(re^{i\theta})=f(r^{-1}e^{i\theta})$ for $0<\theta<\pi/2$, where $f(x,y)=y^{1/2}\sum a_nH_\mu(2\pi nx/\sqrt q)K_\mu(2\pi ny/\sqrt q)$.
For F in S, $F_p$ has no zeros in $\sigma>1/2$ and F has no zeros in $\sigma>1$.
role: Euler product control; uses theta<1/2.

statement: If F in S has a pole or zero at $1+i\tau$ then $\sum_{p\le x}a_p p^{-1-i\tau}$ is unbounded as $x\to\infty$.
role: Link of zero/pole on the 1-line to prime sums; used in Props 4.3, 4.6.

statement: $\kappa\ge 0.4105$ and $\kappa^*\ge 0.4058$, where $\kappa=\liminf_{T\to\infty}N_0(T)/N(T)$, $\kappa^*=\liminf N_0^*(T)/N(T)$, $N_0$ counts zeros $\rho=\tfrac12+i\gamma$, $0<\gamma<T$, and $N_0^*$ counts the simple ones.

With $V(s)=Q(-\frac1L\frac d{ds})\zeta(s)$, $Q(0)=1$, $Q(x)+Q(1-x)=\text{const}$, $L=\log T$, $\sigma_0=\frac12-\frac RL$, and any mollifier $\psi$: $\kappa\ge1-\frac1R\log\Big(\frac1T\int_1^T|V\psi(\sigma_0+it)|^2dt\Big)+o(1)$ (Littlewood's lemma plus Jensen/AM-GM). Choosing $Q$ linear gives the version for $\kappa^*$.

For $\theta_1=4/7-\varepsilon$, $\theta_2=1/2-\varepsilon$ ($\varepsilon>0$ small): $\frac1T\int_1^T|V\psi(\sigma_0+it)|^2dt=c(P,Q,R,\theta_1,\theta_2)+o(1)$ with $c=c_1+2c_{12}+c_2$ given by (3.2),(3.4),(3.6).

For $w$ smooth, $0\le w\le1$, supported in $[T/4,2T]$, $w^{(j)}\ll\Delta^{-j}$ with $\Delta=T/L$, and $\sigma=\frac12-\frac RL$, uniformly for $R\ll1$: $\int w(t)|V\psi(\sigma+it)|^2dt=c(P,Q,R,\theta_1,\theta_2)\hat w(0)+O(TL^{-1+\varepsilon})$.
For $\theta_1<4/7$: $\int_1^T|V\psi_1(\sigma_0+it)|^2dt\sim c_1T$, $c_1=1+\frac1{\theta_1}\int_0^1\!\!\int_0^1e^{2Rv}\big(Q(v)P_1'(u)+\theta_1Q'(v)P_1(u)+\theta_1RQ(v)P_1(u)\big)^2du\,dv$.

For $\theta_2<\theta_1<4/7$ (with (5.1): $\frac52\theta_1+\theta_2<2$, $\frac53\theta_1+\theta_2<\frac43$, $\theta_2<\frac23\theta_1$ for the proof): $I_{12}=\int w|V|^2\psi_1\overline{\psi_2}=c_{12}\hat w(0)+O(T/L)$ with explicit $c_{12}$ (3.4) involving $\frac{d^2}{dxdy}$ of a triple integral with $Q,P_1,P_2''$; the shifted version is $I_{12}(\alpha,\beta)=c_{12}(\alpha,\beta)\hat w(0)+O(T/L)$ uniformly in $\alpha,\beta\ll L^{-1}$.

For $\theta_2<1/2$: $I_2=\int w|V|^2|\psi_2|^2=c_2\hat w(0)+O(TL^{-1+\varepsilon})$, $c_2$ given by the 4-dimensional integral (3.6) with $P_2''$ factors; proof via a twisted second moment (Prop 4.2).

For $L^2\le|t|\le2T$, uniformly for $\alpha,\beta\ll L^{-1}$: $\zeta(\tfrac12+\alpha+it)\zeta(\tfrac12-\beta+it)=\sum_{l\ge1}\frac{\sigma_{\alpha,-\beta}(l)}{l^{1/2+it}}e^{-l/T^3}+O(T^{-1+\varepsilon})$.
role: One-long-sum approximate functional equation; the exponential cutoff truncates l at T^3 and makes the off-diagonal analysis tractable

statement: For $ab\le T^{1-\varepsilon}$, uniformly in $\alpha,\beta\ll L^{-1}$, $\int w(t)(a/b)^{-it}\zeta(\tfrac12+\alpha+it)\zeta(\tfrac12+\beta-it)dt$ equals the diagonal main terms $\sum_{am=bn}$ (two pieces with $V_t$ kernel) $+O(T^{-1/2})$.
role: Twisted second moment (implicit in Balasubramanian-Conrey-Heath-Brown); only diagonal terms contribute for ab<=T^{1-eps}

statement: Under (5.1), $I_{12}(\alpha,\beta)=\sum_{n\le y_1;hk\le y_2;hl=nk}\frac{\mu(n)\mu_2(h)\sigma_{\alpha,-\beta}(l)}{(hkln)^{1/2}}P_1[n]P_2[hk]e^{-l/T^3}\int(\frac t{2\pi})^{-\beta}w(t)dt+O_B(T/L^B)$.
role: Diagonal main term of the cross term

statement: Under (5.1), the off-diagonal contribution $C$ (terms $hl\ne nk$) satisfies $C\ll_B T/L^B$ for any $B\ge0$.
role: Key analytic difficulty for the longer mollifier: off-diagonal bound via Kloosterman-sum/Deshouillers-Iwaniec-type input in the style of Conrey 1989

statement: Under (5.1), $C=C_0+O(T^{1-\varepsilon})$ with $C_0$ an explicit sum over $h\le ny_2/\Delta^{1-\varepsilon}$, $b|f$, $f\ne0$.
role: Isolates a main contribution from the near-diagonal in the off-diagonal sum, which cancels against terms in the main evaluation

statement: The arithmetical factor satisfies $B_0(s,s,s)=\sum_{h_1k_2m=h_2k_1n}\frac{\mu_2(h_1)\mu_2(h_2)}{(h_1k_1h_2k_2mn)^{1/2+s}}=\sum_{l_1m=l_2n}\frac{\mu(l_1)\mu(l_2)}{(l_1l_2mn)^{1/2+s}}=1$ using $\sum_{h|l}\mu_2(h)=\mu(l)$; similarly $A(0,0,0)=1$ in Sec 5.6.
role: Shows the Euler-product arithmetic factors collapse to 1 at the origin

statement: Assume the extended Riemann hypothesis for the Dedekind zeta function of every Galois field Q(b^{1/k_1}, \zeta_k) with k square-free and k_1 | k. Let a be a nonzero integer, not \pm 1 and not a perfect square; N_a(x) is the number of primes p\le x for which a is a primitive root mod p; a_1 is the square-free part of a; h is the largest integer such that a is a perfect h-th power; C(h)=\prod_{q|h}(1-\tfrac{1}{q-1})\prod_{q\nmid h}(1-\tfrac{1}{q(q-1)}). If a_1\not\equiv 1 \pmod 4 then N_a(x)=C(h)\,\frac{x}{\log x}+O\!\left(\frac{x\log\log x}{\log^2 x}\right) as x\to\infty.
hypotheses: a nonzero, a\ne\pm1, a not a perfect square
conditional_on: Extended Riemann hypothesis for Dedekind zeta functions of the fields Q(b^{1/k_1}, 1^{1/k}), k squarefree, k_1|k

statement: Under the same hypothesis, if a_1\equiv 1 \pmod 4 then N_a(x)=C(h)\Big(1-\mu(|a_1|)\prod_{q|h,\,q|a_1}\frac{1}{q-2}\prod_{q\nmid h,\,q|a_1}\frac{1}{q^2-q-1}\Big)\frac{x}{\log x}+O\!\left(\frac{x\log\log x}{\log^2 x}\right).

Under the same hypothesis, if a is neither \pm 1 nor a perfect square then there are infinitely many primes p for which a is a primitive root modulo p. This follows because the density constant A(a) is strictly positive.
location: Section 7, p. 220; positivity of A(a) at p. 219 after (32)

statement: Without any hypothesis, with \xi_1=\tfrac16\log x, \xi_2=x^{1/2}\log^{-2}x, \xi_3=x^{1/2}\log x: N_a(x)=N_a(x,\xi_1)+O\{M_a(x,\xi_1,\xi_2)\}+O\!\left(\frac{x\log\log x}{\log^2 x}\right), where M_a(x,\xi_2,\xi_3)=O(x\log\log x/\log^2x) by Brun's method and Mertens, and M_a(x,\xi_3,x-1)=O(x/\log^2 x).

M_a(x,\xi_1,\xi_2)\le\sum_{\xi_1<q\le\xi_2}\Big(\frac{\operatorname{li}x}{q(q-1)}+O(x^{1/2}\log x)\Big)=O\!\left(\frac{x}{\log^2x}\right), using the conditional prime-ideal-type estimate (28) (stated in Section 5; not read in detail).
conditional_on: extended RH for the Kummer fields

statement: For p\nmid a, a is a primitive root mod p iff there is no prime q | p-1 for which a is a q-th power residue mod p; this gives the sieve N_a(x)=N_a(x,x-1) and the Legendre-type inclusion-exclusion (5) N_a(x,\xi_1)=\sum_{l'}\mu(l')P_a(x,l').
role: Reduces the problem to counting primes splitting completely in Kummer fields.

statement: The primes counted by P_a(x,k) are exactly those p\nmid ak that split completely in G=Q(a^{1/k_1}, 1^{1/k}), with k_1=k/(h,k); [G:Q]=\varphi(k)[G:Z]\text{ where }[G:Z]\mid k_1 and in fact [G:Z]=k_1 or k_1/2 (the latter only if k is even), using that subfields of abelian Z are abelian.
role: Gives the degree n(k) of the Kummer extension so that the prime ideal theorem under GRH produces P_a(x,k)=\mathrm{li}\,x/n(k)+O(\sqrt x\log x\cdot\ldots).

statement: For primes q>x^{1/2}\log x, p\le x with R(q,p), p divides \prod_{m<x^{1/2}\log^{-1}x}(a^{2m}-1), giving M_a(x,\xi_3,x-1)<\frac{2\log|a|}{\log 2}\sum_{m<x^{1/2}\log^{-1}x} m=O(x/\log^2x), with no hypothesis.
role: Handles large q unconditionally by a size argument on the product.

statement: Uniform-in-field polynomial bounds: |\Delta|\le k^{A_2 n(k)}, and |(s-1)\zeta_G(s)|\le\{k(|t|+2)\}^{A_8 n} on -3/2\le\sigma\le 11/2, obtained from the functional equation, Stirling and Phragmen-Lindelof; 1/|(s-1)\zeta(s)|\le A_3^n at \sigma=2.
role: Supplies the explicit dependence on the field degree n(k) needed to apply the explicit formula for \psi(x,k) under GRH uniformly in k up to x^{1/3}-type ranges.

statement: Evaluation of A(a)=\sum_{k\ge1}\mu(k)(h,k)\,\varepsilon(k)/(k\varphi(k))-type series: A(a)=C(h) if a_1\not\equiv1 mod 4, and A(a)=C(h)(1-\mu(|a_1|)\prod_{q|h,q|a_1}(q-2)^{-1}\prod_{q\nmid h,q|a_1}(q^2-q-1)^{-1}) if a_1\equiv1 mod 4; A(a)>0 always.
role: Computes the Artin constant (Heilbronn-corrected) and proves positivity.

statement: $\Lambda \ge 0$, where $H_t(z)=\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi(u)\cos(zu)\,du$, $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{4u})$, and $\Lambda$ is the (Newman) constant with: all zeros of $H_t$ are real iff $t\ge\Lambda$.
hypotheses: unconditional (RH may be assumed WLOG since Lambda<0 implies Lambda<=0 i.e. RH)

statement: For $z=x-i\kappa\log_+x$, $x\ge0$, $0\le\kappa\le C$, $\Lambda<t\le0$: $H_t(z)\ll\exp(-\pi x/8+O_C(\log_+^2x))$; and for $\kappa\ge C'$ (absolute) $H_t(z)=\exp(-\pi x/8+O_C(\log_+^2x))$ and $H_t'/H_t(z)=\frac i4\log\frac{iz}{4\pi}+O_C(\log_+x/x)$.

For $\Lambda<t\le0$, $T>0$, $0\le\alpha\le C$: $N_t([0,T])=\Psi(T)+O(\log_+^2T)$ (Psi the Riemann-von Mangoldt main term $\frac{T}{4\pi}\log\frac{T}{4\pi}-\frac{T}{4\pi}$) and $N_t([T,T+\alpha\log_+T])=\frac{\alpha\log_+^2T}{4\pi}+o_{T\to\infty}(\log_+^2T)$ uniformly in alpha.
For $\Lambda<t\le0$ zeros $x_j(t)$ are simple, C^1 in t, and $\partial_tx_k(t)=2\sum'_{j\ne k}\frac1{x_k(t)-x_j(t)}$ (principal value sum).

For $j\in\mathbb Z^*$, $\Lambda/2\le t\le0$: $\max_{k\ne j}H_{jk}(t)\ll(\log_+^2j)\log_+\log_+j$, where $H_{jk}=\log\frac1{|x_j-x_k|}$-type gap quantity; i.e. $\log\frac1{x_{j+1}-x_j}\ll\log^2 j\log\log j$.
Integrated renormalized energy bound: $\int_{\Lambda/4}^0\tilde E_{[0.5T\log T,3T\log T]_{\mathbb Z^*}}(t)\,dt=o_{T\to\infty}(T\log^3_+T)$.

Energy at time zero: $\tilde E_{[T\log T,2T\log T]_{\mathbb Z^*}}(0)=o_{T\to\infty}(T\log^3T)$. Consequence (eq. 93): $x_{j+1}(0)-x_j(0)=\frac{4\pi+o(1)}{\log T}$ for a proportion $1-o(1)$ of $j\in[T\log T,2T\log T]$, contradicting the Conrey-Ghosh-Goldston-Gonek-Heath-Brown small-gap theorem (proportion c(lambda)>0 of gaps <= lambda*4pi/log T for any lambda>0.77, under RH).
Saddle point / Stirling-type control of the integral representation of H_t(x-iy) with y of size ~ log x.
role: Provides Lemma 4 and thereby the Riemann-von Mangoldt-type counts for t<0.

statement: Quantitative repulsion estimate for finite subsets K of zeros, extending Csordas-Smith-Varga Theorem 1 (finite-set log-gap bound).
role: Gives Prop 13 lower bound on gaps, needed to define cutoff Hamiltonian H(t)=sum log 1/|x_j-x_k|.

statement: Weak integrated energy bound: $\int_{\Lambda/2}^0\sum_{J\le j<k\le2J}E_{jk}(t)\,dt\ll J^2\log_+^{O(1)}J$.
role: Justifies swapping derivative and infinite sum in the Hamiltonian/energy monotonicity formula.

statement: Local (cutoff) versions of d/dt H = -4E and monotonicity (convexity) of renormalized energy, with error terms from spatial cutoffs.
role: Core of the 'relaxation to local equilibrium' mechanism; feeds Thm 17.

statement: Long-range decay of pairwise interaction terms and absolute convergence of truncated energy functionals; bound H~_T(t)=O(delta_T log^3 T) on Lambda/4<=t<=0.
role: Technical control of cutoff errors so the integrated energy bound closes.

statement: Existence (by pigeonholing a la Bourgain) of a good interval I^0 within [0.8 T log T, 2.2 T log T] where dyadic-scale integrated energies are O~(1).
role: Provides the localized initial control for energy propagation.

statement: Energy propagation inequality: energy at t=0 on an interval is controlled by integrated energy at earlier times on slightly larger intervals.
role: Transfers the integrated bound (Thm 17) to the time-zero bound (Prop 26).

statement: Let $\frac{10^9}{H_0}\le k\le1$ (displayed as 109/H_0 in text), $d>0$, $H\in[1002,H_0)$, $\alpha>0$, $\delta\ge1$ (see Lemma 4.14: $\delta>0$), $\eta_0=0.23622\ldots$, $1+\eta_0\le\mu\le1+\eta$, $\eta\in(\eta_0,\tfrac12)$ fixed, $\sigma>\tfrac12+\tfrac d{\log H_0}$, with $H_0=3.0610046\cdot10^{10}$ (Platt: RH verified for |Im rho|<=H_0). Then there exist $C_1,C_2>0$ (defined in (4.72),(4.73)) such that for all $T\ge H_0$: $N(\sigma,T)\le\frac{(T-H)\log T}{2\pi d}\log\Big(1+\frac{C_1(\log kT)^{2\sigma}(\log T)^{4(1-\sigma)}T^{\frac83(1-\sigma)}}{T-H}\Big)+\frac{C_2}{2\pi d}(\log T)^2$ (1.6), hence (1.7): $N(\sigma,T)\le\frac{C_1}{2\pi d}(\log kT)^{2\sigma}(\log T)^{5-4\sigma}T^{\frac83(1-\sigma)}+\frac{C_2}{2\pi d}(\log T)^2$.
hypotheses: k lower bound as in Lemma 4.14, U(alpha,k,H_0)>1 and U(alpha,k,T) decreasing in T
conditional_on: Uses unconditional verification of RH up to height H_0 (Platt) only to subtract N(sigma,H); no RH assumed for the bound

statement: For example $N(0.90,T)<11.499(\log T)^{16/5}T^{4/15}+3.186(\log T)^2$ (for T>=H_0), and $N(0.90,H_0)<130.07$ from (1.6). Table 1 lists A=C_1/(2 pi d), B=C_2/(2 pi d) in $N(\sigma,T)\le A(\log kT)^{2\sigma}(\log T)^{5-4\sigma}T^{\frac83(1-\sigma)}+B(\log T)^2$ for sigma in {0.60,0.65,...,0.99}; Table 2 lists bounds for N(sigma,H_0) for sigma 0.60-0.99 (e.g. 520.28 at sigma=0.60; 130.07 at 0.90; 106.18 at 0.99).

Ramare [24]: for sigma>=0.52 fixed and T>=2000, $N(\sigma,T)\le965(3T)^{8(1-\sigma)/3}(\log T)^{5-2\sigma}+51.5(\log T)^2$; gives $N(0.90,H_0)<2.1529\cdot10^{10}$. (Footnote 1: the originally published constant 4.9 was wrong; a corrected proof was sent by Ramare.)

Let $\eta>0$, f holomorphic for Re s>=-eta, real for real s, with $|f(s)|\le M$ for Re s>=1+eta and $|\Re f(1+\eta+it)|\ge m>0$ for all t. For $\sigma\in(0,1+\eta]$ and U not an ordinate of a zero of f, there is an increasing sequence of naturals N_k with $|\arg f(\sigma+iU)|\le\frac\pi{L_k}\ldots+\frac\pi{\log\ldots}$ (precise bound (4.32) not transcribed); sharper version of a lemma of Titchmarsh p.213; Corollary 4.11 specializes with eta_0=0.23622..., X>=10^9.
For $-\tfrac12\le-\eta\le\sigma\le1+\eta\le\tfrac32$: $|\zeta(s)|\le3\left|\frac{1+s}{1-s}\right|\left(\frac{|1+s|}{2\pi}\right)^{\frac12(1-\sigma+\eta)}\zeta(1+\eta)$.
role: Explicit convexity bound (imported)

statement: $|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|\le0.63\,t^{1/6}\log t$ for t>=3 and $\max_{|t|\le T}|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|\le0.63T^{1/6}\log T+2.851$.
role: Explicit van der Corput subconvexity for zeta (imported, Hiary Indag. Math. 2016)

statement: Explicit mean value theorem for Dirichlet polynomials with real sequence (u_n): bound for $\int_0^T|\sum u_nn^{-it}|^2dt$ with explicit constants (Preissmann version).
role: Bounds M_{g,T}(X,sigma_2) and the mollified second moment

statement: For T>0, X>=kH_0: $\int_0^T|M_X(\tfrac12+it)|^2dt\le(C_1T+C_2X)\log X$ (explicit constants from Ramare's bounds, Lemmas 3.3-3.4).
role: Second moment of mollifier on the critical line

statement: Weight $g(s)=\frac{s-1}{s}e^{\alpha(s/T)^2}$ satisfies (2.12) with beta=2, explicit omega_1,omega_2 giving upper bound $|g(\sigma+it)|\le\omega_1e^{-\alpha(t/T)^2}$ and lower bound $\omega_2\le|g|$ on [H,T].
role: New weight function giving better constants than Ingham's cos-weight (beta=1) and Ramare's s(cos(s/2T))^{1/2}

statement: Explicit bounds for $M_{g,T}(X,\sigma)$ at sigma=1/2 and sigma_2 slightly above 1, combining Lemmas 3.2-3.6 with the weights, and the convexity estimate (2.17) $M(X,\sigma)\le M(X,\tfrac12)^{\frac{\sigma_2-\sigma}{\sigma_2-1/2}}M(X,\sigma_2)^{\frac{\sigma-1/2}{\sigma_2-1/2}}$ (Hardy-Ingham-Polya).
role: Core Ingham smoothing and interpolation

statement: With $\alpha,d,\delta>0$, $\eta_0=0.23622\ldots$, $\eta\in[\eta_0,\tfrac12)$, $\mu\in[1+\eta_0,1+\eta]$, $H_0=3.0610046\cdot10^{10}$, $1002\le H\le H_0$, $\frac{10^9}{H_0}\le k\le1$, $T\ge H_0$, $X=kT$, $\sigma>\tfrac12+\tfrac d{\log H_0}$, $U(\alpha,k,H_0)>1$ and $U(\alpha,k,T)$ decreasing in T: (4.70)/(4.71) hold with C_1,C_2 as in (4.72),(4.73).
role: Technical form of Theorem 1.1 with all parameter constraints

statement: $\zeta(\sigma+it)\ne0$ for $|t|\ge2$ and $\sigma>1-\frac{1}{5.573412\,\log|t|}$. This is the largest known zero-free region in the critical strip for $3.06\cdot10^{10}<|t|<\exp(10151.5)$.
hypotheses: uses RH verification height T_0=3.06e10 (Platt/Wedeniwski-type computation, ref [10]) as input
conditional_on: numerical verification of RH to height 3.06e10 (imported)
validity of the numerical optimization step (finite computation)
location: Sec 1 p.3; proof by Kadiri's method with computed parameters, Sec 3 and Sec 6

statement: Let $P_n$ be the set of even trigonometric polynomials $f_n(\varphi)=\sum_{k=0}^n a_k\cos k\varphi\ge0$ with $a_k\ge0$ and $a_1>a_0$, and $V=\lim_{n\to\infty}\inf_{f_n\in P_n}\frac{f_n(0)-a_0}{(\sqrt{a_1}-\sqrt{a_0})^2}$. Then $34.468305<V<34.4889920009$ (previously $34.468305<V<34.5035864$).
location: Sec 1 p.3; upper bound from the degree-40 polynomial F_40 (V_40<34.488992000856), Sec 6

statement: With $\epsilon_0(x)=\sqrt{8/(17\pi)}\,X^{1/2}e^{-X}$, $X=\sqrt{(\log x)/R}$, $R=6.315$: $|\theta(x)-x|\le x\epsilon_0(x)$ for $x\ge149$ and $|\psi(x)-x|\le x\epsilon_0(x)$ for $x\ge23$ (replacing 6.455 by 6.315 in Trudgian's earlier result).
conditional_on: Theorem 1 converted to the form sigma>=1-1/(6.315 log|t/17|), t>=24 via [19]

statement: For $x\ge229$: $|\pi(x)-\mathrm{li}(x)|\le0.2593\,\frac{x}{(\log x)^{3/4}}\exp\left(-\sqrt{\frac{\log x}{6.315}}\right)$.

Kadiri's inequality $R_0\le\frac{A\,g_1(\theta)(1-\kappa)}{2(K(w,\theta)-C(\eta))}$ with $A=f_n(0)-a_0$, $g_1(\theta)=\sec^2\theta(3-\theta\tan\theta-3\theta\cot\theta)$, $K(w,\theta)=\int_0^{d_1(\theta)}(a_1e^{-u}-a_0)h_\theta(u)e^{wu}du$; improved to $R_0\le\frac A2 g_1(\theta)(1-\kappa)\min_{0<\eta_1\le\eta_0}\max\{1/K(w_1,\theta),1/(K(w_0,\theta)-C(\eta_1))\}$.
role: Master bound; the new parameter eta_1 retains some of the error term to gain a better constant.

statement: Explicit degree-16 nonnegative even trigonometric polynomial with a_k>=0, a_1>a_0, nonnegativity guaranteed by the construction method.
role: Main source of the improvement (together with the error-term saving, about 93.6% of the improvement; remaining 6.4% from larger T_0).

statement: Empirical: the attainable constant is well approximated by $R_0=5.4912+2.0185/\log T_0$, suggesting limited further gain from larger T_0.
role: Heuristic fitted trend (not a theorem).

statement: \lambda_n(Z)=\sum'_{\rho\in Z}[1-(1-1/\rho)^n] (\ast-convergent, \lim_{T}\sum_{|\rho|\le T}), well defined for all n\in\mathbb Z for multisets Z omitting 0 and 1. For Z=Z(\pi), the zeros of \xi(s,\pi), one has \lambda_{-n}(\pi)=\lambda_n(\pi) and \lambda_n(\pi^\vee)=\lambda_n(\pi).

For a multiset Z with \sum_{\rho}\mathrm{Re}(\rho)/(1+|\rho|)^2<\infty, invariant under \rho\mapsto 1-\bar\rho and omitting 0 and 1: \mathrm{Re}\,\lambda_n(Z)\ge0 for all n>0 iff all \mathrm{Re}\,\rho=1/2. In particular RH for L(s,\pi) holds iff \mathrm{Re}\,\lambda_n(\pi)\ge0 for all n\ge0.

For the Li test functions G_n(s)=1-(1-1/s)^n and the Weil scalar product \langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{W(\pi)}: \langle G_n,G_m\rangle_{W(\pi)}=\lambda_n(\pi)+\lambda_{-m}(\pi)-\lambda_{n-m}(\pi), hence \|G_n\|^2_{W(\pi)}=\lambda_n(\pi)+\lambda_{-n}(\pi)=2\,\mathrm{Re}\,\lambda_n(\pi).

For all n\ge1: \lambda_n(\pi)=S_\infty(n,\pi^\vee)-S_f(n,\pi^\vee)+\delta(\pi), where S_\infty(n,\pi)=\sum_{j=1}^n\binom nj\tau_{j-1}(\pi), S_f(n,\pi)=\sum_{j=1}^n\binom nj\eta_{j-1}(\pi), and \delta(\pi)=1 for \pi trivial on GL(1), else 0.

S_\infty(n,\pi) is real, and for n\ge K(\pi)=\max_j|\kappa_j(\pi)|^2: S_\infty(n,\pi)=\tfrac N2 n\log n+C_1(\pi)n+O(N(K(\pi)+1)), with C_1(\pi)=\tfrac N2(\gamma-1-\log 2\pi)+\tfrac12\log Q(\pi), Q(\pi) the conductor; the O-constant is absolute and C_1 is independent of the archimedean parameters.

S_f(n,\pi)=\lambda_n(\sqrt n,\pi^\vee)+O_\pi(\sqrt n\log n), where \lambda_n(T,\pi)=\sum_{|\mathrm{Im}\rho|<T}[1-(1-1/\rho)^n] is the incomplete Li coefficient. If GRH holds for L(s,\pi), then \lambda_n(\sqrt n,\pi^\vee)=O(\sqrt n\log n).

For pi irreducible cuspidal unitary automorphic on GL(N)/Q and n\ge1: \lambda_n(\pi)=\tfrac N2 n\log n+C_1(\pi)n-\lambda_n(\sqrt n,\pi)+O_\pi(\sqrt n\log n). If RH holds for L(s,\pi): \lambda_n(\pi)=\tfrac N2 n\log n+C_1(\pi)n+O_\pi(\sqrt n\log n). If RH fails the incomplete term can be exponentially large in n.
location: Sect. 1, Theorem 1.1 (proved by Lemma 4.2 + Thm 5.1 + Thm 6.1)

statement: (1) For every such pi there is an entire function F_\pi(z) of order one and exponential type with F_\pi(n)=\lambda_n(\pi) for n\in\mathbb Z and F_\pi(-\bar z)=\overline{F_\pi(z)}-type reality on the imaginary axis (7.1)-(7.2). (2) Under GRH for L(s,\pi) there is a unique F_\pi of exponential type at most \pi satisfying (i) and such that F_\pi(z)-e(\tfrac12,\pi)(1-\cos\pi z) has type strictly less than \pi, where e(1/2,pi) is the order of the zero of \xi(s,\pi) at s=1/2; on the real axis |F_\pi(x)|\le C(|x|+2)\log(|x|+2). Its tempered Fourier transform has countable support in [-\pi,\pi] with 0 as the only limit point.
Standard properties: |a_n(\pi)|\le C(\pi)d(n)n^{N/2}; \mathrm{Re}\,\kappa_j>-1/2; zeros of \Lambda(s,\pi) lie in 0<\mathrm{Re}\,s<1; N^\pm_\pi(T)=\tfrac N{2\pi}T\log T+C_0(\pi)T+O(\log T).
role: Imported analytic input on the Godement-Jacquet L-functions needed to define and control lambda_n(pi).

statement: k_n(s)=(1+1/s)^n-1=\sum_{j=1}^n\binom nj s^{-j}; S_f is obtained by integrating (L'/L)(s,\pi) k_n(s) over a rectangle with horizontal segments at height \pm\sqrt n, the vertical segments around the strip, and a residue at s=0.
role: Core of the proof of Theorem 6.1.
location: Sect. 6, proof of Theorem 6.1 (Eq. 6.4) and the Lemma 6.1 estimates

statement: Gamma-function estimates for \mathrm{Re}(z)\ge-3/4 and n\ge|z|+2 (digamma/Stirling-type with explicit error), used to evaluate S_\infty(n,\pi) via the archimedean parameters kappa_j.
role: Archimedean asymptotics in Theorem 5.1.

statement: Power series expansion of (\xi'/\xi)(s,\pi) at s=1 in terms of the Euler-product logarithmic coefficients (\eta_j) and archimedean coefficients (\tau_j).
role: Gives the arithmetic formula (4.6).

statement: GRH holds for Dirichlet L-functions of primitive character modulus $q\le 400{,}000$ up to height $t_0=\max\big(\tfrac{10^8}{q},\tfrac{7.5\cdot10^7}{q}+200\big)$ for even $q$ and $t_0=\max\big(\tfrac{10^8}{q},\tfrac{3.75\cdot10^7}{q}+200\big)$ for odd $q$, i.e. every zero of $L_\chi(s)$ with $|\Im s|\le t_0$ and $0<\Re s<1$ lies on $\Re s=1/2$. Checked 29,565,923,837 L-functions, isolating about $3.8\cdot10^{13}$ zeros (excluding those used in Turing's method).
hypotheses: height bound as stated (a finite rectangle per character)

statement: For every Dirichlet L-function of primitive character of modulus $q\le2{,}000{,}000$, $L_\chi(1/2)\ne0$ (checked for 739,151,526,102 primitive characters; 438,152 double-precision-interval straddles of zero were resolved by interval Euler-Maclaurin, the final 20 using MPFI at 100 bits).

For $q\ge3$ and given $\varphi(q)$ complex values $a(n)$, $n\in[1,q-1]$, $(n,q)=1$, the sums $\sum_{n=1}^{q-1}a(n)\chi(n)$ can be computed for all $\varphi(q)$ characters $\chi$ in $O(\varphi(q)\log q)$ time and $O(\varphi(q))$ space (via CRT decomposition of $U(\mathbb Z/q)$ and FFT incl. Bluestein for prime lengths).

Booker: for an L-function of degree $r$ with Euler product, $N(t)=\Phi(t)+S(t)$ gives the net zero count in $[t_1,t_2)$. Theorem 3.2 (integrated form): $N_\chi(t_0)$ expressed via $\frac{1}{h\pi}\big[2h+\frac{2ht_0+h^2}{2}\log\frac q\pi+2\int\Im\log\Gamma(\frac{1/2+a_\chi+it}2)dt-\ldots\big]$ with error integrals of $S_\chi$. Rumely (Thm 3.3): for $t_0>50$, $h>0$, $|\int_{t_0}^{t_0+h}S_\chi(t)dt|\le1.8397+0.1242\log\frac{q(t_0+h)}{2\pi}$; Trudgian's constants (2.17618, 0.0679955), optimised for $qt_0\approx10^8$, are noted.

Whittaker-Shannon sampling theorem and Weiss's error bound used to rigorously up-sample $\Lambda_\chi$ from coarse samples (step 5/64 of mean zero spacing about 1/5 density) to the sign-change test, with explicit tail/aliasing error bounds (Lemmas 6.3-6.7); not read in full detail.
FFT computation of $\sum a(n)\chi(n)$ over all characters mod $q$ in $O(\varphi(q)\log q)$ time.
role: Core of the large-q algorithm: all $L_\chi(s)$ computed simultaneously through Hurwitz zeta $\zeta(s,a/q)$ lattice (Lemma 4.2 Taylor expansion).

statement: For $s\notin\mathbb Z_{\le0}$, $\alpha\in(0,1]$, $|\delta|<\alpha$: Taylor/Euler-Maclaurin-type expansion of $\zeta(s,\alpha+\delta)$ about $\alpha$ (statement only skimmed).
role: Allows a precomputed lattice of $\zeta(1/2+it+c,r/D)$ to supply all $a/q$ values by interpolation.

statement: Decay/aliasing estimate for the Fourier transform of the completed L-function with parameter $\eta\in(-1,1)$, $\delta=\frac\pi2(1-|\eta|)$ (Lemma 5.6 of Booker specialised).
role: Rigorous truncation error in the small-q algorithm.

statement: Bounds for the Fourier-side gamma factors and error terms of the rigorous computation of $\hat F_{e/o}(x,\chi)$ and of $L_\chi$ on vertical lines (Lemma 5.3 gives bound on $L_\chi$); not read in detail.
role: Error control for the rigorous DFT approximation.

statement: Explicit bounds converting the discrete DFT output to guaranteed enclosures of $\Lambda_\chi(t)$ (including the Weiss band-limited error term and the final combined bound).
role: Final rigorous enclosure used for sign-change counting.

statement: For $1\le A<\infty$: $C(A)=\sup_{0\ne F\in\mathcal A}\frac1{\|F\|_1}\big(|F(0)|-A\int_{[-1,1]^c}|\hat F(t)|dt\big)$; $C(\infty)=\sup_{F\in\mathcal E}|F(0)|/\|F\|_1$ ($\mathcal E$: $\operatorname{supp}\hat F\subset[-1,1]$). $C^+(A)=\sup_{F\in\mathcal A^+}\frac1{\|F\|_1}\big(F(0)-A\int_{[-1,1]^c}(\hat F(t))_+dt\big)$ over even real continuous $F\in L^1$; $C^+(\infty)=\sup F(0)/\|F\|_1$ over even real $F\in L^1$ with $\hat F(t)\le0$ for $|t|\ge1$. $\hat F(t)=\int e^{-2\pi ixt}F(x)dx$.

(a) $A=\infty$: there is an even real extremizer $G\in\mathcal E$, $G(0)=1$, for (1.2); all extremizers are $cG$; $C(\infty)\int\operatorname{sgn}(G)F=F(0)$ for all $F\in\mathcal E$; $1.08185\ldots\le C(\infty)\le1.09769\ldots$ (Gorbachev). (b) $C(1)=2$, no extremizers. (c) For $1<A<\infty$ an even real extremizer exists and, with $c_0=1.07995\ldots$, $d_0=1.09769\ldots$, $\lambda(A)\in(0,1)$ solving $1-\frac1A=\sin\frac{\pi\lambda}2-\frac{\pi\lambda}2\cos\frac{\pi\lambda}2$: $\max\{2A-2\sqrt{A(A-1)},\frac{\pi Ac_0}2\cos\frac{\pi\lambda(A)}2\}\le C(A)\le\min\{\frac{d_0}{1-(A-2)^{-0.3}},2\}$, the first upper bound only for $2.6\le A<\infty$ (exponent 0.3 as read from the text).

(a) $A=\infty$: an extremizer $G\in\mathcal E^+$ exists and $C(\infty)\le C^+(\infty)<1.2$. (b) $C^+(1)=2$, no extremizers. (c) For $1<A<\infty$ an even real extremizer exists and $C(A)\le C^+(A)\le\min\{\frac{1.2}{1-(A-1)^{-0.222}},2\}$ (first bound for $A>1.222$); for $A=36/11$ a numerical example gives $25/21<C^+(36/11)$.

Assume RH. Let $B:=\limsup_{x\to\infty}\frac{\pi(x+\sqrt x)-\pi(x)}{\sqrt x/\log x}$ (so $1\le B\le36/11$ by PNT and Iwaniec). Then for any $\alpha\ge0$, $\inf\{c>0:\liminf_{x\to\infty}\frac{\pi(x+c\sqrt x\log x)-\pi(x)}{\sqrt x}>\alpha\}\le\frac{1+2\alpha}{C^+(B)}<\frac{21}{25}(1+2\alpha)$.

Assume RH. Then $\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{p_{n+1}-p_n}{\sqrt{p_n}\log p_n}\le\frac1{C^+(B)}<\frac{21}{25}$ (improving Dudek's $c=1$; the method cannot go below $1/2$ since $C^+\le2$). The case $\alpha=1$ gives constant $3/C^+(B)<63/25$ (vs Dudek's 3).

Assume RH. For every $x\ge4$ there is a prime in $[x,x+\frac{22}{25}\sqrt x\log x]$; equivalently $p_{n+1}-p_n\le\frac{22}{25}\sqrt{p_n}\log p_n$ for all $p_n>3$. Proved with a dilation of $H(x)=\cos2\pi x/(1-16x^2)$ and Montgomery-Vaughan's explicit Brun-Titchmarsh; for $x\le4\cdot10^{18}$ it follows from verified $p_{n+1}-p_n<\log^2p_n$.

Existence of extremizers by compactness (weak $L^2$ limits plus Fatou) for problems (1.1)-(1.4); Proposition 10: a radial extremizer exists for the Cohn-Elkies sphere-packing problem (7.1) in every dimension.

For $h$ analytic in $|\operatorname{Im}s|\le\frac12+\epsilon$ with $h(s)\ll(1+|s|)^{-(1+\delta)}$: $\sum_\rho h(\frac{\rho-1/2}{i})=h(\frac1{2i})+h(-\frac1{2i})-\frac1{2\pi}\hat h(0)\log\pi+\frac1{2\pi}\int h(u)\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Gamma'}{\Gamma}(\frac14+\frac{iu}2)du-\frac1{2\pi}\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\Lambda(n)}{\sqrt n}(\hat h(\frac{\log n}{2\pi})+\hat h(-\frac{\log n}{2\pi}))$.
role: Imported (Iwaniec-Kowalski Thm 5.12); links zeros to primes.

statement: Under RH, for $f(z)=\Delta F(\Delta z)$ with $\operatorname{supp}\hat F\subset[-N,N]$ and $2\pi\Delta N\le\log a$, applying Lemma 6 to $h(z)=f(z)a^{iz}$ gives $f(\frac1{2i})a^{1/2}+f(-\frac1{2i})a^{-1/2}\le\sum_\gamma|f(\gamma)|+\frac1{2\pi}\hat f(-\frac{\log a}{2\pi})\log\pi+\frac1{2\pi}\int f(u)a^{iu}\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Gamma'}\Gamma du+\frac1{2\pi}\sum\frac{\Lambda(n)}{\sqrt n}(\hat f(\tfrac{\log(n/a)}{2\pi})_++\hat f(-\tfrac{\log(n/a)}{2\pi})_+)$.
role: Core inequality: LHS detects a short interval with few primes; RH makes all zeros real so |f(gamma)| terms are controlled; edge primes bounded by Brun-Titchmarsh.

statement: LHS equals $\Delta F(0)(a^{1/2}+a^{-1/2})+O(\Delta^2a^{1/2})$; combining estimates for zero sum, gamma-factor and prime sum along a sequence of $x$ with few primes in $[x,x+c\sqrt x\log x]$ yields $c\le(1+2\alpha)\|F\|_1/(F(0)-B\int_{[-1,1]^c}(\hat F)_+)$.
role: Translation to extremal problem (1.3).

statement: Extremal $G$ for (1.2) satisfies $C(\infty)\int\operatorname{sgn}(G(x))F(x)dx=F(0)$ for all $F\in\mathcal E$; uniqueness uses that a nonnegative function with $\hat{}$ supported in $[-2,2]$ is the square of a function with transform supported in $[-1,1]$.
role: Optimality characterization for A=infinity.

statement: Lemma 7 gives explicit Fourier-analytic estimates for the dilated $H$ (with $\vartheta\delta=\pi/2$, $a>e^\delta$); Lemma 9 gives explicit bounds for the zero sum via $N(x)$; with Montgomery-Vaughan's explicit Brun-Titchmarsh these make all errors effective.
role: Explicit version of the prime gap bound.

statement: Assume RH. For $t$ large and $0<h\le\sqrt t$: $N(t+h)-N(t)-\dfrac h{2\pi}\log\dfrac t{2\pi}\le\Big(\dfrac12+o(1)\Big)\dfrac{\log t}{\log\log t}$; equivalently $S(t+h)-S(t)\le(\tfrac12+o(1))\frac{\log t}{\log\log t}$.
Assume RH. For $t$ sufficiently large, $|S(t)|\le\Big(\dfrac12+o(1)\Big)\dfrac{\log t}{\log\log t}$.
Assume RH. For $\gamma$ large, the multiplicity of the zero $\tfrac12+i\gamma$ satisfies $m(\gamma)\le(\tfrac12+o(1))\dfrac{\log\gamma}{\log\log\gamma}$.
Assume RH. If $\gamma<\gamma'$ are consecutive zero ordinates, $\gamma'-\gamma\le\dfrac{\pi}{\log\log\gamma}(1+o(1))$.

Guinand-Weil explicit formula: for $h$ analytic in $|\mathrm{Im}\,s|\le\tfrac12+\epsilon$, $|h(s)|\ll(1+|s|)^{-(1+\delta)}$, real on the reals, $\sum_\rho h(\tfrac{\rho-1/2}i)=h(\tfrac1{2i})+h(-\tfrac1{2i})-\tfrac1{2\pi}\hat h(0)\log\pi+\tfrac1{2\pi}\int h(u)\mathrm{Re}\tfrac{\Gamma'}{\Gamma}(\tfrac14+\tfrac{iu}2)du-\tfrac1{2\pi}\sum_{n\ge2}\tfrac{\Lambda(n)}{\sqrt n}(\hat h(\tfrac{\log n}{2\pi})+\hat h(-\tfrac{\log n}{2\pi}))$.
role: Imported (Iwaniec-Kowalski Thm 5.12, (25.10)); converts zero counting to prime sums.

statement: For $L,\delta>0$ there exist even entire $F_\pm$ with $F_-\le\chi_{[-L,L]}\le F_+$, $\int F_+\le2L+1/\delta$, $\int F_-\ge2L-1/\delta$, $F_\pm(w)\ll e^{2\pi\delta|\mathrm{Im}\,w|}$, $F_\pm(u)\ll\min(1,\delta^{-2}(|u|-L)^{-2})$ for $|u|>L$, $\hat F_\pm(x)=0$ for $|x|\ge\delta$, $\hat F_\pm(x)=\frac{\sin2\pi Lx}{\pi x}+O(1/\delta)$.
role: Selberg/Beurling-Vaaler majorant-minorant of an interval of band-limit delta; imported (Montgomery-Odlyzko, Vaaler).

statement: With $h(w)=F(w-t)$, $\delta\ge1$, $0<L\le2\sqrt t$: $\sum_\gamma F(\gamma-t)=\dfrac{\hat F(0)}{2\pi}\log\dfrac t{2\pi}+O(e^{\pi\delta})$.
role: Key estimate: prime-sum side bounded trivially by $\sum_{n\le e^{\pi\delta}}n^{-1/2}\ll e^{\pi\delta}$ using $\mathrm{supp}\,\hat F\subset[-\delta,\delta]$.

statement: Assume RH. For every $\beta>0$ and admissible $R_\beta^\pm$ (i.e. $\hat R^\pm_\beta$ supported in $[-1,1]$, $R_\beta^-\le\chi_{[-\beta,\beta]}\le R_\beta^+$): $\frac12M(R_\beta^-)\le L(\beta)\le U(\beta)\le\frac12M(R_\beta^+)$, where $M(R)=\int R(x)(1-(\sin\pi x/\pi x)^2)dx$, $U(\beta)=\limsup N(T,\beta)/N(T)$, $L(\beta)=\liminf N(T,\beta)/N(T)$; the lower bound holds under the additional assumption $N^*(T)/N(T)\to1$ (almost all zeros simple), (1.11).
hypotheses: for lower bound: almost all zeros simple

statement: For $\beta>0$ and the Beurling-Selberg functions $r_\beta^\pm$ (eqs.
