(1.15)-(1.16)): $\frac12M(r_\beta^\pm)=\beta\pm\frac12-\frac12... $ in the paper's form: $\frac12M(r^\pm_\beta)=\beta\mp\frac12... $ -- exact formula (1.17): $\tfrac12 M(r_\beta^{\pm})=\beta\pm\tfrac12-\tfrac12+\tfrac1{2\pi^2\beta}\cdots$ as printed with sine and sum terms; asymptotically $\frac12M(r_\beta^\pm)=\beta-\frac12\pm\frac12+\frac1{2\pi^2\beta}+O(\beta^{-2})$ (i.e. $\beta+\frac1{2\pi^2\beta}+O(\beta^{-2})$ for the majorant and $\beta-1+\frac1{2\pi^2\beta}+O(\beta^{-2})$ for the minorant), valid for all $\beta>0$; extends Gallagher's $\beta\in\frac12\mathbb N$ formula (1.12).

The Hilbert space $\mathcal H=B_2(\pi,\mu)$ of entire functions of exponential type $\le\pi$ with $\int|f|^2d\mu<\infty$ (norm equivalent to Paley-Wiener norm) has reproducing kernel $K(w,z)=f(w,z)+c(w)g(z)+d(w)h(z)$ with explicit $f,g,h,c,d$ (eqs. (1.19)-(1.20)); at $w=\pm1/(\pi\sqrt2)$ interpreted as a limit.

For $\beta>0$ let $\Delta(\beta)=\inf\{M(R):R\ge0\text{ admissible},R(\pm\beta)\ge1\}$. Then $\Delta(\beta)=\frac{2}{K(\beta,\beta)+|K(\beta,-\beta)|}=2\big(1-\frac{\sin2\pi\beta}{2\pi\beta}\big)+O(\beta^{-2})$ (as printed with $|\sin 2\pi\beta/2\pi\beta|$ in the discussion). Extremals: if $K(\beta,-\beta)=0$, $R(z)=K(\beta,\beta)^{-2}(c_1K(\beta,z)+c_2K(-\beta,z))\overline{(c_1K(\beta,\bar z)+c_2K(-\beta,\bar z))}$, $|c_1|=|c_2|=1$; if $K(\beta,-\beta)\ne0$, $R(z)=\frac{\big(\frac{K(\beta,-\beta)}{|K(\beta,-\beta)|}K(\beta,z)+K(-\beta,z)\big)^2}{K(\beta,\beta)+|K(\beta,-\beta)|}$-type formula as in paper (squared modulus form).

For a Hermite-Biehler function $E$ with (P1)-(P4) (bounded type, no real zeros, $E(iz)$ real entire, $A,B\notin\mathcal H(E)$) and $\beta>0$, define $\Lambda^\pm_E(\beta)=\inf/\sup M_E(R_\beta^\pm)$ over $R^\pm$ of exponential type $\le2\tau(E)$ with $R^-\le\chi_{[-\beta,\beta]}\le R^+$ ($M_E(R)=\int R|E|^{-2}dx$). Then: if $\beta\in\{a_i\}$ (zeros of $A$): $\Lambda^+_E(\beta)=\sum_{A(\xi)=0,|\xi|\le\beta}1/K(\xi,\xi)$, $\Lambda^-_E(\beta)=\sum_{A(\xi)=0,|\xi|<\beta}1/K(\xi,\xi)$; same with $B$ if $\beta\in\{b_i\}$; if $b_k<\beta<a_{k+1}$: $\Lambda^\pm_E(\beta)$ given by $\sum(\xi^2+\gamma_\beta^2)/K_\beta(\xi,\xi)$ over zeros of $A_\beta$ with $|\xi|\le\beta$ (resp. $<\beta$), $\gamma_\beta=\beta B(\beta)/A(\beta)$, $E_\beta(z)=E(z)(\gamma_\beta-iz)$; case $a_k<\beta<b_k$ analogously with $B_\beta$, $\gamma_\beta=-\beta A(\beta)/B(\beta)$.
Assume RH and (1.11). Then $U(\beta)-L(\beta)\le\frac1{K(\beta,\beta)+|K(\beta,-\beta)|}=1-\frac{\sin2\pi\beta}{2\pi\beta}+O(\beta^{-2})$.

Assume RH and (1.11). Then $N(T,0.606894)\gg N(T)$ (i.e. a positive proportion of zeros have a neighbour within $0.606894$ times the mean spacing; implies infinitely often consecutive gap $<$ mean spacing). Improves Montgomery's 0.6695... (stated 0.68) and Goldston-Gonek-Ozluk-Snyder's 0.6072....

Assume RH. For $\beta=\beta(T)>0$ with $\beta\sqrt{\log\log T}/\log T\to0$ (as printed: $(\log\log T/\log T)^{1/2}$ condition): $\frac12M(r_\beta^-)+\frac12(1-N^*(T)/N(T))+o(1)\le N(T,\beta)/N(T)\le\frac12M(r_\beta^+)+\frac12(1-N^*(T)/N(T))+o(1)$ (Theorem 8, printed form; $N^*(T)=\sum_{0<\gamma\le T}m_\gamma$). Corollary 9 (RH only, using Montgomery's $N^*(T)\le(4/3+o(1))N(T)$): $\beta-\frac76+\frac1{2\pi^2\beta}+O(\beta^{-2})+o(1)\le N(T,\beta)/N(T)\le\beta+\frac1{2\pi^2\beta}+O(\beta^{-2})+o(1)$.

Assume GRH for Dirichlet L-functions, $\varepsilon>0$. For $\beta>0$: $\limsup_{Q\to\infty}N_\Phi(Q,\beta)/N_\Phi(Q)\le\beta-\frac14+\varepsilon+\frac1{2\pi^2\beta}+O(\beta^{-2})$; if in addition $N^*_\Phi(Q)\sim N_\Phi(Q)$, then $\liminf\ge\beta-\frac34-\varepsilon+\frac1{2\pi^2\beta}+O(\beta^{-2})$ (family-pair-correlation analogue for primitive Dirichlet L-functions, using Chandee-Lee-Liu-Radziwill large sieve evaluation of the q-analogue of Montgomery's $F(\alpha)$).
Uncertainty-principle (Donoho-Stark/Folland-Sitaram type) inequality for $f\in L^2$, $\|f\|_2=1$ and measurable sets $T,W$ (statement as printed in Section 3).
role: Shows that the measure $\mu$ and Lebesgue measure give equivalent norms on exponential-type-$\le\pi$ functions, so $\mathcal H=B_2(\pi,\mu)$ is a Hilbert space.

statement: Entire $f\in B_2(\pi)$ iff $f\in B_2(\pi,\mu)$, with comparable norms ($c>0$ constant).
role: Used to show $A,B\notin\mathcal H(E)$ (property P4) and the identification $\mathcal H=\mathcal H(E)$.

statement: Abstract Hilbert space lemma (statement as printed in Section 3, concerning minimization over a Hilbert space with given vectors $v_1,v_2$).
role: Abstract two-point (two-delta) minimization used to derive Theorem 4 from the reproducing kernel.

statement: Let $R\ge0$ be admissible with $R(0)\ge1$. Then $M(R)\ge\ldots$ (one-delta bound: lower bound for the proportion of simple zeros; exact value as in paper).
role: One-delta analogue; gives $N^*(T)/N(T)$ bounds referenced in the Remark after Corollary 9.

statement: Lemma 16: an entire $F$ of exponential type $\le2\tau(E)$ with $F\ge0$ on $\mathbb R$ and a suitable integrability condition factors as $|G|^2$ with $G\in\mathcal H(E)$-type representation (de Branges / Krein factorization used for the extremal problem). Lemma 15 concerns an interpolation property for $\beta\in$ ... (statement partly read).
role: Reduction of the majorant/minorant extremal problem to quadrature (Gaussian-type) formulas at zeros of A or B, giving the sums in Theorem 5.

statement: Assume RH and fix $A>1$. As $T\to\infty$, a lower-bound asymptotic for a second moment of Montgomery's pair-correlation weight (as printed in Section 5); used to improve Montgomery's small-gap threshold in Theorem 7.
role: Second Montgomery-formula application with a different test function; feeds Theorem 7.

statement: The entire function $E(z)=L(i,z)/L(i,i)^{1/2}$ defined by (1.26) satisfies the Hermite-Biehler property (1.22) and $L(w,z)=E(z)E^*(w)-E^*(z)E(w)$ (1.27).
role: Identifies the Hilbert space $B_2(\pi,\mu)$ with a de Branges space $\mathcal H(E)$, key identity (1.28).

label_in_source: Part I, ch. III-IV (stated aim, nos. 2, 42)
statement: \zeta(s) has no root of the form \rho=1+\beta i (\beta real, \beta\ne0); the proof is by contradiction: supposing such a root, the fundamental equation (no. 28/31) gives a function of y represented in two incompatible ways as a sum 'L+P' (a limit plus an almost-periodic / purely oscillatory part), contradicting uniqueness theorems II-V.
hypotheses: Riemann zeta function, continuation via formula (2) of no. 3
location: Part I, no. 2 (statement of object), nos. 31-42 (L+P theorems), proof in ch. III

statement: From the fundamental equation with y\to\infty (the series over the zeros tends to zero because \Re(\rho-1)<0 for all zeros): \sum_{p}\ldots\int\ldots=y-\ldots+\epsilon_y and (eq.(9)) \int^y\!\sum_{p<x}\log p\,\frac{dx}{x}-type identity; changing y to (1+k)y and subtracting yields that the ratio \frac1y\sum_{p\le y}\log p tends to 1 (equivalent of Tchebycheff function \theta(y)\sim y), and hence \pi(x)\sim x/\log x (prime number theorem; the PNT statement itself I did not locate verbatim in the OCR).
hypotheses: no zeros of zeta on Re s=1 (ch. III)
location: Part I ch. IV, nos. 55-56 (pp. ~62-66 of the offprint), eq.(5)-(9)

statement: Functions \int\theta(x)e^{\ldots}x^{s}dx with \theta continuous bounded as x\to\infty and a>0 are entire of genus at most 1 in s (Theorem II, no. 16); consequently the auxiliary functions \varphi_1,\varphi_2 built from \psi_1(a,x)=\sum_n e^{-\pi(n+a)^2 x} are entire of genus 1, which supplies the zero-sum representation of \zeta'/\zeta.

No Dirichlet L-function L(s,\chi) vanishes on \Re s=1 (Part II ch. IV §2 'Aucune fonction L(s,\chi) ne s'annule pour s=1+beta i'), whence the theorem of Dirichlet on primes in arithmetic progressions is re-proved (ch. IV §3), and the primes \equiv N (mod M) have asymptotic density 1/\varphi(M) (asymptotic form in ch. V).
location: Part II ch. IV §§2-3, ch. V (headings seen at OCR lines 5055, 5206); statements not read in detail

statement: Title-level: primes representable by a quadratic form of negative determinant have the asymptotic distribution expected (Part III); positive determinant in Part IV (1898). Exact statements not read.
location: Part III (and Part IV of 1898 in the same bound volume)

statement: A function \Phi(y)=L(y)+P(y) with L\to0 (limit part) and P purely periodic/almost periodic is uniquely decomposed; operations (multiplication by cos, change of y to ky, summation of the associated series) preserve the form and the periodic part carries the same trigonometric lines with the same coefficients (Theorems III-V).
role: Replaces the 3-4-1 positivity argument by a uniqueness-of-almost-periodic-part argument: two contradictory expressions in the form L+P (from real and imaginary parts of the fundamental equation, nos. 34-42) refute \rho=1+\beta i

statement: For \Re\alpha>1: an exact identity expressing \frac{\zeta'}{\zeta}-weighted sums over primes via the sum over zeros \rho of terms e^{\rho y}/(\ldots), a constant, three rapidly decaying terms, and periodic terms \sum a_n\cos(\alpha_n y)+b_n\sin(\alpha_n y) arising from the pole at s=1 and zeros on \Re s=1.
role: Source of the representation to which L+P theorems are applied

statement: If \Re(\alpha+k_n) stays between two positive bounds, \sum|\cdot| converges and a further series converges, then the representation by partial fractions extends (general convergence theorem enabling the zero-sum expansion).
role: Justifies the infinite partial-fraction sum for the logarithmic derivative

statement: More than five-twelfths of the non-trivial zeros of $\zeta(s)$ lie on the critical line, i.e. $\kappa>5/12$. Proved with $d=1$, $K=3$, $\theta=4/7-\epsilon$, $R=1.3036$ and explicit polynomials $P_1,P_2,P_3,Q$ (Sec. 8), giving $\kappa\ge0.417293962$; and $\kappa^*\ge0.407511457$ for the proportion of simple zeros on the line (linear $Q$, $R=1.1167$).

Let $\alpha,\beta\ll L^{-1}$, $\psi_1=\sum_{n\le N}a_nn^{-s}$, $\psi_2=\sum_{n\le N}b_nn^{-s}$, $N=T^\theta$. Then $I(\alpha,\beta)=\int\zeta(\tfrac12+\alpha+it)\zeta(\tfrac12+\beta-it)\psi_1\psi_2(\tfrac12+it)\Phi(t/T)dt=\sum_{d,e\le N}\frac{a_db_e(d,e)^{\alpha+\beta}}{[d,e]d^\alpha e^\beta}\int(\zeta(1+\alpha+\beta)+\zeta(1-\alpha-\beta)(\frac{2\pi de}{t(d,e)^2})^{\alpha+\beta})\Phi(t/T)dt+O(E)$ with $E=T^{3/20}N^{33/20}+N^{1/2}T^{1/2+\epsilon}$ if $a_n\ll n^\epsilon$ (as read); $E=T^\epsilon(N^{11/6}+N^{11/12}T^{1/2})$ if $a_n=\mu^2(n)(\mu*\Lambda^{*k_1}_1*\cdots*\Lambda^{*k_D}_D)(n)$; $E=T^\epsilon(N^{7/4}+N^{7/8}T^{1/2})$ if $a_n=(\mu*\Lambda^{*k_1}_1*\cdots*\Lambda^{*k_D}_D)(n)$ with no square-free restriction. Hence $\theta<4/7$ for the whole family.

Feng's unproved claim that terms with $\mu^2(n)=0$ contribute only a lower-order term to the mean value integral is proved in the case $K=2$ (other $K$ asserted to work out similarly) by splitting $a_d=b_d+c_d$ with $b_d$ the Feng coefficient (sum over distinct primes $q_1\ne q_2|d$) and showing the remainder $c_d$ contributes lower order.

For the general mollifier coefficients $a_d,b_e$ of (7.1),(7.2) built from $(\mu*\Lambda^{*\ell_1}*\cdots)$ with polynomials $P_{d,\ell_d}$, the mollified twisted moment equals $\sum_{i,j}\frac{p_{d,\ell_d,i}p_{d,\bar\ell_d,j}\,i!\,j!}{(\log N)^{i+j}}\frac1{(2\pi i)^2}\iint\frac{1}{(\log N)^{\sum r_\ell\ell+\sum\bar r_{\bar\ell}\bar\ell}}\Big[\frac1{(2\pi i)^{L_d+\bar L_d}}\oint\oint M_{\alpha,\beta}(z,w;s,u)DZ\,DW-T^{-\alpha-\beta}\oint\oint M_{-\beta,-\alpha}(z,w;s,u)DZ\,DW\Big]\frac{ds\,du}{s^{i+1}u^{j+1}}+O(T^{1-\epsilon})$ (up to the normalization of the integral sign as printed), where $M_{\alpha,\beta}$ is a ratio of products of shifted zeta functions times an arithmetical factor $A_{\alpha,\beta}$ with $A(0,0;\beta,\alpha)=M(0,0;\beta,\alpha)=1$ (7.6)-(7.7).

Conrey-Farmer-Zirnbauer ratios conjecture for $R(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta)=\int\frac{\zeta(s+\alpha)\zeta(1-s+\beta)}{\zeta(s+\gamma)\zeta(1-s+\delta)}dt$ with main term $\frac{\zeta(1+\alpha+\beta)\zeta(1+\gamma+\delta)}{\zeta(1+\alpha+\delta)\zeta(1+\beta+\gamma)}A(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta)$ plus the $(t/2\pi)^{-\alpha-\beta}$ swapped term and error $O(T^{1/2+\epsilon})$; the Conrey-Snaith derivation is for $\int\zeta'/\zeta\cdot\zeta'/\zeta$. Used only as the template for the rigorous contour-integral combinatorics.

$M(s,d)=1/(\zeta(s)+\lambda_1\zeta'/L+\cdots+\lambda_d\zeta^{(d)}/L^d)$; for $d=1$, $M(s,1)=\sum_k\frac1{\log^kT}\sum_n\frac{(\mu*\Lambda^{*k})(n)}{n^s}$; for square-free $n$, $(\mu*\Lambda^{*k})(n)=(-1)^k\mu(n)\sum_{p_1\cdots p_k|n}\log p_1\cdots\log p_k$ (Feng's formula); general coefficients are organized by Bell-polynomial combinatorics (Secs. 3.4-3.5; e.g. 250 diagrams in one case).
role: Defines the new family of mollifier coefficients.

statement: Main terms are unchanged from Pratt-Robles; only error terms change. To separate $d$ from $n_1$ in $(\mu*\Lambda^{*\ell_1}*\cdots)(dn_1)$, factor $n_1\to hn_1$ with $h|d^\infty$ and $n_1$ coprime to $d$, so $\mu^2$ is no longer needed; then Vaughan/Heath-Brown identities and additivity of the logarithm yield length $4/7$.
role: Key step improving 6/11 to 4/7.

statement: Technical evaluations of sums over $\ell_r$, truncation parameters and arithmetic-factor identities supporting the residue/contour computation of Theorem 7.1 (statements in Sec. 7; not read in detail).
role: Support the main-term evaluation of Theorem 7.1.

statement: $\kappa\ge0.4128$, where $\kappa=\liminf_{T\to\infty}N_0(T)/N(T)$ (at least 41.28% of zeros of zeta lie on the critical line; multiplicity counted).

Let $L=\log T$, $R>0$, $\theta<4/7$, $\theta_1<1/2$, $I\ge2$, $P_1(0)=0,P_1(1)=1$, $P_l(0)=0$ ($l\ge2$) real polynomials, $Q$ real with $Q(0)=1$, $Q'(x)=Q'(1-x)$. Then $\kappa\ge1-\frac1R\log\Big(\int_0^1Q(-\frac d{da})Q(-\frac d{db})\frac{F(\theta,\theta_1,b,a,t)-e^{-a-b}F(\theta,\theta_1,-a,-b,t)}{\theta_1(a+b)}\Big|_{a=b=-R}dt+\int_1^{\theta/\theta_1}Q(-\frac d{da})Q(-\frac d{db})\frac{F^*(\theta,\theta_1,b,a,t)-e^{-a-b}F^*(\theta,\theta_1,-a,-b,t)}{\theta_1(a+b)}\Big|_{a=b=-R}dt\Big)$, with $F,F^*$ given by (4.48),(4.49).

$B(s)=\sum_{j\le y}a_jj^{-s-R/L}$, $y=T^\theta$; for $y_1<j\le y$, $a_j=\mu(j)P_1(\frac{\log y/j}{\log y})$; for $j\le y_1=T^{\theta_1}$, $a_j=\mu(j)\big[P_1(\frac{\log y/j}{\log y})+\sum_{p_1p_2|j}\frac{\log p_1\log p_2}{\log^2y_1}P_2(\frac{\log y_1/j}{\log y_1})+\sum_{p_1p_2p_3|j}\frac{\log p_1\log p_2\log p_3}{\log^3y_1}P_3(\cdot)+\dots+\sum_{p_1\cdots p_I|j}\frac{\prod\log p_i}{\log^Iy_1}P_I(\cdot)\big]$.
If Lemma 2 (hence Theorem 2) were valid for every $\theta=\theta_1<1$ (the 'theta=1 conjecture'), then $\kappa\ge0.6107$ (with $\theta=\theta_1=1-\varepsilon$, $R=0.7721$, $I=3$).

Under the standard Levinson-Conrey reduction (1.1), Littlewood's lemma and $a_j\ll1,a_1=1$: $\kappa\ge1-\frac1R\log\Big(\frac1T\int_1^T|BV(\sigma_0+it)|^2dt\Big)+o(1)$, $\sigma_0=\frac12-\frac RL$, $V(s)=Q(-\frac1L\frac d{ds})\zeta(s)$, with the mollifier coefficients (2.3)-(2.4).
role: Reduction to a mean-value integral

statement: With $\Delta=T^{1-\delta}$, $0<\delta<1$, $g(\alpha,\beta,w)=\frac1{i\Delta\pi}\int_{(1/2)}e^{((s-s_0)/\Delta)^2}\zeta(s+\alpha)\zeta(1-s+\beta)B(s)B(1-s)ds$ and $\Sigma(\alpha,\beta)=\sum_{h,k\le y}\frac{a_ha_k}{h^{1+\alpha}k^{1+\beta}}(h,k)^{1+\alpha+\beta}$: $g(\alpha,\beta,w)=\frac{\Sigma(\beta,\alpha)-e^{-(\alpha+\beta)L}\Sigma(-\alpha,-\beta)}{\alpha+\beta}+o_\delta(1)$ uniformly, for $y\le T^{4/7-\varepsilon}$ and bounded $a_j\ll1$.
role: Imported from Conrey 1989 (uses Deshouillers-Iwaniec Kloosterman sum bounds); reduces the whole mean-value problem to the arithmetic quadratic form Sigma(alpha,beta)

statement: For real polynomial $P$ with $P(0)=0$: $S=\sum_{n\le y/j,(n,j)=1}\frac{\mu(n)}{n^{1+\alpha}}P(\frac{\log y/nj}{\log y})=\frac1{F(j,1+\alpha)}\big(\alpha P(\frac{\log y/j}{\log y})+\frac1{\log y}P'(\frac{\log y/j}{\log y})\big)+O\big(\frac{(\log\log y)^2F_1(j,1-2\delta)}{\log^2y}\big)+\dots$ uniformly for $j\le y$, $\alpha\ll1/\log y$.
role: Evaluates the Mobius sums inside E_alpha(j) with the main polynomial P_1

statement: Mertens' theorem (L4), Levinson's Lemmas 5 and 6, and lemmas L7-L9 on sums over m, square-free j and prime tuples with weights f(log/log y).
role: Technical tools for evaluating E_alpha(j) (Sec 3) and Sigma(alpha,beta) (Sec 4); not read in detail

statement: Selberg's minimization: $\sum_{m,n\le y}\frac{a_ma_n}{mn}(m,n)\ge1/\sum_{n\le y}\frac{\mu^2(n)}{\varphi(n)}=\frac{1+o(1)}{\log y}$ for $a_1=1$, equality at $a_n=\mu(n)\frac{nL(y/n;n)}{\varphi(n)L(y;1)}\approx\mu(n)\frac{\log y/n}{\log y}$.
role: Explains the Levinson mollifier as minimization of a quadratic form and motivates adding prime-sum terms to mollify zeta+zeta'/log T through the expansion 1/(zeta+zeta'/L)=1/zeta - zeta'/(zeta^2 L)+...

statement: The first $1{,}500{,}000{,}001$ zeros $\sigma+it$ with $0<t<545{,}439{,}823.215$ all have $\sigma=1/2$ and are simple (RH verified in this rectangle).
conditional_on: correctness of FORTRAN/COMPASS programs on CDC Cyber 175/750 and Cyber 205, and of the extended error analysis

statement: For $t=2\pi\tau$ in $(3.5\times10^7,5.6\times10^8)$ (zero #81,000,000 to #1,500,000,000): $|\tilde Z(t)-Z(t)|<3\times10^{-7}\tau^{-1/4}$ (method A) and $<5.5\times10^{-3}\tau^{-5/4}$ (method B); safe constant bounds $3\times10^{-5}$, $2.1\times10^{-11}$; the program used $10^{-4}$ and $2.5\times10^{-7}$. (Exponents as extracted from OCR; sign/exponent forms unverified.) Not a single Gram point failed method B.
hypotheses: truncated arithmetic with eps_s=2^{-46}, eps_d=2^{-93} on the Cyber 205

statement: Using Theorem 3.2 of Brent [1], five Gram blocks of lengths 1,1,2,1,1 in $[g_{1,500,000,000},g_{1,500,000,006})$ all satisfy Rosser's rule, giving $N(g_{1.5\cdot10^9})$ upper bound and so $H(1{,}500{,}000{,}001)$.

Exact counts on $[g_0,g_{1.5\cdot10^9})$: average Gram block length 1.2089; 1,036,704,539 blocks of length 1; 3055 exceptions to Rosser's rule (2973 of length 2, 82 of length 3), the missing two zeros always in an adjacent Gram block.

Closest pair of zeros observed lies in $B_{1,048,449,112}$ with $(t_{n+1}-t_n)\log t_n/2\pi=0.00034$; first Gram block of length 9 is $B_{542,964,969}$; maxima of |S| near exceptions are about 2.0-2.2.

For q sufficiently large, $\prod_{\chi \bmod q}L(s,\chi)$ has at most one zero in $\sigma\ge 1-\frac{0.348}{\log q},\ |t|\le 1$; such a zero is real, simple, and belongs to a non-principal real character.

For q large, $\prod_\chi L(s,\chi)$ has at most 2 zeros (with multiplicity) in $\sigma\ge1-\frac{0.696}{\log q},|t|\le1$; moreover there is a character $\chi_1$ such that $L(s,\chi)\ne0$ for $\sigma\ge 1-\frac{0.702}{\log q},|t|\le1$ for all $\chi\ne\chi_1,\bar\chi_1$.

For q large there are $\chi_1,\chi_2$ such that $L(s,\chi)\ne0$ for $\sigma\ge1-\frac{0.857}{\log q},|t|\le1$ for all $\chi\notin\{\chi_1,\bar\chi_1,\chi_2,\bar\chi_2\}$. (Author notes 0.857 is $6/7+o(1)$.)

Let $\varepsilon>0$, $\chi$ real non-principal mod q with $L(1-\lambda/\log q,\chi)=0$, $\lambda\le0.348$. For q large, $\prod_\chi L(s,\chi)$ has only the zero $s=1-\lambda/\log q$ in $\sigma\ge1-\min\{(\tfrac{12}{11}-\varepsilon)\log\lambda^{-1},\tfrac13\log\log\log q\}/\log q$ (with $|t|\le 1$ as in the preceding theorems; the exact range of $t$ was not re-verified in the extracted text).
hypotheses: q sufficiently large depending on epsilon

statement: Let $N(\lambda)$ be the number of L-functions mod q with a zero in $\sigma\ge1-\lambda/\log q,|t|\le1$. For $\varepsilon>0$, q large, $\lambda\le\frac13\log\log\log q$: $N(\lambda)\le(1+\varepsilon)\frac{67}{6\lambda}\big(e^{73\lambda/30}-e^{16\lambda/15}\big)$.
$P(a,q)\ll q^{5.5}$ for $(a,q)=1$, with effectively computable implied constant (improving 13.5 of Chen-Liu).

Burgess bounds $\sum_{N<n\le N+H}\chi(n)\ll q^{(k+1)/(4k^2)+\varepsilon}H^{1-1/k}$ (k=2,3, or any k if q cube-free), extended to non-cube-free moduli via Lemma 2.3 (factor v = cube-full part) and Lemma 2.4 (dependence on order of chi).
role: Imports Burgess into zero-free region analysis; yields the smaller constant phi in Lemma 2.5 / 3.1.

statement: For non-principal chi mod q and phi as in Lemma 2.5, $-\Re\frac{L'}{L}(s,\chi)\le-\sum_{|1+it-\rho|\le\delta}\Re\frac1{s-\rho}+(\frac{\phi}{2}+\varepsilon)\log q$ uniformly for $1+\frac1{L\log L}\le\sigma\le1+\frac{\log L}{L}$, $|t|\le L=\log q$, q large.
role: Replaces the 1/2 L term in the standard inequality (3.2) (and Stechkin's 0.2764) by phi/2 with phi=1/6 or 1/8 via Burgess; discarding only nearby zeros.

statement: For q large there is an integer $L'\le\frac{3}{10}...$ (extracted text garbled: some $\mathcal L\le \frac{4}{5}$-type bound on an auxiliary height parameter) such that no $L(s,\chi)$, $\chi$ mod q, vanishes in $1-\frac{\log\log\mathcal L}{3\mathcal L}\le\sigma\le1,\ \mathcal L<|t|\le10\mathcal L$.
role: Pigeonhole via Jutila's density bound $\sum_\chi N(\sigma,T,\chi)\ll_\varepsilon (qT)^{(2+\varepsilon)(1-\sigma)}$ to clear a window of heights; imports Jutila.

statement: Positivity inequalities for test function f (conditions 1,2) with F its transform: e.g. Lemma 6.2: $F(-\lambda_1)-F(0)-F(\lambda_2-\lambda_1)+f(0)(\psi+\varepsilon)\ge0$; Lemma 6.3 (chi_1, rho_1 real): $2F(-\lambda_0)-2F(\lambda_1-\lambda_0)-F(0)+f(0)(\tfrac14+\varepsilon)\ge0$.
role: Generalized Stechkin/Landau-type positivity ($1+\chi(n)$ times $1+\Re\chi(n)n^{-i\gamma'}$) arguments that bound distance between zeros; the constants theorems 1-4 come from optimizing f.

statement: Explicit optimal choice of f (calculus of variations) in several parameter regimes theta in (0,pi/2), =0 limit, hyperbolic, and (pi/2,pi).
role: Makes the optimization of the test function explicit; reduces constants to numerical computation.

statement: For chi_1, rho_1, rho_0 real: $\lambda_0\ge2.427\ldots$ (Pintz obtains 4+o(1) by a different method).
role: Quantitative Deuring-Heilbronn repulsion between the exceptional zero and next real zero.

statement: If q sufficiently large then $\lambda_3\ge\frac67-\varepsilon$.
role: Source of the 6/7 behind Theorem 3's 0.857.

statement: For $\lambda_1\ge0.384$ a bound for $K-2\sum_{\chi\ne\chi_0}\sum_{\rho}|F((1-\rho)L)|$ in terms of zero-density counts $N_0(\Lambda_r)$ and constants C(.), used with L=5.5, K=0.3.
role: Final numerical verification step in the Linnik-constant argument: the exponent 5.5 appears as the parameter L of the argument.

statement: Assume RH and the Generalized Lindel\"of Hypothesis (GLH: $L(\sigma+it,\chi)\ll_\epsilon (q(|t|+1))^\epsilon$ for $\sigma\ge 1/2$, $\chi$ mod $q$). Then $C_s>19/27$ and $C_d>5/6+1/81$ (the latter read from garbled OCR; reconstruct from source before citing).
hypotheses: GLH (used via sixth-moment bound for Dirichlet L-functions)

statement: Let $B(s)=\sum_{k\le y} b(k)k^{-s}$, $y=T^{v}$, $v<1/2$, $b(k)=\mu(k)P(\log(y/k)/\log y)$, $P$ real polynomial with $P(0)=0,P(1)=1$. Under GLH, $S_1=\sum_{\gamma\le T}B\zeta'(\rho)\sim(1/2+v)\int_0^1P\,dx\cdot \frac{T L^2}{2\pi}$ and $S_2=\sum_{\gamma\le T}B\zeta'(\rho)B\zeta'(1-\rho)\sim\lambda\frac{TL^3}{2\pi}$ with $\lambda=\frac13+v\left(\int_0^1P\right)^2... $ (exact form (2.7) garbled in OCR: involves $v$, $\int P$, $\int P^2$ and $\frac{1}{12 v}\int P'^2$), where $L=\log(T/2\pi)$.

Cauchy-Schwarz $\left|\sum_{\gamma\le T}B\zeta'(\rho)\right|^2\le N_s(T)\sum|B\zeta'(\rho)|^2$ together with RH ($S_2=\sum|B\zeta'(\rho)|^2$) gives $N_s/N\ge |S_1|^2/(N\cdot S_2)$; optimal $P(x)=-vx^2+(1+v)x$; letting $v\to1/2$ gives $S_1\sim\frac{19}{24}N L$-normalization and $S_2\sim\frac{57}{64}NL$-normalization, hence ratio $19/27$.

Mean values $M_1,M_2$ of $\int|B F(1/2+it)|^2dt$ (with $F$ built from $\zeta$-derivative combinations, via Conrey's earlier machinery) are evaluated for $v<1/2$ (remark: valid for $v<4/7$ by Conrey [4], Levinson-type, 'two-fifths' mollifier work).
Averaging over all $t$ instead of zero ordinates suggests the method would give 3/4 of zeros simple (Levinson: $\int|GB|^2\sim\frac43TL^2$), but the zero-ordinate average differs slightly.
Stationary-phase evaluation of $\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{c+i}^{c+iT}\chi(1-s)r^{-s}ds$: equals $e(-r)+E(r,c)$ for $r\le T/2\pi$, and $E(r,c)$ otherwise, with $E\ll T^{c-1/2}\cdot$(explicit factor).
role: Gonek's lemma converting contour integrals with $\chi(1-s)$ into additive-character sums $e(-m/k)$

statement: Dirichlet-series version of Lemma 1 for $A(s)=\sum a(n)n^{-s}$, giving $I_n=M_n+E_n$ with $E_n\ll T^{1/2}yL^7$ and $M_n=\sum_{k\le y}\sum_{m\le kT/2\pi}a_n(m)b(k)k^{-1}e(-m/k)$.
role: Reduction of $I_1,I_2$ to sums with additive characters

statement: Perron's formula (standard).
role: Handling the m-sum with analytic continuation of generating function $A_n(s;w,d)$

statement: Small conductors $q$: $A_n(s;w,d)$ continued to the left of $\sigma=1$ via $L$-function factors; contribution negligible for $q>1$.
role: Shows only principal character contributes to main term

statement: Large q: large sieve estimates with a Vaughan-type identity $A_n=H_n+I_n$ (parameters $u=x^2$, $v=T^{1/2}$) to bound sums over primitive characters.
role: Uses GLH-type sixth-moment bounds; the technical heart

statement: Main-term evaluation: only $q=1$ (principal character, $\tau(\chi_0)=\mu(K)$) contributes, replacing $e(-m/k)$ by $\mu(K)/\varphi(K)$; uses $R_j(0)=R_j'(0)=0$ and a Conrey Lemma-10-style sum; yields the closed form for $\lambda$ in (2.7). Credited to a referee's simplification.
role: Produces S_2 asymptotic

statement: For all $x\ge2$: $|\psi(x)-x|\le9.39\,x(\log x)^{1.515}\exp(-0.8274\sqrt{\log x})$. More generally for each row (X,A,B,C,eps_0) of Table 1, $|\psi(x)-x|\le Ax(\log x)^B\exp(-C\sqrt{\log x})$ and $|\psi(x)-x|\le\epsilon_0x$ for all $\log x\ge X$ (e.g. X=3000: A=8.86, B=1.514, C=0.8288, eps_0=3.14e-14; X=1e10: A=45.17, B=1.501, C=1.0903).
For (X,A,B,C) from Table 1 and A_1=A+0.01: $|\theta(x)-x|\le A_1x(\log x)^B\exp(-C\sqrt{\log x})$ for $\log x\ge X$.
For all $x\ge2$: $|\pi(x)-\mathrm{li}(x)|\le9.59\,x(\log x)^{0.515}\exp(-0.8274\sqrt{\log x})$.

For x>=23 (Ford's Vinogradov-Korobov region): $|\psi(x)-x|\le0.026x(\log x)^{1.801}\exp(-0.1853\log^{3/5}x(\log\log x)^{-1/5})$; $|\theta(x)-x|\le0.027\cdots$; and (stated as |pi(x)-x|, evidently li(x) intended) $\le0.028x(\log x)^{0.801}\exp(\cdots)$. Asymptotically better than Thm 1.1 but worse for exp(59)<=x<=exp(2.8e10).
Ramanujan's inequality $\pi^2(x)<\frac{ex}{\log x}\pi(x/e)$ holds for all x>=exp(3361) (improving exp(3915) of Platt-Trudgian); conjecturally for x>=38,358,837,683.
Imported: if zeta(beta+it)=0 with |t|<=H=3 000 175 332 800 and 0<beta<1 then beta=1/2 (Platt-Trudgian 2021 RH verification).
role: Finite verification height; used for small zeros and in Buthe-type explicit bounds.

statement: For max{50,log x}<T/1.8<(x^{1/35}-2)/4 and x>=exp(1000): $\frac{|\psi(x)-x|}{x}\le\sum_{|\Im\rho|\le T}\frac{x^{\Re\rho-1}}{|\Im\rho|}+\frac{4.3128}{T}\log^{0.6}x$ (from Cully-Hugill-Johnston explicit Riemann-von Mangoldt, Table 5, T* in [T/1.8,T]).
role: Explicit truncated explicit formula with controlled error.

statement: Zero-density: N(sigma,T)<=C_1(sigma)T^{8(1-sigma)/3}log^{5-2sigma}T+C_2(sigma)log^2T for tabulated sigma (Table 3, Appendix B), recomputed from Kadiri-Lumley-Ng using Hiary-corrected |zeta(1/2+it)|<=0.77 t^{1/6} log t (t>=3) and the new RH height.
role: Controls zeros with real part >sigma (the dominant contribution).

statement: Zero-free regions: classical beta<1-1/(R_0 log|t|), R_0=5.5666305 (Mossinghoff-Trudgian, |t|>=2); Ford-type improved region for |t|>=5.45e8; simplified region beta>=1-nu_2(t), nu_2=(1/(3.359 log|t|))(1-8.02 loglog|t|/log|t|) for |t|>=3; Vinogradov-Korobov nu_3=1/(c log^{2/3}|t|(loglog|t|)^{1/3}), c=57.54; nu=max(nu_1,nu_2,nu_3) with transitions exp(91.2), exp(54563).
role: Zero-free regions used in bounding the sum over zeros with Re rho>sigma.

statement: For T>=4 pi e: $\frac1{4\pi}\log^2\frac T{2\pi}-0.9321\le\sum_{0<\Im\rho\le T}\frac1{\Im\rho}\le\frac1{4\pi}\log^2\frac T{2\pi}$.
role: Bounds the contribution of zeros with Re rho<=sigma.

statement: Buthe-type bounds: |psi(x)-x|<sqrt(x)log^2 x/(8 pi) for 59<x<=2.169e25 (similarly theta, pi); |psi(x)-x|/x<=1.570e-12 for x>=exp(2000).
role: Cover small x ranges (Sec 3.1).

statement: If $|\zeta(\sigma+it)|\le A|t|^{B(1-\sigma)^{3/2}}\log^{2/3}|t|$ ($|t|\ge3$, $1/2\le\sigma\le1$) holds with constant B, then for $|t|$ large, $\zeta(\beta+it)\ne0$ when $1-\beta\le \dfrac{0.05507B^{-2/3}}{(\log|t|)^{2/3}(\log\log|t|)^{1/3}}$.
conditional_on: (1.2); with B=4.45 (Ford's companion paper) gives c=1/49.13

statement: Suppose (1.2) holds with $0<B<10$, $A\ge1$, $T_0\ge e^{30000}$, $\log T_0/\log\log T_0\ge1740/B$ (as printed), and all zeros $\beta+it$ with $T_0-1\le t\le T_0$ satisfy $1-\beta\ge M_1B^{-2/3}(\log t)^{-2/3}(\log\log t)^{-1/3}$, where $M_1=\min\{0.05507,\,0.1652/(2.9997+\max_{t\ge T_0}X(t)/\log\log t)\}$ and $X(t)=1.1582\log A+0.8332+0.234\log(B/\log\log t)+(1.239B^{-4/3}-2.065B^{-1/3})(\log\log t/\log t)^{1/3}$. Then the same bound holds for all zeros with $t\ge T_0$.

kind: theorem (uses RH-verification to height 5.45e8 and Cheng-Graham-type bound (1.6))
statement: With $T_0=5.45\times10^8$, $J(t)=\min(\tfrac14\log t+1.8521,\tfrac16\log t+\log\log t+\log3)$, $\zeta(\beta+it)\ne0$ for $t\ge T_0$ and $1-\beta\le\frac{0.04962-c_6(t)}{J(t)+0.155\log\log t+0.675}$, with $c_6(t)$ given by (1.8)-(9.9).
hypotheses: bound (1.6) $|\zeta(1/2+it)|\le\min(6t^{1/4}+57,3t^{1/6}\log t)$; per footnote the 3t^{1/6}log t proof of [2] is flawed (Lemma 3 false), corrected via Hiary-Patel-Yang

statement: $\zeta(\beta+it)\ne0$ for $|t|\ge3$ and $1-\beta\le\frac1{8.464\log|t|}$.
$\zeta(\beta+it)\ne0$ for $|t|\ge3$ and $1-\beta\le \dfrac1{57.54(\log|t|)^{2/3}(\log\log|t|)^{1/3}}$ (uses A=76.2, B=4.45 from companion paper and T_0=e^{54550}).
hypotheses: none beyond cited Theorem 1 of Ford 2002 (Vinogradov's integral)

statement: For f a quotient of entire functions of finite order, no zero/pole at z_0, 0, and a.e. $\eta>0$: $-\Re\frac{f'(z_0)}{f(z_0)}\cdot\frac{\pi}{2\eta}=\sum_{|\Re(z_0-\rho)|\le\eta}m_\rho\Re\frac{\pi}{2\eta}\cot\frac{\pi(\rho-z_0)}{2\eta}+\frac1{4\eta}\int_{-\infty}^\infty[\log f(z_0-\eta+\tfrac{2\eta iu}{\pi})-\log f(z_0+\eta+\tfrac{2\eta iu}{\pi})]\cosh^{-2}u\,du$ (exact normalisation as printed in paper; text OCR garbled)
role: main 'zero detector': integrates over two vertical lines instead of a circle, replacing Heath-Brown's Lemma 3.2

statement: For real $a_1,a_2$, $b_j$ per (5.2) and any $\eta>0,t_1,t_2$: $\int_{-\infty}^\infty\cosh^{-2}u\sum_{j=1}^4 b_j\log|\zeta(1+\eta+ijt_1+iut_2)|du\ge-2b_0\log\zeta(1+\eta)$
role: combines the log|zeta| terms via a trigonometric-polynomial positivity (5.1) instead of the trivial |zeta|>=1/zeta(sigma); main source of improvement over Heath-Brown

statement: Under (1.2), for $0<\eta<\pi/4$, $\sigma-\eta\ge1/2$, $1\le\sigma\le1+\eta$, $t\ge100$: $-\Re\zeta'/\zeta(s)\le-\sum_{\rho\in S}\Re\frac\pi{2\eta}\cot\frac{\pi(s-\rho)}{2\eta}+\frac1{2\eta}(\tfrac23\log\log t+B(1-\sigma+\eta)^{3/2}\log t+\log A)-\frac1{4\eta}\int\frac{\log|\zeta(s+\eta+2\eta iu/\pi)|}{\cosh^2u}du$
role: upper bound for -Re zeta'/zeta using zero detector

statement: For $t\ge10000$, $\zeta(\beta+it)=0$, (6.1), (1.2), $1-\beta\le\eta/2$, $\eta\le1/4$, $0<\lambda\le\min(1-\beta,\eta/250)$: $\frac1\lambda(0.16521-0.1876(\frac{1-\beta}\lambda-1))\le1.471\ldots$ (as printed; inequality garbled by OCR)
role: key inequality linking real part of a zero to eta, optimized in Sec. 8

statement: $\sum_\rho|\rho|^{-2}\le0.0463$ over nontrivial zeros; proof uses $\sum\Re\rho/|\rho|^2=1+\gamma/2-\log(4\pi)/2$ (as printed) and zeros on the critical line for $|\Im\rho|\le5.45\times10^8$.
role: bounds contribution of far zeros

statement: If $|\zeta(\sigma+iy)|\le Xt^Y(\log t)^Z$ for $1\le|y|\le t$ ($Y+Z\ge0.1$) then for $0<a\le1/2$, $t\ge100$, $1/2\le\sigma\le1-1/t$: $\int\frac{\log|\zeta(\sigma+it+iau)|}{\cosh^2u}du\le2(\log X+Y\log t+Z\log\log t)$.
role: bounds the log-integral term

statement: Variants of the above for $t\ge5.45\times10^8$ using $J(t)$ from (1.6), giving (9.8) for $1-\beta\le1/160$.
role: small-height (classical) zero-free region Theorem 3-4

statement: Let $\omega$ be uniform on $(0,1)$, $\varepsilon_t\to0$, $\varepsilon_t\gg 1/\log t$, and $0\le f_t^{(1)}<\dots<f_t^{(\ell)}<c<\infty$ with $\log|f_t^{(j)}-f_t^{(i)}|/\log\varepsilon_t\to c_{i,j}\in[0,\infty]$ for all $i\ne j$. Then $(-\log\varepsilon_t)^{-1/2}\big(\log\zeta(\tfrac12+\varepsilon_t+if_t^{(j)}+i\omega t)\big)_{j\le\ell}$ converges in law to a centered complex Gaussian vector with $\mathrm{cov}(Y_i,Y_j)=1$ if $i=j$, $1\wedge c_{i,j}$ if $i\ne j$. If $\varepsilon_t\ll1/\log t$ the same holds with normalization $(\log\log t)^{-1/2}$ (and in the definition of $c_{i,j}$).

Finite-dimensional distributions of $(\log\log t)^{-1/2}\log\zeta(\tfrac12+i\omega t+i(\log t)^{-\delta})$, $0\le\delta\le1$, converge to a centered Gaussian process with kernel $\gamma\wedge\delta$ ($\gamma\ne\delta$), $1$ ($\gamma=\delta$); realized as $X_\delta=B_\delta+D_{1-\delta}$, B Brownian motion, D totally disordered (independent coordinates, variance delta); no measurable version exists.

Let $K_t>\epsilon$ with $\log K_t/\log\log t\to\delta\in[0,1)$. Then the finite-dimensional distributions of $\tilde\Delta_t(\alpha,\beta)=\frac{1}{\pi\sqrt{(1-\delta)\log\log t}}\Delta(\omega t+\alpha/K_t,\omega t+\beta/K_t)$ ($\Delta$ = zero count minus smooth expectation) converge to a centered Gaussian process with covariance 1 if (alpha,beta)=(alpha',beta'); 1/2 if exactly one endpoint coincides (same side); -1/2 if beta=alpha'; 0 otherwise. Realized as $\tilde D_\beta-\tilde D_\alpha$, D~ independent N(0,1/2). Recovers Fujii's CLT for delta in [0,1].

For $u_n$ Haar on $U(n)$, $\varepsilon_n\to0$, $\varepsilon_n\gg1/n$, $0\le\varphi_n^{(1)}<\dots<\varphi_n^{(\ell)}<2\pi-\delta$ with $\log|\varphi^{(j)}_n-\varphi^{(i)}_n|/\log\varepsilon_n\to c_{i,j}$: $(-\log\varepsilon_n)^{-1/2}(\log Z(u_n,e^{\varepsilon_n+i\varphi_n^{(k)}}))_k\to$ complex Gaussian with covariance (1.6); for $\varepsilon_n\ll1/n$ replace by $\log n$.

If $a_{pt}\in\mathbb C$ with $\sup_p|a_{pt}|\to0$, $\sum_p|a_{pt}|^2\to\sigma^2$, and there is $m_t$ with $\log m_t/\log t\to0$ and $\sum_{p>m_t}|a_{pt}|^2(1+p/t)\to0$, then $\sum_p a_{pt}p^{-i\omega t}\to\sigma Y$ in law ($\omega$ uniform on (0,1), Y standard complex normal).

For $\varepsilon_n\gg1/n$, $\varepsilon_n\to0$, $0<\Delta_n\le2\pi-\delta$, $\log\Delta_n/\log\varepsilon_n\to c$: $\frac1{-\log\varepsilon_n}\sum_{j\le n}\frac{e^{ij\Delta_n}}{je^{2j\varepsilon_n}}\to c\wedge1$.
role: Produces the covariance 1^c in the U(n) case via the Diaconis-Evans theorem.

statement: Analogue for $\varepsilon_n\ll1/n$: $\frac1{\log n}\sum_{j\le n}x_n^j/j\to c\wedge1$ with $-\log\Delta_n/\log n\to c$ (as used in proof; exact statement not fully read).
role: Critical-line covariance, also used in Sec. 4 construction.

statement: Prime-sum analogues of Lemmas 2.2/2.3: $\frac{1}{-\log\varepsilon_t}\sum_{p\le t}p^{-1-2\varepsilon_t+i\Delta_t}\to c\wedge 1$ (and log log t version), proved through the prime number theorem.
role: Covariance computation for the zeta side.

statement: $\frac1t\int_1^t|\log\zeta(\sigma+is)-\sum_{p\le x}p^{-\sigma-is}|^{2k}ds\le c_{k,a}$ for $1/2\le\sigma\le1$, $t^{a/k}\le x\le t^{1/k}$ (k=1 used).
role: Reduces log zeta to a short Dirichlet polynomial; imported from Selberg.

statement: Define $F(x,T)=\sum_{\rho,\rho'\,(0<\gamma,\gamma'\le T)}x^{\rho-\rho'}w(\rho-\rho')$ with $w(u)=\frac{4}{4-u^2}$ and $F(\alpha)=\frac{T^{-1}}{\,}\!\left(\tfrac{T}{2\pi}\log T\right)^{-1}\!F(T^\alpha,T)$ i.e. $F(\alpha)=(\tfrac{T}{2\pi}\log T)^{-1}\sum T^{\alpha(\rho-\rho')}w(\rho-\rho')$ (zeros counted with multiplicity). Then $F(\alpha)$ is real, even and nonnegative, and $F(\alpha)=T^{-2\alpha}(\log T+O(1))+\alpha+O(1/\sqrt{\log T})$ as $T\to\infty$, uniformly for $0\le\alpha\le1$.

kind: theorem (conditional on a thin-box zero-location hypothesis, weaker than RH-free statement)
statement: Suppose all zeros $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ of $\zeta$ with $T^{3/8}<\gamma\le T$ satisfy $\frac12-\frac1{2\log T}<\beta<\frac12+\frac1{2\log T}$. Then for all sufficiently large $T$, at least $61.7\%$ of the nontrivial zeros $0<\gamma\le T$ are simple (precisely: $\liminf\frac1{N(T)}\#\{\text{simple }\rho\}\ge0.6174837\dots$ with the Montgomery-Taylor kernel; $0.6086\dots$ with the Fejer kernel).
hypotheses: (1.5) thin box for T^{3/8}<gamma<=T, which does not require beta=1/2

statement: Assume $N(\sigma,T)=o(T^{2(1-\sigma)})$ for $\frac12+\frac1{2\log T}\le\sigma\le\frac{25}{32}+\eta$, for every fixed $\eta>0$, where $N(\sigma,T)=\#\{\rho:\beta\ge\sigma,0<\gamma\le T\}$. Then as $T\to\infty$ at least $61.7\%$ of the nontrivial zeros are simple.
hypotheses: (1.6); Bourgain's estimate N(sigma,T)=o(T^{2(1-sigma)}) for sigma>=25/32+eta covers the rest of the range (eq. 6.5)

statement: For $\rho=\tfrac12+\delta+i\gamma$, $x\ge1$ and all $t$: $\sum_\rho\frac{2x^{\delta+i(\gamma-t)}}{1+((t-\gamma)+i\delta)^2}=-\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{\Lambda(n)}{n^{1/2+it}}\min(\tfrac nx,\tfrac xn)+x^{-1}(\log(|t|+2)+O(1))+O(\tfrac{x^{1/2}}{1+t^2})+O(\tfrac{x^{-5/2}}{|t|+2})$. Derived from Landau's explicit formula using $s=\sigma$ and $1-\sigma$ at $\sigma=3/2$, without RH.
role: Unconditional replacement of Montgomery's explicit formula identity (valid for zeros with real parts different from 1/2).

statement: For $x>0$, $T\ge3$: $F(x,T)=\frac2\pi\int_{-\infty}^\infty\left|\sum_{0<\gamma\le T}\frac{x^{\rho-1/2}}{1-(\rho-(1/2+it))^2}\right|^2dt$ (unconditional; shown by residues using $\int(1+t^2)^{-1}(1+(t+a)^2)^{-1}dt=2\pi/(4+a^2)$). Hence F(x,T)>=0 and real.
role: Establishes nonnegativity and reality of F(alpha) without RH (the weight $w(u)=4/(4-u^2)$ replaces $4/(4+(\gamma-\gamma')^2)$).

statement: For $x\ge1$, $T\ge3$ and a zero-free region $\sigma>1-\eta(t)\ge\Theta(t)$: $F(x,T)=\frac1{2\pi}L(x,T)+O(x^{1-2\eta(T\log^2T)}\log^3T)+O(x)$ where $L(x,T)=\int_0^T|\sum_\rho\frac{2x^{\delta+i\gamma}}{1+((t-\gamma)+i\delta)^2}|^2dt$. With Vinogradov-Korobov $\eta(t)=c/((\log t)^{2/3}(\log\log t)^{1/3})$ the error is $O(T)+O(x)$ for $1\le x\le T$.
role: Replaces Montgomery's truncation argument by an explicit loss controlled by the unconditional zero-free region; this is the only place where non-RH zeros cost anything.

statement: If $r\in L^1$ is real, even, supported in $[-1,1]$ and Lipschitz at 0, then $\sum_{0<\gamma,\gamma'\le T}\hat r(i(\rho-\rho')\tfrac{\log T}{2\pi})w(\rho-\rho')=\tfrac T{2\pi}\log T\big(r(0)+2\int_0^1\alpha r(\alpha)d\alpha+O(1/\sqrt{\log T})\big)$ (unconditional).
role: Unconditional version of Montgomery's sum over pairs of zeros for kernels with Fourier transform supported in [-1,1].

statement: The Tsang kernel $K(z)=\frac1\pi\int_0^1 j(\alpha)\operatorname{sech}(\alpha)\cos(z\alpha)d\alpha$ ($\hat K(t)=j(2\pi t)\operatorname{sech}(2\pi t)$) is even entire with (a) $K(x)>0$ on R, (b) $K(z)\ll e^{|\Im z|}/|z|^2$, (c) $\Re K(x+iy)>0$ for $|y|<1$.
role: Positivity of Re K(-i(rho-rho')log T) in the region |beta-beta'|<1/log T lets one bound sum m_rho by the pair sum, off the half line.

statement: With $K$ the Tsang kernel: $2\pi\sum_{\rho,\rho',\,|\beta-\beta'|<1/\log T}\Re K(-i(\rho-\rho')\log T)+S(T)=\big(\hat K(0)+2\int_0^1\alpha\hat K(\tfrac\alpha{2\pi})d\alpha+O(1/\sqrt{\log T})\big)\tfrac T{2\pi}\log T$, where $S(T)=2\pi\Re\sum_{|\beta-\beta'|\ge1/\log T}K(-i(\rho-\rho')\log T)w(\rho-\rho')$.
role: Splits pair sum into diagonal-near terms (positive) and an error S(T) controlled by zero-density or thin-box hypotheses.

statement: Either the thin-box hypothesis (6.1) or the density hypothesis (6.2) implies $S(T)=o(T\log T)$, via $|K(-i(\rho-\rho')\log T)|\ll T^{|\beta-\beta'|}/(\ldots)^2$, AM-GM $T^{|\beta-\beta'|}\le\frac12(T^{|2\beta-1|}+T^{|2\beta'-1|})$, reduction to $\sum_{\beta\ge1/2+1/(2\log T)}T^{2\beta-1}=o(T\log T)$ via partial summation against $N(u,T)$, and Bourgain's $N(\sigma,T)=o(T^{2(1-\sigma)})$ for $\sigma\ge25/32+\eta$.
role: The only place the extra hypothesis is used; shows RH is not needed, only that off-line zeros are rare/near the line.

statement: Let $|b_n|\le1$ and $(t_r)_{r\le R}$ be 1-separated points in $[0,T]$ with $|\sum_{n=N}^{2N} b_n n^{it_r}|\ge V$ for all r. Then $R\le T^{o(1)}\left(N^2V^{-2}+N^{18/5}V^{-4}+TN^{12/5}V^{-4}\right)$.

Unconditionally $N(\sigma,T)\le T^{15(1-\sigma)/(3+5\sigma)+o(1)}$; combined with Ingham for $\sigma\le 7/10$, $N(\sigma,T)\le T^{30(1-\sigma)/13+o(1)}$ uniformly in $\sigma\in[1/2,1]$. Here N(sigma,T) = #{rho: Re rho>=sigma, |Im rho|<=T}.
For $y\in[x^{17/30+\epsilon},x^{0.99}]$: $\pi(x+y)-\pi(x)=\frac{y}{\log x}+O_\epsilon\!\left(y\exp(-\sqrt[4]{\log x})\right)$.
For $y\in[X^{2/15+\epsilon},X^{0.99}]$, for all but $O(X\exp(-\sqrt[4]{\log X}))$ integers $x\in[X,2X]$: $\pi(x+y)-\pi(x)=\frac y{\log x}+O_\epsilon(y\exp(-\sqrt[4]{\log x}))$.

Let $\sigma\in[7/10,8/10]$, $|b_n|\le1$, W a $T^\epsilon$-separated set in an interval of length $T=N^{6/5}$ with $|\sum_n w(n/N)b_nn^{it}|\ge N^\sigma$ for t in W. Then $|W|\le TN^{(12-20\sigma)/5+o_\epsilon(1)}$.

If $T^{5/6}\le N\le T$, $V=N^\sigma$, $\sigma\ge7/10$, then $R\lesssim N^{2-2\sigma}+T^{1/2}N^{3-4\sigma}+T^{(30\sigma-21)/5}N^{(46-60\sigma)/5}$ (with an inf-over-k form). At sigma=3/4 improves (1.1) by a factor (T/N)^{1/2}.

For a $T^\epsilon$-separated W in an interval of length T: $S_3\lessapprox T^2|W|^{1/2}E(W)^{1/2}$ (Prop 8.1) and refined $S_3\lessapprox T^2|W|^{3/2}+TN|W|^{1/2}E(W)^{1/2}$ (Prop 10.1), where $E(W)=\#\{w_1+w_2-w_3-w_4\in[-1,1]\}$ is additive energy.

For W T^epsilon-separated with |D_N(t)|>N^sigma: $|W|\ll N^{2-2\sigma}+N^{1-2\sigma}\left(\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z^3\setminus0}I_m\right)^{1/3}$ where I_m comes from the expansion of the cubic trace tr((M^*M)^3), M=(n^{it}).
role: Reduces large values to a cubic-trace bound (s_1(M)^6 <= tr((M^*M)^3) after removing near-diagonal terms).
Controls one error term (S2) via approximate functional equation.

statement: $|I_m|\ll N^3\left|\int\!\!\int R(v_1)R(v_2/v_1)R(v_2)\,dv_1dv_2\right|+O(T^{-200})$ where $R(x)=\sum_{t\in W}|x|^{it}$.
role: Cancellation inside the u-integrals avoiding stationary phase; moves to the 2-dim subvariety z1 z2 z3=1.
Gives Prop 8.1 (energy-controlled S_3).

statement: Equidistribution over affine transformations: for f>=0 supported on u~1 with Fourier decay $|\hat f(\xi)|\lessapprox_j (T/|\xi|)^j\sup f$, $J(f)\lessapprox M^6(\int f)^2+M^4\int f^2$.
role: Key new input: a small set U cannot be approximately closed under many affine maps u->(m1 u+m3)/m2; yields the T N |W|^{1/2}E^{1/2} refinement.

statement: For $T^{3/4}\le N\le T$, $|D|\ge N^\sigma$ on W: $E(W)\lessapprox|W|N^{4-4\sigma}+|W|^{21/8}T^{1/4}N^{1-2\sigma}+|W|^3N^{1-2\sigma}$.
role: Energy bound using Heath-Brown's Thm 1.6 (imported) to cover the large-energy case.
Large additive energy forces Montgomery's conjecture bound.

statement: For 1-separated set T in an interval of length T and |a_n|<=T^{o(1)}: $\sum_{t_1,t_2}|\sum a_n n^{i(t_1-t_2)}|^2\le T^{o(1)}(|T|^2N+|T|N^2+|T|^{5/4}T^{1/2}N)$.
role: Imported difference-set mean-value bound.

statement: $S_{0,\alpha}(t)=\frac1\pi\arg\zeta(\alpha+it)$ (continuous variation from 2, averaged at zeros); $S_{n,\alpha}(t)=\int_0^tS_{n-1,\alpha}(\tau)d\tau+\delta_{n,\alpha}$ with $\delta_{2k-1,\alpha}=\frac{(-1)^{k-1}}{\pi}\int_\alpha^\infty\!\!\int_{\sigma_{2k-2}}^\infty\cdots\int_{\sigma_1}^\infty\log|\zeta(\sigma_0)|d\sigma_0\cdots d\sigma_{2k-2}$ and $\delta_{2k,\alpha}=\frac{(-1)^{k-1}(1-\alpha)^{2k}}{(2k)!}$; $S_{-1,\alpha}(t)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\zeta'}\zeta(\alpha+it)$.

Assume RH. For $n\ge0$: $-(C_n^-+o(1))\frac{\log t}{(\log\log t)^{n+1}}\le S_n(t)\le(C_n^++o(1))\frac{\log t}{(\log\log t)^{n+1}}$ with $C_0^\pm=\frac14$; for $n=4k+1$: $C_n^-=\frac{\zeta(n+1)}{\pi2^{n+1}}$, $C_n^+=\frac{(1-2^{-n})\zeta(n+1)}{\pi2^{n+1}}$; for $n=4k+3$ the roles swap; for even $n\ge2$, $C_n^+=C_n^-=\Big(\frac{2(C_{n+1}^++C_{n+1}^-)C_{n-1}^+C_{n-1}^-}{C_{n-1}^++C_{n-1}^-}\Big)^{1/2}$.

Assume RH, $n\ge-1$, $\frac12<\alpha<1$, $c>0$, $\log\log t\ge4$ and $(1-\alpha)^2\log\log t\ge c$. (i) $n=-1$: $-C^-_{-1,\alpha}(t)(\log t)^{2-2\alpha}+O_c\big(\frac{(\alpha-\frac12)(\log t)^{2-2\alpha}}{(1-\alpha)^2\log\log t}\big)\le S_{-1,\alpha}(t)\le C^+_{-1,\alpha}(t)(\log t)^{2-2\alpha}+O_c\big(\frac{(\log t)^{2-2\alpha}}{(\alpha-\frac12)(1-\alpha)^2\log\log t}\big)$. (ii) $n\ge0$: $-C^-_{n,\alpha}(t)\frac{(\log t)^{2-2\alpha}}{(\log\log t)^{n+1}}+O_{n,c}\big(\frac{(\log t)^{2-2\alpha}}{(1-\alpha)^2(\log\log t)^{n+2}}\big)\le S_{n,\alpha}(t)\le C^+_{n,\alpha}(t)\frac{(\log t)^{2-2\alpha}}{(\log\log t)^{n+1}}+O_{n,c}(\text{same})$. For odd $n\ge-1$: $C^\pm_{n,\alpha}(t)=\frac1{2^{n+1}\pi}H_{n+1}\big(\pm(-1)^{(n+1)/2}(\log t)^{1-2\alpha}+\frac{2\alpha-1}{\alpha(1-\alpha)}\big)$ with $H_n(x)=\sum_{k\ge0}x^k/(k+1)^n$; $n=0$ uses (1.8) (built from $C^\pm_{1,\alpha}$ and $C^-_{-1,\alpha}$); even $n\ge2$ uses interpolation formula (1.9), the strip analogue of the formula in Thm 1.
Assume RH. For $t$ large, $|S(t)|\le\frac14\frac{\log t}{\log\log t}+O\big(\frac{\log t}{(\log\log t)^2}\big)$ (new proof of the CCM bound, with a $\log\log\log t$ factor removed from the error).

Assume RH. For large $t$: $\log|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|\le\frac{\log2}{2}\frac{\log t}{\log\log t}+O\big(\frac{\log t}{(\log\log t)^2}\big)$, deduced from the lower bound for $S_{-1,\alpha}$ in Thm 2 together with the strip bound $\log|\zeta(\sigma+it)|\le\log\frac1{1-\sigma}+O(\frac{(\log t)^{2-2\sigma}}{(1-\sigma)\log\log t})$ for $\frac12+\frac1{\log\log t}\le\sigma\le1-\frac1{\log\log t}$.

Assume RH, $n\ge-1$, fixed $\frac12<\alpha<1$. Then $|S_{n,\alpha}(t)|\le\frac{\omega_n}{2^{n+1}\pi}\Big(1+\frac{2\alpha-1}{\alpha(1-\alpha)}+o(1)\Big)\frac{(\log t)^{2-2\alpha}}{(\log\log t)^{n+1}}$ as $t\to\infty$, where $\omega_n=1$ for $n$ odd and $\omega_n=\sqrt2$ for $n$ even.

Assume RH. For $n\ge-1$, $t\ge2$: $S_{2m,\alpha}(t)=\frac{(-1)^m}{\pi(2m)!}\sum_\gamma f_{2m,\alpha}(t-\gamma)+O_m(1)$ and $S_{2m+1,\alpha}(t)=\frac{(-1)^m}{2\pi(2m+2)!}(\frac32-\alpha)^{2m+2}\log t-\frac{(-1)^m}{\pi(2m)!}\sum_\gamma f_{2m+1,\alpha}(t-\gamma)+O_m(1)$ (second formula as read), with $f_{2m,\alpha}(x)=\int_\alpha^{3/2}(\sigma-\alpha)^{2m}\big(\frac{x}{(\sigma-\frac12)^2+x^2}-\frac x{1+x^2}\big)d\sigma$, $f_{2m+1,\alpha}(x)=\frac12\int_\alpha^{3/2}(\sigma-\alpha)^{2m}\log\frac{1+x^2}{(\sigma-\frac12)^2+x^2}d\sigma$, $f_{-1,\alpha}(x)=\frac{\alpha-\frac12}{(\alpha-\frac12)^2+x^2}$.

Under RH, for $n\ge0$, $\frac12\le\alpha\le1$: $S_{n,\alpha}(t)=-\frac1\pi\operatorname{Im}\{\frac{i^n}{n!}\int_\alpha^\infty(\sigma-\alpha)^n\frac{\zeta'}\zeta(\sigma+it)d\sigma\}$; and $S_{-1,\alpha}=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\zeta'}\zeta(\alpha+it)$.
role: Integral representation (Selberg/Fujii) for all iterates, by induction on n.

statement: Guinand-Weil explicit formula (as in CAND-01806).
role: Imported tool.

statement: For $\beta>0$, $\Delta>0$ there is a unique pair of real entire functions $m^\pm_{\beta,\Delta}$ of exponential type $2\pi\Delta$ with $m^-\le h_\beta\le m^+$ on $\mathbb R$ ($h_\beta$ the Poisson kernel) minimizing $\int(m^+-m^-)$; they are even with explicit Fourier transforms.
role: Step 2 for n=-1 (Gaussian subordination of Carneiro-Littmann-Vaaler).

statement: For $m\ge0$, $\frac12\le\alpha\le1$, $\Delta\ge1$ there is a unique pair of extremal minorant/majorant $g^\pm_{2m+1,\alpha,\Delta}$ of exponential type $2\pi\Delta$ for $f_{2m+1,\alpha}$ minimizing the $L^1$ gap, with explicit Fourier transforms.
role: Step 2 for odd n.

statement: Under RH, for $0<\beta<\frac12$, $\Delta\ge1$: $\frac1\pi\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\Lambda(n)}{\sqrt n}m^\pm_\Delta(\frac{\log n}{2\pi})\cos(t\log n)$ is bounded below by an explicit expression (4.1) of size $-O(\beta e^{(1-2\beta)\pi\Delta}/\ldots)$ plus $O(\Delta^4/\beta)$.
role: Prime-power sum for n=-1 with alpha>1/2.

statement: For $m\ge0$, $\frac12\le\alpha<1$, $\Delta\ge1$, $\pi\Delta(1-\alpha)^2\ge c$: $\mp\frac1\pi\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\Lambda(n)}{\sqrt n}\hat g^\pm_\Delta(\frac{\log n}{2\pi})\cos(t\log n)\le\frac{(2\alpha-1)(2m)!e^{(2-2\alpha)\pi\Delta}}{\alpha(1-\alpha)(2\pi\Delta)^{2m+2}}+O_{m,c}\big(\frac{e^{(2-2\alpha)\pi\Delta}}{(1-\alpha)^2\Delta^{2m+3}}\big)$.
role: Technical heart: prime sum for alpha>1/2, much harder than alpha=1/2.

statement: Even $n$ (and $n=0$) obtained from odd neighbors via the mean value theorem $S_{n,\alpha}(t)-S_{n,\alpha}(t-h)=hS_{n-1,\alpha}(t^*_h)$ and optimization of $h$, giving (1.9) with the $\sqrt2$ loss of Cor. 5.
role: Step 4: handles odd kernels f_{2m,alpha} for which the Beurling-Selberg problem is unsolved.

statement: Let q be cube-free, chi primitive mod q and not quadratic. Then for some B>2, $\sum_{m|q}\sum_{|t_j|\le T}\sum_{f\in H_{it_j}(m,\chi^2)}L(1/2,f\otimes\chi)+\int_{-T}^{T}|L(1/2+it,\chi)|^6\,dt\ll_\varepsilon T^{B}q^{1+\varepsilon}$.

Same hypotheses, and T >> q^delta for some delta>0: $\sum_{m|q}\sum_{T\le t_j<T+1}\sum_f L(1/2,f\otimes\chi)+\int_T^{T+1}|L(1/2+it,\chi)|^6dt\ll_{\varepsilon,\delta}T^{1+\varepsilon}q^{1+\varepsilon}$.
If chi has cube-free conductor q (any primitive chi, quadratic case from Conrey-Iwaniec/earlier work): $|L(1/2+it,\chi)|\ll_\varepsilon q^{1/6+\varepsilon}(1+|t|)^{1/6+\varepsilon}$.
p odd prime, F Hecke-Maass newform of level p^2, trivial central character, not twist-minimal (F=f otimes chi): $L(1/2,F)\ll_\varepsilon (p(1+|t_F|))^{1/3+\varepsilon}$.

Holomorphic analogue, q cube-free: $\sum_{m|q}\sum_{\kappa\le T}\sum_{f\in H_\kappa(m,\chi^2)}L(1/2,f\otimes\chi)^3\ll_\varepsilon T^{B}q^{1+\varepsilon}$ for some B>2, and << T^{1+eps}q^{1+eps} for the unit-window sum if T>>q^delta.
For $g(\chi,\psi)=\sum_{t,u\bmod q}\chi(t)\chi(t+1)\chi(u)\chi(u+1)\psi(ut-1)$ with chi primitive mod q and q=p or q=p^2: $|g(\chi,\psi)|\ll q$.
location: Sec 6.4; proved in Sec 9 (9.1 prime via Deligne/Katz trace functions; 9.2 q=p^2 elementary)

statement: Cubic moment M(q,chi) (even-parity spectral sum of L(1/2,f otimes chi)^3 plus Eisenstein contribution) << T^B q^eps for cube-free non-quadratic chi; implies Thm 1.1 via nonnegativity L(1/2,f otimes chi)>=0 (Waldspurger/Guo) and L(1/2,E otimes chi)=|L(1/2+it,chi)|^2 * (analogous), after normalization by Petersson norms.
If the dual sums S_{N1,N2,N3,C}^{\pm} << T^B q^eps for N1<<(qT)^{1+eps}, N2N3<<d^{-2}(qT)^{2+eps}, q<<C<<(qT)^{100}, then Theorem 4.1 holds.
role: Reduction of cubic moment, after approximate functional equation, Kuznetsov/Petersson and Poisson summation, to a bound for dual Kloosterman-type sums.

statement: For q cube-free, Z=Z_0+Z_1 with Z_0 meromorphic/analytic as stated with Z_0<<q^eps for Re s_j>1, and $\int_{-T}^{T}|Z_1(\sigma+it,\sigma+it,\sigma+it,\sigma-it)|dt\ll q^{3/2+\varepsilon}T^{1+\varepsilon}$ for T>>1 (Z_1 analytic for Re s_j>=1/2).
role: Analytic continuation/fourth-moment type Dirichlet series control; remarked essentially equivalent to [PY1, Prop 3] (fourth moment of Dirichlet L-functions, q^{1+eps}).

statement: For nontrivial chi, psi mod p, the trace function of the sheaf G is the cohomological (Katz affine) transform of F_1 with kernel K: t_G(x)=-sum_y t_{F1}(y)t_K(x,y); the sheaf G_e is geometrically irreducible/Fourier-type enough to give square-root cancellation.
role: Proof of |g(chi,psi)|<<q for q=p via Deligne's Riemann Hypothesis (Katz, Fouvry-Kowalski-Michel trace function formalism).

statement: Evaluation of Gauss/Ramanujan-type sums H(psi^,chi,m1,m2,m3,r) for prime powers; vanishing unless psi trivial when some m_j=0; Conjecture 6.6 proved here only for k=2,j=1 (q=p^2).
role: Local arithmetic of the dual sum; the unproved Conjectures 6.6 and 8.2 for q=p^k, k>=3 were later proved in Petrow-Young [PY2] (remark of 28 Aug 2019).

statement: Archimedean analysis: bounds for weight functions V_j and Bessel-transform kernels J^{\pm}(x,.), oscillatory and non-oscillatory cases of the integral transform in the dual sum.
role: Make the Poisson/Kuznetsov dual sums tractable with polynomial dependence T^B on spectral parameter.

statement: $\zeta(s)\ne0$ for $\Re s\ge1-\dfrac{1}{R_0\log|\Im s|}$ with $|\Im s|\ge2$, where $R_0=5.70176$ (arXiv v1 and its abstract). The published Acta Arith. version is recalled (by the triage field, unverified here) as $R_0=5.69693$.
hypotheses: uses verification of RH up to height $T_0=3.3\cdot10^9$ (Wedeniwski)
conditional_on: numerical zero verification to height 3.3e9 imported as a hypothesis for zeros below that height

statement: The region is wider than the Ford-Vinogradov region (with $R_1=57.54$) up to $|\Im s|<e^{9402.562}$; the method generalizes to Dirichlet L-functions (author's reference [8]).

Weil-type explicit formula for $\Re\sum_n\Lambda(n)n^{-s}g(\log n)$ in terms of the Laplace transform $\tilde F$ of $f*f$-type weight $F$, involving the sum over all zeros $\sum_{\varrho}\Re D(s-\varrho)$, with $D=\tilde F-\kappa\tilde F(\cdot+\delta)$.
role: Expresses the prime-side positive quantity as an integral/gamma term minus a sum over zeros.

statement: Weight $f\in C^2([0,d])$ with support in $[0,d)$ and $f(d)=f'(0)=f'(d)=f''(d)=0$; Laplace transform $\tilde F(X,Y)\ge0$ for $X\ge0$. Weight built from Heath-Brown's compactly supported function $h_\theta$ times Stechkin's $1-\kappa e^{-\delta x}$.
role: Positivity of zero-sum terms.

statement: For $\sigma>1$, $\tau=(1+\sqrt{1+4\sigma^2})/2$: $\Re\!\left[\frac1{\sigma-1+\beta+i y}\right]\!+\!\ldots-\frac1{\sqrt5}\ldots\ge0$ (exact form garbled in extracted text), the symmetric-zero positivity trick.
role: Imported; generalized in the paper to $\Re\tilde F(s-\varrho)+\Re\tilde F(s+1-\varrho)\ge0$ for $\Re(s-\varrho)>0$ (Sec 2.4).

statement: Bounds: gamma-factor term $\le\frac A2(1-\kappa)g_1(\theta)\eta\log\gamma_0+C_1(\eta)$; pole term $\le a_0\tilde F(\sigma-1,0)+C_2(\eta)$; zeros beyond $\gamma\ge\gamma_0+t_0$ contribute $\ge a_1\tilde F(\sigma-\beta_0,0)-C_3(\eta)$; $\Delta_2$ term $\le C_4(\eta)$. Constants such as $C(\eta)=\alpha_1\eta+\alpha_2\eta^2+\alpha_3\eta^3$ with $\alpha_2=344602.439$, $\alpha_3=5799250.773$ (as extracted).
role: Make each piece explicit, yielding cubic polynomial in eta whose sign gives the zero-free condition.

statement: Degree-4 non-negative cosine polynomial $\sum_{k=0}^4a_k\cos k\theta$ (a_4=1, a_1=18.63362, a_2=11.4517, A=sum a_k=35.78532), a variant of Rosser-Schoenfeld's, positive by a product form $(\cdot+\cos y)^2(0.265+\cos y)^2$.
role: Final positivity argument giving the 3-1-cos inequality analogue.

statement: Parameters $(r,R)$, $\eta_0$, $\kappa$, $\delta$ iterated to a fixed point: $R_0\mapsto5.974849,5.730454,5.704873,5.702090,5.701785,5.701753$ ending at $R_0=5.70175$ stated, announced rounded to 5.70176 with precision $10^{-5}$.
role: Numerical fixed-point optimization of the constant; $\kappa_0=0.4389$, $\delta_0=0.6208$.

statement: For positive integer $k$ and $\epsilon>0$: $\int_0^T|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|^{2k}dt=\int_0^TP_k(\log\tfrac t{2\pi})dt+O_{k,\epsilon}(T^{1/2+\epsilon})$, where $P_k(x)=\dfrac{(-1)^k}{k!^2(2\pi i)^{2k}}\oint\!\!\cdots\!\oint\dfrac{G(z)\Delta^2(z)\,e^{\frac x2\sum_{i=1}^k(z_i-z_{i+k})}}{\prod_{i=1}^{2k}z_i^{2k}}dz$, $G=A_k(z)\prod_{i,j\le k}\zeta(1+z_i-z_{j+k})$, $A_k$ the Euler product (1.4)=(1.5).

Writing $P_k(x)=c_0(k)x^{k^2}+c_1(k)x^{k^2-1}+\dots+c_{k^2}(k)$: $c_r(k)=a_k\prod_{l=0}^{k-1}\frac{l!}{(k+l)!}\sum_{|\alpha|+|\beta|=r}2^{1-\delta(\alpha;\beta)}b_k(\alpha;\beta)N_k(\alpha;\beta)$, where $a_k=\prod_p(1-p^{-1})^{k^2}{}_2F_1(k,k;1;1/p)$, $b_k(\alpha;\beta)$ are Taylor coefficients of $a_k^{-1}A_k(z)\prod_{i,j}(z_i-z_{j+k})\zeta(1+z_i-z_{j+k})$, $\delta(\alpha;\beta)=1$ iff $\alpha=\beta$, and $N_k(\alpha;\beta)=2^{k^2-r}\big(\prod_l\frac{l!}{(k+l)!}\big)^{-1}\sum_{\text{distinct rearrangements}}\tilde M_k(\sigma(\alpha),\tau(\beta))$ with $\tilde M_k$ a $2k\times2k$ determinant (2.63). (Exponent of 2 in $N_k$ as extracted: $1/2^{k^2-r}$ prefactor.)
hypotheses: k positive integer for the residue interpretation; formulas continue meromorphically in k

statement: $c_0(k)=a_k\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\dfrac{j!}{(j+k)!}$ with $a_k=\prod_p(1-p^{-1})^{k^2}{}_2F_1(k,k;1;1/p)$, agreeing with the Keating-Snaith leading constant.
$N_k(\alpha;\beta)$ is a polynomial in $k$ of degree at most $2(|\alpha|+|\beta|)$ (hence determined by evaluation at $2(|\alpha|+|\beta|)+1$ integer values and interpolation).

The Taylor coefficients $b_k(\alpha;\beta)$ are polynomials in $k$, the Taylor coefficients of $s\zeta(1+s)$, and the Taylor coefficients of $\log A_k(z_1,\dots,z_{2k})$; the latter are sums over primes $p$ of rational functions in $k,p,\log p$ and finitely many ${}_2F_1(k_1,k_2;m;1/p)$, $k_1,k_2\ge k$, $m\ge1$.

For $F$ symmetric in $u_1..u_k$ and in $v_1..v_k$, regular near 0, and $f$ with a simple pole of residue 1 at 0, $H=F\prod_{i,j}f(u_i-v_j)$: the $2k$-fold residue $\frac{(-1)^k}{k!^2(2\pi i)^{2k}}\oint H\Delta^2/\prod_{i,j}(z_i-\alpha_j)$ equals $\sum_{\sigma\in\Xi}H(\alpha_{\sigma(1)},\dots,\alpha_{\sigma(2k)})$, over the $\binom{2k}k$ permutations with $\sigma(1)<..<\sigma(k)$, $\sigma(k+1)<..<\sigma(2k)$.

$\int_0^TZ(\tfrac12+it+\alpha_1)\cdots Z(\tfrac12+it+\alpha_{2k})dt\sim\int_0^TP_k(\alpha,\log\frac t{2\pi})dt$ with $Z(s)=\chi(s)^{-1/2}\zeta(s)$, $-1/4<\Re\alpha_j$, $P_k(\alpha,x)$ the residue integral (1.10) around poles $z_i=\alpha_j$.

For $k=3,\dots,7$ and seventeen intervals $[50000n,50000(n+1)]$, $n=0..16$, the integral of $|\zeta|^{2k}$ (computed by integrating between consecutive zeros) agrees with $\int P_k(\log\frac t{2\pi})dt$ to ~3 significant figures or better (relative differences plotted in Figure 1); for non-integer $k=0.5,1.8,3.2,0.5+i$ the truncated series $\sum_{r\le R}c_r(k)\log(t/2\pi)^{k^2-r}$ is compared at $D=10^3,10^4,10^5$.
$\Delta(\partial_{x_1},\dots,\partial_{x_n})\prod_if(x_i)=\det\big(f^{(j-1)}(x_i)\big)_{n\times n}$.
role: Converts Vandermonde differential operator into a Wronskian-type determinant.

statement: $\Delta(\partial_{x_{1..2k}})\Delta(\partial_{x_{1..k}})\Delta(\partial_{x_{k+1..2k}})\prod_{i\le2k}f(x_i)$ at $x_{1..k}=1$, $x_{k+1..2k}=-1$ equals $k!^2\det$ of a $2k\times2k$ matrix with the first $k$ rows $f^{(i+j-2)}(1)$ and last $k$ rows $f^{(i+j-2)}(-1)$.
role: Gives the leading coefficient and the determinant $\tilde M_k$ for lower coefficients (with $f(x)=x^{2k-1}/(2k-1)!$ exponential generating structure).

statement: The determinant $\tilde M_k(\sigma(\alpha),\tau(\beta))$ in (2.63) vanishes unless $\alpha_{\sigma_1},\dots$ satisfy a distinctness/consecutiveness condition on the shifted indices (so only $O_r(1)$ rearrangements contribute).
role: Makes the sum over rearrangements finite and independent of $k$ in count.

statement: For $e_i,f_i$ with $e_1,e_2+1,..,e_k+k-1$ distinct and likewise $f$, the $2k\times2k$ determinant of reciprocal Gamma values reduces to a $k\times k$ determinant of binomial-type entries after eliminating the complementary subset $c_1..c_k$ of $\{0,..,2k-1\}$.
role: Step reducing $2k\times 2k$ to $k\times k$ determinant to prove polynomiality in $k$.

statement: If $c_j=k+j-1-\epsilon_j$ with $\epsilon_j=0$ for $j>t$ and $\tilde\lambda_1\ge\dots\ge\tilde\lambda_s>0=\tilde\lambda_{s+1}=\dots=\tilde\lambda_k$, then $\det\big((c_i)_{\tilde\lambda_j+k-j}\big)_{k\times k}=(-1)^{k(k-1)/2}\Delta(c)\times(\text{polynomial in }k\text{ of degree}\le2\sum\tilde\lambda_i)$.
role: Core of the polynomiality proof via Chen-Louck factorial Schur functions [CL].

statement: Evaluation of the Euler-factor integral $\int_0^1\prod_j(1-e(\theta)/p^{1/2+z_j})^{-1}(1-e(-\theta)/p^{1/2-z_{k+j}})^{-1}d\theta$ at zero shifts gives ${}_2F_1(k,k;1;1/p)$ (A,B,C integer statement; used to show $A_k(0)=a_k$).
role: Identifies leading arithmetic factor.
location: Sec. 2.1, Lemma 2.3 (statement summarized from line 787; hypotheses A,B>=1 integers, 0<=t<1)

statement: Let $T\ge H_0=3.0610046\cdot10^{10}$ and $\sigma\in[1/2,0.831]$. Then $N(\sigma,2T)-N(\sigma,T)\le a\,T^{1-\frac14(\sigma-\frac12)}\log T+b\log^2T+c\log T\log\log T+d\log T$ with $a=10395.2,\ b=1.104,\ c=0.173,\ d=0.51$. Here N(sigma,T) counts zeros with real part >sigma and 0<Im<=T.

For T>=2H_0: $N(\sigma,T)\le \frac{10395.21}{2^{1-\frac14(\sigma-\frac12)}-1}\,T^{1-\frac14(\sigma-\frac12)}\log\frac T2$; of interest only for sigma in (1/2,5/8] relative to Kadiri-Lumley-Ng bound (4).

For larger verification height (T>=10^{50}) and sigma in [1/2,0.569]: $N(\sigma,2T)-N(\sigma,T)\le5.357\,T^{1-\frac14(\sigma-\frac12)}\log T+1.11\log^2T$; the method cannot give a leading constant below 3.259.
hypotheses: T>=10^{50} (stated as T>=1050 in extracted text; exponent presumably lost)

statement: Explicit approximate functional equation $\zeta(s)=\sum_{n\le x}n^{-s}+\chi(s)\sum_{n\le y}n^{s-1}+R_1(s;x,y)$, $2\pi xy=|t|$, x,y>=1, sigma in [1/2,1], |t|>=2pi, with $|R_1|\le E x^{-\sigma}+F(|t|/2\pi)^{1/2-\sigma}y^{\sigma-1}$ and E,F tabulated (e.g. |t|>=2pi: E=36.094 (x<=y), F=127.126 (x>y); symmetric x=y: E=4.257; |t|>=10^3: 10.983/15.726/1.195).
location: Sec 2, Thm 4, Tables 1-3; general-parameter version Thm 6

statement: For sigma in (1/2,sigma_0], T>=T_0>=2pi, coprime integers 1<=mu_1<=mu_2<=T/2pi, S(z)=\int_T^{2T}|\zeta(\sigma+it)|^2(2\mu_1/\mu_2)^{it}... dt; then $|S-\tilde S|\le S_1(z)(\mu_2/\mu_1)^\sigma T^{1-\sigma/2}\log\frac{T\mu_2}{\pi\mu_1}+S_2(z)\mu_1\mu_2T^{1-\sigma}\log\frac{T\mu_1\mu_2}{\pi}$ with main term tilde S = zeta(2sigma)/(mu1 mu2)^sigma T + ...; S_1,S_2 explicit and bounded for fixed sigma_0,T_0.

For T>=2pi, $\int_0^T|\zeta(1/2+it)|^2dt=T\log T-(1+\log2\pi-2\gamma)T+E(T)$ with $|E(T)|\le13.803\,T^{3/4}\log\frac T{2\pi}+83.964\sqrt T\log\frac T{2\pi}+2\cdot10^3\log T+3691.24$ (proof via T_0=10^3, T>=2T_0).
Explicit approximate functional equations for zeta^2 (Dirichlet polynomials of length ~ |t|/2pi form) with explicit remainders for sigma in [1/2,1], |t|>=10^3.

For sigma_0 in (1/2,1), T>=T_0, X=T^{1/6-eps}, 0<eps<=1/6-1/((sigma_0-1/2)log T_0) (garbled in extraction): $\int_T^{2T}|\Phi_X(\sigma+it)|^2dt\le T+\phi(\sigma_0,T_0,\epsilon,T)T^{1-2(1/6-\epsilon)(\sigma-1/2)}$ for sigma in [1/2+1/((1/6-eps)log T), sigma_0], where Phi_X is the Selberg mollified zeta (zeta times Dirichlet-polynomial mollifier).
role: Explicit mean square of mollified zeta at height off the line; main input to Littlewood's lemma.

statement: For U>=T_0>2sigma_1-1>=3.8, U not an ordinate of a zero of Phi_X: $|\arg\Phi_X(\sigma+iU)|\le\frac{\pi(\frac12+\sigma_1)}{2\log2}\log U+\frac{\pi\sigma_1}{2\log2}\log X+\frac{\pi}{2\log2}\log\log X+b_3$, sigma in (0,sigma_1].
role: Explicit bound for the argument of mollified zeta, needed for horizontal segments in Littlewood's lemma.

statement: Corollary 7 (T or 2T not an ordinate of zero, X=T^{1/8}): $\frac1{2\pi}\int_\sigma^{\sigma_1}|\arg\Phi_X(\tau+2iT)|+|\arg\Phi_X(\tau+iT)|d\tau\le\frac1{2\pi}(\sigma_1-\frac12)\bigl(\frac{\pi(9\sigma_1+4)}{8\log2}\log T+\frac{\pi}{2\log2}\log\log T-\frac{\pi}{2}(11/2-\sigma_1)+2b_3\bigr)$.
role: Explicit contributions of arguments at horizontal edges.

statement: Explicit versions of Montgomery-Vaughan-type mean value/large-sieve inequalities for Dirichlet polynomials (Lemma 4 with sequences a_n, n<=X) and oscillatory integral/sum lemmas.
role: Control off-diagonal terms in Theorem 7 and Proposition 2.

statement: Explicit bounds for Dirichlet-series tails (sigma>=sigma_1>=2.4) and for zeta in the strip sigma in [1-sigma_1,sigma_1] used to bound log|Phi_X| on the right line.
role: Anchor Littlewood's lemma at sigma_1>=2.4.

statement: Assume RH. For large $x$, $M(x)\ll \sqrt{x}\,\exp\big((\log x)^{1/2}(\log\log x)^{14}\big)$.

Assume RH. Let $T$ be large, $0\le h\le\sqrt T$, $(\log\log T)^2\le V\le \log T/\log\log T$. The number $R$ of well-spaced points $T\le t_1<\dots<t_R\le 2T$ ($t_{j+1}-t_j\ge1$) with $N(t_j+h)-N(t_j-h)-\frac{h}{\pi}\log\frac{t_j}{2\pi}>V$ satisfies $R\ll T\exp\!\big(-V\log\frac{V}{\log\log T}+3V\log\log V\big)$.
hypotheses: ranges of h and V as stated

statement: $t\in[T,2T]$ is $V$-typical if (i) with $x=T^{1/V}$, $\big|\sum_{n\le x}\frac{\Lambda(n)\log(x/n)}{n^{\sigma+it}\log n\log x}\big|\le 2V$ for all $\sigma\ge1/2$; (ii) every subinterval of $(t-1,t+1)$ of length $2\pi V/\log T$ contains at most $3V$ zero ordinates; (iii) every subinterval of $(t-1,t+1)$ of length $2\pi V/((\log V)\log T)$ contains at most $V$ zero ordinates.

Assume RH. Every $t\in[T,2T]$ is $V$-typical when $V\ge(\tfrac12+o(1))\log T/\log\log T$. For $(\log\log T)^2\le V\le\log T/\log\log T$ the number of well-spaced $V$-atypical points in $[T,2T]$ is $R\ll T\exp(-V\log\frac{V}{\log\log T}+4V\log\log V)$.

Assume RH, $T\le t\le 2T$ $V$-typical for some $(\log\log T)^2\le V\le\log T/\log\log T$, $\sigma_0=\frac12+\frac V{\log T}$. For $2\ge\sigma\ge\sigma_0$: $\log|\zeta(\sigma+it)|\ge -V\log\log V$ (stated; proof gives $\ge -CV$). For $\frac12<\sigma\le\sigma_0$: $\log|\zeta(\sigma+it)|\ge -V\log\frac{\sigma_0-1/2}{\sigma-1/2}-8V\log\log V$.

Selberg/Beurling-Vaaler extremal minorant and majorant $F_\pm$ of $\chi_{[-h,h]}$: even entire, $F_-\le\chi\le F_+$, $\int|F_\pm-\chi|\le1/\Delta$, $\hat F_\pm(x)=0$ for $|x|\ge\Delta$, $\hat F_\pm(x)=\frac{\sin 2\pi hx}{\pi x}+O(1/\Delta)$, and $|F_\pm(z)|\ll e^{2\pi\Delta|y|}/(\Delta|z|^2)$ for $|z|\ge2h$.
role: Band-limited approximation to the indicator of an interval, fed into the explicit formula (imported, Selberg/Vaaler)

statement: Explicit formula for $\sum_\rho h(\gamma)$ with $h$ analytic in $|\mathrm{Im}\,s|\le\frac12+\epsilon$, $|h(s)|\ll(1+|s|)^{-1-\delta}$.
role: Converts zero counting in a window into a prime sum (imported, standard)

statement: Large-sieve-type moment inequality: for $A(s)=\sum_{p\le N}a(p)p^{-s}$, well-spaced $s_r=\sigma_r+it_r$, $\sigma_r\ge\alpha$, $N^k\le T$: $\sum_r|A(s_r)|^{2k}\ll T(\log T)^2k!\big(\sum_{p\le N}|a(p)|^2p^{-2\alpha}\big)^k$.
role: High-moment bound on prime sums at well-spaced points; the source of the exp(-V log V) tail (imported from Maier-Montgomery Lemma 5)

statement: For $T\le t\le2T$ $V$-typical and $\frac12<\sigma\le\sigma_0$: $\log|\zeta(\sigma+it)|\ge\log|\zeta(\sigma_0+it)|-V\log\frac{\sigma_0-1/2}{\sigma-1/2}-7V\log\log V$.
role: Propagates the bound from sigma_0 toward the critical line using zero spacing conditions (ii),(iii)

statement: Uniformly for $\frac12<\sigma\le2$, $2\le x\le T$: $\log|\zeta(\sigma+it)|\ge\mathrm{Re}\sum_{n\le x}\frac{\Lambda(n)\log(x/n)}{n^{\sigma+it}\log n\log x}-\Big(1+\frac{x^{1/2-\sigma}}{(\sigma-1/2)\log x}\Big)\frac{F(\sigma+it)}{\log x}+O(1)$, where $F(s)=\sum_\rho\mathrm{Re}\frac1{s-\rho}$.
role: Smoothed prime-sum lower bound for log|zeta| in terms of zero-sum F

statement: For $t\in[T,2T]$ $V$-typical and $2\ge\sigma\ge\sigma_0$ there is an absolute $C$ with $\log|\zeta(\sigma+it)|\ge -CV$.
role: Gives (3) of Prop 5

statement: For continuous $f:[0,2\pi]^n\to\mathbb C$: $\int_{U(N)}\sum^*_{1\le j_1,\dots,j_n\le N}f(\theta_{j_1},\dots,\theta_{j_n})dX_N=\frac1{(2\pi)^n}\int_{[0,2\pi]^n}f(\theta_1,\dots,\theta_n)\det_{n\times n}S_N(\theta_k-\theta_j)d\theta_1\cdots d\theta_n$, $S_N(\theta)=\frac{\sin(N\theta/2)}{\sin(\theta/2)}$, sum over distinct indices.

For $\Re\gamma>0,\Re\delta>0$ ($\gamma\in C,\delta\in D$), $|C|\le|A|+N$, $|D|\le|B|+N$: $R(A,B;C,D)=\sum_{S\subset A,T\subset B,|S|=|T|}e^{-N(\sum_{\hat\alpha\in S}\hat\alpha+\sum_{\hat\beta\in T}\hat\beta)}Z(S+T^-,T+S^-;C,D)$, where $A=S+S^-$, $B=T+T^-$ and $Z$ is the ratio of $z$-products (eq. (20)).

If $\Re\alpha_j>0$, $\Re\beta_j>0$ for $\alpha_j\in A,\beta_j\in B$, then $J(A;B)=J^*(A;B)$, where $J(A;B)=\int_{U(N)}\prod_{\alpha\in A}\big(-e^{-\alpha}\tfrac{\Lambda_X'}{\Lambda_X}(e^{-\alpha})\big)\prod_{\beta\in B}\big(-e^{-\beta}\tfrac{\Lambda_{X^*}'}{\Lambda_{X^*}}(e^{-\beta})\big)dX$ and $J^*$ is an explicit sum over set partitions with factors $e^{-N(\ldots)}Z(S,T)Z(S^-,T^-)\times$ (sums over partitions of the remaining shifts as in Lemma 1).

Let $C_\mp$ be vertical paths $-\delta+\pi i\to-\delta-\pi i$ and $\delta-\pi i\to\delta+\pi i$ and $f$ a $2\pi$-periodic holomorphic function of $n$ variables. Then $\int_{U(N)}\sum_{j_1,\dots,j_n=1}^Nf(\theta_{j_1},\dots,\theta_{j_n})dX$ is expressed as a sum over $K+L+M=\{1..n\}$ of $N^{|M|}$ times $n$-fold contour integrals of $J(-iz_K;iz_L)f(z)$ over $C_\pm$ (all indices, not distinct).

With $J^*$ as in Theorem 3: $\int_{U(N)}\sum^*_{1\le j_1,\dots,j_n\le N}f(\theta_{j_1},\dots,\theta_{j_n})dX_N=\frac1{(2\pi)^n}\int_{[0,2\pi]^n}\sum_{K+L+M=\{1,\dots,n\}}N^{|M|}J^*(-i\theta_K;i\theta_L)f(\theta_1,\dots,\theta_n)d\theta_1\cdots d\theta_n$ (distinct indices, integration along the imaginary axis; the integrand has no poles on the path). Moving contours onto the imaginary axis gives principal value terms that cancel exactly with extra terms in Theorem 4. Proven via the more general Theorem 6 (parameter $0\le R\le n$, by induction).

With $Z_\zeta(A,B)=\prod_{\alpha\in A,\beta\in B}\zeta(1+\alpha+\beta)$, $Z_\zeta(A,B;C,D)=\frac{Z_\zeta(A,B)Z_\zeta(C,D)}{Z_\zeta(A,D)Z_\zeta(B,C)}$, and $A_\zeta=\prod_pZ_p\int_0^1A_{p,\theta}d\theta$: the integral over an interval $I$ of ratios of shifted zeta functions equals $\int_I\big[\text{sum over swaps }(t/2\pi)^{\ldots}Z_\zeta A_\zeta\big]dt+O(|I|^{1/2+\epsilon})$ (same structure as CAND-01203 Conj 5.1), valid in the standard shift ranges.

Assuming the ratios conjecture, if $\Re\alpha_i,\Re\beta_j>0$ then $J_{\zeta,I}(A;B;U)=J^*_{\zeta,I}(A;B;U)+O(|I|^{1/2+\epsilon})$ where $J_{\zeta,I}=\int_I\prod_{\alpha\in A}\frac{\zeta'}{\zeta}(\tfrac12+it+\alpha)\prod_{\beta\in B}\frac{\zeta'}\zeta(\tfrac12-it+\beta)\prod_{\mu\in U}\big(-\tfrac{\chi'}\chi(\tfrac12+it+\mu)\big)dt$ and $J^*_{\zeta,I}=\int_IJ^*_{\zeta,t}dt$ with $J^*_{\zeta,t}$ the analogue of $J^*$ with $N\to\log(t/2\pi)$-type factors and arithmetic factors.

Assume RH and Ratios Conjecture 1. For $f$ holomorphic: $\sum_{0<\gamma_1\ne\cdots\ne\gamma_n\le T}f(\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_n)=\frac1{(2\pi)^n}\int_{[-T,T]^n}\frac1T\int_{I^*}\sum_{K+L+M=\{1..n\}}J^*_{\zeta,t}(-iz_K;iz_L;iz_M)\,dt\,f(z_1,\dots,z_n)dz_1\cdots dz_n+O(T^{1/2+\epsilon})$ with the integrand having no poles on the path; Corollary 2 (translation invariance of $f$) rewrites this as $\frac1{(2\pi)^n}\int_0^T\int\ldots J^*_{\zeta,t}(-iz_K+it;iz_L-it;iz_M-it)f(z)\,dz\,dt$. In the scaling limit, arithmetic terms vanish and the leading term is the determinantal $\det S(z_j-z_k)$ form for arbitrary $f$ (stated in the text, Sec 1, with proof sketched via the RMT formula).
For differentiable $H$ of $w\in W$: $\prod_{w\in W}\frac d{dw}e^H=e^H\sum_{W=W_1+\cdots+W_r}H(W_1)\cdots H(W_r)$ (Faa di Bruno formulation by set partitions).
role: Converts derivatives of the ratios theorem into the logarithmic derivative averages $J(A;B)$.

statement: Suppose $\alpha^*\in A,\beta^*\in B$, $A'=A-\{\alpha^*\}$, $B'=B-\{\beta^*\}$. Then $J^*(A;B)$ has at most a simple pole at $\alpha^*+\beta^*=0$ with explicit residue $\propto J^*(A';B')$ (residue identity).
role: Key for moving contour integrals to the imaginary axis (no poles on path; principal value terms cancel).

statement: Zeta analogues of Lemmas 1 and 2 (residue identity for $J^*_{\zeta}$) used in Sec 4.3 to prove Theorem 8 (contour version) and Theorem 9.
role: Transfers the RMT residue structure to the ratios conjecture setting.

statement: With $0\le R\le n$, $(2\pi i)^n\int_{U(N)}\sum^{n,R}f(\theta_{j_1},\dots,\theta_{j_n})dX=\sum_{K+L+M=\{1..n\}}(-1)^{|(L+M)\cap\{1..R\}|}N^{|M|}I^{n,R}_{f;K,L,M}$, where indices $1..R$ run over distinct-sum and the remaining $n-R$ over all indices; proved by induction on $n$ and $R$ (move $z_R$ integral to the imaginary axis, residues at $z_R=z_t$).
role: Induction engine interpolating between Theorem 4 (R=0) and Theorem 5 (R=n).

statement: Contour-shifted version of the ratios-conjecture $n$-correlation formula over $C_\pm$ analogous to Thm 4 (with vertical segments of height $T$ contributing only $O(T^\epsilon)$).
role: Intermediate step to Theorem 9.

statement: $\Lambda>3.18$, where $\Lambda=\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{t_{n+1}-t_n}{2\pi/\log t_n}$ over consecutive zeros on the critical line. Consequently, assuming RH, $\lambda>3.18$ for consecutive zeros $\gamma_n$.

$\Lambda^\star>4.05$, where $\Lambda^\star=\limsup (t^\star_{n+1}-t^\star_n)/(2\pi/\log t_n^\star)$ over ordinates of multiple zeros on the critical line (set $\Lambda^\star=\infty$ if only finitely many multiple zeros).
hypotheses: unconditional; vacuous-in-spirit if no multiple zeros

statement: For f,f' continuous complex-valued on [a,b]: (i) if $f(a)=f(b)=0$ then $\int_a^b|f|^2\le((b-a)/\pi)^2\int_a^b|f'|^2$; (ii) if $f(a)=f(b)$ and $\int_a^bf=0$ then $\int_a^b|f|^2\le((b-a)/2\pi)^2\int_a^b|f'|^2$.

For $\vartheta<1/4$, $F(t,v,\kappa,M)=e^{ivtL}\zeta(\tfrac12+it)\zeta(\tfrac12+it+i\tfrac{\kappa\pi}{L})M(\tfrac12+it)$, $M(s)=\sum_{h\le y}d_r(h)P[h]h^{-s}$, $y=T^\vartheta$: $\int|F^{(j)}|^2w(t/T)dt=\frac{c_j(v,\kappa)A_{r+2}(\log y)^{r^2+4r}L^{4+2j}}{2(r^2-1)!((r-1)!)^4}\hat w(0)T+O(TL^{(r+2)^2+2j-1})$, j=0,1,2, with $c_j$ an explicit 9-fold integral over $[0,1]^9$.
hypotheses: w smooth supported in [1,2] with w^{(j)}<<T^eps

statement: If $\Lambda\le\kappa$ then $\int_T^{2T}|F|^2\le(1+o(1))\frac{\kappa^2}{L^2}\int_T^{2T}|F'|^2$, so $h_1:=\limsup\frac{L^2}{\kappa^2}\frac{\int|F|^2}{\int|F'|^2}>1$ implies $\Lambda>\kappa$ (apply Wirtinger (i) between consecutive zeros of F; F mimics a real function via factor $e^{ivtL}$).
role: Reduction of gap problem to mean-value ratios.

statement: For multiple zeros a,b of F one has $F'(a)=F'(b)=0$ and $\int_a^bF'=0$, so Wirtinger (ii) gives $\int|F'|^2\le((b-a)/2\pi)^2\int|F''|^2$; $h_2:=\limsup\frac{4L^2}{\kappa^2}\frac{\int|F'|^2}{\int|F''|^2}>1$ implies $\Lambda^\star>\kappa$.
role: First use of Wirtinger (ii) for zeros of zeta.

statement: For $\vartheta<1/4$ and shifts $\alpha_j,\beta_j\ll L^{-1}$, $I_{\alpha,\beta}(M)=\int\zeta(\tfrac12+\alpha_1+it)\zeta(\tfrac12+\alpha_2+it)\zeta(\tfrac12+\beta_1-it)\zeta(\tfrac12+\beta_2-it)M(\tfrac12+\alpha_3+it)M(\tfrac12+\beta_3-it)w(t/T)dt=\frac{c(\alpha,\beta)A_{r+2}(\log y)^{r^2+4r}L^4}{2(r^2-1)!((r-1)!)^4}\hat w(0)T+O(TL^{(r+2)^2-1})$ uniformly, with c(alpha,beta) an explicit integral over [0,1]^9.
role: Core shifted twisted fourth-moment asymptotic; derivatives in shifts (Cauchy integral formula on radius ~1/L) give the j=1,2 mean values.

statement: Twisted fourth moment of zeta against Dirichlet polynomial of length $y=T^\vartheta$, $\vartheta<1/4$, with explicit six-term main term $Z_{\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\beta_1,\beta_2,h,k}$ and error $O_\epsilon(T^{1/2+2\vartheta+\epsilon}+T^{3/4+\vartheta+\epsilon})$.
role: Imported input extending admissible length from 1/11 (Hughes-Young) to 1/4.

statement: Lemma 4.1: evaluation of sums over $d_r$-weighted divisor-type sums producing Mellin-Barnes integrals; Lemma 4.2: smooth-function identity used to convert sums over $h,k\le y$ into the 9-dimensional integral.
role: Combinatorial/analytic evaluation of the off-diagonal main terms.

statement: RH is equivalent to: $\sigma(n)/(n\log\log n)<e^{\gamma}/2$ for all odd $n\ge c_0=18565284664427130919514350125=3^4\cdot5^3\cdot7^2\cdot11\cdot13\cdots67$.
hypotheses: Equivalence; the forward direction assumes RH

statement: RH is equivalent to $\sigma(n)\le \frac{3n}{\log n}+\exp(H_n')\log H_n'$ for all odd $n\ge3$, where $H_n'=2H_n-H_{2n}=\sum_{k=1}^{n}1/k-\sum_{k=n+1}^{2n}1/k\cdot(-1)\ldots$, as defined by $H_n'=2\sum_{k\le n}1/k-\sum_{k\le 2n}1/k$.
Unconditionally, odd squarefree $n\ge4849845$ satisfy $\sigma(n)/(n\log\log n)<e^{\gamma}/2$.
As n runs through odd squarefree integers, $\limsup \sigma(n)/(n\log\log n)= 4e^{\gamma}/\pi^{2}$ (read from the text extraction).

If $n=2^k m$ with $m$ odd squarefree and $n\ge841$, then Robin's inequality $\sigma(n)<e^{\gamma}n\log\log n$ holds, unconditionally. This extends the Chandee-type/Choie et al. result for squarefree n>30.

If p does not divide n, then $f(p^k n)<f(n)$ under an explicit condition relating $\log n$ and $p^k$ (Thm 5.6, so that the exponent of 2 maximizing $f(2^m n)$ is determined by the equation $(\log xn)(\log\log xn)-2x+1=0$ with $x=2^k$). Prop 5.11 shows the optimal k increases with n.

For $0<\epsilon\le -1+\log_3 4$, odd colossally abundant numbers are $N=\prod_{p\ge3}p^{\alpha_p(\epsilon)}$ with $\alpha_p(\epsilon)=\lfloor\log(p^{1+\epsilon}-1)-\log(p-1))/\log p\rfloor-1$ (for 1+eps exponents as in (2.1)).
role: explicit parametrisation of odd CA numbers, the extremal set

statement: For odd CA N with parameters $x_1>x_2$: if $x_2\ge347$ then $\log N>\theta_0(x_1)+0.998x_2$; if $x_1\ge120409$ then $\log\log N>\log\theta(x_1)\exp(0.99154\,x_2/(x_1\log x_1))$.
role: effective Chebyshev-type estimates controlling log log N

statement: If an odd n violates the odd analogue of Robin's inequality and $N\le n\le N'$ are consecutive odd CA numbers, then N or N' violates it.
role: reduces the verification to odd colossally abundant numbers (as in Robin's [13, Sec 3, Prop 1])

statement: Assuming RH, $\sigma(n)/(n\log\log n)<e^\gamma/2$ for all odd $n\ge c_0$; verified by computer for odd CA numbers with $61<x_1<120409$ (actually up to $x_1\le10^6$) and analytically for $x_1\ge120409$ using Robin-style explicit bounds on theta(x) under RH.
role: forward direction of Thm 1.2

statement: 4.4: assuming RH, if odd n violates the Lagarias-analogue and $N_1\le n\le N_2$ with $N_1\ge490$ consecutive odd CA, then N_1 or N_2 violates it. 4.5: if RH is false there are $0<\beta<1/2$, $C>0$ with $\sigma(N)\ge \frac{e^\gamma}{2}N\log\log N+CN\log\log N/(\log N)^\beta$ for infinitely many odd CA N.
role: reduction and the reverse direction for the Lagarias analogue

statement: Let $\theta>0$ and suppose that for every $\varepsilon>0$, $I_N(0,T)\ll_\varepsilon T^{1+\varepsilon}$ uniformly for $2\le N\le T^\theta$, where $I_N(T_1,T_2)=\int_{T_1}^{T_2}|M_N(\tfrac12+it)|^2|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|^2dt$ and $M_N(s)=\sum_{n\le N}\frac{\mu(n)}{n^s}\big(1-\frac{\log n}{\log N}\big)$. Then $\zeta(s)$ has no zeros in $\Re s>\tfrac12+\tfrac1{2\theta}$. In particular, if this holds with $\theta$ arbitrarily large, RH is true.

Let $\theta>0$ and suppose for every $\varepsilon>0$, $I_N(T,2T)\ll_\varepsilon T^{1+\varepsilon}$ for $2\le N\le T^\theta$. Then $\zeta(s)$ has no zeros in $\Re s>\tfrac12+\tfrac2\theta$; if true for arbitrarily large $\theta$, RH holds (nontrivial only for $\theta>4$).

If $\zeta$ had a unique simple zero $\rho_0=\beta_0+i\gamma_0$, $\gamma_0>0$, $\beta_0>1/2$, then $I_N(T,2T)=c_1\frac{N^{2\beta_0-1}\log T}{T^3\log^2N}\big(1+\Re N^{2i\gamma_0}\frac{|\zeta'(\rho_0)|^2}{\zeta'(\rho_0)^2}+o(1)\big)+O(T^{1+\varepsilon}+N^{\beta_0-1/2+\varepsilon}/T)$, consistent with the bound only if $\theta<4$; and $I_N(0,T)=\frac{N^{2\beta_0-1}}{\log^2N}(C(N)+o(1))+O(T^{1+\varepsilon}+N^{\beta_0-1/2+\varepsilon}T^\varepsilon)$ with $C(N)$ bounded away from 0 (stated without proof), so $I_{T^\theta}(0,T)\ll T^{1+\varepsilon}$ implies $\beta_0\le\frac12+\frac1{2\theta}$.
location: Introduction after Theorem 2 (formulas as printed, no proof given)

statement: $g_t(u)=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{3-i\infty}^{3+i\infty}G_t(w)u^{-w}dw$ vanishes for $u>1$ and is $O(1)$ for $0\le u\le1$ (G_t holomorphic in $\Re w\ge0$ with $G_t(w)\ll(1+|w+it|)^{-5/2}$).
role: Compactly supported kernel making the Mellin convolution J_t(x) depend only on M_y for y<=x

statement: $J_t(x)=\frac1{2\pi i}\int G_tH_tx^wdw$ satisfies $J_t(x)\ll\int_1^x|M_y(\tfrac12+it)|\log y\,dy$ and, by shifting to $\Re w=0$, $J_t(x)=O(1)+\frac{x^{\rho_0+\frac12-it}(\rho_0-1)}{(\frac32+\rho_0-it)^2(\rho_0+\frac32)^4}$ (residue at the pole w=rho_0+1/2-it of 1/zeta(w-1/2+it)).
role: Isolates a single off-line zero rho_0 as a growing term x^{beta_0+1/2}/(1+|t|)^2 dominating the mollifier integral
