statement: Cauchy-Schwarz gives $\frac{x^{2\beta_0}}{(1+|t|)^4}+\frac1x\ll\int_1^x|M_y(\tfrac12+it)|^2\log^2y\,dy$; multiplying by $|\zeta(\frac12+it)|^2$ and integrating over [T_1,T_2] with $\int_{T_1}^{T_2}|\zeta(1/2+it)|^2dt\gg T_2\log(T_2+2)$ ($0\le T_1\le T_2/2$) gives $\frac{x^{2\beta_0}\log(T_1+2)}{|1+T_1|^3}+\frac{T_2\log(T_2+2)}{x}\ll\log^2x\int_1^xI_y(T_1,T_2)dy$.
role: Converts pointwise lower bound into lower bound for the mollified second moment

statement: Assume RH. For sufficiently large t, $|S(t)|\le\left(\frac14+o(1)\right)\frac{\log t}{\log\log t}$ with the $o(1)$ term $O(\log\log\log t/\log\log t)$.

Let $L(s,\pi)$ be an L-function of degree m with the stated analytic hypotheses (Euler product with $|\alpha_{j,\pi}(p)|\le p^\vartheta$, completed $\Lambda(s,\pi)=L(s,\pi_\infty)L(s,\pi)$ entire of order 1 up to poles at 0,1, functional equation $\Lambda(s,\pi)=\kappa\Lambda(1-s,\tilde\pi)$, $\Re\mu_j>-1$). Assume GRH for $\Lambda(s,\pi)$. Then for all $t>0$: $|S(t,\pi)|\le\left(\frac14+\frac\vartheta2\right)\frac{\log C(t,\pi)}{\log\log[C(t,\pi)^{3/m}]}+O\left(\frac{\log C(t,\pi)\log\log\log[C(t,\pi)^{3/m}]}{(\log\log[C(t,\pi)^{3/m}])^2}\right)$, and consequently $\mathrm{ord}_{s=1/2}\Lambda(s,\pi)\le\left(\frac12+\vartheta\right)\frac{\log C(\pi)}{\log\log[C(\pi)^{3/m}]}+O\left(\frac{\log C(\pi)\log\log\log[C(\pi)^{3/m}]}{(\log\log[C(\pi)^{3/m}])^2}\right)$, with universal implied constants, where $C(t,\pi)=C(\pi)(|t|+1)^m$, $C(\pi)=N\prod_j(|\mu_j|+3)$ is the analytic conductor.
location: Sec 4, eqs (4.4)-(4.5); proof in Sec 4. NOTE: as extracted, the order-of-vanishing constant in (4.5) reads 1/2+vartheta (consistent with S(t,pi)+S(t,pi~) giving a factor of 2); I did not verify the printed constant beyond this reading.

statement: Let $\pi$ be an irreducible unitary cuspidal representation of GL(m) over Q. Assuming GRH for $L(s,\pi)$, $|S(t,\pi)|\le\frac m4\frac{\log t}{\log\log t}+O\left(\frac{\log t\,\log\log\log t}{(\log\log t)^2}\right)$ for t sufficiently large, with the implied constant depending on m and on pi.
conditional_on: Rankin-Selberg: L(s,pi x pi~) has a simple pole at s=1 (imported)

statement: Assume GRH for $\Lambda(s,\pi)$. Then there is a zero $\rho_\pi=\frac12+i\gamma_\pi$ of $\Lambda(s,\pi)$ with $|\gamma_\pi|\le\left(\frac12+\vartheta\right)\frac{\pi}{\log\log[C(\pi)^{3/m}]}+O\left(\frac{\log\log\log C(\pi)^{3/m}}{(\log\log[C(\pi)^{3/m}])^2}\right)$ when $C(\pi)^{3/m}$ is sufficiently large, universal implied constant.
location: Sec 5. NOTE: the printed form in the extracted text has pi/(loglog) with factor (1/2+vartheta); the exact placement of constants was read from a garbled extraction.

statement: Under GRH: Dirichlet L(s,chi) mod q: $|S(t,\chi)|\le(\frac14+o(1))\frac{\log q(|t|+1)}{\log\log q(|t|+1)}$ and $\mathrm{ord}_{1/2}\le(\frac12+o(1))\frac{\log q}{\log\log q}$. Weight k level q newform: bound with $\log q(k+3)^{?}$ factors and constants 1/2 for the S-bound (as printed: $\frac12+o(1)$) and 1 for ord. Dedekind zeta of K: $|S_K(t)|\le\frac{[K:Q]}{4}\frac{\log r_{d_K}(|t|+3)}{\log\log r_{d_K}(|t|+3)}$ and $\mathrm{ord}_{1/2}\zeta_K\le(\frac12+o(1))\frac{\log(|d_K|+3)}{\log\log(|d_K|+3)}$.
location: Sec 6, Examples 8, 9, 10 (the displayed constants for Example 9 are partly garbled in the extraction; see audit_notes)

statement: Beurling-Selberg: for the even real entire functions $R^\pm(z)=\frac12\{H^\pm(\Delta(t+z))+H^\pm(\Delta(t-z))\}$: (i) $R^-\le\chi_{[-t,t]}\le R^+$; (ii) $\int|R^\pm-\chi_{[-t,t]}|=1/\Delta$; (iii) $R^\pm(z)\ll e^{2\pi\Delta|\Im z|}$; (iv) $R^\pm(x)\ll\min(1,\Delta^{-2}(|x|-t)^{-2})$ for $|x|>t$; (v) $\hat R^\pm(\xi)=0$ for $|\xi|\ge\Delta$; (vi) $\hat R^\pm(\xi)=\frac{\sin2\pi t\xi}{\pi\xi}+O(1/\Delta)$ for $|\xi|\le\Delta$.
role: The key point: the L^1 gap 1/Delta does not depend on the interval length, so the symmetric interval [-t,t] is as sharp as [0,t] and gives S(t)-S(-t)=2S(t), the factor 2 gain over Goldston-Gonek.

statement: For all t>0, $N(t)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{-t}^t\frac{\Gamma_R'}{\Gamma_R}(\frac12+iu)du+S(t)+1$ where $N(t)$ counts zeros with $0<\gamma\le t$ (weight 1/2 at endpoint) and $\Gamma_R(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)$.
role: Symmetric form of the zero-counting formula via functional equation.

statement: Guinand-Weil explicit formula (same as Lemma 5 of CAND-01181 but with the argument normalized with $h((\rho-1/2)/i)$), imported from Goldston-Gonek Lemma 1.
role: Connects zeros to prime sums.

statement: Assuming RH, the Pair Correlation Conjecture is equivalent to $\int_1^X(\psi(x+h)-\psi(x)-h)^2dx\sim hX\log(X/h)$ uniformly for $X^{\epsilon}\le h\le X^{1-\epsilon}$ (quoted as ref. [3]; the paper's displayed range 'X^e <= h <= X^{1-e}' is partly garbled in the extract). The Cramer model would instead predict $\sim hX\log X$.

For $0\le x\le X=10^{10}$ and $h=10^5$, the moments $\mu_k=\frac1X\int_0^X(\psi(x+h)-\psi(x)-h)^kdx$ were computed. They give $\mu_2=9.0663\times10^5$ (the Cramer prediction is $h\log X=23.02\times10^5$ and the PCC prediction $h\log(X/h)=11.51\times10^5$). The normalized moments $\tilde\mu_4\approx3.04$ and $\tilde\mu_6\approx15.53$ (Gaussian values 3 and 15) show the distribution is close to normal, with a slightly heavy sixth moment. The extremes are about $+5.30\sigma$ and $-5.17\sigma$. $\operatorname{meas}\{x\le10^{10}:|\psi(x+10^5)-\psi(x)-10^5|>3000\}=3080882$, fewer than expected for a Gaussian.

Let $\mathfrak S(k)=\prod_{p\mid k}\bigl(1-\frac1{p-1}\bigr)\prod_{p\nmid k}\bigl(1-\frac1{(p-1)^2}\bigr)$ for even $k$ and $0$ for odd $k$ (written as $2C\prod_{p\mid k,p>2}\frac{p-1}{p-2}$ with $C=\prod_{p>2}(1-(p-1)^{-2})$ for even $k$). Then, for every $\epsilon>0$, $\sum_{k=1}^{h}(h-k)\mathfrak S(k)=\tfrac12h^2-\tfrac12h\log h+Ah+O(h^{1/2+\epsilon})$ with $A=(1-\gamma_0-\log 2)/2$ ($\gamma_0$ Euler's constant).

Given the Theorem and the Hardy-Littlewood conjecture with $E(X,k)\ll X^{1/2+\epsilon}$ uniformly in $1\le k\le X$ and cancellation in the error sum: $\int_0^X(\psi(x+h)-\psi(x)-h)^2dx=hX\log(X/h)+BhX+\text{smaller terms}$, with $B=\gamma_0-\log2\pi... $ in the extract. The extract gives $B=C_0-\log 2=\,$'2.41509' (garbled), and the printed value $2.41509$ cannot equal $\gamma_0-\log 2$ read literally. Treat the exact closed form of $B$ as unverified against the PDF image. The conjectured error is $\ll h^{1/2}X^{1/2+\epsilon}+h^{3/2+\epsilon}X^{1/2}$.
conditional_on: quantitative Hardy-Littlewood prime-pair conjecture with E(X,k) << X^{1/2+eps}

statement: With $s(k)=\prod_{p\mid k,p>2}\frac{p-1}{p-2}$, $\sum_{k\le h}(h-k)\mathfrak S(k)=2\sum_{k\le h/2}(h/2-k)\,s(k)\cdot 2$ after the even-$k$ substitution, so it suffices to show $\sum_{k\le K}(K-k)s(k)=\frac{K^2}{2}\cdot\frac{?}{}$ ... (extract: $=\frac{K^2}{2}\cdot\frac{2}{\pi^2}$-type main term) $-\frac{K\log K}{2}+\frac K2(1-\gamma_0-\log 4)$ plus an error term. The exact constant in front of $K^2$ in the extract is garbled.
role: reduces the Theorem to a Dirichlet series computation

statement: $S(s)=\sum_{k\ge1}s(k)k^{-s}=\zeta(s)T(s)$ with $T(s)=\prod_{p>2}\bigl(1+\frac{p-2}{(p-1)... }\bigr)$ (symbol-level garbled); $T(s)=\zeta(s+1)^{-1}(1-2^{-s-1})\,U(s)$ for $\Re s>-1/2$, where $U$ is an absolutely convergent Euler product with $U(0)=2/\pi^2\cdot$(the extract prints $2/\pi$, ambiguous) and $U'(0)=0$.
role: Perron/Mellin representation of the Cesaro sum

statement: Writing $\sum_{k\le K}(K-k)s(k)=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{(a)}S(s)\frac{K^{s+1}}{s(s+1)}ds$ ($a>1$) and shifting to $\Re s=b\in(-1/2,0)$ picks up a simple pole at $s=1$ (from $\zeta$) and a double pole at $s=0$ (using $\zeta(s+1)=1/s+\gamma_0+O(|s|)$, $\zeta(0)=-1/2$, $\zeta'(0)=-\frac12\log2\pi$). The remaining integral is $\ll_b K^{b+1}$, using the functional equation with Stirling and the mean-square estimate for $\zeta$ on $[\frac12+\eta,\ldots]$ (Titchmarsh Thm 7.2) with Cauchy-Schwarz.
role: gives the $K\log K$ and linear secondary terms

statement: There is an absolute, effectively computable constant $A_1$ such that for every finite extension $K/\mathbb{Q}$, every finite Galois extension $L/K$ and every conjugacy class $C\subset \mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$, there exists a prime ideal $P$ of $K$ unramified in $L$ with $\left[\frac{L/K}{P}\right]=C$, $N_{K/\mathbb{Q}}P$ a rational prime, and $N_{K/\mathbb{Q}}P\le 2\,d_L^{A_1}$.

There is an absolute effectively computable constant $A_2$ such that for every number field $K$ and Hecke character $\chi$ of $K$: if $\zeta_K(s)L(s,\chi,K)$ has no zeros $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ with $1-\delta\le\beta<1$, $0<|\gamma|\le \delta^{-2}... $ (region of height $\delta^{2}(\log A(\chi))(1+c_3(\log A(\chi))^{1/2})$ as printed; OCR garbled) for some $\delta$ with $(c_2\log A(\chi))^{-1}\le\delta\le 1/2$, and $\zeta_K$ has no zero on $[1-\delta,1]$, then there is a prime ideal $P$ of degree 1 over $\mathbb{Q}$ with $\chi(P)\neq1$ and $N_{K/\mathbb{Q}}P<(A_2\,\delta^{-1}\log A(\chi))^{1/\delta}$ (exact form of last bound garbled). Here $A(\chi)=d_KN_{K/\mathbb{Q}}f(\chi)$.
hypotheses: zero-free region hypothesis on zeta_K L(s,chi,K) as stated
conditional_on: zero-free region of the stated shape

statement: There is an absolute effective constant $A_3$ such that for every number field $K$ and Hecke character $\chi$ of $K$, if $\zeta_K(s)L(s,\chi,K)$ has no zeros $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ in the region $\tfrac12<\beta<1$ (written 1/2<beta<1, with |gamma| bounded as in Thm 1.2 at delta=1/2; OCR garbled), then there is a degree-1 prime $P$ with $\chi(P)\ne1$ and $N_{K/\mathbb{Q}}P<A_3(\log A(\chi))^2$. (K=Q: Ankeny.)

There are absolute effective constants $c_7,c_8>0$ such that if $\zeta_L(s)$ has a real zero $\beta_0>0$ then $\zeta_L(\sigma+it)\ne0$ for $\sigma>1-c_8\,\log\!\big(c_7 d_L^{-1}... /\log\tau...\big)/\log d_L\tau^{n_L}$ with $\tau=|t|+2$, apart from $\sigma+it=\beta_0$ (displayed bound garbled in OCR).
There is an absolute effective constant $c_{10}$ such that any real zero $\beta_0$ of $\zeta_L(s)$ satisfies $1-\beta_0>d_L^{-c_{10}}$.

There are absolute effective constants $A_4,A_5$ such that if $L\ne\mathbb{Q}$ and $x>\exp\{A_4(\log d_L)(\log\log d_L)(\log\log\log d_L^{e^{2}})\}$ (OCR garbled), then $\pi_C(x)\le A_5\frac{|C|}{|G|}\mathrm{Li}(x)$.
location: Sec.1, p.274; proof sketched in Sec.7

statement: Let $s_j=\sum_{n\ge1}b_nz_n^j$ with (i) $|z_n|<|z_1|$ for all $n>1$, (ii) $b_n$ real, (iii) $b_n\ge0$ for those $n$ with $\tfrac13|z_1|<|z_n|<\ldots$ (as printed). Set $L=(b_1|z_1|)^{-1}\sum_n|b_nz_n|$. Then there exists $j_0$ with $1\le j_0\le 24L$ such that $\mathrm{Re}\,s_{j_0}>\tfrac{b_1}{8}|z_1|^{j_0}$ (fraction printed ambiguously).
The number $n_\chi(T)$ of zeros $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ of $L(s,\chi,K)$ with $0<\beta<1$, $|\gamma-T|<1$ is $\ll \log A(\chi)+n_K\log(|T|+2)$.
role: zero density (local count) used throughout

statement: For $\mathrm{Re}(s)>1$ and $r>0$, $n(r;s)\ll 1+r(\log A(\chi)+n_K\log(|s|+2))$ for the number of zeros within r of s.
role: counts zeros near 1 for small radii

statement: There is an absolute effective constant $c_2$ such that $L(s,\chi,K)$ has at most one zero $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ with $\beta>1-(c_2\log A(\chi))^{-1}$, $|\gamma|<(c_2\log A(\chi))^{-1}$; it can occur only if $\chi^2=\chi_0$, is real and simple (exceptional zero), and apart from it no zero has $\beta>1-c_2\{\log A(\chi)+n_K\log(|\gamma|+2)\}^{-1}$.
role: zero-free region with exceptional zero; the only input about zeros besides density

statement: Estimates for ramified prime contributions and for prime powers of non-rational-prime norm in the Mellin sum expressing the Artin-symbol-weighted prime count through Hecke L-functions (Artin L eliminated).
role: reduction of Artin L-function sums to Hecke L-functions

statement: With $P(r,\theta)=\sum_{j\ge1}(1-j/J)r^j\cos j\theta$ type Fejer-kernel sums: (i) $P>-1/2$ for $0\le r\le1$, (ii) $P(1,\theta)=J/2$-type value, (iii) $|P(r,\theta)|<3r$ for small r (OCR garbled).
role: ingredient for Theorem 4.2

statement: Let $F\in S^\#$ with no real zeros of $F(s)$ except possibly at $s=1/2$. Then GRH for F holds iff $\Re(-g_F(t))\ge0$ for all $t\ge t_0$ for some $t_0\ge0$, where $g_F(t)=-iB_Ft-\frac{m_0}{2}t^2+\sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma_F\setminus\{0\}}m_\gamma\frac{e^{-i\gamma t}-1}{\gamma^2}$.
Let $F\in S$ (Selberg class), $F(1)\ne0$, and $\Re(-g_F(t))\ge0$ for all $t\ge t_0$. Then there is $\delta>0$ with no zeros of F in $\Re s>1-\delta$.

For $F\in S^{\#\flat}$ (log-derivative has Dirichlet series $-F'/F=\sum_{n\ge2}c_F(n)n^{-s}$), $\Psi_F(t)=4m_F(e^{t/2}+e^{-t/2}-2)-\sum_{n\le e^t}\frac{c_F(n)}{\sqrt n}(t-\log n)+(\log Q+\sum_j\lambda_j\frac{\Gamma'}{\Gamma}(\frac{\lambda_j}2+\mu_j))t+\sum_j\ldots$ (Lerch-transcendent terms (4.2)) equals $-g_F(t)$ for all real $t$.
For $F\in S^\#$: GRH for F iff $g_F$ is a screw function on $\mathbb R$ (even, with $g_F(t-u)-g_F(t)-g_F(-u)+g_F(0)$ non-negative definite kernel).

For $F\in S^{\#\flat}$, GRH holds iff $\sum_{\gamma}\hat\phi(\gamma)\overline{\hat\phi(\gamma)}\ge0$ for all $\phi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$ (Weil-type positivity via Smajlovic's explicit formula/Li criterion), i.e. analog of Thm 1.3 in [10].
$\int_0^\infty g_F(t)e^{izt}dt=z^{-2}\frac{\xi_F'}{\xi_F}(\tfrac12-iz)$ for $\Im z>1/2$.
role: Laplace transform linking g_F to the log-derivative of xi_F.

statement: $2\int_0^\infty\Re g_F(t)e^{izt}dt=z^{-2}\frac{\xi_F'F^*}{\xi_FF^*}(\tfrac12-iz)$, using $g_F(t)=g_{F^*}(t)$-type symmetry and $\xi_{F^*}(s)=\xi_F(\bar s)$.
role: Passes to the real part so that Widder's theorem controls the abscissa of convergence.

statement: If a Laplace transform of a real-valued function that is eventually of one sign converges, its abscissa is a singularity on the real axis.
role: Gives that xi_F xi_{F*} has no zeros for Re s>max(sigma_0,1/2).

statement: xi_F(1/2-iz)=e^{A+Bz}z^{m_0}\prod(1-z/\gamma)^{m_\gamma}e^{m_\gamma z/\gamma}; B_F real; (2.5)-(2.6).
role: Defines B_F and g_F.

statement: Assume RH and Conjecture 1. Then $I_4(T)\sim\frac{24024\,a_4}{16!}\,T(\log T)^{16}$ as $T\to\infty$, with $a_4=\prod_p(1-1/p)^{16}\sum_{m\ge0}\binom{m+3}{m}^2p^{-m}$ (k=4 case of (1.5)).

There is C>0 such that for any eps_0,eps'>0, P>1, X,Y>1/2 with Y≍X, f smooth with supp in [X,2X]x[Y,2Y] and $x^my^nf^{(m,n)}\ll_{m,n}P^{m+n}$, for X sufficiently large and $1\le|r|\ll X^{1-\epsilon'}$: $D_{f;4,4}(r)=\frac1{(2\pi i)^2}\iint_{B_1\times B_2}\zeta^4(z_1)\zeta^4(z_2)\sum_{q\ge1}\frac{c_q(r)G_4(z_1,q)G_4(z_2,q)}{q^{z_1+z_2}}\int_0^\infty f(x,x-r)x^{z_1-1}(x-r)^{z_2-1}dx\,dz_2dz_1+O(P^CX^{1/2+\epsilon_0})$, where $D_{f;4,4}(r)=\sum_{m-n=r}\tau_4(m)\tau_4(n)f(m,n)$.
conditional_on: is a conjecture (no numerical confirmation exists per authors)
location: Sec. 1, eq. (1.12); derived heuristically in Appendix 1 (Sec. 9)

statement: Assume RH, k>=12, T large, $|t_0|\le0.5T$. Then $\int_0^T|\zeta(\tfrac12+it+it_0)|^k|\zeta(\tfrac12+it-it_0)|^k\,dt\ll_kT(\log T)^{k^2/2}G(T,t_0)^{k^2/2}$ with $G=\min\{1,\log T/|2t_0|\}$ for $|t_0|\le1/200$ and $\log(2+|2t_0|)$-type for larger (as printed in the paper).
Under RH, for any eps>0 and T>=T_eps, $I_\omega-\tilde I_\omega=O(\epsilon T(\log T)^{16})$ with implied constant independent of eps, where $\tilde I_\omega$ uses the truncated Vt~ with U=T^{1-eps}.
Unconditionally $I_D=\frac{4a_4(\log U)^{16}}{638512875}\int\omega(t)dt+O(T(\log T)^{15})$ (diagonal terms).

Assuming Conjecture 1, $I_O=-\frac{13381a_4}{2615348736000}\int\omega(t)(\log T)^{16}dt+O(\epsilon T(\log T)^{16})+O(T(T/T_0)^{1+C})$ (off-diagonal). Together: $I_\omega=a_4\frac{24024}{16!}\int\omega(t)(\log T)^{16}dt+O(\epsilon T(\log T)^{16})+O(T(T/T_0)^{1+C})$ (3.9).
Approximate functional equation: for G entire with |G(s)|<<exp(-c|t|), $|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|^8=2\sum_{m,n}\frac{\tau_4(m)\tau_4(n)}{(mn)^{1/2}}(m/n)^{-it}V_t(\pi^4mn)+O((1+|t|)^{-B})$.

For M,N >> T_0^{1-eps_1}, M≍N, MN<<U^{4+eps_2}: $I_{M,N}=\frac{2T}{\sqrt{?}}\sum_{r\neq0}D_{f_r}(r)+O(T^{-B})$ with f_r given by (6.6) a smooth weight built from W(x/M)W(y/N), G(s), g(s,t), (1+r/y)^{-it}, (U/t)^{4s}.
role: Reduces the off-diagonal to quaternary additive divisor sums D_{f;4,4}(r) so that Conjecture 1 can be applied.

statement: (i) $g(s,t)=(t/2)^{4s}(1+O((|s|^2+1)/t))$; (ii) derivative bounds $\ll |s|^iT^{4\epsilon_0-i}$; (iii) $\tilde V_t(x)=O((U^4/x)^A)$ for $x>U^4$.
role: Truncation lemma allowing mn<<U^{4+eps} with U=T^{1-eps}.

statement: Evaluation of the main-term integrals after applying Conjecture 1, for |u_i|<delta'; moving contours to Re(s)=eps_3, 0<delta<eps_3<0.15.
role: Executes the contour shifts and bounds the secondary terms of the off-diagonal.

statement: For z in C: $G_k(s,p^j)\approx\tau_k(p^j)-p^{s-1}\tau_k(p^{j-1})$ near s=1 (precise statement in Lemma 8.1).
role: Arithmetic factor in the off-diagonal main term.

statement: Bounds for G_{s,t}(1,1) and H_s(1,1) arising in the singular-series residue computations; conditions |a_i|,|b_i|<=delta.
role: Residue bookkeeping giving the explicit constant 13381/2615348736000.

statement: Assuming RH, $\kappa^*:=\liminf_{T\to\infty}N^*(T)/N(T)\ge 19/27$, where $N^*(T)$ counts simple zeros with $0<\gamma<T$ and N(T) counts zeros with multiplicity.

Assuming RH, $\kappa_d:=\liminf N_d(T)/N(T)\ge 0.84665$, obtained from the Theorem, Montgomery's inequality $2N^*(T)\le\sum_{0<\gamma\le T}\frac{(m(\rho)-2)(m(\rho)-3)}{m(\rho)}\le\sum m(\rho)-5N(T)+6N_d(T)$, and Cheer-Goldston's $\sum_{0<\gamma\le T} m(\rho)\le(1.3275+o(1))N(T)$ so that $\kappa_d\ge(5+2\kappa^*-1.3275)/6$.
conditional_on: Cheer-Goldston bound (imported; as stated its hypothesis is RH)

statement: For fixed $\epsilon>0$ and mollifier $B(s)=\sum_{k\le y}b(k)k^{-s}$ with $b(k)=\mu(k)P(\log(y/k)/\log y)$, P real polynomial, $P(0)=0,P(1)=1$: $S_1=\sum_{0<\gamma\le T}B\zeta'(\rho)=\frac{TL^2}{2\pi}-M_1+O(TL)+O_\epsilon(yT^{1/2+\epsilon})$ and $S_2=\sum B\zeta'(\rho)B\zeta'(1-\rho)=\frac{TL^3}{2\pi}(\frac12+3\vartheta)\int_0^1P^2... -2\Re M_2+\dots$ (see source for exact main term).
role: Imported essentially from Conrey-Ghosh-Gonek (3.13),(3.21),(3.26),(3.27),(5.1),(5.4),(5.5); reduces the problem to bounding M_1,M_2.

statement: For any integer $r\ge1$: $\zeta'/\zeta(s)=\sum_{j=1}^r(-1)^{j-1}\binom rj\zeta(s)^{j-1}\zeta'(s)M(s)^j+(1-\zeta(s)M(s))^r\zeta'/\zeta(s)$ with $M(s)=\sum_{n\le X}\mu(n)n^{-s}$ (Heath-Brown's generalised Vaughan identity).
role: Writes a_2 = -Lambda * log * log * b as a convolution of 9 factors (taking r=3, X=T^{1/2}) so that the character sums can be split into products of short Dirichlet polynomials and the maximal large sieve applied. The last term vanishes since Md<T^{3/2}.

statement: Cauchy-Schwarz: $N^*(T)\ge\left|\sum_{0<\gamma\le T}B\zeta'(\rho)\right|^2/\sum_{0<\gamma\le T}|B\zeta'(\rho)|^2$ for any regular B; RH is used to identify $S_2=\sum|B\zeta'(\rho)|^2$.
role: Entry point of the mollifier method; this is the only place RH is used in the deduction.

statement: Let $M(x)=\sum_{n\le x}\mu(n)$, $L(x)=\sum_{n\le x}\lambda(n)$. If the positive ordinates $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\dots$ of the distinct zeros $\tfrac12+i\gamma_n$ of $\zeta$ (assumed all on $\sigma=1/2$ and simple, otherwise the conclusion is classical) satisfy no linear relation $\sum c_n\gamma_n=0$ ($c_n\in\mathbb Z$ not all 0), or only finitely many independent such relations, then $\limsup x^{-1/2}M(x)=+\infty$, $\liminf x^{-1/2}M(x)=-\infty$, $\limsup x^{-1/2}L(x)=+\infty$, $\liminf x^{-1/2}L(x)=-\infty$.
hypotheses: linear independence (LI) of ordinates, or all but finitely many relations
conditional_on: LI (finite relation-rank) hypothesis on zero ordinates
location: sec. 1 Theorem A p.314; proof sec. 3 pp.318-319

label_in_source: Corollary in sec. 1 / start of sec. 3
statement: If any one of $M(x)<Kx^{1/2}$, $M(x)>-Kx^{1/2}$, $L(x)<Kx^{1/2}$, $L(x)>-Kx^{1/2}$ holds for all large $x$ (for some constant K), then RH holds and all zeros of $\zeta$ are simple; hence the Mertens conjecture $|M(x)|<x^{1/2}$ and Polya's $L(x)\le0$ (x>=2) each imply RH and simple zeros. Combined with Theorem A: either they fail or the ordinates are linearly dependent over $\mathbb Q$ (infinitely many independent relations).

Let $F(s)=\int_0^\infty A(u)e^{-su}du$ ($A$ locally integrable, convergent for $\sigma>\sigma_1>0$) and $A^*(u)=\sum_{-N}^Na_ne^{i\gamma_nu}$ ($\gamma_{-n}=-\gamma_n$, real trigonometric polynomial) with $F^*(s)=\int_0^\infty A^*e^{-su}du$ ($\sigma>0$). If $F-F^*$ is regular (or continuous with regular interior) on $\sigma\ge0,\ |t|\le T$, then $\varliminf A(u)\ge\varliminf A^*_T(u)$ and $\varlimsup A(u)\le\varlimsup A_T^*(u)$... (inequality (5) in source: $\underline\lim A^*_T\le\underline\lim A\le\overline\lim A\le\overline\lim A_T^*$) where $A_T^*(u)=a_0+\sum_{0<|\gamma_n|<T}(1-|\gamma_n|/T)a_ne^{i\gamma_nu}$ (Fejer-weighted truncation).

Assume all complex zeros of $\zeta$ are simple and on $\sigma=1/2$: $\tfrac12+i\gamma_n$, $\gamma_{-n}=-\gamma_n$, $0<\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\dots$. Let $\alpha_n$ be the residue at $s=i\gamma_n$ of $F(s)=\dfrac1{(\tfrac12+s)\zeta(\tfrac12+s)}$ (case (i), Mobius) or $\dfrac{\zeta(1+2s)}{(\tfrac12+s)\zeta(\tfrac12+s)}$ (case (ii), Liouville). Then $\sum_{n}|\alpha_n|$ diverges (indeed $\sum_{0<\gamma_n<T}|\alpha_n|\gg\log T$ along a sequence $T_m\to\infty$).

Wiener-type smoothing: with Fejer kernel $K_T(v)=T[\sin(Tv/2)/(Tv/2)]^2\ge0$ and Landau's theorem on Laplace transforms of one-signed functions (regularity on positive real axis gives convergence for $\sigma>0$), the Riemann-Lebesgue lemma gives $\int A(u)K(u-\omega)du=\int A^*(u)K(u-\omega)du+o(1)$.
role: Passes from analytic data of F to limits of A.

statement: If $\gamma_n$ ($0<\gamma_n<T$) are linearly independent over $\mathbb Q$ then $\overline\lim_{u\to\infty}A^*_T(u)=a_0+2\sum_{0<\gamma_n<T}(1-\gamma_n/T)|a_n|$ by Kronecker's theorem, and $\ge 2\sum_{0<\gamma_n<T/2}|a_n|/2$.
role: Gives arbitrarily large limsup as $T\to\infty$ by Theorem 2.

statement: If $A-A(u)\ge0$ for $u>0$ (one-sided bound), Landau's theorem makes $G(s)=\int(A-A(u))e^{-su}du$ regular for $\sigma>0$ so $F(s)$ has no singularities in $\sigma>0$ (no zeta zero off 1/2) and no multiple pole on $\sigma=0$.
role: Shows one-sided Mertens/Polya-type bounds imply RH and simple zeros.

statement: Assume RH. For every real $k>0$: $J_k(T)\ll_k(\log T)^{k(k+2)}$ as $T\to\infty$, where $J_k(T)=\frac1{N(T)}\sum_{0<\operatorname{Im}\rho\le T}|\zeta'(\rho)|^{2k}$. Implied constant grows like $e^{e^{Ak}}$.

Assume RH, $k>0$. $\frac1{N(T,2T)}\sum_{T<\gamma\le2T}|\zeta'(\rho)|^{2k}\ll_k(\log T)^{k(k+2)}$ (dyadic version; Thm 1.1 follows by summing over dyadic ranges using $N(2^{-i}T,2^{1-i}T]\asymp2^{1-i}N(T)$).

Assume RH, $k>0$, $|\alpha|\le(\log T)^{-1}$ complex. Then $\frac1{N(T)}\sum_{0<\operatorname{Im}\rho\le T}|\zeta(\rho+\alpha)|^{2k}\ll_k(\log T)^{k^2}$. Improves Milinovich's Theorem 1.2 (which had an $\varepsilon$ loss).
location: Sec.1, p.2-3; proved in last section

statement:
Assume RH, $k\ge1/2$, $
u\in\mathbb N$. Then $ rac1{N(T)}\sum_{0<\gamma\le T}|\zeta^{(
u)}(ho)|^{2k}\ll_{k,
u}(\log T)^{k(k+2
u)}$ (Cauchy integral formula on circle radius $(\log T)^{-1}$, Holder, then Thm 1.2).

Assume RH, $T$ large, $2\le x\le T^2$, $\sigma_x=\tfrac12+\tfrac1{\log x}$. For a zero $\rho=\tfrac12+i\gamma$ with $T<\gamma\le2T$: $\log|\zeta'(\rho)|\le\operatorname{Re}\sum_{n\le x}\frac{\Lambda_L(n)\log(x/n)}{n^{\sigma_x+i\gamma}\log n\log x}+\log\log T+\frac{\log T}{\log x}+O(1)$, with $\Lambda_L(n)=\Lambda(n)$ for $n=p,p^2$, $n\le L$ and 0 otherwise.
role: Harper/Soundararajan-type upper bound for log|zeta'(rho)| by a short Dirichlet polynomial over primes and prime squares; first ingredient of the method.

statement: Assume RH. For integers $a>b$: $\sum_{T<\gamma\le2T}(a/b)^{i\gamma}=-\frac{T\Lambda(a/b)}{2\pi\sqrt{a/b}}+O(\sqrt{ab}(\log T)^2)$ (Gonek's uniform Landau formula).
role: Discrete analogue of continuous orthogonality $\int e^{irt}dt$; computes moments of prime Dirichlet polynomials over zeros.

statement: For $k>0$ and good $\gamma$: $\exp(2k\sum_iG_{i,j}(\gamma))\ll\prod_i(\sum_{n\le e^2k\beta_i^{-3/4}}(kG_{i,j}(\gamma))^n/n!)^2$ (Taylor truncation of exponential).
role: Replaces exponentials of the Dirichlet polynomial by short polynomials so the Landau formula applies (Harper's Euler-product-free technique).

statement: Assume RH. For tuples $\ell_i\le2e^2k\beta_i^{-3/4}$: $\sum_\gamma\prod_iG_{i,j}^{\ell_i}(\gamma)\le N(T,2T)\,\mathbb E[\prod_iG_{i,j}(X)^{\ell_i}]+O(T^{e/25}(\log T)^2)$ with $X$ a random model (independent random variables $X_p$ on the unit circle).
role: Transfers zero-sum of products of Dirichlet-polynomial powers to a probabilistic model.

statement: $\sum_{\gamma}\exp(2k\sum_{i\le I}G_{i,I}(\gamma))\ll N(T,2T)\mathbb E[\exp(2k\sum_i G_{i,I}(X_p))]+e^{2k}T^{e/5}(\log T)^2$, and an inductive step over $j$ with factor $e^{-\beta_{j+1}^{-1/2}\log(1/\beta_{j+1})/21}$ for $\gamma\in S(j)$ (the set where $G_{i,j'}$ small for $j'<j$).
role: Handles zeros where the Dirichlet polynomial is atypically large via Markov/Chebyshev on higher moments.

statement: Assume RH: $N^*(T)\le(1.3208+o(1))N(T)$. Assume GRH for Dirichlet L-functions: $N^*(T)\le(1.3155+o(1))N(T)$, where $N^*(T)=\sum_{0<\gamma\le T}m_\rho$ counts zeros with multiplicity.
Under RH, $N_s(T)\ge(0.6792+o(1))N(T)$; under GRH, $N_s(T)\ge(0.6845+o(1))N(T)$ (simple zeros), via $N_s\ge2N-N^*$.
Under RH, $N_d(T)\ge(0.8477+o(1))N(T)$; under GRH, $N_d(T)\ge(0.8486+o(1))N(T)$ (distinct zeros), combining Theorem 1 with Bui-Heath-Brown $N_s\ge(19/27+o(1))N$ and inequality $2N_s\le N^*-5N+6N_d$.

Assuming RH and the simple-zeros-type hypothesis (2) ($N^*(T)\sim N(T)$): $N(0.6039,T)\gg N(T)$. Assuming GRH and (2): $N(0.5769,T)\gg N(T)$, where $N(x,T)=\#\{0<\gamma,\gamma'\le T:0<\gamma'-\gamma\le 2\pi x/\log T\}$.
hypotheses: RH and N^*(T)~N(T) (all zeros simple asymptotically)

statement: Assuming GRH, for the Chandee-Lee-Liu-Radziwill averaged simple-zeros functional over primitive Dirichlet characters with $\Phi$, $M\Phi(ix)\ge0$: $N_{\Phi,s}(Q)\ge(0.9350+o(1))N_\Phi(Q)$.
Assuming RH, zeros of $\xi'(s)$ satisfy $N_1^*(T)\le(1.1175+o(1))N_1(T)$, hence $N_{1,s}\ge(0.8825+o(1))N_1$ and $N_{1,d}\ge(0.9412+o(1))N_1$.

For $f\in\mathcal A_{LP}$ and $Z(f)=r(f)+\frac2{r(f)}\int_0^{r(f)}f(x)x\,dx$: under RH $N^*(T)\le(Z(f)+o(1))N(T)$; under GRH (using $F(x,T)\ge\frac32-|x|-o(1)$ for $1\le|x|\le\frac32-\delta$ from Goldston-Gonek-Ozluk-Snyder) $N^*(T)\le(\tilde Z(f)+O(\delta)+o(1))N(T)$ with the extended functional $\tilde Z$.
role: Reduces counting multiplicity to a convex optimisation: uses Montgomery F(x,T)=T^{-2|x|}\log T+|x|+o(1) for |x|\le1 (Goldston-Montgomery), non-negativity of F, and \hat g(x)\le0 for |x|\ge1.

statement: For $f\in\mathcal A_{LP}$ and $\varepsilon>0$, assuming RH and (2): $N(P(f)+\varepsilon,T)\gg N(T)$ with $P(f)=\inf\{\lambda>0:p_f(\lambda)>0\}$, $p_f(\lambda)=-1+\frac\lambda{r(f)}+\frac{2r(f)}\lambda\int_0^{r(f)/\lambda}\hat f(x)x\,dx$; GRH analogue with $\tilde p_f$.
role: Converts small-gap problem to finding f with p_f(lambda)>0 for smallest lambda.

statement: GRH analogue for Dirichlet L-functions averaged over q in [Q,2Q] (Chandee-Lee-Liu-Radziwill framework): bound on proportion of simple zeros in terms of an LP-type functional.
role: Yields Theorem 5.

statement: RH bound for N_1^*(T) for zeros of xi'(s) in terms of a functional Z_1(f) based on F_1(x,T) (Farmer-Gonek-Lee Theorem 1.1).
role: Yields Theorem 6.

statement: Functions f(x)=-(s_1(x^2)+(x^2-R^2)s_2(x^2))e^{-\pi x^2} with SOS polynomials s_i and \hat f=(s_3(x^2)+x^2s_4(x^2))e^{-\pi x^2} (Laguerre basis L_k^{-1/2}) ; objective Z(f) linear in the Gram matrices, so for fixed R the inner problem is an SDP; outer one-dimensional search over R (Brent). d=40, sdpa-gmp, Julia/Nemo/Arb.
role: Numerical optimisation plus rigorous verification: positive definiteness of Gram matrices checked in interval arithmetic with b>=(1+2d)B correction making the identity I(X1,...,X4)=0 exact; Z(f) upper-bounded by interval arithmetic with incomplete Gamma identity (16).

statement: The global difference representation $\pi$ of $C_K$ is smooth and summable and its character is the raw Weil distribution $W$: $W(f)=\chi_\pi(f)=\sum_{\omega\in\Omega(C_K)}\mathrm{mult}(\omega,\pi)\hat f(\omega)$, with uniform absolute convergence for $f$ in bounded subsets of $\mathcal D(C_K)$, where $W(f)=\sum_{v}\int'_{K_v^\times}\frac{f(x)|x|}{|1-x|}d^\times x-f(1)\ln D_K$.
hypotheses: K algebraic number field (function fields with modifications)

statement: The spectrum of $\pi$ consists of the poles and zeros of $L_K:\Omega(C_K)\to\mathbb C$ (complete L-function as function of quasi-characters, $L_K(\chi|x|^s)=L(\chi,s)$) and $\mathrm{mult}(\omega,\pi)=\mathrm{ord}(\omega,L_K)$ for all $\omega$; poles appear in $\pi_+$ (2-dim, spec $\{1,|x|\}$), zeros in $\pi_-$.

For $S$ sufficiently large there are natural isomorphisms $\mathbb C(1)\hat\otimes^L_{\mathcal D(K^\times)}\mathcal S(\mathbb A_K)^S\cong\mathbb C(1)\hat\otimes^L\mathcal S(\mathbb A_S)\cong T(C_S)$ in the derived category of smooth $\mathcal D(C_K)$-modules; in particular $H_+^S\cong T(C_S)$ and higher homology $H_n(K^\times,\mathcal S(\mathbb A_K))=0$ for $n\ge1$.
hypotheses: S large finite set of places

statement: Any $\chi\in\mathrm{spec}\,\pi_-$ satisfies $0<\mathrm{Re}\,\chi<1$ (no zeros on the boundary of the critical strip), via a reformulation of Deligne's abstract Hadamard-de la Vallee-Poussin argument with the Bohr compactification of $C_K$ and GNS construction.

Generalized PNT: with $S$ large, prime ideals of $O_S$ viewed as a discrete subset of $C_S$, for open $A\subseteq C_S^1$ and $\pi_A(\xi)=\#\{$prime ideals in $A\times[1,\xi]\}$, $\pi_A(\xi)\approx\mathrm{vol}(A)\,\xi/\ln\xi$ as $\xi\to\infty$ (Chebotarev-type equidistribution).
hypotheses: A open, relatively compact boundary presumably

statement: The modified Weil distribution $f\mapsto\hat f(|x|^{-1/2})+\hat f(|x|^{1/2})-W(f|x|^{-1/2})=\chi_{\pi_-}(f|x|^{-1/2})$ is positive definite iff $\mathrm{spec}\,\pi_-\subset|x|^{1/2}\widehat{C_K}$, equivalent to GRH. Meyer does not prove positivity.

For $f\in\mathcal S(C_S)_{1/2}$ the operators $\int\lambda(f)T$ and $T\int\lambda(f)$ on $L^2(C_S)_{1/2}$ are uniformly nuclear and $\mathrm{tr}(\int\lambda(f)T)=\mathrm{tr}(T\int\lambda(f))=\tau(\mathcal F\partial(\mathcal F^*f))$ (local trace formula, essentially Connes'), where $T=M_\phi-\mathcal F M_\phi\mathcal F^*$.
role: Local trace formula in Hilbert-space setting.

statement: $i_+(H_+)+i_-(H_-)=\{(f_0,f_1)\in\mathcal S(C_K)_{><}: f_0-f_1=c_0-c_1|x|^{-1}\}$; hence $\pi_+$ is 2-dimensional (consequence of Poisson summation).
role: Identifies the poles $\{1,|x|\}$.

statement: For $\alpha>1$, $\int\lambda(f)(P_--P_+^S)$ and $(P_--P_+^S)\int\lambda(f)$ extend to uniformly nuclear operators $L^2(C_S)_\alpha\oplus L^2(C_S)_{1-\alpha}\to\mathcal S(C_K)_{><}$ for $f\in\mathcal D(C_S)$.
role: Key estimate for summability of pi and trace computation using auxiliary operators P_pm.

statement: Bornological extension and isocohomological properties of Bruhat-Schwartz algebras S(G); S(G) is isocohomological for every such G.
role: Homological machinery used to prove S(A_K)/K^x ~ T(C_S).

statement: Summable representations: character computable both spectrally (sum of eigenvalues) and traciallly; summability hereditary under smoothening, contragradients, subquotients.
role: Abstract framework needed for trace = spectral sum.

statement: RH is true iff $J^{d,n}(X)=\sum_{j=0}^d\binom dj\gamma(n+j)X^j$ is hyperbolic for all $d\ge1,n\ge0$, where $\gamma(m)=\frac{m!}{(2m)!}\xi^{(2m)}(1/2)$, the Taylor coefficients of $\Theta(z)=\xi(1/2+\sqrt z)$.

RH is true iff $P^{d,n}(X)=\sum_{j=0}^{d}\binom dj\gamma(n+j)H_{d-j}(X)$ is hyperbolic for all $d\ge1,n\ge0$ (a special case of a general theorem where $H$ is replaced by Jensen polynomials of any Laguerre-Polya function).
location: Sec 1, Thm 3.5 with Omega = Hermite generating function

statement: For all sufficiently large $d$, $P^{d,n}(X)$ is hyperbolic whenever $n/\log^2 n\ge d^{3/4}/2$.

With $w=W(2n/\pi)$ (Lambert W), as $n\to\infty$: $\gamma(n)=4\pi^2e^{7w/4}\sqrt{\frac{w}{w+1}}\big(\frac{e^{w}}{16ne^{2/w}}\big)^{n}\big(1+\sum_{k=1}^{K-1}c_k(w)n^{-k}+O(\log^K(n)/n^K)\big)$ with $c_1(w)=-\frac{w^4+58w^3+29w^2-24w-16}{192(w+1)^3}$ (the displayed form uses the extraction of (1.8)).

With $w=W(2n/\pi)$: $\xi^{(2n)}(1/2)=4\pi^2 e^{7w/4}\sqrt{\frac{2w}{w+1}}\,(\frac{w}{2e^{1/w}})^{2n}\,(1+\sum_{k<K}\mu_k(w)n^{-k}+O(\log^K n/n^K))$, a reformulation of GORZ Thm 9 with the Lambert function in place of $L$ with $n=L(\pi e^L+3/4)$.

For the Turan expansion $\Xi(z)=\sum(-1)^nb_{2n}H_{2n}(z)$, $b_{2n}=4\pi^2\frac{e^{7w/4-w^2/16}}{(2n)!}\sqrt{\frac{2w}{w+1}}\big(\frac{w}{4e^{1/w}}\big)^{2n}(1+\sum\tau_k(w)n^{-k}+O(\log^{3K}n/n^K))$, extending Romik's asymptotics.

3.5: for Phi real entire of genus 1 with coefficients c_j and Omega in the Laguerre-Polya class, Phi is hyperbolic iff $\sum_j\binom dj c_j g^*_{d-j}(\Omega;x)$ is hyperbolic for all d. 3.6 gives a further criterion in terms of $\sum_j (c_j/j!)\Omega^{(j)}(z)$ for Phi, Omega both in LP.

If $J^{d,n}$ is hyperbolic then $P^{d,n}$ is hyperbolic, so all known J-results transfer to P; the converse fails: $P^{2,n}$ hyperbolic iff $\gamma(n+1)^2+2\gamma(n)^2\ge\gamma(n)\gamma(n+2)$, strictly weaker than Turan.
If $G=\sum_{j\le d}c_jH_j$ is real and $\sum_{j=0}^{d-2}2^jj!\,c_j^2<2^d(d-1)!\,c_d^2$ then all zeros of G are real and simple.
role: imported tool that gives Thm 1.3

statement: Complete asymptotic expansion for $I_\alpha(f;n)=\int_1^\infty(\log t)^ne^{-\alpha t}f(t)\,dt$ with $u=W(n/\alpha)$, with explicit error terms.
role: general Laplace-method engine for Thms 1.4-1.6

statement: Tails of the integral beyond $|x|\le\delta=n^{-2/5}$ are negligible and the central part is approximated by a Gaussian-type integral with controlled corrections.
role: error control in the Laplace method

statement: $\Theta^{(n)}$ is hyperbolic iff $J^{d,n}$ is hyperbolic for all $d\ge1$; and if $\Theta^{(n)}$ is hyperbolic then so is $\Theta^{(m)}$ for $m>n$ (Polya/Laguerre).
role: link between derivative RH_n and shifts

statement: Let $L=\log T$, $\alpha,\beta\ll L^{-1}$, $A(s)=\sum_{n\le N}a_n n^{-s}$, $N=T^\theta$, $\Phi$ smooth supported in $[1,2]$ with $\Phi^{(j)}\ll_j L^j$. Then $I(\alpha,\beta)=\sum_{d,e\le N}\frac{a_d\overline{a_e}}{[d,e]}\frac{(d,e)^{\alpha+\beta}}{d^{\alpha}e^{\beta}}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\Big(\zeta(1+\alpha+\beta)+\zeta(1-\alpha-\beta)\big(\tfrac{2\pi de}{t(d,e)^2}\big)^{\alpha+\beta}\Big)\Phi(t/T)\,dt+O(E)$, with $E=T^{3/20}N^{33/20}+N^{1/2}T^{1/2+\epsilon}$ if $a_n\ll n^\epsilon$ (exponents as read from the garbled text layer); $E=T^\epsilon(N^{11/6}+N^{11/12}T^{1/2})$ if $a_n=\mu^2(n)(\mu*\Lambda^{*k})(n)f(n)$, $f\in\mathcal F$; $E=T^\epsilon(N^{7/4}+N^{7/8}T^{1/2})$ if $a_n=\mu(n)f(n)$, $f\in\mathcal F$. Here $\mathcal F=\{f(n)=P(\log(N/n)/\log N)\}$, $P$ a polynomial. The asymptotic is therefore nontrivial for $\theta<17/33$ (generic), $\theta<6/11$ (Feng), $\theta<4/7$ (Conrey).

As $\alpha,\beta\to0$ the main term of Thm 1.1 tends to $\sum_{d,e\le N}\frac{a_d a_e}{[d,e]}\int(\log\frac{t(d,e)^2}{2\pi de}+2C_0)\Phi(t/T)dt$, the Bettin-Chandee-Radziwill main term (via $\zeta(1+s)=1/s+C_0+O(s)$).

Cross-moment with two Dirichlet polynomials $A=\sum_{n\le N}a_n n^{-s}$, $B=\sum_{k\le K}b_k k^{-s}$, $N=T^{\theta_1}$, $K=T^{\theta_2}$: $\Upsilon(\alpha,\beta)=\int\zeta(\tfrac12+\alpha+it)\zeta(\tfrac12+\beta-it)AB(\tfrac12+it)\Phi(t/T)dt$ equals $\sum_{n\le N,k\le K}\frac{a_nb_k(n,k)^{\alpha+\beta}}{[n,k]n^\alpha k^\beta}\int(\zeta(1+\alpha+\beta)+\zeta(1-\alpha-\beta)(\frac{2\pi nk}{t(n,k)^2})^{\alpha+\beta})\Phi(t/T)dt+O(E)$ with three explicit error terms (generic coefficients, Feng-type $a_n$ with $b_n\ll n^\epsilon$, Conrey-type $a_n=\mu f$ with $b_n\ll n^\epsilon$), listed on p. 4 of the source.
Coupling the Conrey mollifier with a generic polynomial in Thm 1.2, the limiting exponent in the error becomes $4/7$.

For $a_n,b_n\ll n^\epsilon$, $N\ge K$, the moment $J(\alpha,\beta)=\int\zeta(\tfrac12+\alpha+it)\zeta(\tfrac12+\beta-it)|A|^2|B|^2(\tfrac12+it)\Phi(t/T)dt$ has main term as in Thm 1.1 with $a_d:=\sum_{nk=d}a_nb_k$ and sums over $d,e\le NK$, with error $E=T^\epsilon(T^{1/2}N^{3/4}K+T^{1/2}NK^{1/2}+N^{7/4}K^{3/2})$.

With two-piece mollifier $\psi=\psi_1+\psi_2$ ($\psi_1$ Conrey, $N_1=T^{\theta_1}$, $\theta_1=4/7-\epsilon$; $\psi_2$ Feng with $K=3$, $N_2=T^{\theta_2}$, $\theta_2=6/11-\epsilon$), $R=1.3025$ and the explicit polynomials $P_1,P_2,P_3,Q$ on p. 21, the Levinson/Littlewood-lemma inequality $\kappa\ge1-\frac1R\log\big(\frac1T\int_1^T|V\psi(\sigma_0+it)|^2dt\big)+o(1)$ yields unconditionally $\kappa\ge0.41491637$ (cf. Bui-Conrey-Young 0.4105, Feng 0.4107 corrected, Feng's contested 0.4128).
hypotheses: Q real polynomial, Q(0)=1, Q(x)+Q(1-x) constant

statement: For $A,B,N,V\ge1$, $|c(a,n)|\le1$: $\sum_{v\le V,b\le B}\sum_{n\le N}\sum_{a\le A}c(a,n)e(\bar{\varrho}ab\bar n/v)$ (with coprimality conditions) $\ll(ABNV)^{1/2+\epsilon}\{(BV)^{1/2}+(A+N)^{1/4}[BV(N+\varrho A)(V+\varrho A^2)+\varrho A^2B^2N]^{1/4}\}$.
role: Imported; bounds Type II / incomplete Kloosterman sums after separating variables for Feng and Conrey coefficients.

statement: $\sum_{a\sim A}\sum_{m\sim M,n\sim N,(m,n)=1}\nu_a\alpha_m\beta_n e(a\bar m/n)\ll\|\alpha\|\|\beta\|\|\nu\|(1+A/(MN))^{1/2}((AMN)^{7/20+\epsilon}(M+N)^{1/4}+(AMN)^{1/8+\epsilon}(AN+AM)^{3/8})$.
role: Imported; gives the generic-coefficient exponent 17/33 (Bettin-Chandee-Radziwill).

statement: With pole annihilator $G(s)=e^{s^2}p(s)$, $p(s)=((\alpha+\beta)^2-(2s)^2)/(\alpha+\beta)^2$: $\zeta(\tfrac12+\alpha+it)\zeta(\tfrac12+\beta-it)=\sum_{m_1,m_2}\frac{(m_1/m_2)^{-it}}{m_1^{1/2+\alpha}m_2^{1/2+\beta}}V_{\alpha,\beta}(m_1m_2,t)+X_{\alpha,\beta,t}\sum\frac{(m_1/m_2)^{-it}}{m_1^{1/2-\beta}m_2^{1/2-\alpha}}V_{-\beta,-\alpha}(m_1m_2,t)+O_A((1+|t|)^{-A})$.
role: Starting point (adapted from Young and Bui-Conrey-Young); G vanishes at +-(alpha+beta)/2 to cancel poles as alpha+beta->0.

statement: Split $m_1n_2=m_2n_1$ (diagonal, yields $\zeta(1+\alpha+\beta+2s)$ contour integral) from $m_1n_2-m_2n_1=\Delta\ne0$; truncate $|\Delta|\le D=MN_1T^{-1+\epsilon}$ by repeated integration by parts after a dyadic partition of unity; the off-diagonal supplies the second main term and an error expressed via sums of $e(a\bar n_1/n_2)$.
role: Reduces the moment to exponential sums.

statement: For coprime $u,g$, $(\mu*\Lambda^{*j})(ug)=\sum_{s}\sum(\mu*\Lambda^{*s})(u)(\mu*\Lambda^{*(j-s)})(g)$ ($2^j$ terms); with $\mu^2(dn_1)=\mu^2(d)\mu^2(n_1)$ and the binomial theorem in $(\log n_1)^j$ one separates $d$ from $n_1$, enabling Type I/II treatment with incomplete Kloosterman sums.
role: Key new input exploiting mollifier structure; gives 6/11 instead of 17/33.

statement: Let \xi(t) be Riemann's function with zeros \alpha_\nu (Re > 0 normalisation; zeros of the t-variable). For real h>0 let N(h) be the number of zeros with real part in (0,h]. Then N(h)=0 for h \le 12, and for h>12 \left| N(h)-\Big(\frac{h}{2\pi}\log\frac{h}{2\pi}-\frac{h}{2\pi}\Big)\right| < 0.34\,\log h\,+\,2.58 (the constants and exact form read from OCR: '0,34 l h + 2,58'; the main term is Riemann's h/2\pi\cdot\log(h/2\pi) - h/2\pi).
location: Introduction p.256; proved in Part I (pp.257-280), eq.(2)-(4),(17)-(18), numerics p.264 (h=12, h<=53 bounds)

statement: If k=k(h)\to\infty with k of higher order than \log h and lower order than h, the number of zeros with real part between h and h+k is k\,\frac{1}{2\pi}\log\frac{h}{2\pi}+o(k); so the density of zeros at height h grows like \frac1{2\pi}\log\frac h{2\pi}.

\xi(t)=0 has at least one root whose real part lies in (0,53]; all roots have real part (absolute) greater than 12. (Shown by the numerical evaluation of the argument-increase \Phi from the Riemann-Siegel-type formula for \xi.)

\xi(t)=\xi(0)\prod_{\nu}(1-t^2/\alpha_\nu^2), the product converging unconditionally, restated from Hadamard 1893 Part III with zeros counted by multiplicity and ordered by non-decreasing real part. (imported, not new.)

For the zeros \alpha_
u of \xi ordered by non-decreasing real part, the series \sum_
u  rac{1}{\alpha_
u}\,W_
u(x,r) (the terms of the analytic expression of the weighted prime-power function f(x,r)=\sum_{p^m\le x}\ldots L(n)\,n^{-r}-type) converges for every real r and all real positive x, and for x>1 its sum is given by the explicit expression with the contributions  rac{x^{1-r}}{r-1}, \sum_n rac{x^{-2n-r}}{2n(r+2n)} and the Euler constant (eq.(46)-(55); formula p.285 'Satz').
hypotheses: zeros ordered by non-decreasing real part
x>0 real (x>1 for the displayed closed form)
r real, with the indeterminate term replaced by its limit when 0 form arises
location: Part II, p.285 (theorem on ordering and convergence), proof pp.285-292

statement: The infinite series \sum_\rho\{ li(x^{\rho})+li(x^{1-\rho})\} in Riemann's memoir converges with the arrangement indicated by Riemann (zeros ordered by absolute imaginary part) and has the sum Riemann stated; so Riemann's assertions are confirmed in all essentials. (stated in the introduction p.256 and consequence of p.292 Satz.)
hypotheses: ordering of terms by non-decreasing real part of \alpha_\nu

statement: If it were shown that all roots \alpha_\nu are real, or merely that Im \alpha_\nu lies in a strip narrower than (-i/2,+i/2), then asymptotic laws follow, e.g. \lim_{x\to\infty}\theta(x)/x=1 (sum of logs of primes up to x); the argument of Cahen for \theta(x)\sim x is rejected as not rigorous (existence of a rectangle with required properties not shown; would fail if zeros accumulated near Re s=1). Mangoldt notes this before Hadamard 1896/de la Vallee Poussin 1896 proved nonvanishing on Re s=1.
conditional_on: narrower strip for zeros (not proved here)

label_in_source: Part I, inequalities (2)-(4) (argument principle by angles)
statement: Move t along the segment a-i\eta to b-i\eta (all zeros lie in the Riemann strip |Im t|<1/2); each zero seen from t rotates positively, hence for the sum S of the angles subtending the path from the zeros with real part in [a,b] one has S \le \Phi (\Phi = increase of the argument of \xi) and S \ge A\arctan(\cdot), giving upper bounds for the count A.
role: Converts the argument increase of \xi (explicit via Stirling and the functional equation) into a count of zeros by a geometric positivity argument that does not need non-vanishing on the critical line

statement: From the Gamma-factor representation \xi(t)=\Pi(\tfrac{s}{2}-1)(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\zeta(s) and Stirling's formula, \Phi = h\log(h/2\pi)\cdot\tfrac12 - \ldots with explicit remainder bounds; the zeta part contributes a bounded argument along Re s=1+\delta by absolute convergence of the Euler product.
role: Evaluates the main term and controls the error with explicit numerical constants

label_in_source: Part I, sums over zeros: Satz 1)-3) (pp.267-272)
statement: Counting lemmas bounding the number of zeros in sub-intervals and the sum \sum\arctan\frac{\cdot}{h-\beta_\nu}, used to bootstrap sharper bounds (Satz 1: no zero in a first sub-interval; Satz 2: upper bound on the number of zeros in the second; Satz 3 proved p.272).
role: Iterative sharpening from O(h\log h) to the full asymptotic with explicit error

statement: Weighted Perron integral for the von Mangoldt function L(n): for a+r>1, x>1 define L(n)=\log p if n=p^a, else 0; integrate -\zeta'(s+r)/\zeta(s+r)\cdot x^{s}/s... over Re s=a, |Im s|\le h, then shift contours using the product formula to get the sum over zeros plus the 'trivial' terms \sum_n \frac{x^{-2n}}{2n(r+2n)}.
role: Origin of the explicit formula for the weighted prime-power sum

u}\,(\ldots) converges for every x>0 when terms are ordered with growing index, and for x>1 equals an explicit elementary expression; eq.(58) yields 	heta(x)/x	o1 under the conditional narrower-strip hypothesis.
role: Connects the explicit formula with Riemann's trigonometric series

statement: The function \zeta(s) has no non-trivial zero \rho=\alpha+i\beta with \alpha\neq 1/2 unless |\beta|>28.558 (a preliminary, weak statement; the strategy is to rule out zeros near Re s=1 for large height). Wording of the source: zeta(s) has no imaginary root a+bi with a different from 1 [sic OCR; context is a zero-free region] unless |b| exceeds 28.558. The exact formulation could not be recovered from the garbled OCR.
location: Chap. I, n. 17 (pp. ~21-23 of the memoir)

statement: For \beta>514 (later improved to \beta>105 in n. 78), every zero \rho=\alpha+i\beta of \zeta satisfies a bound of the form 1-\alpha \ge \rho_0/(\log\beta + \eta_0) with explicit constants \rho_0=0.03282\ldots, \eta_0=4.49737\ldots (garbled OCR: the displayed inequality reads like "\log \beta - 3.506" in the denominator; treat the exact shape of the denominator as unverified). This is the quantitative zero-free region c/\log t.

label_in_source: No. 78 Theoreme (note at end of memoir, n. 71-78)
statement: Improved constants: for \beta>105 the same inequality holds with \rho_0=0.034666\ldots and \eta_0=47.886\ldots (the OCR reads "\rho = 0.034666..., \eta = 47.886 ... pour \beta > 105").

For the Chebyshev-type function (the OCR text is the end of Chap. IV before Chap. V) the remainder r satisfies r\to 0 as x\to\infty, with order at least that of \sqrt{\rho\log x}\,e^{-\sqrt{\rho\log x}}, where \rho=0.03282\ldots, i.e. \psi(x)=x+O\big(x\,\sqrt{\log x}\,e^{-\sqrt{\rho\log x}}\big)-type relative error. The exact form of the displayed formula is garbled.

Let F(x)=\pi(x) denote the number of primes <x. Then F(x)=\mathrm{Li}(x)+O\!\big(x\,e^{-c\sqrt{\log x}}\big)-type: the error relative to Li(x) tends to zero at a rate at least that of \sqrt{\rho'\log x}\,e^{-\sqrt{\rho'\log x}}\cdot x (exact constant and form garbled). The proof transfers the result for f(x)=\sum_k \pi(x^{1/k})/k to F(x) via f(x)-F(x)=O(\sqrt x) (OCR: f(sqrt x)<sqrt x). Li(x) is the principal term of F(x).

For Re s>1, \zeta'(s)/\zeta(s)=-\sum_p \log p/(p^s-1) and the Hadamard product representation / partial fractions of -\zeta'/\zeta in terms of zeros, used to extract real parts (Chap. I, eq. (3), (25))
role: Starting identity: taking real parts with s=u+it, u slightly above 1, turns the sum over zeros into a positive quantity; a trigonometric positivity (1+cos-type) argument then bounds Re rho from above.

label_in_source: Chap. I, n. 5-16 (integral representation (7) and its real part)
statement: Explicit evaluation of \Re\sum_\rho 1/(s-\rho) and of \Re\,\zeta'/\zeta in terms of Gamma-function terms with numerical constants (e.g. 0.046192).
role: Quantitative upper bounds for the contribution of trivial factor and pole, giving inequality (24).

statement: For u close to 1 from above and t>12 real, an inequality combining zeta'/zeta(u+it) and the zero sum with a trigonometric polynomial 1+cos kappa t, yielding the real part of rho bounded away from 1 by c/log beta.
role: Core zero-free region mechanism (positivity of 3+4cos+cos2 in modern phrasing; the memoir uses a different, more elaborate auxiliary polynomial with parameters h, m).
location: Chap. II, n. 22-31; parameters in n. 71

statement: Bounds for sums over zeros such as \sum_\rho 1/|\rho| and \sum_\rho 1/|\rho|^2 and tail sums over \beta>b, using von Mangoldt's zero counting (imported) and the Chap. II inequality.
role: Controls the zero sum in the explicit formula of Chap. IV-V.

statement: f(x)=\mathrm{Li}(x)-\sum_\rho(\ldots)+\text{(integrals)} with f(x)=\sum_k \pi(x^{1/k})/k, an Euler-Mascheroni-free explicit formula obtained by integrating the log-derivative identity.
role: Turns the zero-free region estimates into an estimate for pi(x).

label_in_source: Ramanujan's Theorem (as formulated by Nicolas-Robin in Note 71; quoted in arXiv:1211.6944 section 1)
statement: If RH holds, then for $n_0$ large enough, $n>n_0\Rightarrow \sigma(n)/n< e^{\gamma}\log\log n$. The proof uses $\limsup_{n\to\infty}(\sigma_{-1}(n)-e^\gamma\log\log n)\sqrt{\log n}\le -e^\gamma(2\sqrt2-4-\gamma+\log 4\pi)=-1.393\ldots<0$, which is the corrected form of Ramanujan's formula (382).
location: HCN Part 2, p. 133 and formula (382), Note 71; second-hand via arXiv:1211.6944 section 1

statement: Under RH, for $1/2<s<1$ and all sufficiently large $n$: $\sigma_{-s}(n)\le|\zeta(s)|\exp\Bigl\{\mathrm{Li}((\log n)^{1-s})-\frac{2s(2^{2s-1}-1)(\log n)^{1/2-s}}{(2s-1)\log\log n}-\frac{s}{\log\log n}\sum_\rho\frac{(\log n)^{\rho-s}}{\rho(\rho-s)}+O\bigl(\frac{(\log n)^{1/2-s}}{(\log\log n)^2}\bigr)\Bigr\}$. This is the survey's transcription, and the exact constants were not checked against the paper.

label_in_source: Robin's Theorem (imported, not in this paper)
statement: RH holds iff $\sigma(n)<e^\gamma n\log\log n$ for all $n>5040$. It is the Robin 1984 theorem that the annotations cite.

label_in_source: Definition of generalized (superior) highly composite number
statement: $N$ is generalized highly composite if $\sigma_{-s}(N')<\sigma_{-s}(N)$ for all $N'<N$. It is generalized superior if $\sigma_{-s}(N)/N^\varepsilon\ge\sigma_{-s}(N')/N'^\varepsilon$ for $N'<N$ and $>$ for $N'>N$. At $s=1$ these are superabundant and colossally abundant numbers.
role: extremal family on which sigma_{-s} is controlled

statement: With $x_r^{\varepsilon}=\frac{1-x_r^{-s(r+1)}}{1-x_r^{-sr}}$, one has $N=\prod_{r\le R}e^{\vartheta(x_r)}$ and $\sigma_{-s}(N)=\prod_r\prod_{p\le x_r}\frac{1-p^{-s(r+1)}}{1-p^{-sr}}$.
role: reduces the estimate of sigma_{-s}(N) to sums over primes up to x_r

statement: $\sum_{p\le x}\frac{\log p}{p^s-1}$ is expressed through $\int (x-\vartheta(x))\,dx$-type integrals, using the explicit formula $x-\vartheta(x)=\sqrt x+x^{1/2}\cdot\ldots+\sum_\rho x^\rho/\rho+\ldots$. This is where RH enters.
role: input of RH

statement: Under suitable regularity of N(u), for Re(s) large, $\lim_{q\to1}F(q,s)=\int_1^\infty N(u)u^{-s}d^*u$ and $\frac{\partial_s\zeta_N(s)}{\zeta_N(s)}=-\int_1^\infty N(u)u^{-s}d^*u$, with $\zeta_N(s)=\lim_{q\to1}Z(q,q^{-s})(q-1)^{N(1)}$ (Soule).

The tempered distribution N(u) solving $-\partial_s\zeta_{\mathbb Q}/\zeta_{\mathbb Q}=\int_1^\infty N(u)u^{-s}d^*u$ is positive on $(1,\infty)$ and on $[1,\infty)$ equals $N(u)=u-\frac{d}{du}\Big(\sum_{\rho}\mathrm{order}(\rho)\frac{u^{\rho+1}}{\rho+1}\Big)+1$ (derivative in distribution sense, rho over nontrivial zeros; value at u=1 via principal-value term omega).

$H^0(\mathbb P^1_{\mathbb F_1},\Omega)=\{(f,F(f))\mid f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb A_K)_0/\{f-f_q\}\}\oplus\mathbb C^{2}\oplus(\mathbb C[1])^{2}$, i.e. the graph of the Fourier transform up to finite dimensions; the representation $\vartheta[-\tfrac12]$ of $C_K$ on $H^1(\mathbb P^1_{\mathbb F_1},\Omega)$ gives the spectral realization of zeros of L-functions and is invariant under chi(g) -> chi(g^{-1}).
hypotheses: Omega = sheaf of half-densities on P^1(F_1)(M), M=A_K/K^*

statement: For commutative ring R and proper subgroup G of R^x, the hyperring R/G contains the Krasner hyperfield K={0,1} as sub-hyperfield iff {0} U G is a subfield of R. Hence the adele class space H_K=A_K/K^x is a hyperring extension of K.

On R there is a unique hyperfield structure $\mathbb R^{convex}=(\mathbb R,+_c,\cdot)$ with $x+_cy=\{\alpha x+\beta y\mid\alpha,\beta>0,\ \mathrm{sign}(\alpha x+\beta y)=\alpha\,\mathrm{sign}(x)+\beta\,\mathrm{sign}(y)\}$ and ordinary multiplication, characterized by $x+_cy=(x,y)$ for $y>x>0$ and containing the hyperfield of signs S as sub-hyperfield; $x+_c(-x)=\{-x,0,x\}$, $x+_cx=\{x\}$.

$\mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb R^{convex})\cong\mathbb R^\times$ via $\lambda\mapsto\theta_\lambda$, $\theta_\lambda(x)=x^\lambda$ for x>0 and fixing S; Remark 5.8: no intermediate sub-hyperfield between S and R^convex.

The finite functions $D_{finite}(S)\subset\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbb Z[T],S)$ form under hyperaddition $\star_{\Delta+}$ a canonical hypergroup isomorphic to $\mathbb R\times_{\bar{\mathbb Q}^c}S$; the subset with Re(phi) != 0 under hypermultiplication is isomorphic to $\mathbb R^\times\times_{\bar{\mathbb Q}^c}S$ (recovering R from function theory over Spec S).

(9.1) Principal prime ideals of H_K are p_w for a unique place w, C_K acts transitively on generators of p_w with isotropy K_w^x. (9.2) For K of characteristic p != 0 with curve X/F_q, the loop groupoid Pi_1^{ab}(X)' is canonically isomorphic, W-equivariantly, to the groupoid P(H_K) of prime elements of the hyperring H_K=A_K/K^x.
hypotheses: K global field (9.2: positive characteristic, X non-singular projective curve)

statement: For commutative group G and subgroup K of Aut(G), the orbit set H={K(g)} carries the hypergroup law $K(g_1)\cdot K(g_2):=(Kg_1\cdot Kg_2)/K$.
role: Source of hyperring structure on adele classes

statement: For a monoid scheme X, the geometric space |X| is characterized by $X(M)=\mathrm{Hom}(\mathrm{Spec}M,|X|)$, with underlying set X(F_1).
role: Monoid-scheme framework for P^1 over F_1

statement: In the fiber over {0}, hyperaddition with generic point delta: delta*delta = whole fiber; delta*alpha = whole fiber for alpha algebraic irrational; delta*alpha = delta for alpha in Q.
role: Function theory on Spec K (Krasner hyperfield)

statement: alpha -> phi_alpha gives a bijection of Omega/Aut(Omega) (Omega=algebraic closure of F_p) with the fiber over p in Hom(Z[T],K), compatible with hyperoperations.
role: Fiber over a prime p

statement: Characterization of sign-convex subsets C of R (x,y in C implies the convex-combination-with-matching-sign set lies in C).
role: Construction of R^convex

statement: Let $E/\mathbb Q$ be an elliptic curve. If $\mathrm{Prod}(E,x)=\prod_{p\le x}\#E_{ns}(\mathbb F_p)^{-1}p\sim C/(\log x)^r$ with $C>0$, $r\in\mathbb R$, then $L(E,s)$ satisfies RH ($L(E,s)\ne0$ for $\Re s>1$), $r=\mathrm{ord}_{s=1}L(E,s)$ and $C=\frac{L^{(r)}(E,1)}{r!}\cdot\frac1{\sqrt2\,e^{r\gamma}}$.
hypotheses: asymptotic of partial products with C>0

statement: Let $L(s)=\prod_p\prod_{j\le d}(1-\alpha_{p,j}Np^{-s})^{-1}$ over a number field with $|\alpha_{p,j}|\le1$, holomorphic on $\Re s\ge1/2$, and with second-moment Euler product $L_2(s)=\prod(1-\alpha_{p,j}^2Np^{-s})^{-1}$ holomorphic nonvanishing on $\Re s=1$ except at $1+it_0$ with order $R_0\in\mathbb Z$. If $\prod_{Np\le x}(\ldots)\sim C_t(\log x)^{-r_t}$ at $1/2+it$ with $C_t\in\mathbb C^\times$, then with $B_t$ the leading Taylor coefficient of $L$ at $1/2+it$: $C_t=B_t/e^{r_t\gamma}$ if $t\ne t_0/2$ and $C_t=B_t/(\sqrt2^{R_0}e^{r_t\gamma})$ if $t=t_0/2$.
location: Intro; Thm 5.11 (full statement also gives L(s)!=0 on Re s>1/2 and r_t=ord)

statement: For $E/\mathbb Q$ (Thm 1.3), $\prod_{p\le x}$ asymptotic (1.2) is equivalent to $\psi_E(x)=\sum_{p^k\le x,(p,N)=1}(\alpha_p^k+\beta_p^k)\log p=o(x\log x)$. General form Thm 6.3: for a normalized Euler product with analytic continuation, functional equation and second-moment hypothesis, the following are equivalent: (1) the partial-product asymptotic at $1/2+it$ for some real t, (2) for all real t, (3) $\psi_L(x)=o(\sqrt x\log x)$. Thm 6.2 (no second moment): convergence of $\sum_{n\le x}b_nn^{-1/2-it}+m_t\log\log x$ is equivalent to $\psi_L(x)=o(\sqrt x\log x)$.

Thm 4.3: if $\tilde L$ is a normalized Euler product extending holomorphically nonvanishing to $\Re s=1$ except order $R_0$ at $1+it_0$, then $\lim_{x\to\infty}\sum_{\sqrt x<Np\le x}(\beta_{p,1}+\ldots+\beta_{p,d})Np^{-1-it}$ equals $0$ if $t\ne t_0$ and $-R_0\log2$ if $t=t_0$. Thm 4.9: under the second-moment hypothesis, $\sum_{Np\le x}\sum_{k\ge1}=\sum_{Np^k\le x}+o(1)$ if $t\ne t_0/2$ and $+(-R_0\log\sqrt2)+o(1)$... (printed: $-R_0\log\sqrt2$) if $t=t_0/2$. This explains $\sqrt2$ as a prime-vs-prime-power rearrangement.

Thm 3.3: for $\Re s_0>1/2$, nonzero limit of the partial Euler product at $s_0$ is equivalent to existence of $\lim\sum_{Np^k\le x}\sum_j\alpha_{p,j}^k/(kNp^{ks_0})$, and then $L$ continues holomorphically nonvanishing to $\Re s>\Re s_0$ with $L(s)=$ the limit. Thm 5.3: if $\sum_{Np^k\le x}\sum_j\alpha_{p,j}^k/(kNp^{k/2})=-r\log\log x+C'+o(1)$ then $L$ is holomorphic nonvanishing on $\Re s>1/2$ and $L(s)\sim e^{C'}e^{r\gamma}(s-1/2)^r$ as $s\to1/2^+$.

If $f(s)=\sum a_nn^{-s}$ converges for $\Re s\ge\sigma_0>\sigma_1$ and has a meromorphic continuation to $\Re s\ge\sigma_1$ with a simple pole on the line $\Re s=\sigma_1$, then the Dirichlet series converges at no point of that line. Consequently the Dirichlet series of $L'/L$ converges nowhere on the critical line.

Function fields over $\mathbb F_q$: with $L(z)$ entire and satisfying (8.4), the partial-product asymptotic at $|u|=1/\sqrt q$ holds with $C_u=B_u/e^{m_u\gamma}$ (or with extra $\sqrt2^{R_0}$ when $u^2=z_0$) under RH and the second moment hypothesis (Cor 8.5, unconditional in suitable cases); Thm 8.4: the convergence condition is equivalent to all inverse zeros satisfying $|\lambda_i|=\sqrt q$. Lemma 3.2 (logs vs. products) fails over function fields (Example 8.3).

For $\Re s\ge1/2$: $\sum_{Np\le x}\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{\sum_j\alpha_{p,j}^k}{kNp^{ks}}=\sum_{Np^k\le x}(\cdots)+\sum_{\sqrt x<Np\le x}\frac{\sum_j\alpha_{p,j}^2}{2Np^{2s}}+o(1)$, and the middle sum is $o(1)$ for $\Re s>1/2$.
role: Switches sums over primes vs prime powers; source of the sqrt2 effect at the center.

statement: For $\gamma_{p,i}$ in the open unit disk tending to 0 with Np, the product asymptotic $\sim C/(\log x)^r$ is equivalent to $-\sum\log(1-\gamma_{p,i})=-r\log\log x+C'+o(1)$.
role: Reduces product asymptotics to sums over number fields (false over function fields).

statement: Tauberian theorem: for $f=\sum a_nn^{-s}$ with $a_n\ge0$ and a simple pole at 1 only on Re s=1, and $g=\sum b_nn^{-s}$, $|b_n|\le Ca_n$, with $g=r\log(s-1)+G(s)$ then $\sum_{n\le x}b_n/n=-r\log\log x-r\gamma+G(1)+o(1)$. Proof omitted.
role: Source of $e^{r\gamma}$.

statement: Lemma 5.1: as $s\to0^+$ asymptotics giving $e^\gamma$; Lemma 5.2: Abelian lemma for piecewise continuous h with $h(x)\to0$.
role: Abelian-direction ingredients (statements not read in detail).

statement: If $\sum_{n\le x}c_n=o(\sqrt x\log x)$ then an associated Dirichlet-series/partial-sum quantity converges (exact form not read).
role: Used in Theorem 6.2 to link $\psi_L(x)=o(\sqrt x\log x)$ with convergence of the log series via explicit formulas.

statement: Let A\ge1 be fixed and \mathcal F the class of multiplicative f with |f(p)|\le A for all primes p and \sum_{n\le N}|f(n)|^2\le A N for all N (eq. (1)). If q\le N and (a,q)=1 then, uniformly for f\in\mathcal F, S(a/q)\ll_A N\Big\{(\log 2N)^{-1}+\varphi(q)^{-1/2}+(q/N)^{1/2}\big(\log(2N/q)\big)^{3/2}\Big\}. (Exponent of the last log read from the proof, (10).)
hypotheses: f multiplicative, f in class F
implied constant depends on A only
location: Section 1, eq. (6), p. 70; proved in Sections 2-5

statement: If |\alpha-a/q|\le q^{-2}, (a,q)=1 and 2\le R\le q\le N/R, then S(\alpha)\ll_A N/\log N+N R^{-1/2}(\log R)^{3/2}, uniformly for f\in\mathcal F (form reconstructed from (22) and the proof in Section 6; OCR of the display is corrupted).

For almost all real \alpha, and for all real irrational algebraic \alpha, S(\alpha)\ll_{A,\alpha} N(\log\log N)^{3/2}/\log N-type bound (N>N_0(\alpha)), uniformly in f\in\mathcal F; the printed display is OCR-corrupted, and the form here is reconstructed from the proof which takes R of size (\log N)^2.
hypotheses: \alpha in the set with \|q\alpha\|\ge\exp(-q^{1/2}) for q>q_0 (Khintchine: almost all; Liouville: algebraic irrationals)

statement: (i) For every real \alpha and N\ge2 there is a totally multiplicative f with |f(n)|\le1 and |S(\alpha)|\gg N/\log N. (ii) If q\le N^{...}, (a,q)=1 there is f (a primitive character mod q or induced) with |S(a/q)|\gg N q^{-1/2}. (iii) If N(\log N)^{-?}\le Q\le N there exist \alpha,q,f with Q/3\cdot... \le q\le Q, (a,q)=1, |S(a/q)|\gg (N q)^{1/2}\cdot... [as in the paper; precise ranges garbled]. In all three f is totally multiplicative with |f(n)|\le1.
Assume the Grand Riemann Hypothesis (no Dirichlet L(s,\chi) has a zero with \Re\rho>1/2). Then for every non-principal character \chi modulo q and every x, \sum_{n\le x}\chi(n)\ll q^{1/2}\log\log q.
hypotheses: GRH for all Dirichlet L-functions (used for modulus up to q^2 in Lemma 2 and Littlewood's bound L(1,\chi)\ll\log\log q)

statement: For disjoint rectangles \mathcal R(k)=I(k)\times J(k) in (0,Q]\times(0,M], with Q''\le2Q', |I|\le X, |J|\le Y... and (a,q)=1,\ q\le XY: \Big|\sum_k\sum_{(p,n)\in\mathcal R(k)}f(p)f(n)e(pna/q)\log p\Big|\ll M Q\{(\log2Q)^{-?}+\ldots\}\text{, i.e. } \ll MQ\big\{(XY)^{-1/2}\ldots+\varphi(q)^{-1/2}\ldots\big\}\ (\text{exact form of (16) garbled}).
role: Core bilinear (type I/II) estimate: Cauchy-Schwarz over n, smoothing weight, then a sieve upper bound for prime pairs (p,p+h) and a bound on sum min(Y,||h a/q||^{-1}) using divisor-type sums.

statement: Using \log n=\sum_{m|n}\Lambda(m), it suffices to show \sum_{mn\le N}f(m)f(n)\Lambda(m)e(mna/q)\ll N+N\varphi(q)^{-1/2}\log N+(Nq)^{1/2}(\log 2N/q)^{3/2}\log N; replacing f(mn) by f(m)f(n) costs O(N) by (1),(4),(9); prime-power m=p^k, k\ge2 contribute O(N).
role: Reduces the claim to a bilinear sum over primes p times n, i.e. a Vinogradov-type bilinear form.

statement: Partition the region pn\le N into dyadic rectangles \mathcal R_i and iteratively placed rectangles \mathcal R_{i,j,k} of the form (P,P']\times(N',N''] with P'-P\ge1, N''-N'\ge1 and (P''-P)(N''-N')>q; leftover regions are bounded crudely using Brun-Titchmarsh and Cauchy, giving \ll N+(Nq)^{1/2}(\log 2N/q)^{3/2}\log N.
role: Geometry of the bilinear decomposition and treatment of boundary regions.

statement: For a primitive character \chi mod q, q>1: \sum_{n\le x}\chi(n)=\frac{\tau(\chi)}{2\pi i}\sum_{1\le|h|\le q}\bar\chi(h)h^{-1}(1-e(-hx/q))+O(1)+O(q^{1/2}\log q\cdot q^{-1}\ldots) (printed error garbled).
role: Fourier expansion converting the character sum to exponential sums with the multiplicative coefficient \bar\chi(h)/h.

statement: Let \chi be non-principal mod k, L(s,\chi)\ne0 for \Re s>1/2, (\log k)^{10}\le y\le k, x\le k. Then \sum_{n\le x}\chi(n)=\sum_{n\le x,\ n\in S(y)}\chi(n)+O(xy^{-1/2}(\log k)^{c}) where S(y) is the set of n with all prime factors \le y (exponents garbled).
role: GRH-derived smoothing: character sums equal sums over y-smooth numbers up to small error; proved by contour integration with M(s,\chi)=\prod_{p\le y}(1-\chi(p)p^{-s})^{-1} and N=L/M.

statement: Via Dirichlet approximation: if r>(\log u)^{?}, Corollary 1 gives S(\alpha,u)\ll u/\log u; if r\le(\log u)^{?}, Lemma 2 (applied to \psi\chi mod qr/d) reduces to y-smooth sums, whence \sum_{n\le u}\chi(n)e(n\alpha)\ll u/\log u+\sum_{n\in S}1; summation by parts gives \sum_n\chi(n)e(n\alpha)/n\ll\log\log q; with Littlewood's L(1,\chi)\ll\log\log q under GRH, Theorem 2 follows from Lemma 1.
role: Combines major arcs (GRH, Lemma 2) with minor arcs (Theorem 1/Corollary 1).

statement: $\Lambda\le0.22$ (unconditional). Combined with Rodgers-Tao $\Lambda\ge0$ and RH$\Leftrightarrow\Lambda\le0$.
hypotheses: unconditional; uses Platt's verification of RH to height 3.06e10 and computer-assisted numerical verification of H_t zero-freeness
conditional_on: Platt's numerical RH verification up to T=3.06e10
correctness of the interval-arithmetic zero-free certificates for H_t in regions (b),(c)

statement: Let $t_0,X>0$, $0<y_0\le1$. Suppose (i) no zeros $\zeta(\sigma+iT)=0$ with $\frac{1+y_0}{2}\le\sigma\le1$, $0\le T\le X/2$; (ii) no zeros of $H_{t_0}(x+iy)$ with $x\ge\sqrt{X+1-y_0^2}$, $y_0\le y\le\sqrt{1-2t_0}$; (iii) no zeros of $H_t(x+iy)$ with $X\le x\le\sqrt{X+1-y_0^2}$, $\sqrt{y_0^2+2(t_0-t)}\le y\le\sqrt{1-2t}$, $0\le t\le t_0$. Then $\Lambda\le t_0+\tfrac12y_0^2$ (barrier-region criterion; as printed the X-thresholds are in extracted form and the barrier is x in [X, sqrt(X+1-y0^2)] shape).
location: Sec. 1 p.2; proof Sec. 3 (Prop 3.3 + de Bruijn Thm 3.2)

statement: For $0<t\le1/2$, $0\le y\le1$, $x\ge200$: $\frac{H_t(x+iy)}{B_t(x+iy)}=f_t(x+iy)+O_{\le}(e_A+e_B+e_{C,0})$ with $f_t=\sum_{n\le N}\frac{b_n^t}{n^{s_*}}+\gamma\sum_{n\le N}\frac{b_n^t}{n^{\bar s_*...}}$ (as in (14)), $b_n^t=\exp(\frac t4\log^2n)$, $N=\lfloor\sqrt{x/4\pi+t/16}\rfloor$, $B_t(x+iy)=M_t(\frac{1+y-ix}2)$, $M_t(s)=\exp(\frac t4\alpha(s)^2)M_0(s)$, and explicit error terms e_A,e_B,e_{C,0} (eqs (23),(24), (71)-(74)); with $|\gamma|\le e^{0.02y}(x/4\pi)^{-y/2}$, $\Re s_*\ge...$, $|\kappa|\le ty/(2(x-6))$.
If $|f_t(x+iy)|>e_A+e_B+e_{C,0}$ in region (5) then $H_t(x+iy)\ne0$.

Let $0<t\le1/2$, C large, c small absolute constants; $g(x,t)=\frac x{4\pi}\log\frac x{4\pi}-\frac x{4\pi}+\frac{11}8+\frac t{16}\log\frac x{4\pi}$, $x_n$ the unique solution $>4\pi$ of $g(x_n,t)=n$. (i) If $x\ge\exp(C/t)$ and $H_t(x+iy)=0$ then $y=0$ and $x=x_n+O(x^{-ct})$ for some n. (ii) For $n\ge\exp(C/t)$ there is exactly one zero in $|z-x_n|\le\log^{-c}x_n$ (real, within $O(x^{-ct})$ of $x_n$). (iii) For $X\ge\exp(C/t)$: $N_t(X)=g(X,t)+O(1)$. (iv) For all $X\ge0$: $N_t(X+1)-N_t(X)\le O(\log(2+X))$ and $N_t(X)=g(X,t)+O(\log(2+X))$.

Conditional on numerical RH verification to height T (e.g. $T\approx4.5\times10^{21}$), one obtains $\Lambda\le0.1$ using $X=9\times10^{21}+70686$, $t_0=0.093$, $y_0=0.11832$; intermediate rows give $\Lambda\le0.21,\dots,0.11$. Heuristic: $\Lambda\le O(1/\log T)$ is the natural limit.
hypotheses: extended numerical RH verification (not in the literature at time of writing)
conditional_on: numerical verification of RH to the listed heights

statement: (i) At a simple zero $z_j(t_0)$ of $H_{t_0}$: $\frac{dz_j}{dt}=2\sum'_{k\ne j}\frac1{z_j-z_k}$. (ii) At a zero of order $m\ge2$ the m zeros nearby behave as $z_j+\sqrt{2}(t-t_0)^{1/2}\lambda_i+O(|t-t_0|)$ with $\lambda_i$ the roots of Hermite polynomial $He_m$.
role: Zero dynamics for all t (including complex or repeated zeros, i.e. t<=Lambda), extending Csordas-Smith-Varga.

statement: If $H_{t_0}$ has no zeros $x+iy$ with $x\in\mathbb R$, $y>y_0$, then for $t>t_0$ no zeros with $y>\max(y_0^2-2(t-t_0),0)^{1/2}$; in particular $\Lambda\le t_0+\frac12y_0^2$.
role: Converts a zero-free 'canopy' at time t_0 into a bound on Lambda.

statement: Under hypotheses (i)-(iii) (barrier region version) there are no zeros of $H_{t_0}(x+iy)$ with $y\ge y_0$.
role: Barrier/continuity argument: first time t_1 a zero crosses the boundary Y(t)=sqrt(y_0^2+2(t_0-t)) forces dY/dt=-1/Y > Im dz/dt, using (28) and y_k^2<= (x-x_k)^2+Y^2 for zeros outside the barrier, a contradiction.

statement: Effective estimates for the main terms r_{t,n} and the remainder R_{t,N} in the Riemann-Siegel-type decomposition obtained from a saddle-point contour shift after writing H_t as a Gaussian convolution of H_0.
role: Core analytic estimates for Theorem 1.3.

statement: Fast numerical bounds for sums f_t via Taylor expansion over multiple x and Euler-product mollification (Sec. 8.5, Sec. 7 fast evaluation of multiple sums).
role: Make verification of (ii),(iii) at X~6e10 feasible.

statement: Asymptotics $e_A,e_B,e_{C,0}=O(x^{-ct})$, $f_t=1+O(x^{-ct})$ for fixed t,y and x large (region of x >= 200, |y|<=10).
role: Feeds Theorem 1.5.

statement: Assume RH, $b\ge1$, $\varepsilon>0$. For large $\ell$, as $T\to\infty$: $(C^--\varepsilon)\ell+o(1)\le\int_b^{b+\ell}F(\alpha,T)\,d\alpha\le(C^++\varepsilon)\ell+o(1)$, with $C^\pm$ defined by extremal problems (2.52), (2.57) and $0.9278<C^-\le C^+<1.3302$. Corollary 2: $0.9278\,\ell+o(1)\le\int_b^{b+\ell}F\,d\alpha\le1.3302\,\ell+o(1)$. Previous best constants 1/3 (lower) and 2 (upper) (Goldston; Goldston-Gonek). Conjectured value is $\ell+o(1)$.
location: Section 1.3.1, p.3; Section 2.4 (C+ in 2.52, C- in 2.57)

statement: Assume RH, $b\in\mathbb R$, $\ell>0$. As $T\to\infty$: $W^-(\ell)+o(1)\le W^-_*(b,b+\ell)+o(1)\le\int_b^{b+\ell}F(\alpha,T)\,d\alpha\le W^+(\ell)+o(1)$, where $W^+(\ell)$ is the infimum of $\sum_j\rho(g_j)$ over finite families $g_j\in\mathcal A,\xi_j\in\mathbb R$ with $\sum_j\hat g_j(\alpha-\xi_j)\ge\chi_{[0,\ell]}(\alpha)$ (EP1), $W^-$ the supremum of $\sum_j(2g_j(0)-\rho(g_j))$ over families with $\sum_j\hat g_j(\alpha-\xi_j)\le\chi_{[0,\ell]}(\alpha)$ (EP2), $W^-_*$ the supremum in EP3. Here $\mathcal A$ = continuous even nonnegative $g\in L^1$ with $\hat g(\alpha)\le0$ for $|\alpha|\ge1$, and $\rho(g)=\hat g(0)+\int_{-1}^1\hat g(\alpha)|\alpha|\,d\alpha$.
hypotheses: (1.5) Fourier inversion identity and (1.6) Goldston-Montgomery asymptotic for |alpha|<=1

statement: Assume RH, $b\ge1$, $\ell>0$. Then $C_N^-(\ell)+o(1)\le\int_b^{b+\ell}F\le C_N^+(\ell)+o(1)$ with explicit $C_N^\pm$; for $\ell\ge1$ the upper bound is $C_N^+(\ell)=\frac43(\ell+1)+\frac{\{\ell\}^3}{12}-\frac{\{\ell\}}{3}-\frac14(1-\{\ell\}-\{\ell\}^2)_+$ (as transcribed, one branch shown). In particular $W^-(\ell)>0$ for $\ell>6-2\sqrt6=1.10102\dots$. Uses the Fejer (triangle) test function and shows $W^+\le 4\ell/3+O(1)$.

Assume RH, $\beta>1$, $c_0=\min_{x}\sin x/x=-0.21723\dots$. Then $C^-(1,\beta)+o(1)\le\int_1^\beta F\le C^+(1,\beta)+o(1)$ with $C^+(1,\beta)=C_N^+(2\beta)/2-1$ and $C^-(1,\beta)=\max_nG_n(\beta)\ge(1+c_0/3)(\{\beta\}-1)-(\pi+1)/3$. Corollary 11 combines to $C^\pm(b,\beta)$ via $C^-(b,\beta)=\max\{C_N^-(\ell),C^-(1,\beta)-C^+(1,b)\}$ and $C^+(b,\beta)=\min\{C_N^+(\ell),C^+(1,\beta)-C^-(1,b)\}$. The constant $1+c_0/3=0.92758\dots$ (eq. 1.9) is the lower-bound mechanism: Dirichlet kernels cannot be too negative.

Assume RH, $\varepsilon>0$. For large $\beta$: $\big((L^-C^--\varepsilon)\beta+o(1)\big)\frac{\log^2T}{T}\le J(\beta,T)\le\big((L^+C^++\varepsilon)\beta+o(1)\big)\frac{\log^2T}{T}$, with $L^-=0.9028\dots$, $L^+=1.0736\dots$ (Fejer-kernel 'sunrise' constants, (3.1),(3.2)); Corollary 4: $0.8376\,\beta\le\cdot\le1.4283\,\beta$ (previous 0.153 and 10.824). Theorem 14 (Tauberian step): for $\beta>b>0$, $L^-\lim_{\varepsilon\to0^+}\liminf_\tau\int_{b+\varepsilon}^{\beta-\varepsilon}F(\alpha,\tau)d\alpha\cdot\frac{\log^2T}{T}\le J(\beta,T)-J(b,T)\le L^+\lim\limsup\int_{b-\varepsilon}^{\beta+\varepsilon}F\cdot\frac{\log^2T}{T}$. Here $J(\beta,T)=\int_1^{T^\beta}(\psi(x+x/T)-\psi(x)-x/T)^2x^{-2}dx$.

Assume RH. For $T^{-1}(\log T)^{5/2}\le a\le(\log T)^{1/4}/(\log\log T)^{1/2}$: $(1+o(1))U^-(a)\,T\log^2T\le I(a,T)\le(1+o(1))U^+(a)\,T\log^2T$, with $U^-(a)=\frac{1-(1+2a)e^{-2a}}{4a^2}+\big(\frac1{2a}+\frac1{\sqrt3}\big)e^{-2a(1+1/\sqrt3)}$ and $U^+(a)=\frac{\coth a(\operatorname{csch}a)^2}{4a^2}-\frac{\coth a}{4a}+\frac{\coth a}{2}-\frac12$ ($o(1)=O(1/\sqrt{\log\log T})$). With $G^\pm(a)=U^\pm(a)\big/\frac{1-e^{-2a}}{4a^2}$: $G^-(0^+)=1$, $G^+(0^+)=4/3$, $\min G^-=0.899\dots$ at $a=0.998\dots$, $\max G^+=1.434\dots$ at $a=0.620\dots$, both tending to 1 rapidly; improves Goldston-Gonek-Montgomery $V^\pm$. Here $I(a,T)=\int_1^T|\frac{\zeta'}{\zeta}(\frac12+\frac a{\log T}+it)|^2dt$.
hypotheses: Beurling-Selberg extremal problem for Poisson kernel (Carneiro-Littmann; Holt-Vaaler type)

statement: Let $\mathcal B_2(\pi)$ be the Paley-Wiener space of entire functions of exponential type $\pi$ in $L^2(\mathbb R)$ and $d\mu$ the pair-correlation measure from (6.1). The sharp embedding constant is $D^2=\inf_{f\in\mathcal B_2(\pi),f\ne0}\|f\|^2_{L^2(d\mu)}/\|f\|_2^2=1-\frac1{2\pi^2\theta^2}=0.3244\dots$ where $0<\theta<\tfrac12$ is the unique root of $(\pi\theta)\tan(\pi\theta)=1$ ($\theta=0.27385\dots$). The extremizer is unique up to scalar: $f(z)=\frac{\sin\pi(z+\theta)}{\pi(z+\theta)}+\frac{\sin\pi(z-\theta)}{\pi(z-\theta)}$.
hypotheses: none (exact analysis); proofs by interpolation and by a variational method

statement: $W^+,W^-,W_*^-$ are non-decreasing in $\ell$; $W^-(\ell)\le W_*^-(b,b+\ell)$; $W^+$ is subadditive and $W^-$ superadditive in $\ell$; $W_*^-(b,d)\ge W_*^-(b,c)+W_*^-(c,d)$.
role: Structural properties used to patch interval estimates and to chain bounds in Corollary 11.

statement: Assume RH, $\beta>1$: $\frac{W^-_*(-\beta,\beta)}{2}-1+o(1)\le\int_1^\beta F\,d\alpha\le\frac{W^+(2\beta)}2-1+o(1)$, using $\int_{-1}^1F=2+o(1)$ (from 1.6) and evenness of F.
role: Symmetrization giving the b=1 bounds used in Theorem 10.

statement: Assume RH, $0<a\le\sqrt{\log T}$. Then $I(a,T)=\log T\sum_{0<\gamma,\gamma'\le T}h_{a/\pi}\!\big((\gamma-\gamma')\tfrac{\log T}{2\pi}\big)w(\gamma-\gamma')-\tfrac12\int_1^T\log^2\tfrac t{2\pi}dt+O(\log^4T/a^2)+O(aT\log T)$ with Poisson kernel $h_b(x)=b/(b^2+x^2)$.
role: Converts I(a,T) into a pair-correlation sum, enabling Beurling-Selberg extremal majorants/minorants for the Poisson kernel.

statement: Auxiliary asymptotic lemmas for the Tauberian step (Lemma 13: continuous nonnegative f(t,eta) << log^2(t+2)) and for I(a,T) (Lemma 17). Statements not extracted in detail.
role: Technical estimates for Theorem 14 and Theorem 5.

statement: Explicit bounds for n in N tied to Theorem 19's extremal problem (EP8); statement not extracted in detail.
role: Support for the sharp embedding computation.

statement: The nontrivial zeros of \zeta(s) have real part 1/2; equivalently all zeros of \xi(t)=\tfrac12 s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s), s=\tfrac12+it, are real.
RH is equivalent to \pi(x)=\mathrm{Li}(x)+O(\sqrt x\log x); Littlewood: \pi(x)-\mathrm{Li}(x) changes sign with size at least \mathrm{Li}(\sqrt x)\log\log\log x.

van de Lune-te Riele-Winter: the first 1.5 billion zeros are simple and on the line (T about 5x10^8). Odlyzko: more than 3x10^8 zeros at heights near 2x10^20 satisfy RH. A planned interval is [10^22,10^22+10^10].

N(\alpha,T)=O(T) (Bohr-Landau 1914); N(\alpha,T)=O(T^{4\alpha(1-\alpha)+\epsilon}) (Carlson 1920); Ingham exponent 3(1-\alpha)/(2-\alpha) for 1/2<\alpha<=3/4; more than 40 percent of nontrivial zeros are simple and on the line (Selberg, Levinson, Conrey).

For a smooth projective curve C over F_q, Z(t,C) is rational with numerator of degree 2g and its zeros have |t|=q^{-1/2}. This is Hasse (g=1, 1934) and Weil (general g, 1940s), generalized by Deligne to varieties; the proof uses the index theorem for surfaces (Severi 1906).

For f in the class W (continuous, piecewise C^1, f=O(x^\delta) at 0, O(x^{-1-\delta}) at infinity, Mellin transform \hat f(s)=\int_0^\infty f(x)x^s dx/x): \hat f(0)-\sum_\rho\hat f(\rho)+\hat f(1)=\sum_n\Lambda(n)[f(n)+\tfrac1n f(\tfrac1n)]+(\log 4\pi+\gamma)f(1)+\int_1^\infty[f(x)+\tfrac1x f(\tfrac1x)-\tfrac2x f(1)]\frac{x\,dx}{x^2-1}, with the zero sum taken as \lim_{T\to\infty}\sum_{|\mathrm{Im}\rho|<T}.

RH is equivalent to a sign condition (negativity) of the right-hand side of the explicit formula for all f(x)=\int_0^\infty g(xy)g(y)dy with g in W and \int_0^\infty g(x)dx/x=\int_0^\infty g(x)dx=0. In the function-field case this is the index theorem for surfaces.

For a nonsingular projective surface X over an algebraically closed field, the self-intersection form (D.D) on divisors of degree 0 for a projective embedding is negative semidefinite (Severi 1906; Hodge in characteristic 0).
role: Geometric source of positivity in the function-field Riemann hypothesis, offered as the model for a hoped-for general index theorem.

statement: The set of points of the arithmetic site $(\widehat{\mathbb N^\times},\mathbb Z_{max})$ over $\mathbb R^{max}_+$ coincides with the quotient $\mathbb Q^\times\backslash\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q}/\hat{\mathbb Z}^\times$; the Frobenius automorphisms $Fr_\lambda(x)=x^\lambda$ of $\mathbb R^{max}_+$ act on these points as the idele class group action.
hypotheses: arithmetic site = topos of N^x-sets (functors N^x -> Sets) with structure sheaf Z_max, N^x acting by k -> (n -> kn)

statement: The category of points of the topos $\widehat{\mathbb N^\times}$ is canonically equivalent to the category of totally ordered groups isomorphic to non-trivial subgroups of $(\mathbb Q,\mathbb Q_+)$ with injective ordered-group morphisms (Thm 2.4: for $\widehat{\mathbb N^\times_0}$, to subgroups of Q including zero, with all morphisms).

The stalk of the structure sheaf O=Z_max at the point of $\widehat{\mathbb N^\times}$ associated to an ordered group $H\subset\mathbb Q$ is canonically isomorphic to the semiring $H_{max}=(H\cup\{-\infty\},\max,+)$.

The zeta function attached through $\partial_s\zeta_N/\zeta_N=-\int_1^\infty N(u)u^{-s}d^*u$ to the counting distribution of the Frobenius action on points over $\mathbb R^{max}_+$ is the complete Riemann zeta $\zeta_{\mathbb Q}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$; moreover $N(u)=u-\frac{d}{du}\big(\sum_{\rho}\mathrm{order}(\rho)\frac{u^{\rho+1}}{\rho+1}\big)+1$ in the distribution sense.
hypotheses: periodic orbits of Frobenius flow, counting function of Sec 4.2

statement: The functor $F:\mathbb N^\times_0\to Sh(\mathrm{Spec}\,\mathbb Z)$ sending * to the sheaf S is filtering and defines a geometric morphism $\Theta:\mathrm{Spec}\,\mathbb Z\to\widehat{\mathbb N^\times_0}$, sending the point p to the point attached to H(p)⊂Q; the stalk of $\Theta^*(\mathcal O)$ at p is $H(p)_{max}$ and equals B at the generic point.

For $\lambda,\lambda'\in\mathbb R^*_+$ with $\lambda\lambda'\notin\mathbb Q$, $\Psi(\lambda)\circ\Psi(\lambda')=\Psi(\lambda\lambda')$; the same holds for rational lambda, lambda'; if lambda, lambda' irrational and $\lambda\lambda'\in\mathbb Q$ then $\Psi(\lambda)\circ\Psi(\lambda')=\mathrm{Id}_\epsilon\circ\Psi(\lambda\lambda')$ with Id_epsilon the tangential deformation of the identity correspondence.
hypotheses: Psi(lambda) = Frobenius correspondence defined as reduced congruence on the reduced square (N^x2, Conv_>=(Z x Z))

statement: The points of the unreduced square $(\widehat{\mathbb N^{\times2}},\mathbb Z_{min}\otimes_{\mathbb B}\mathbb Z_{min})$ over $\mathbb R^{max}_+$ coincide with the product of the points of the arithmetic site over $\mathbb R^{max}_+$.

The semigroup End(K) of non-degenerate endomorphisms of the C*-algebra K of compact operators on l^2(Z) is an extension of the group Int(K) of inner automorphisms by the semigroup N^x via the modulus homomorphism Mod: End(K) -> N^x (action on K_0(K)=Z), with kernel Int(K); links the arithmetic site to the structure of the point in NCG and Dixmier's classification of matroids.
A flat functor F: N^x -> Sets determines a totally ordered group (H,H_+) by symmetrization of the filtered monoid (X,+).
role: Classification of points of the topos

statement: Any non-trivial subgroup of Q is uniquely of the form H=(ordered) given by supernatural-number-type data.
role: Parametrize points of the topos

statement: Map Phi: (A_f/Z^x) x R_+^x -> subgroups of R defined by adelic data yields the identification of points over R^max_+ with the adelic quotient.
role: Core of the adelic interpretation (Thm 3.8)

statement: For Re(s) large, $\lim_{q\to1}F(q,s)=\int_1^\infty N(u)u^{-s}d^*u$ and $\partial_s\zeta_N/\zeta_N=-\int N(u)u^{-s}d^*u$.
role: Hasse-Weil limit q->1

statement: Zmin tensor_B Zmin carries a unique bilinear multiplication; the reduced semiring Conv_>=(Z x Z) of closed convex subsets is multiplicatively cancellative; congruences F(lambda,q) separate distinct lambda.
role: Construction of reduced square and Frobenius correspondences

statement: Reduction of R(lambda) tensor R(lambda') is R(lambda lambda', lambda') when lambda lambda' not in Q lambda' + Q, with explicit left/right actions; analogous formula when lambda lambda' in Q lambda'+Q for irrational lambda,lambda'.
role: Composition law proof

statement: There is an absolute constant $c>0$ such that $J^{d,n}(X)=\sum_{j\le d}\binom dj\gamma(n+j)X^j$ is hyperbolic for all $d\ge1$ and $n\ge c\,e^{d/2}$, where $\psi(z)=\xi(1/2+z)=\sum\gamma(j)z^{2j}/j!$.

If $RH_m(T)$ holds (all zeros $\rho^{(m)}$ of $\xi^{(m)}$ with $|\mathrm{Im}\rho^{(m)}|\le T$ lie on $\mathrm{Re}=1/2$) and $d\le\lfloor T\rfloor^2$, then $J^{d,n}$ is hyperbolic for all $n\ge m$. (A mild generalization of Chasse's Thm 1.8, recovers it for m=0.)
hypotheses: RH_m(T) for the zeros of xi^{(m)} up to height T

statement: Using Platt's verification $RH_0(3.06\times10^{10})$, $J^{d,n}$ is hyperbolic for all $n\ge0$ whenever $d\le9.36\times10^{20}$.
