There is a self-adjoint extension $W_{sa}$ of $W_{\min}$ (domain $L_\beta$ spanned by $\mathrm{Dom}\,W_{\min}$ and $\beta_\pm,\hat\beta_\pm$) such that: (i) $W_{sa}$ commutes with the Fourier transform; (ii) it commutes with $P_\lambda$ and $\hat P_\lambda=\tilde F P_\lambda\tilde F^{-1}$; (iii) it is the only self-adjoint extension of $W_{\min}$ commuting with $P_\lambda,\hat P_\lambda$; (iv) its spectrum is discrete and unbounded in both directions.

For $\lambda=1$ (even functions): if $\mu$ is a negative eigenvalue of $W_{sa}$, the eigenfunction $\phi_\mu$ belongs to Sonin's space (orthogonal complement of the eigenspaces attached to the classical prolate functions and their Fourier transforms). The authors do not claim all eigenvalues of $W_{sa}$ on Sonin space are negative (numerics: at most finitely many exceptions).

The semiclassical approximation to the number of negative eigenvalues $\xi$ of $W_{sa}$ with $-\xi\le E^2$ on even functions (equally on odd functions) is $2\sigma(E,\lambda)$, $\sigma(E,\lambda)\sim\frac{E}{2\pi}\left(\log\frac{E}{2\pi}-1+\log4-2\log\lambda+\lambda^2\right)+o(1)$.

For $\lambda=\sqrt2$ the operator $\sqrt2\,\slashed D$ (Dirac square root of $W_\lambda$ via Darboux/Riccati, with a deformation parameter) has discrete simple spectrum in $\mathbb R\cup i\mathbb R$, imaginary eigenvalues symmetric under conjugation, and the counting function $N(E)$ of eigenvalues with $0<\Im\xi<E$ satisfies $N(E)\sim\frac{E}{2\pi}\left(\log\frac{E}{2\pi}-1\right)+O(1)$.
If $\xi\in\mathrm{Dom}\,W_{\min}$ then $P_\lambda\xi\in\mathrm{Dom}\,W_{\max}$ and $WP_\lambda\xi=P_\lambda W\xi$; same for $\hat P_\lambda$.
role: Allows an extension commuting with the cutoff projections.

statement: (i) The Fourier transform of $f(x)=\frac12\log((\lambda^2-x^2)^{-2})$ coincides off $0$ with $\cos(2\pi\lambda y)/|y|$; (ii) $\tilde F 1_{[-\lambda,\lambda]}(y)=\sin(2\pi\lambda y)/(\pi y)$.
role: Fourier images of boundary data for the symplectic Omega pairing.

statement: $\{\alpha_\pm,\beta_\pm,\hat\alpha_\pm,\hat\beta_\pm\}$ forms a basis of $E_\pm=\mathrm{Dom}(W_{\max})/\mathrm{Dom}(W_{\min})$.
role: Parametrizes self-adjoint extensions by boundary data.

statement: For real $\mu$ the unique solution $\xi_\mu$ with asymptotics $-\sin(2\pi x)/(\pi x)$ at infinity has Borel-summable expansion and equals the Fourier transform of the unique even solution $\phi_\mu$ vanishing on $[-1,1]$ and equal to $f_\mu$ for $x>1$.
role: Links boundary behavior to support of the transform, hence Sonin-space membership.

statement: Darboux construction with $p=x^2-\lambda^2$, $V=4\pi^2\lambda^2x^2$, $L=\partial p\partial+V$: Dirac operator whose square is two copies of $W_{sa}$ (exact statement not verified).
role: Produces the isospectral family of Dirac operators.

statement: There exists (theta,C) in [1/2,3/2) x [0,infty) such that for I={a_1,a_2,a_3}, J={b_1,b_2,b_3} distinct shifts with |a_i|,|b_i|<<(log X)^{-1}, f smooth supported in [X,2X]x[Y,2Y], Y<<X, x^m y^n f^{(m,n)}<<P^{m+n}: $D_{f;I,J}(r)=\sum_{i_1,i_2=1}^3\prod_{j_1\ne i_1}\zeta(1-a_{i_1}+a_{j_1})\prod_{j_2\ne i_2}\zeta(1-b_{i_2}+b_{j_2})\sum_{\ell\ge1}\frac{c_\ell(r)G_I(1-a_{i_1},\ell)G_J(1-b_{i_2},\ell)}{\ell^{2-a_{i_1}-b_{i_2}}}\int_{\max(0,r)}^\infty f(x,x-r)x^{-a_{i_1}}(x-r)^{-b_{i_2}}dx+O(P^CX^{\theta+\epsilon})$ uniformly for 1<=|r|<<X^{1/2-eps_2}.
hypotheses: ternary additive divisor asymptotic AD(theta,C) (open for k>=3)

statement: Assume AD(theta,C) with theta in [1/2,3/2), C>0 (as in Conj 2); I,J of size 3 with |a_i|,|b_i|<<1/log T; omega smooth, supported in [c_1T,c_2T], omega^{(j)}<<T_0^{-j} for some T_0>=T^{3/4+eps_0}, T_0<<T^b with b>(C+3theta)/2/(C+1), int|omega|<<T. Then $I_{I,J}(\omega)=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\sum_{S\subset I,T\subset J,|S|=|T|}Z_{I_S,J_T}(0)(t/2\pi)^{-\sum_{S}-\sum_T}\omega(t)dt+O\bigl(T^{\frac{3\theta}2+\epsilon}(T^{1+C}/T_0)\bigr)$, where $I_{I,J}(\omega)=\int\prod_{j=1}^3\zeta(\frac12+a_j+it)\zeta(\frac12+b_j-it)\omega(t)dt$.
location: Sec 1, Thm 1.1, eq (1.22) (exponent printed as T^{3theta/2+eps}(T^{1+C}/T_0))

statement: If AD(theta,C) holds for some theta in [1/2,3/2), C>=0, there exists a degree-9 polynomial P_9 with, for every eps>0, $\int_0^T|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|^6dt=TP_9(\log T)+O(T^{\frac{3\theta+1+C}{2+C}+\epsilon})$.
location: Sec 1, Cor 1.2; proof by smooth majorant/minorant of 1_[T,2T], dyadic summation, P_9 from CFKRS contour integral

statement: If AD(1/2,C) holds then error in (1.22) is O(T^{3/4+eps}) for T_0=T^{1-eps} (matching Ivic/Motohashi speculation), and the exponent in Cor 1.2 becomes 1-1/(8+4C)+eps (which exceeds 7/8+eps).
Under a strengthened Conjecture 2 with |a_i|,|b_i|<=delta_0 (small constant) in place of <<1/log X, Thm 1.1 holds with (1.16) replaced by (1.15).
Approximate functional equation for the product of three zeta values with shifts (A>0, delta in (0,1/6), t>=2A+3), used to write the shifted sixth moment as sums of divisor-type sums.
role: Starting point: express I_{I,J}(omega) as diagonal plus off-diagonal (shifted convolution) sums.

statement: Decomposition of I_{I,J}(omega) for |a_i|,|b_i|<=delta<1/2 into main terms and off-diagonal sums under conditions (3.1),(3.3).
role: Reduction to diagonal contribution plus additive divisor sums D_{f;I,J}(r).

statement: Off-diagonal terms: after separating variables (support of f_{r;M,N} in [M,2M]x[N,2N]) and applying AD(theta,C) with error P^C X^{theta+eps} summed over r, the off-diagonal contributes main terms matching the 'swap' terms plus O(T^{3theta/2+eps}...) error; Lemma 5.4 bounds an auxiliary sum for 0<theta<1.
role: Evaluation of off-diagonal via the conjectured additive divisor formula.

statement: Evaluation of the resulting main terms as sums of residues; Prop 6.2 gives identities identifying them with Z_{I_S,J_T}(0) (j-swap terms); Lemma 6.3 (delta in (0,1/7)) handles analytic properties; Prop 6.5 finishes with residue at poles s=p_j.
role: Match arithmetic main terms to the CFKRS recipe.

statement: Euler factors: Z_{X,Y}(s)=prod_{x,y} zeta(1+s+x+y) A_{X,Y}(s) with explicit A for |X|=|Y|=3; multiplicative functions g_X(s,n), G_X(s,n).
role: Arithmetic factor of the conjectured main term; matches Conrey-Gonek singular series.

statement: (i) The category of points of the topos $\widehat{\mathbb N^\times}$ is equivalent to the category of totally ordered groups isomorphic to non-trivial subgroups of $(\mathbb Q,\mathbb Q_+)$ with injective order-preserving morphisms. (ii) The space of isomorphism classes of points is canonically $\mathbb Q^\times_+\backslash\mathbb A_f/\hat{\mathbb Z}^*$, with $\mathbb A_f$ the finite adeles of $\mathbb Q$ and $\mathbb Q^\times_+$ acting by multiplication.

The category of points of $\widehat{\mathbb N^\times}$ is equivalent to the category of algebraic extensions $F\subset K\subset\bar F=\mathbb Q_{\max}$ of the semifield $F=\mathbb Z_{\max}$ (fraction semifield of $\overline{\mathbb N}$), morphisms being injective semifield morphisms.

At the point of $\widehat{\mathbb N^\times}$ attached to an intermediate semifield $F\subset K\subset\bar F=\mathbb Q_{\max}$, the stalk of the structure sheaf $\mathcal O=\overline{\mathbb N}$ is the semiring $\mathcal O_K=\{r\in K: r\vee1=1\}$ ($\vee$ = semiring addition).

The points of the arithmetic site $(\widehat{\mathbb N^\times},\overline{\mathbb N})$ over the maximal compact subring $[0,1]_{\max}\subset\mathbb R^{\max}_+$ form the quotient $\mathbb Q^\times_+\backslash\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q}/\hat{\mathbb Z}^*$ of the adele class space of $\mathbb Q$ by $\hat{\mathbb Z}^*$ (the extracted text writes the quotient as $\mathbb Q^\times/\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q}/\hat{\mathbb Z}^*$ in the statement). The Frobenius action $\mathrm{Fr}_\lambda\in\mathrm{Aut}([0,1]_{\max})$ corresponds to the action of the idele class group mod $\hat{\mathbb Z}^*$. The quotient is the disjoint union of (i) $\mathbb Q^\times_+\backslash\mathbb A_f/\hat{\mathbb Z}^*$ (archimedean component 0; the points defined over $\mathbb B$) and (ii) $\mathbb Q^\times_+\backslash((\mathbb A_f/\hat{\mathbb Z}^*)\times\mathbb R^*_+)$, in bijection with rank-one subgroups of $\mathbb R$ via $(a,\lambda)\mapsto\lambda H_a$, $H_a=\{q\in\mathbb Q: qa\in\hat{\mathbb Z}\}$.

Let $N(u)$, $u\in[1,\infty)$, be the counting distribution of the Frobenius action on the points of the arithmetic site over $[0,1]_{\max}$. The zeta function $\zeta_N$ defined by $\frac{\partial_s\zeta_N(s)}{\zeta_N(s)}=-\int_1^\infty N(u)u^{-s}d^*u$ is the complete Riemann zeta function $\zeta_{\mathbb Q}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$.
hypotheses: N(u) obtained from the trace formula (1) applied to test functions $h(u)=g(|u|)$ with $\mathrm{supp}\,g\subset(1,\infty)$, plus [6] Sec. 2

statement: 3.1: $\mathbb N\otimes_{\mathbb B}\mathbb N\simeq\mathrm{Sub}_{\ge}(\mathbb N\times\mathbb N)$ (hereditary subsets for product order), with unique bilinear multiplication $(q^a\otimes q^b)(q^c\otimes q^d)=q^{a+c}\otimes q^{b+d}$ making it a semiring of characteristic 1 with an action $\mathrm{Fr}_{n,m}$ of $\mathbb N^\times\times\mathbb N^\times$. 3.6: $\mathrm{Conv}_{\ge}(\mathbb N\times\mathbb N)$ (closed convex $C\subset\mathbb R_+^2$ with $C+Q=C$, extreme points in $\mathbb N^2$; operations convex hull of union and Minkowski sum) is multiplicatively cancellative, the convex-hull map $\gamma$ coincides with the reduction $\iota$ to the image in the fraction semifield, and it is universal among homomorphisms $\rho$ to multiplicatively cancellative semirings with $\rho^{-1}(0)=\{0\}$.

3.3: the range of $\mu\circ\mathrm{Fr}_{n,m}$ depends only on $r=n/m$; for coprime $n,m$ it contains the ideal $\{q^a: a\ge(n-1)(m-1)\}$; and it coincides with $m_r(\sum q^{n_i}\otimes q^{m_i})=q^{\alpha}$, $\alpha=\inf(rn_i+m_i)$. 3.4: for $\lambda\in\mathbb R^*_+$, $q\in(0,1)$, $F(\lambda,q)(\sum q^{n_i}\otimes q^{m_i})=q^{\alpha}$, $\alpha=\inf(\lambda n_i+m_i)$ is a homomorphism $\mathbb N\otimes_{\mathbb B}\mathbb N\to\mathbb R^{\max}_+$; its image $R(\lambda)$ is independent of $q$, and $R(\lambda)\cong R(\lambda')$ iff $\lambda'=\lambda$ or $\lambda'=1/\lambda$.

For $\lambda,\lambda'\in\mathbb R^*_+$ with $\lambda\lambda'\notin\mathbb Q$, the composition of Frobenius correspondences is $\Psi(\lambda)\circ\Psi(\lambda')=\Psi(\lambda\lambda')$; the same holds for $\lambda,\lambda'$ rational. When $\lambda,\lambda'$ are irrational and $\lambda\lambda'\in\mathbb Q$, $\Psi(\lambda)\circ\Psi(\lambda')=\Psi(\lambda\lambda')\circ\mathrm{Id}^\epsilon=\mathrm{Id}^\epsilon\circ\Psi(\lambda\lambda')$, where $\mathrm{Id}^\epsilon$ is the tangential deformation of the identity correspondence on the sub-semiring $\overline{\mathbb N}^\epsilon$ of germs at $0$ of continuous functions $\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^{\max}_+$ generated by $q$ and $q^{1+\epsilon}$.
hypotheses: Reduced correspondences (Def. 4.1): triple (R, l, r) with R multiplicatively cancellative, l,r: N-bar to R with l^{-1}(0)=r^{-1}(0)={0}, R generated by l(N-bar)r(N-bar)

statement: $\mathrm{Tr}_{\mathrm{distr}}(\int_G h(u)\vartheta_u d^*u)=\sum_{v\in\Sigma_{\mathbb Q}}\int_{\mathbb Q_v^*}\frac{h(u^{-1})}{|1-u|}d^*u$, $\vartheta_u\xi(x)=\xi(u^{-1}x)$ on $\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q}/\mathbb Q^*$, $G=GL_1(\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q})/GL_1(\mathbb Q)$.
role: Imported (Connes 1999, Connes-Marcolli, Meyer 2005); used with $h(u)=g(|u|)$, supp g in (1,infinity), to obtain the counting distribution N(u) in Thm 2.7. The note only states it.

statement: Universal property of $\mathrm{Conv}_{\ge}(\mathbb N\times\mathbb N)$ as the reduced (multiplicatively cancellative) quotient of $\mathbb N\otimes_{\mathbb B}\mathbb N$.
role: Identifies the structure sheaf of the reduced square, on which Frobenius correspondences are built.

statement: For coprime $n,m$, the range of $\mu\circ\mathrm{Fr}_{n,m}$ contains $\{q^a: a\ge(n-1)(m-1)\}$.
role: Frobenius (coin) problem bound; shows rational Frobenius correspondences are genuinely curves in the square.

statement: Let f satisfy TF1 (symmetric), TF2 ($f(x+t(1,\dots,1))=f(x)$) and TF3 (rapid decay on $\sum x_j=0$), with $\hat f$ supported in $\sum_{j}|\xi_j|<2$. Let $g\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$, $h(r)=\int g(u)e^{iru}du$. Then as $T\to\infty$, $R_n(T,f,h)=\sum^{\ne}_{j_1..j_n}h(\gamma_{j_1}/T)\cdots h(\gamma_{j_n}/T)f(\tfrac L{2\pi}\gamma_{j_1},\dots,\tfrac L{2\pi}\gamma_{j_n})\sim \frac{1}{2\pi}T\log T\int h(r)^n dr\int_{\mathbb R^n}f(x)W_n(x)\delta(\tfrac{x_1+\dots+x_n}{n})dx$, with $L=\log T$ (formula reconstructed; displayed equation lost in OCR). No RH assumed (sums over zeros with complex ordinates).
hypotheses: h Fourier transform of compactly supported smooth g

label_in_source: Theorem 1.2 (n-level correlations of the zeros, under RH)
statement: Assume RH. For f with TF1-3 and $\mathrm{supp}\,\hat f\subset\{\sum|\xi_j|<2\}$, $R_n(B_N,f)\to\int_{\mathbb R^n}f(x)W_n(x)\delta(\tfrac{x_1+\dots+x_n}n)dx$ as $N\to\infty$ (GUE n-level correlations). n=2 is Montgomery's theorem; n=3 is announced by Hejhal in different form.

The same GUE n-level correlation holds for principal L-functions of cuspidal automorphic representations of GL(m)/Q (proof deferred to the Duke paper, with support restriction $\sum|\xi_j|<2/m$ there).
hypotheses: Hypothesis H on prime-power coefficients (automatic for m<=3)

statement: Smoothed Riemann explicit formula relating $\sum_\rho h(\gamma)$ to sums over prime powers $\Lambda(n)n^{-1/2}g(\pm\log n)$.
role: Converts n-fold sums over zeros into n-fold sums over primes; avoids RH in Theorem 1.1.

statement: Identity relating the all-indices sums $C_F$ (variables in a block of a set partition identified) via Moebius inversion on the partition lattice to the GUE determinant's Fourier transform; precise formula lost in OCR.
role: Passes from unrestricted sum $C_n$ (over all indices) to distinct-index sum $R_n$.

statement: Identity coupling the pairing structure of the prime sums (diagonal pairs) with the cycle structure of the determinant defining $W_n$; proved by Spitzer's combinatorial lemma.
role: Core combinatorial step producing the sine-kernel determinant from primes.

statement: The categories of algebraic endomotives $\mathcal E V^0_{K,E}$, Artin motives $\mathcal C V^0_{K,E}$, and analytic endomotives $C^*V^0_E$ are related: (1) $G\mapsto G(\bar K)$ gives a tensor functor $F:\mathcal E V^0_{K,E}\to C^*V^0_E$; (2) $\mathrm{Gal}(\bar K/K)$ acts by natural transformations of $F$; (3) Artin motives embed as a full subcategory of algebraic endomotives; (4) the composite $k\circ F:\mathcal E V^0_{K,E}\to KK\otimes E$ is well defined (statement partially read).

If $\varphi$ is a regular extremal $KMS_\beta$ state on $\bar A$ whose GNS factor is of type $I_\infty$, there is an irreducible representation $\pi_\varphi$ on $H(\varphi)$ and an unbounded self-adjoint $H$ with $e^{-\beta H}$ trace class, $\varphi(x)=\mathrm{Trace}(\pi_\varphi(x)e^{-\beta H})/\mathrm{Trace}(e^{-\beta H})$ and $e^{itH}\pi_\varphi(x)e^{-itH}=\pi_\varphi(\sigma_t(x))$.

For the Bost-Connes endomotive and a character $\chi$ of $\hat{\mathbb Z}^*$, the representation of $\mathbb R_+^*$ on $M=HC_0(p_\chi D(A,\varphi))$ realizes the zeros of $L_\chi$: for $z\in I_\beta$ viewed as character of $\mathrm{Hol}(I_\beta)$ with one-dimensional module $\mathbb C_z$, $M\otimes_{\mathrm{Hol}(I_\beta)}\mathbb C_z\ne\{0\}\iff L_\chi(-iz)=0$.

The representation of $C_K$ on $H^1_{K,\mathbb C,\chi}=HC_0(H^1_{K,\mathbb C,\chi})$ gives the spectral realization of the zeros of the L-function with Grossencharakter $\chi$ (variant of Thm 1 of Connes 1999).
hypotheses: K global field; noncanonical $C_K\simeq C_{K,1}\times N$

statement: For $f\in\mathcal S(C_K)$, the operator $\vartheta_m(f)=\int\vartheta_m(\gamma)f(\gamma)d^*\gamma$ on $H^1_{K,\mathbb C,\chi}$ is trace class with $\mathrm{Trace}(\vartheta_m(f)|_{H^1})=\sum_{L(\tilde\chi,\rho)=0,\ \rho\in\mathbb C/N^\perp}\hat f(\tilde\chi,\rho)$.

For $h\in\mathcal S(C_K)$: $\mathrm{Trace}(\vartheta_m(h)|_{H^1})=\hat h(0)+\hat h(1)-\Delta\bullet\Delta h(1)-\sum_v\int'_{(K_v^*,e_{K_v})}\frac{h(u^{-1})}{|1-u|}d^*u$ (Lefschetz-type trace formula with explicit formula; statement as extracted, terms partly garbled).
hypotheses: preferred additive characters $e_\mathbb R(x)=e^{-2\pi ix}$, $e_\mathbb C(z)=e^{-2\pi i(z+\bar z)}$, nonarchimedean $\ker e_L=O$

statement: The following are equivalent: (i) all L-functions with Grossencharakter on $K$ satisfy RH; (ii) $\mathrm{Trace}\,\vartheta_m(f\star f^\sharp)|_{H^1}\ge0$ for all $f\in\mathcal S(C_K)$, where $(f_1\star f_2)(g)=\int f_1(k)f_2(k^{-1}g)d^*g$ and $f^\sharp(g)=|g|^{-1}\bar f(g^{-1})$.

Lefschetz formula for archimedean local factors: for $K_v=\mathbb C$ (resp. $\mathbb R$, Weil group $W$), $m\in\mathbb N$, $z=\frac{1+m}{2}+is$: $\int'_{\mathbb C^*}\mathrm{Trace}(\pi(H^m,u))|u|_{\mathbb C}^{z}\frac{d^*u}{|1-u|_{\mathbb C}}=-2\,\Im\frac{d}{ds}\log L_{\mathbb C}(H^m,z)$ (resp. analogous over $W$).
Assuming (4.26), the map Trace composed with pi defines a cyclic morphism (cooling to distilled module D(A,phi) = coker of Trace o pi).
role: Distillation step producing the Lambda-module.

statement: Decay/analytic estimates (e.g. |Trace(g(H+c))|=O(e^{-beta c}c^{-N})) and for BC case with beta>1 on Hol(I_beta) acting on A_beta; elements of A_beta cap Ker tau.
role: Analytic control making the cooling morphism well defined.

statement: For M type III_1 and lambda in ]0,1[, T=-ln2pi/lambda... M_T=M x_{sigma_T} Z is type III_lambda with Mod = lambda^Z and dual action of R_+^*/lambda^Z with fixed points M.
role: Type III factors and unramified extensions: passage from III_1 to III_lambda mirrors unramified extension of finite fields.

statement: Identification Omega-tilde_beta ~ hat Z^* x R_+^* ~ C_Q for beta>1; character-twisted trace expression.
role: Matches the space of extremal KMS states with the idele class group of Q, connecting BC system to adele class space.

statement: G acts canonically on X(K-bar); semigroup S acts by partial isomorphisms on projective limit X.
role: Foundation of endomotive category.

statement: For K the function field of a curve C over F_q the (adelic) trace formula holds (statement not fully read).
role: Consistency check in positive characteristic.

statement: Let $f(s)=\sum a_n n^{-s}$, $a_1\neq0$, absolutely convergent for $\sigma>\sigma_a$, and suppose $f$ has a zero in $\sigma>\sigma_a$. Put $\alpha(f)=\sup\{\Re\rho: f(\rho)=0,\ \Re\rho>\sigma_a\}$. Then $1/f(s)=\sum b_n n^{-s}$ converges for $\sigma>\alpha(f)$ and $\limsup_{n\to\infty}\log|b_n|/\log n=\alpha(f)$.
hypotheses: f has a zero with real part >sigma_a

statement: Let $f(s)=\sum a_n n^{-s}$ with $a_1=1$, $a_n=O(n^{\varepsilon})$, and suppose $f$ has a zero $\rho$ with $\Re\rho=\beta>1$. Then for $1/f=\sum b_n n^{-s}$: $\sum_{n\le X}|b_n|^2/n\gg X^{2\beta-1+o(1)}$ as $X\to\infty$. Corollary 6: with $\sigma^*>1$ the supremum of real parts of zeros, $\sum_{n\le X}|b_n|^2/n\gg X^{2\sigma^*-1+o(1)}$.
location: Sec. 4, p. 236-238 (proof via Carlson-type truncation of 1/f, reversed)

statement: For the Davenport-Heilbronn-type family $f(s,\xi;\psi)=\tfrac12[(1-i\xi)L(s,\chi_1\psi)+(1+i\xi)L(s,\chi_3\psi)]$ (chi mod 5 quartic characters, psi principal mod q), let $\sigma(\xi,q)$ be the sup of $\sigma>1$ with a zero at height some $t$. (1) For $\xi=\tan\theta$ real, $\sigma(\xi,q)$ is the unique $\sigma>1$ with $\sum_{p\equiv2,3\ (5),(p,q)=1}\arctan(p^{-\sigma})=\pi/2-|\theta|$. (2) For $\xi$ purely imaginary, $|\xi|>1$, it is the $\sigma>1$ with $\sum_{p\equiv 2,3(5),(p,q)=1}\log\frac{1+p^{-\sigma}}{1-p^{-\sigma}}=\log\frac{1+i\xi}{1-i\xi}$.
hypotheses: xi real, or purely imaginary with |xi|>1
location: Sec. 5, p. 241 (via Kronecker's theorem on log p independence, as in Bombieri-Mueller)

statement: For $\xi$ real and a set $P$ of primes, $\sigma(\xi,P)$ solves $\sum_{p\in P,\ p\equiv2,3(5)}\arctan(p^{-\sigma})=\pi/2-|\theta|$. For $P=\{p,q\}$, $p\equiv2,q\equiv3 \pmod 5$, a zero with $\sigma>1$ exists iff $|\xi|>(pq-1)/(p+q)$. Numerically $\sigma(\tau_-,\{2,3\})=2.314909762289685\ldots$ for the second Davenport-Heilbronn function.

For $\xi$ real, $\sigma(\xi,q)\le\sigma(\xi,1)-\delta(q)$ where $\delta(q)=\frac{S}{1+S}(\sigma(\xi,1)-1)>0$, $S=\sum_{p|q,\,p\equiv2,3(5)}\arctan p^{-\sigma(\xi,1)}$. Consequently, for $n$ coprime to $P(z)=\prod_{p\le z,p\equiv2,3(5)}p$, $b(n,\xi)=O(n^{\sigma(\xi,1)-\nu(z)+o(1)})$ with $\nu(z)\sim z^{-\sigma(\xi,1)}$.

For $p\equiv2,q\equiv3 \pmod 5$ and $\alpha(u,\xi;\{p,q\})=\limsup_{h/(h+k)\to u}\log|b(p^hq^k,\xi)|/\log(p^hq^k)$: $\alpha\le-\frac{u\log|r(u)|+(1-u)\log|s(u)|}{4(u\log p+(1-u)\log q)}$, with $(r,s)$ the minimizing admissible critical point among the list in Lemma 12 (singular points of the generating polynomial $f(z,w)$); equality holds when $(r,s)=(z_\pm(u),z_\pm(1-u))$ with $z_\pm$ given by (7.39). Lemma 12 locates the extrema of $m\log|z|+n\log|w|$ on $\{f=0,|z|,|w|<1\}$, $\xi\ne0,\xi^4\ne1$.

For $p,q=2,3$, $\xi=\tau_-$: $\max_u\alpha(u,\tau_-;\{2,3\})$ is attained at $u=0.71201279109227\ldots$ with value $2.31490976228968512350665794\ldots=\sigma(\tau_-,\{2,3\})$, agreeing with Theorem 3 (which equates limsup growth with $\alpha(f)$). Authors note a direct proof of this equality of the two numbers is not known.

Linear combinations of L-functions with functional equation of L-type: Selberg's method gives $N_0(f;T)>c\,n^{-1}T\log T$ zeros on the critical line (GL(1)-type, n terms); Bombieri-Hejhal give $\sim n(2\pi)^{-1}T\log T$ zeros on the line under (i) Euler products with Ramanujan, (ii) same functional equation, (iii) independence, (iv) a Riemann hypothesis for the constituents, (v) a weak pair-correlation property; Montgomery conjectured almost all zeros on the line.
If $a_1\ne0$, $f=\sum a_nn^{-s}$ converges for $\sigma>1$ then $1/f$ is a Dirichlet series for large $\sigma$; if moreover $f\ne0$ for $\sigma>1$, then $b_n=O(n^{1+\varepsilon})$.
role: baseline bound sharpened by Theorem 3

statement: If $f$ converges and has no zeros for $\sigma>\alpha$, $a_1\ne0$, then $1/f$ converges for $\sigma>\alpha$.
role: gives abscissa of 1/f

label_in_source: Hille truncation argument inside proof of Thm 3
statement: Truncation $f_z$ to $\langle P_z\rangle$ (z-smooth integers) preserves a zero near rho by Rouche/argument principle; Landau applied to $1/f_z$ gives upper bound, pole at $\rho_z$ forces $\sum_{n\in\langle P_z\rangle}|b_n|n^{-\beta_z}$ divergent; counting $\#\{n\le2^\nu\}\le\nu^z$ gives $|b_n|>n^{\alpha(f)-o(1)}$.
role: core lower-bound mechanism

statement: For psi principal mod q, the closure of $\{g(\sigma+it,\psi)\}$ equals $V(\sigma,q)=\{\sum F(p^{-\sigma-i\theta_p})\}$ with independent $\theta_p$, where $F(z)=\log\frac{1+z}{1-z}$; zeros with $\sigma>1$ correspond to $\alpha+2i\theta+(2k+1)\pi i\in V(\sigma,q)$.
role: reduces two-Euler-product combinations to a prime-supported series; used exactly because only two Euler products appear

statement: $\sum_{h,k}a(p^hq^k,\xi)x^hy^k=\frac{1+\xi x-\xi y+xy}{(1+x^2)(1+y^2)}$ for p=2,q=3; reciprocal generating function $F(x,y;\xi)=\frac{(1+x^2)(1+y^2)}{1+\xi x-\xi y+xy}$.
role: alternative (Bohr power series) route to coefficient asymptotics

statement: Let $N_0(T)$ be the number of zeros $\rho=\tfrac12+it$ of $\zeta$ with $0<t<T$. There exist $K>0$ and $T_0$ such that $N_0(T)>KT$ for all $T>T_0$. (Proof gives at least $T/(4H)$ zeros in $(T,2T)$ for a sufficiently large absolute constant $H$.)
Let $U=T^a$ with $a>\tfrac12$. There exist $K=K(a)>0$ and $T_0=T_0(a)$ such that $N_0(T+U)-N_0(T)>KU$ for all $T>T_0$.
location: Sec. 1, p. 283; proved in Sec. 3-5, pp. 298-315 (conclusion at 5.5, p. 315)

statement: If $T^a<U<T^b$ with $a>\tfrac12$ (and $b=5/8$ first, then removed) and $0<H<T^c$ with $c=c(a)>0$ small, then with $I(t,H)=\int_t^{t+H}X(u)\,du$: $J=\int_T^{T+U}I^2\,dt=\pi\sqrt{2\pi}\,HU+O\!\left(U/\log T\right)$ (constant as I read it off the scan; not independently re-derived).
For $H,K$ as in Lemma 18, $\int_T^{T+U} I(t,H)\,I(t+H,K)\,dt=O(U/\log T)$ uniformly in $0\le H,K\le T^c$ (orthogonality of consecutive block integrals).

For $\sigma>0,s\ne1,x>0$: $\zeta(s)+\frac{x^{1-s}}{1-s}-\sum_{n\le x}'n^{-s}=2(2\pi)^{s-1}\sum_{n\ge1}n^{s-1}\int_{2n\pi x}^\infty u^{-s}\cos u\,du$ (valid for $\sigma>-1$ in the second form); proof suggested by H. Cramer.
role: Exact representation of zeta that gives the approximate functional equation and, with $x\to0$, the functional equation.

statement: For $\sigma\ge\sigma_0>0$, $|s-1|\ge\delta>0$, $|t|<2\pi x/C$, $C>1$: $\zeta(s)=\sum_{n\le x}n^{-s}-\frac{x^{1-s}}{1-s}+O(x^{-\sigma})$ uniformly.
role: Dirichlet-polynomial approximation of zeta by van der Corput-type stationary-phase-free argument.

statement: For $\sigma\ge\sigma_0>0$, $|t|<Ax$: $\eta(s)=(1-2^{1-s})\zeta(s)=\sum_{n\le x}(-1)^{n-1}n^{-s}+O(x^{-\sigma})$ and $\Theta(s)=\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{(-1)^{n-1}n^{-s}}{\log n}=\sum_{n\le x}\frac{(-1)^{n-1}n^{-s}}{\log n}+O(x^{-\sigma})$.
role: Alternating (eta) series on the critical line, whose antiderivative-in-$s$ ($1/\log n$ weights) controls $\int\eta\,dt$ in Theorem A.

statement: With $\psi(t)=\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{(-1)^{n-1}}{\log n}n^{-1/2-it}$: $\int_T^{2T}|\psi(t+u)|^2dt=O(T)$ uniformly for $0\le u\le T$; and $\frac1{2T}\int_{-T}^T|\chi(\tfrac12+it)|^2dt\sim\sum_{n\ge2}\frac1{n(\log n)^2}$.
role: Mean square bound for the error term $\Psi$ in $\underline I>AH+\Psi$.

statement: $\int_0^T\{I(t,H)\}^2dt<AHT$ for $T>T_0(H)$.
role: Upper mean-square bound for $\int X$ over blocks of length $H$; obtained via Lemma 10 (Mellin/Hankel-function formula for $\int\Gamma(s+a)\Gamma(s+b)\zeta(2s+2a)\zeta(2s+2b)y^{-2s}ds$), the Abel weight $e^{-\epsilon t}$, and the divisor-type diagonal estimate $\underline C_m=O(Hm)$ (2.783) with $k=1-1/H$.

statement: For fixed $0\le\sigma<1$, $x,y>A$, $2\pi xy=|t|$: $\zeta(s)=\sum_{n<x}n^{-s}+\chi\sum_{n<y}n^{s-1}+O\big((x^{-\sigma}+|t|^{1/2-\sigma}y^{\sigma-1})\log t\big)$, where $\chi=\left(\frac{|t|}{2\pi e}\right)^{-it}\left(\frac{t}{2\pi}\right)^{1/2-\sigma}e^{\frac14\pi i\,\mathrm{sgn}\,t}$. Lemma 14 is the sharp version without the $\log t$ and is stated but not proved here.
role: Hardy-Littlewood approximate functional equation (pre-Hardy-Littlewood 1929); feeds Lemma 17: $X(t)=\Theta+\bar\Theta+O(t^{-1/4}\log t)$ with $\tau=\sqrt{t/2\pi}$.

statement: There is $A$ such that $\underline I=\int_t^{t+H}|X(u)|du>\tfrac12H$ on $(T,T+U)$ except in a set $\underline S$ of measure $<AU/H^2$ (for $H\ge4$).
role: Lower bound for absolute-value integral, via $|\int\zeta|$, mean square of $M$ and Lemma 19; combined with $\int I^2<AHU$ (Lemma 18, 5.51) to force $|I|<\underline I$ and hence sign changes.

statement: RH (Bombieri-Lagarias form): $\mathrm{RH}\iff s(f,f)\le 0$ for all real compactly supported $f$ on $\mathbb R_+^*$ with $\int f(u)\,d^*u=\int f(u)\,du=0$, where $s(f,g)=N(f\star\tilde g)$, $\tilde g(u)=u^{-1}g(u^{-1})$, $N(h)=\sum_{n\ge1}\Lambda(n)h(n)+\int_1^\infty\frac{u^2h(u)-h(1)}{u^2-1}d^*u+c\,h(1)$, $c=\tfrac12(\log\pi+\gamma)$. Interpreted (via explicit formulas, ref [22]) as $s(f,f)=D\bullet D$ with $D=\int f(\lambda)\Psi_\lambda d^*\lambda$ on the square of the Scaling Site; the strategy is to assume $s(f,f)>0$, use a (missing) Riemann-Roch to make $D$ or $-D$ effective and contradict degree/codegree zero.
hypotheses: f compactly supported real, vanishing integrals
conditional_on: existence of a Riemann-Roch formula on the square of the Scaling Site (not available)
definition of H^1 as idempotent-monoid cohomology (open)

statement: For $f$ holomorphic on an annulus $A(r_1,r_2)$, with $\tau(f)(x)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}\log|f(e^{-x+i\theta})|d\theta$, the values $-\log|z_i|$ of the zeros are the tropical zeros (with multiplicity) of the convex piecewise affine integral-slope function $\tau(f)$ on $(-\log r_2,-\log r_1)$; $\tau(fg)=\tau(f)+\tau(g)$ and $\tau(f(z^n))(x)=\tau(f)(nx)$ (compatibility with the $\mathbb N^\times$ action). Non-archimedean analogue (Thm 3.1) via Newton polygons.
hypotheses: K complete algebraically closed over Q_p in the non-archimedean case

statement: A real function $\varphi(\sigma)$ on $\alpha<\sigma<\beta$ is the Jensen function of an almost periodic analytic function on the strip iff $\varphi$ is convex and on each compact $I\subset(\alpha,\beta)$ there is a finite $\mathbb Q$-linearly independent $F\subset\mathbb R$ and $C<\infty$ with slope jumps $\varphi'(\sigma_2)-\varphi'(\sigma_1)=\sum_{\mu\in F}r(\mu)\mu$, $r(\mu)\in\mathbb Q$, $\sum r(\mu)^2\le C|\varphi'(\sigma_2)-\varphi'(\sigma_1)|^2$.
hypotheses: almost periodic analytic function in a strip

statement: 4.3: the asymptotic distribution function $\mu(\sigma)$ of a real almost periodic sequence $U(k)$ is constant on an open interval iff $U$ takes no value there, and then that constant is a rational number in $\frac1{2\pi}M_U$. 4.4: for a dense subgroup $M\subset\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$, a distribution function is the asymptotic distribution of an almost periodic sequence with exponents in $M$ iff it has compact support and its values on constancy intervals lie in $\frac1{2\pi}M$.
hypotheses: U almost periodic sequence on Z

statement: For a prime $p$ there is a unique sequence $U:\mathbb Z\to\mathbb R$ with $U(\sum a_jp^j)=\sum a_jp^{-j-1}$ (digit reversal), $|U(x+np^m)-U(x)|\le p^{-m}$, almost periodic with modul $2\pi H_p$ and distribution function $\mu(\sigma)=\sigma$ on $[0,1]$. Corollary 4.1: for $h\in C[0,1]$, $h(U(n))$ is almost periodic with $d\mu=h_*(\text{Lebesgue})$; for any strictly increasing continuous $\mu$ on $[\alpha,\beta]$ with $\mu(\alpha)=0,\mu(\beta)=1$, $\mu$ is the distribution function of $h(U)$ with $h=\mu^{-1}$.

Let $C=\int f(\lambda)\delta_\lambda d\lambda$ be a continuous divisor on $\mathbb R_+^*$ with compact support. Then there exist finitely many graphs $G_j^\pm$ of maps $g_j^\pm:D_j^\pm\to\mathbb R_+^*$, $D_j^\pm\subset\hat{\mathbb Z}\subset G$, such that the leafwise discrete divisor $D=\sum\pm G_j^\pm$ is a lift of $C$ (proof reduces to Lemma 4.2 of the almost-periodic construction).

Two parabolic 2-dim Q-lattices $(\Lambda_j,\phi_j)=(\alpha_j^{-1}\Lambda_0,\alpha_j^{-1}\rho_j)$, $\rho_j\in P(\hat{\mathbb Z})$, $\alpha_j\in P^+(\mathbb R)$, are commensurable iff there is $g\in P^+(\mathbb Q)$ with $\rho_2=g\rho_1$, $\alpha_2=g\alpha_1$; hence the space of parabolic Q-lattices up to commensurability is canonically isomorphic to the quotient $C_{\mathbb Q}^o$ (eq. 65). Together with Prop. 6.2 the map from parabolic Q-lattices to 2-dim Q-lattices up to scale is injective except in degenerate cases.

For an elliptic curve $E$ with $(\xi,\eta)\in TE\times TE$ (total Tate module), $\xi\ne0$, the associated Q-lattice lies in the range of $\theta$ iff $\langle\xi^\perp,\eta\rangle=\hat{\mathbb Z}$ where $\langle\xi^\perp,\eta\rangle=\{T(\chi)(\eta):\chi\in\xi^\perp\}$. A triangular structure is such a pair; points of $C_{\mathbb Q}$ correspond to triangular elliptic curves modulo the equivalence generated by isogenies (Def. 6.4, Prop. 6.3), and the complex structure of the moduli of triangular curves agrees with that on $C_{\mathbb Q}$ from the right action of $P(\mathbb R)$ (Sect. 6.6).

With $W$ the Witt-type ring of characteristic-one lift, characters $\chi_\lambda:W\to\mathbb C$ ($\chi_\lambda([x])=x^\lambda$), holomorphy of $W$-valued $f$ on a $P^+(\mathbb R)$-orbit defined by $(\lambda X+iY)\chi_\lambda(f)=0\ \forall\lambda$, the Frobenius correspondences $\mathrm{Fra}_\mu(f):=\theta_\mu(R(\mu^{-1})(f))$ preserve this holomorphy condition (uses $[Y,X]=X$).
hypotheses: W-valued function on a leaf of the right P^+(R)-action

statement: Topological lemmas on $\mathbb Z(+\infty)$ and an action of $\mathbb Q_+^*$ on a locally compact metrizable space; Thm 2.2: the space of points of the topos $[0,\infty)\rtimes\mathbb N^\times$ is canonically isomorphic to the (sector of the) adele class space of Q (recalled from [25]).
role: Identifies the Scaling Site's points with the adele class space; the starting geometry for the lift.

statement: $u(q)=-\log|q|$ on $D^*$ extends to a geometric morphism $D^*\rtimes\mathbb N^\times\to[0,\infty)\rtimes\mathbb N^\times$ of toposes.
role: Gives the first complex lift (ringed topos with sheaf of analytic functions).

statement: The classical orbit $\Gamma_{\mathbb Q,cl}\simeq G\times\mathbb R_+^*=\varprojlim H/n\mathbb Z$ is canonically isomorphic to the pro-etale cover $\tilde D^*=\varprojlim(E_n,p_{n,m})$ of the punctured disk, $E_n=D^*$, $p_{n,m}(z)=z^a$ for $m=na$.
role: Links adelic leaf to analytic pro-etale cover of the punctured disk.

statement: On $G=\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q}/(\mathbb Q,+)$ with foliation flow W, $d_W(e_q)=2\pi i q\,e_q$; kernel is 1-dim, cokernel given by Haar measure, so foliated de Rham cohomology is 1-dim in degrees 0 and 1 and zero above.
role: Computes cohomology of the leafwise structure (a substitute H^1 input).

statement: Q-lattice parametrization via $(\Lambda,\phi)$, parabolic specialization and a description of $\xi^\perp=\mathbb Z\chi$ for primitive character $\chi$ of $E$ when $\xi\neq0$ (Lemma 6.5).
role: Used in the proof of Theorem 6.2 (triangular structure criterion).

statement: A zeta-cycle is a circle $C_\mu=\mathbb R_+^*/\mu^{\mathbb Z}$, $L=\log\mu$, such that $\Sigma_\mu E(\mathcal S_0^{ev})$ is not dense in $L^2(C_\mu,d^*u)$, where $E(f)(x)=x^{1/2}\sum_{n>0}f(nx)$, $\Sigma_\mu g(u)=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}g(\mu^ku)$, $\mathcal S_0^{ev}$ = real even Schwartz functions with $f(0)=0=\int f$.

(i) For a zeta-cycle $C$, the spectrum of the scaling action of $\mathbb R_+^*$ on the orthogonal complement of $\Sigma_\mu E(\mathcal S_0^{ev})$ in $L^2(C)$ consists of imaginary parts $s$ of zeros $\tfrac12+is$ of $\zeta$ on the critical line. (ii) Conversely if $s>0$ and $\zeta(\tfrac12+is)=0$, any circle of length an integer multiple of $2\pi/s$ is a zeta-cycle and its spectrum contains $is$.
hypotheses: part (ii): zero on the critical line, $s>0$ real

statement: With $Z$ the set of ordinates of critical zeros: $H(L)=(\Sigma_\mu E(\mathcal S_0^{ev}))^\perp\ne\{0\}\iff\exists s\in Z,n\in\mathbb Z$ with $sL=2\pi n$.
The $n$-fold cover of a zeta-cycle of length $L$ is a zeta-cycle of length $nL$.

If $f$ has bounded variation on $(0,\infty)$, is rapidly decaying at $\infty$, $O(u^2)$ at $0$, and $\int_0^\infty f=0$, then $E(f)(u)$ is pointwise defined, $O(u^{1/2})$ as $u\to0$, rapidly decaying at $\infty$, and $\Sigma_\mu E(f)$ converges geometrically to a bounded measurable function.

For $\lambda^2=11$ the smallest positive eigenvalue of the Weil form $Q^W_\lambda$ on $L^2([\lambda^{-1},\lambda],d^*u)$ is $2.389\times10^{-48}$; eigenvectors are approximated by prolate vectors from $E(\hat\psi_{m,\lambda})$, $m\le\nu(\lambda^2)\sim2\lambda^2$. For $D(\lambda,k)=(1-\Pi)D_0(1-\Pi)$, $D_0=-iu\partial_u$, eigenvalues become $k$-independent at special $\lambda$ and then equal zeta ordinates; first 31 zeros reproduced for $5\le\lambda^2\le16.5$ (authors estimate random-agreement probability ~$10^{-50}$).

$\mathcal S_0^{ev}$ is scaling invariant; $E\circ\lambda^{-1/2}\vartheta(\lambda)=\vartheta(\lambda)\circ E$, $\vartheta(\lambda)\Sigma_\mu=\Sigma_\mu\vartheta(\lambda)$; scaling induces an action of $\mathbb R_+^*/\mu^{\mathbb Z}$ on $\Sigma_\mu E(\mathcal S_0^{ev})$.
role: Makes the complement a unitary representation of a compact abelian group (sum of characters $u^{is}$, $\mu^{is}=1$).

label_in_source: Mellin identity in proof of Thm 6.4
statement: For $f\in\mathcal S_0^{ev}$: $\int u^{is}E(f)(u)d^*u=\zeta(\tfrac12+is)\int u^{is}f(u)d^*u$ (Fubini for $\Im$ large, then analytic continuation; pole of $\zeta(\tfrac12-iz)$ at $z=i/2$ cancelled since $\hat f(0)=0$).
role: Core analytic step linking orthogonality to zeta zeros.

statement: For $f(x)=e^{-\pi x^2}\pi x^2(-2\pi x^2+3)\in\mathcal S_0^{ev}$: $\int u^{is}E(f)(u)d^*u=(\tfrac14+s^2)\zeta_{\mathbb Q}(\tfrac12+is)$ ($\zeta_{\mathbb Q}$ completed zeta).
role: A single test function forces $\tfrac12+is$ to be a zero.

statement: For $\lambda>1$, an explicit formula defines a lower-bounded lower semicontinuous quadratic form $Q^W_\lambda$ on $L^2([\lambda^{-1},\lambda],d^*u)$; its lower bound is the limit of smallest eigenvalues of finite-dimensional compressions (exact statements not read in detail).
role: Rigorous framework for numerics.

statement: $D(\lambda,k)$ with periodic function multiplication gives a spectral triple; counting of nonzero eigenvalues for $E=2\pi\mu$ (not read in detail).
role: Defines the spectral triple compared with zeros.

statement: With $C_k=\sum_{n\ge1}n^{-2k}=\zeta(2k)$ and $F(x)=\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{(-1)^{k+1}x^k}{C_k\,\Gamma(k)}$, one has $F(x)=\frac1{2i}\int_{a-i\infty}^{a+i\infty}\frac{x^z}{\zeta(2z)\Gamma(z)\sin(\pi z)}\,dz$ for $a$ in a fixed range with $a\ge 1/2$ (garbled in translation; unconditionally valid at $a=1/2$ up to $1$), absolutely/uniformly convergent for $-\pi/2+\delta\le\arg x\le\pi/2-\delta$ (sign of angle range garbled in translation).
$F(x)=o(x^{1/2})$ as $x\to\infty$ uniformly in an angle $|\arg x|\le \pi/2-\delta$.
hypotheses: unconditional; uses the classical bound for $1/\zeta$ on Re s=1 (Landau Handbuch I pp.177-178)

statement: For $\delta\le\Re s\le 2-\delta$ (strip given in translation as $z+\delta\le\Re s\le 2-\delta$, garbled, $1\ldots$ lower bound $\delta$ unconditional range $0<\Re s<2$ intersected with convergence) : $\dfrac{\Gamma(1-s/2)}{\zeta(s)}=\int_0^\infty x^{-(s/2+1)}F(x)\,dx$.
hypotheses: unconditional in the strip where the integral converges by (3)

statement: RH holds iff for every $\delta>0$, $F(x)=O\big(x^{1/4+\delta}\big)$ as $x\to+\infty$ along the positive real axis.
$F(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}\mu(n)\frac{x}{n^2}e^{-x/n^2}$; also $\sum_{n\ge1}F(x/n^2)=xe^{-x}$.

If $F(x)=O(x^{1/4+\delta})$ holds on some sector (half-plane-like angle) inside $|\arg x|<\pi/2$, it holds on the positive real axis; conversely (6) on the positive real axis implies it in any such angle.

$F$ is entire of order 1 (exponential type 1, $|F(x)|<|x|e^{|x|}$), $F(x)/ (xe^{-x}\cdot)$-type limit $e^{x}F(-x)/x	o -1$ hmm (translation: $\lim e^{-x}F(-x)/x=-1$) as $x	o+\infty$; its zeros $\gamma_
u$ satisfy $\sum|\gamma_
u|^{-1-\epsilon}<\infty$ but $\sum|\gamma_
u|^{-1}=\infty$; canonical form $F(x)=xe^{\gamma x}\prod(1-x/\gamma_

u}$; $F$ has infinitely many non-real zeros and changes sign on $(0,\infty)$ at least once.

statement: Interchange of $\sum_n$ and $\int_0^\infty$ in $\zeta(s)\phi(s)=\sum_n\int x^{-(s/2+1)}F(x/n^2)dx$ is legitimate, using $|F(x/n^2)|<M(x/n^2)^a$ with $1/2<a<\Re s/2$.
role: Gives Mellin identity (5).

statement: Under RH, $1/\zeta(s)=O(|s|^r)$ for $\Re s\ge 1/2+\delta$, $r=r(\delta)$.
role: Imported: lets one shift $a$ down to $1/4+\epsilon$ in (1), giving $F=O(x^{1/4+\epsilon})$ (necessity).
location: sec. 4, cites Landau Handbuch II p.870

statement: Entire $\Phi=\sum a_nx^n$ of the form (8) (genus<=1 with real/complex zero data) also has form (9) (all real zeros of one sign) iff one of the sequences $(a_n)$, $((-1)^na_n)$ has finitely many sign changes.
role: Imported; shows F has infinitely many non-real zeros.

statement: For K a global field and any $f\in\mathcal S(C_K)$, the operator $\vartheta_m(f)$ acting on $H^1(\mathbb A_K/K^*,C_K)$ is of trace class and $\mathrm{Tr}(\vartheta_m(f)|H^1)=\sum_{\rho\in\mathbb C/N^\perp,\ L(\tilde\chi,\rho)=0}\hat f(\tilde\chi,\rho)$ (all zeros, including off-critical, with multiplicity as in the setting of Meyer's nuclear spaces).
hypotheses: f in Schwartz-Bruhat space of C_K (Meyer's setting)
H^1 defined as cokernel of the restriction map in cyclic modules (Def 4.10)

statement: $\mathrm{Tr}(\vartheta_m(f)|H^1)=\hat f(0)+\hat f(1)-(\log|a|)f(1)-\sum_{v\in\Sigma_K}\int'_{(K_v^*,e_{K_v})}\frac{f(u^{-1})}{|1-u|}d^*u$, with $|a|$ the module of the differential idele (log|a| = -log of discriminant for number fields; $=(2-2g)\log q$ analogue in function fields) and principal values taken w.r.t. $e_{K_v}$.

All L-functions with Grossencharakter on K satisfy RH iff $\langle\Delta^{-1/2}f,\Delta^{-1/2}f^*\rangle\ge0$ for all $f\in\mathcal S(C_K)$, where $f^*(g)=f(g^{-1})$, $\Delta_z f(g)=|g|^zf(g)$; equivalently $\langle f,f^\sharp\rangle\ge 0$ with $f^\sharp(g)=|g|^{-1}f(g^{-1})$, pairing $\langle f_1,f_2\rangle=\mathrm{Tr}(\vartheta_m(f_1\star f_2)|H^1)$ (eq 4.47).
hypotheses: Weil's positivity criterion imported from Weil [41]

statement: If f lies in V = range of Tr∘rho (restriction from adeles), then $\vartheta_m(f)|_{H^1}=0$ (because V is a convolution ideal and C_K is commutative); hence $\langle f,f^\sharp\rangle=0$ on V and by adding elements of V one can make $f\star f^\sharp(1)=\int_{C_K}|f(g)|^2|g|d^*g<\epsilon$ for any $\epsilon>0$ (surjectivity of E, App. 1 of [10]).

RH for all Grossencharakter L-functions on K is equivalent to the Weil-type estimate $Z(f)\bullet_{trans}Z(f)\le 2d(Z(f))d'(Z(f))-\Delta\bullet\Delta\,(f\star f^\sharp)(1)$ for all f in S(C_K), where Z(f)=correspondence attached to f, with $\log|a|$ interpreted as $-\Delta\bullet\Delta\log q$ analogue (self-intersection of diagonal).
hypotheses: dictionary of Sec 7 (degree, codegree, transverse intersection defined via local principal values in (6.3))

statement: For y in X_{K,v}, the representation $\pi_y$ of the groupoid C*-algebra of the v-valuation system is a positive-energy representation iff $y\in\Xi_{K,v}$ (the locus of adeles with y_w!=0 and |y_w|=1 for almost all w).

For the C*-dynamical system $(C^*(G(p)),\sigma^p_t)$ over K=Q: (1) pi_y positive energy for y in A*_{Q,p}; (2) for $y_\infty=\lambda^{-1}$, $\lambda\in(1,p]$ the partition function is $Z_p(\lambda,\beta)=2\frac{1-p^{-\beta}}{1-p^{1-\beta}}f_p(\lambda,\beta)$; (3) the functionals $\psi_{\beta,y}(a)=\mathrm{Tr}(e^{-\beta H_y}\pi_y(a))$ are KMS_beta states depending weakly continuously on y.
The representation of C_K on $H^1_\chi(\mathbb A_K/K^*,C_K)$ gives the spectral realization of the zeros of L(chi,.) (all zeros, via Meyer's nuclear function spaces; variant of Cor 2 of [10]).
role: Spectral side of the trace formula

statement: For f in V, theta_m(f) vanishes on H^1.
role: Source of the large radical of the trace pairing (analogue of trivial correspondences)

statement: The projection from the lifted locus $\tilde\Xi_{\mathbb Q}$ to $\Xi_{\mathbb Q}$ is surjective; two elements of the same v-component have the same image in $C_{\mathbb Q}$ iff they lie on one orbit of T (Tx=px at p, Tx=-x at infinity).
role: Identification of periodic orbits / classical points

statement: Algebra B generated by the functions phi_a, psi_a; defines N(f)=... counting-function type expression on the cover.
role: Arithmetic subalgebra, Frobenius and monodromy

statement: Exact sequence $0\to C(T_j)\otimes\mathcal K\to A_j\to C^*(U)\to0$ for two real places model, with A the fibered product of A_j over C*(U).
role: Vanishing-cycles analogy (Sec 10)

statement: Assume RH. As $y\to0^+$, $F(y)=\sum_{n\ge1}(\Lambda(n)-1)e^{-ny}=O(y^{-1/2})$, and there is a constant $K>0$ such that each of $F(y)<-K y^{-1/2}$ and $F(y)>K y^{-1/2}$ holds for a sequence of $y\to0$, i.e. $F(y)=\Omega_\pm(y^{-1/2})$.

There is $K>0$ with $\psi(x)-x<-K\sqrt x$ and $\psi(x)-x>K\sqrt x$ each for arbitrarily large $x$, i.e. $\psi(x)-x=\Omega_\pm(\sqrt x)$ (substantially Schmidt's theorem); stated unconditionally in the paper, deduced from Theorem 2.24 in the case RH holds and from the known $\Omega_\pm(x^{\Theta-\delta})$ result when $\Theta>1/2$.
hypotheses: none beyond the case split on Theta (sup of real parts of zeros)

statement: Assuming RH, all Riesz means (hence Cesaro means) formed from $\sum(\Lambda(n)-1)$ are of the forms $O(\sqrt\omega)$, $\Omega_+(\sqrt\omega)$, $\Omega_-(\sqrt\omega)$.

Let $L(s)=1^{-s}-3^{-s}+5^{-s}-\cdots$ ($\sigma>0$). If all complex zeros of $L(s)$ have real part $1/2$, then Tchebychev's 1853 claim holds: $F(y)=e^{-3y}-e^{-5y}+e^{-7y}+e^{-11y}-\dots=\sum_{p>2}(-1)^{(p+1)/2}e^{-py}\to+\infty$ as $y\to0^+$; quantitatively Thm 2.34 gives a lower bound of order $H/\sqrt{y\log(1/y)}$-type (OCR of exact form of (2.341) unreliable), and Thm 2.35: the Riesz/Cesaro mean of the first order of $\sum(-1)^{(p-1)/2}\log p$ tends to $-\infty$ at least as fast as a constant multiple of $-\sqrt\omega$. (Exact constants/forms: statement of Thm 2.33 garbled in OCR.)
hypotheses: all complex zeros of the Dirichlet L-function L(s,chi_4) have real part 1/2 (GRH for the character mod 4)

statement: $\int_{-T}^{T}|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|^2dt\sim 2T\log T$ as $T\to\infty$.

For real $a,b,\omega$ with $a,b>0$ (b a scale parameter), a Landau-type bound for the exponential sum $\sum_{0<\gamma\le T}e^{i\omega\gamma\log(b\gamma)}$-type sums over ordinates of zeros (sum $\sum'$ in the paper; exact exponents garbled in OCR), of size $O(T^{(1+a)/2})$ (trivial for $a\ge1$), with $O(\log T)$ when $\omega<$ an explicit threshold depending on $a$, uniform for $b$ in compact intervals; and convergence of the sum continued to infinity when $\omega$ is below that threshold. Introduction: conjecture that the true order is $o(T^{1/2+\epsilon})$ for all $a$.
hypotheses: a,b>0 and omega real (RH may be assumed in simplified forms)

statement: For every $\epsilon>0$ there is $T_0(\epsilon)$ such that for $T>T_0$ the segment $\{\tfrac12+it:\ T<t\le T+T^{1/4+\epsilon}\}$ contains at least one zero of $\zeta(s)$ of odd order. Hence $N_0(T)$, the number of zeros on $\sigma=1/2$ with $0<t\le T$, satisfies $N_0(T)=\Omega(T^{3/4-\epsilon})$? -- as printed: $N_0(T)=\Omega(T^{1/4-\epsilon})$ for every $\epsilon>0$ (the OCR of the exponent in (1.41)/Thm 4.42 is ambiguous; the zero-spacing $T^{1/4+\epsilon}$ implies a lower bound $T^{3/4-\epsilon}$, so the printed exponent should be checked against the page image).

Thm 5.8: $\psi(x)-x=\Omega_+(\sqrt x\log\log\log x)$ and $\psi(x)-x=\Omega_-(\sqrt x\log\log\log x)$. Thm 5.81: $\Pi(x)-\mathrm{li}(x)+\tfrac12\mathrm{li}(\sqrt x)=\Omega_{\pm}\big(\tfrac{\sqrt x\log\log\log x}{\log x}\big)$ [Littlewood's theorem]. In particular $\Pi(x)>\mathrm{li}(x)$ for arbitrarily large $x$ (so (1.53) $\Pi(x)<\mathrm{li}(x)$ is false). Thm 5.6: if $F(i x)$ boundary values, $-\Im F(ix)=\Omega_+(\log\log x)$ and $-\Im F(ix)=\Omega_-(\log\log x)$ hmm as printed; Thm 5.2 gives the corresponding inequalities on the strip.
hypotheses: unconditional (zeros off the line only strengthen the result)

statement: $e^{-y}=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{\kappa-i\infty}^{\kappa+i\infty}\Gamma(s)y^{-s}ds$, $\Re y>0$, $\kappa>0$.
role: Basic transform linking Dirichlet series to e^{-ny} sums throughout section 2.

statement: If $\sum a_n\lambda_n^{-s}$ converges absolutely for $\sigma>\sigma_0$, the sum function F(s) is regular for $\sigma>c$ (continuous on $\sigma=c$) with $F(s)=O(e^{C|t|})$, $C<\pi/2$ uniformly for $\sigma\ge c$, then $f(y)=\sum a_ne^{-\lambda_ny}=o(y^{-c})$ as $y\to0$.
role: Tauberian-type input yielding PNT-equivalent forms (1.121)-(1.124) via Thm 2.121, 2.13, 2.14.

statement: Tauberian-type lemma (equivalent to Theorems D, E, F of Hardy-Littlewood, Messenger of Math.): Abel-type summability f(y)->F(0) implies Riesz/convergence under one-sided conditions on a_n.
role: Passes from e^{-ny} means to convergence of the series.

statement: Lemmas on the integral representation of $K_\nu(y)$ and its asymptotics for $y=re^{i\theta}$, $|\theta|<\pi/2-\delta$ used for the mean-square computation.
role: Evaluates the diagonal and off-diagonal terms in the proof of Theorem 2.41 by the Cahen-Mellin route.

label_in_source: Lemma 5.3 and Dirichlet's theorem on simultaneous approximation (5.4)
statement: Kronecker/Dirichlet approximation lemma: simultaneous diophantine approximation lets one align the phases of the first many terms $\gamma_n\log$ of $\sum \rho^{-1}x^{\rho}$ so that the sum of the first $N$ terms of the explicit formula is as large as $\sqrt{x}\log\log\log x$.
role: Drives Theorem 5.2 / 5.6 (Omega results for the oscillating sum).

statement: As $T\to\infty$: $\int_0^T|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|^4dt=\frac1{2\pi^2}T\log^4T+O(T\log^3T)$.
hypotheses: unconditional; relies on the Hardy-Littlewood approximate functional equation for zeta(s)^2 (18), communicated privately and then unpublished

location: Introduction p. 277; proof in sec. 7, pp. 298-300
